This guy is a joke. Genuinely awful. First day of class he'll tell you there will be no feedback on homework and it's completion and it takes hours upon hours to complete it and it often serves zero purpose for the class. This is the worst professor I've ever had. I took the elective because it sounds interesting but he completely ruins it.

This class wasn't awful but it's a lot of work. I took the online version so there were less opportunities for content review, but it's still doable and tests were alright. The TA was a big help (and also basically ran the whole class). Taking it in-person might be better for concepts to be cleared up, but overall I still learned a lot.
Probably one of the best teachers I've had. Classes were well done and informative. Office hours were easily accessible and he is good with managing time and answering questions.

Scottie is a great guy, and if you are looking for some cool things that can apply to your everyday computing life this is a great class. I still use some of the applications that we discuss such as VM's in this class that I did not know about before.

Scottie is a fine professor, he can get lost in his own world sometimes haha. HW can be unclear sometimes but gives plenty of time to get it done and will explain it if you have questions on discord or next time in class just don't wait. Lecture can get bland and boring sometimes. He does care though and tries to engage the class.

Mickey Mouse class. Could chat gpt the entire course. There is no lectures its a textbook that you follow. Theres a project at the end that is full stack development but the grading is fairly easy. Another easy scottie Murrell class im not sure how the university lets this slide.

Scottie Murrell is a really good guy who is always willing to help you with the concepts. However, he doesn't teach anything. Nothing he says makes any sense. His lectures and slide shows somehow leave me even more confused than before. He basically expects you to already know everything he is talking about. Good luck in his class.
I really liked this class. We got to do some really cool stuff. The lectures sometimes got a little boring but overall it was ok.

Scottie seems like a great guy, was always available to answer questions and extremely knowledgeable about Unix. However, some of his lectures or assignment requirements were very incoherent and unrelated to what we were learning in class or doing for an assignment. Midterm + Final were honestly drastically easier than smaller weighted assignments.

Pretty much completion assignments all the way up until the last 4 weeks of class, which is a final project, that no one understands and he expects you to know/learn full stack development on your own.

This is for CS4050. His slides, labs, and exams are all AI generated or stolen from other professors. He comes to class completely unprepared every day and is incapable of answering questions from students. No feedback when you lose points, but he's an extremely generous grader. Seems like a good dude, but I'd still avoid his courses at all costs.

Dr. Goggins is incapable of teaching any topic, no matter the simplicity. Attending lecture will only leave you more confused than never attending. He is bad about giving feedback to students for labs. Lectures primarily consist of him getting corrected by students after he guessed what a slide meant. Overall, a likeable guy, but can't teach.

He gives some confusing, cobbled-together lectures that make it look like he hasn't taught this class before, even though he has many times. It's hard to understand what you should be studying. You won't get much from this class, but at least he's a lenient grader. He's very easy to talk to in class, but was not there when I went to office hours.

The first 2 thirds of the class consisted of confusing lectures and easy labs with most covering what you've already learned, but the last third contained 2 much harder experimental labs covering poorly taught/uncovered material. Currently this class is an easy A, but you will not learn much.
Pretty chill professor. Easy to reach out too.

Extremely disorganized throughout the course. He used other prof's slides and didn't seem to understand half of them: he would read verbatim and was unable to answer questions about stuff on it. Tests are unnecessarily confusing and he occasionally had the wrong answers. Fortunately his grading is lax, but I will still avoid him in the future.

Goggins assigns work that is extremely unclear; almost no one in the class has any idea what they're doing. It's not that the assignments are hard, it's that there's a huge lack of direction. It seems like Goggins forgets about the class as soon as he leaves it every day. It's intentionally vague and frustrating.

Unfortunately SE is a required course. Its unfortunate because Goggins teaches this course. You probably won't know what is going on, the lectures are almost random and the homework assignments were difficult only because we have no idea what to do. Oftentimes does not respond in his own discord server for the class. His communication is asinine

By pop quizzes, I mean extra credit attendance points. Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable, but was extremely difficult to talk to outside class (and even avoided students close to due dates). Lots of homework and huge accounting projects, so don't wait until the last minute to do them. She didn't assign our second textbook until end of semester.

Professor Ferguson is strict but a good teacher. The homework doesn't take too long but is due before class starts in person. On most days that there is no homework due she will give out extra credit for attendance. Her tests are honestly really easy; the multiple choice is a breeze and then the problems come from the hw or in class. Just study!

This woman is the worst teacher I have ever had. She refuses to work with students on their grades as I went to her several times about it. For instance, one time Canvas closed the submission box for an assignment early, and when I went to explain it to her she said I could email it in. I did and she then refused to give me any points for it. awful

Class is taught in ways that make simple concepts overall complicated and so much harder than it needs to be. Cheat sheets are given but only one side and there is to much material dumped on you where you couldn't get it all on the sheet if you wanted to. Exams are given at bad times and overall set up to make a simple class hard.
Stacy really cares about students and she provides plenty of opportunities for extra credit. Also, she teaches well.

She is a great teacher; the only downside is that she sometimes overcomplicates the easy things and makes you question it all together. The larger topics sometimes feel like she's just showing you what to do and not really explaining it clearly. She's great, just pay close attention and make your notes easy to read for when you go back to study.
Overall just not applicable at all. Just a crazy amount of busy work. Felt like high school again.

Stacy is caring and a fantastic professor!  She is a professional who really cares about her students.  You get a cheat sheet on exams and lab attendance is optional (you can earn extra credit by going, but you can also choose to do the online assignment instead).  Exams are straightforward, lectures are useful/she points out what will be on exams.

Stacy is a great professor and a very nice person! She is always willing to help if you have any questions. Make sure to go to lab and class because it is very helpful (and will lead to success in the class). You get a cheat sheet on the tests. To prepare for the tests: go through the class workbook and do all the "on your owns" in it as well.

As far as content, this class was easier than Accounting 1. Sometimes, lab attendance is extra credit, so make sure to utilize that and go to lectures because they honestly help. She goes through lots of examples that are similar to exam questions. Stacy sometimes, however, can overexplain simple things and be repetitive. But that's okay :)

Good prof who made sure to have good TAs and be accessible to students. Labs are in-person (10-point quiz during each) but an assignment can be done online giving flexibility (but you can get extra credit going to labs). She only takes attendance a few times a semester, but it's worth 5% of your grade. I did badly on the exams and still got a B.

Boy, where do I start? Monotone + shrill voice (one-two punch combo), rude, tough grader. When a student isn't presenting (everyone has to), she just fills out notes on an iPad. I wish I had checked the grade distribution before taking this, lesson learned. Study hard, or be happy with a C. You have been warned.

This tax course is a first for all students, nonetheless she is strict for grading, lecturing and extra credit. She reads off a tablet and fills in notes over each chapter. Projects are vague, and she doesn't explain anything. She repeats the same words and phrases. She doesn't allow people to leave early or talk in class.

A lot is expected from students learning taxes for the first time. She lectures the entire time and acts like an old lady about leaving at the end of lecture and talking. There is a lot of material to memorize for weekly quizzes on top of 2 exams. Projects use reports and she assumes students understand and know how to figure everything out already

Professor Neuman illustrates the highest degree of preparedness and professionalism. All that she asks back is your respect. Very low tolerance for students who disrespect their peers by talking in class.

Neuman expects a high level of respect from students that isn't given back in return. She spends a lot of class time repeatedly yelling at everyone to be quiet. The whole class is based on quizzes, tests, and projects to be done outside of class. She mostly just writes notes on her Ipad for lectures and is a harsh grader. Wouldn't recommend

You must print out the lecture notes and bring them to class every day. All assignments are graded extremely harshly and if your answers aren't 100% exactly correct, expect to loose points. Also, she gets easily frustrated by students talking during class and will not hesitate to call you out. Overall I would not recommend this professor.
Very hard class to follow when he expects us to learn 95% of the material at home. Exams are nuts

Get ready to study. Exams are worth 75% of grade, so if you are a bad test taker like me... good luck. Did move the entire grading scale down 2% before the final exam. Lectures aren't great, and problem explanations are confusing to follow. Attendence points are only earned when you get answers correct on material he poorly covered 30 seconds prior
Professor extremely confusing to follow.
Really good and worthwhile class if you put in the work. Tim is an excellent professor too
Homework is nothing like what we see on the exams. Tim forgets the fact that in real life we can just google something, so one would think a one sided cheat sheet on exams would be acceptable.

He is a good person, but not a good teacher. I clicker is for attendance but not multiple choice, so if you put even a wrong decimal in, you do not get attendance credit for being there. He likes to repeat himself. His life's mission is to make the exams hard, and for us to memorize dozens of formulas. The lectures are also disorganized.
The expectations for tests are insane

Howald is a good person, but his ADHD-ridden lectures and inability to finish thoughts make his lectures nearly impossible to comprehend. His lectures do not pertain to the exams in any sort on the bright side. He usually provides a 200-question test bank, so I recommend memorizing formulas instead of listening to an "um ummm uh" filled word salad.

Took for Structural Analysis/CVENG3300. Great professor and lenient grader. If you understand the material and explain your work on exams, you will do well. Very accessible and willing to help in office hours and after class. Genuinely cares about the teaching and super reasonable if you have a request or question about grades/rounding.

Professor Jiang truly tried to make this class good and was very open outside class. However, this was his first time teaching software engineering and he was very unprepared. He did not know how to filter relevant information. Everything was group work with upwards of 150+ pages written per group. I truly believe he will improve with time.

Dr. Duan seems ok. He taught a couple classes and had the TAs teach the rest. This class was so easy to pass, but it felt like a waste of time. The grade is based on a few things: 5 WebGL assignments and a final project. This course doesn't have a ton of content, and the content that it does have is glossed over and poorly taught. Please avoid.

Deep learning is a very important class for any CS student. This class course slides are based on Stanford's CS231n . Grading is based on mid-term and final project. Lectures are good . Exam is easy. Prof Duan will help you form groups for the final project. So,it's killing two birds with one stone. Easy 'A' and you will learn something on the way.

Prof Duane's class is one of the toughest I took He himself said it The prerequisites were laid out clearly You need top be very very good at Data structures,a bit of Linear Algebra Mat lab and Open CV and Geometry It has only 3 assignments but prepare to sweat a lot He is a generous grader through

One of the professors everyone dreads having, but has no other choice. Will teach you how to do a specific example, and be tested on completely different examples. Mizzou CS deserves better CS Algo curriculum.

Saab is quite possibly the worst communicator to ever exist. He wouldn't talk to the TA's, so even they didn't know what was going to be on the exams. His lectures are painfully terrible. There is little explanation on anything, and it is difficult to understand and YouTube video can do a better job All assignment answers found online, so easy A
gives a fraction of the lecture time you pay for, tests on content he never explained

This class has optional homework, which is nice. It's also graded on weekly quizzes, which I find more agreeable than homework or projects when it comes to assessing understanding of this particular subject. The professor's just really quite dry, but if you can tolerate that and have a decent grasp on computer logic, it's an easy A.

He teaches math concepts. He does not really teach how to translate math concepts into programs. Good luck getting him to respond to your email. Considering that the lectures are pre-recorded and that theres not any real way to ask questions, this is easily one of the worst classes Ive ever been in. Prepare to do a lot of online searching.
Rough content, but explained decently. Hard to understand.

Your grade is divided into four 25% categories: Test 1, Test 2, Quizzes, and Programs. Quizzes are weekly, and the questions are exactly the same as the optional homework. The answers are on google. Go to the TA's for help on programs (if you need it). For the tests, review the book chapters he gives you, and prepare for conceptual questions.

Class was fine, everything is in the textbook (I found it online). Weekly quizzes were directly from the unassigned optional homework each week, so know how to do them. 2 in-class exams, no final. A single question on the exam can be worth a lot of points (KNOW TIME COMPLEXITIES) otherwise if you read the book and/or attend class you'll be fine.
Try and avoid taking her class if possible.  She's a nice person but the other professor for this class gives out easy A's.  Labs are insanely difficult and so is the final.
Lectures aren't mandatory, but if you miss one you'll have no idea what's going on.  Labs are insanely difficult, and class slides make no sense without attending the lecture.
Impossible to succeed in class if you fall behind, even if it is just a little bit. Miss a lecture and you are in trouble, because the slides make no sense without the lecture.
dont take her please

Please understand that the lectures don't really help with any of the homework or quizzes you take. The quizzes get astronomically harder as the semester continues. Because this is online, the way you enter in your results ends up in a lot of misses points. Don't rely on the final exam as you will most likely not do well. Do Extra credit

Smart, but not very good at teaching. She put no prerequisites but requires that you know linear algebra and statistics to a higher degree than they were taught. She will teach as if you know everything perfectly. As she teaches, she expects you to know everything she covered, or just covered last time. 6 weeks in and I have learned nothing.
Her accent makes it very hard to understand her. She goes way to fast with examples and she only does them once.

This is coming from a student who is going to receive an A in the class by the way. She goes so freaking fast it's unbelievable. You don't have time to even write down notes. She also barely speaks English and can't even understand her half of the time. The worst professor I've ever had, would not recommend this class. Take the electrical eng one

He seems terrifying, but get on his good side by participating in discussion & following his instructions to the T. If you don't participate he will single you out, so make sure you're always prepared & on your toes.

Pro Tip: after finishing the assigned readings, form a few comments or thoughtful questions beforehand so you're always ready.

Excellent section professor if you like a challenge. Very dry humor. Speak up in discussion or prepare to be singled out. Sends grades through email and doesn't input them in Canvas, so it's hard to keep track of your cumulative grade. However, there's opportunities for extra credit and the assignments are very structured and don't sneak up on you.

He challenges his class by: calling on people randomly, asking about outside knowledge, and questioning peoples' assertions. At first I struggled a lot with his grammar/punctuation based grading system for papers, but I adapted over time. He asks difficult questions about the reading that force you to think. Pro tip: show up and participate.

Our essays and the midterm were graded with no rubric or standardized system and those were 60% of our grade. Discussion sections were stressful as they were graded and I always felt like I needed prior knowledge to understand what we were talking about--even though I had read. He also did not put a single grade in Canvas until the end of the year.

He's the worst. Expects outside knowledge from his students with stuff that doesn't relate to the class. Rants about philosophy in the middle of the lecture. Honestly, he is extremely pretentious and arrogant.
The guy takes everything personal and is relentless when it comes to grading.

He definitely comes off as rough around the edges at first. I'll be honest, the first couple weeks I wanted to drop the class, but I found that though he may be gruff at times, he actually really does care about your learning and development. Participate in class, appear intrigued, and ready to learn and you'll be fine.

Can seem a little rude at first, but he does care about student learning. Do the readings, there are quizzes over the material. He asks A LOT of questions in class. If you participate, he respects you more. Tests are heavy on essays. Go to class, take good notes, and read over them occasionally. You'll learn a lot!
Not worth the credit.

Definitely one of the weirdest experiences I have had with a class. I can honestly say, with no exaggeration, that I learned nothing. The only reason anyone passes is he gives out "practice" quizzes and tests that are the actual assessment. You simply need to memorize what is on these for an easy A. No homework, attendance not mandatory.

Statics in the beginning is pretty intuitive, I think Aaron did a good job at giving the class a solid foundation for the rest of the course. However, Exam 1 is by far the easiest exam, and Exam 2 is miles harder (likely on purpose). Do not get discouraged, though, Aaron and all the TA's/PLA's are available every day of the week.
Great professor and his notes are easy to follow and organized. He also recognized me as his student in the engineering building one time even though I never went to office hours

He gets mad if he is asked about his logic during example problems. Essentially, prepare to watch him do only example problems that aren't near as challenging as the exams, while rarely explaining his logic during the example problems. Only one person out of 200 in the class got full points on a problem (25% of exam pts) and he blamed the class.
His lectures were very good and if you were able to follow those then you'll do fine on exams.

He is a very good professor teaching a pretty difficult class. The way it is set up gives you no excuse not to pass other than a lack of effort. Anyone can get a good grade in this class but you have to work for it for sure. The second test was definitely the hardest, so beware. Also, weekly quizzes, so stay on top of things.

Aaron's a good professor. Lectures are just practice problems the entire time. Once a week in class quizzes. Review sessions held outside of class multiple times a week and Aaron was always available for questions or help. Statics isn't the easiest subject but there are so many resources available to succeed in this class if you want to.

Dr. Saucier was good at explaining problems. Held review sessions with himself or the Ta's. Lots of Ta office ours during the week and 2 weekly review sessions with them are held. Ta help session before each exam too. Tells you what will be exactly on the exam. It is just like the homework and in class stuff, just a little harder on the exams.

Saucier was a cool professor who explained concepts well. Posts notes online, posts practice exams, and exams were a little tough but he curved the lowest grade. Only issue is he could come off as a little derogatory when answering questions for students who were really confused. Slightly more homework than usual but still a reasonable amount

This is the class you want to attend if you're in the MU IT program or any degree! Absolutely fun to attend and he has a deep understanding in how life is tough as a college student. Very informational and passionate in cyber sec and loves to help you out when possible.

Loved this class! Professor Scantlin has a huge passion for infosec and his passion shows throughout the course and makes the course that much more enjoyable. Very understanding of his students and also is very approachable and helpful. Brian his TA is incredible as well and was available almost 24/7 for help. Highly recommend this course!
He was good for Cyber Sec. I enjoyed his current events portion of the lectures. Kind of a slow class if you already have some experience in cyber sec.

Professor Sullivan is one of my favorite professors. He is incredibly nice and he genuinely cares about your well-being. He talks about his life a lot which is really nice because he feels more like a genuine human being rather than just a professor. He doesn't check homework for accuracy just asks that you do it. Pay attention to Truth Tables.
Professor Sullivan is great and was my favorite professor. He makes the class interesting and easy to understand. If you have to take a Philosophy class definitely take it with Aaron.

He is the funniest professor ever. He doesnt mind in you skip class. There homework and quizzes but you cant fail the quiz and he doesnt check homework. He is absolutely hilarious and nice. Not difficult at all and the work was easy to understand.

best intro philosophy prof anyone could ask for, is very attentive to student's needs if something comes up and tries to explain concepts as best he can. Tests are straightforward and exactly what was taught in class

Best ethics class ever! Super fun, not stressful, relevant, and Sullivan is super nice! Only 3 tests and a few pop quizzes he grades generously. Just read the assignment or watch black mirror and discuss!
dope philosophy teacher that cares about his students and their knowledge about philosophy

Professor Sullivan is the absolute best. Love his class. He is very caring and gives extensions when you need them. While there isn't really a penalty for missing class, I highly recommend you go as it helps on the tests (which are entirely multiple choice). The lectures are also really interesting. Half the homework is watching Black Mirror.

Prof Sullivan's class was always interesting. He always expanded on questions and didn't make anyone feel bad about asking too many. He was respectful of different perspectives. He had a few pop quizzes to incentives us to come to class, but if you missed a class/ quiz he would let you retake it if you asked. Tests were online which was nice.
Great professor! Really cares about his students learning.

Rabbani did a good job teaching this course, but he isnt the most organizing. Lectures move slowly. There were a good number of assignments given, and he gives random top hat quizzes. I did learn a lot in this class and I overall had a positive experience.

He abuses his academic freedom and deviates from his own syllabus. Very unclear grading criteria. He is very approachable at the beginning of the course, and very difficult to work with during the last month of class. His lectures are slow and unclear. He maybe covers 5 slides in one class. He's a nice person, but a bad professor.
Do the practice test and you will be fine. The test is a direct copy of it with different numbers. That is virtually all you need to do to get at least a B.

The study guide is exactly like the test which makes tests a lot easier. Professor Helfer is a super smart and really nice guy, but his lectures can be really confusing and he talks really quiet. He is a super lenient grader and his tests are easy if you understand the study guide. Overall he is a solid professor.
Great professor, a very lenient Calc 3 professor. Super nice guy, always approachable for help and understanding. The exams are always exactly like the study guide he gives out, very helpful.
Absolutely incredible. Helfer is one of the most knowledgeable and engaging professors I've ever had.

Super nice guy, but not a great teacher. Grading guidelines are completely different than what's on the syllabus, so beware of that. Likes to talk quietly, write in tiny font, and stand in front of what he's writing on the board, making him very difficult to follow. His tests are a joke, though, and you can easily ace them if you study.

Required intense critical thinking and generation of new ideas to get high scores on papers. His grading turnaround is slow because of how he assigns work. Coursework follows no schedule. Papers are 20-25 pages in length. Double spaced 12 pt. You can write an entire rough draft and if he doesnt like the idea he asks you to doover for less grade

Not available for help, get ready to read. Has no defined textbook. Makes up course as semester drags on. If you don't have writing skills, don't take this MATH course. Will grade on the most specific details as possible.
He's hard to follow, but it's pretty easy to get an A if you use the book to clear up the lectures. He's very passionate, but almost too knowledgeable.

Somewhat rude, and harsh with his course. Kind of aggressive with his grading. Miss any class for any reason whether it is sickness or school sanctioned events and he deducts from your total participation 5 points each time. (Post Normal Biochemistry)
Dr. Yokom's lack of student engagement makes this course very difficult for students.

Professor Yokom is knowledgeable about the subject, he cannot convey it in a way that is understandable to non-major students taking a lower level Biochemistry course. Weekly quizzes online. Group assignments once a week also. No homework which sucks because it would make the class better to understand. You MUST pay attention and study HARD to pass
Her lectures include everything she says on the slides, so you can take easy notes. As long as you actually do a quizlet get the information in your head you'll do great on the tests and quizzes

Lectures are very fun to listen to and do not require a lot of critical thinking. There are weekly quizzes on Friday's but if you review your notes and pay attention, they are not that hard. Difficulty depends on what section you are in but overall pretty easy. The final is VERY easy if you take notes and review them beforehand. Labs are so fun!!!!

He is honestly a great professor, I wish he taught more classes so I could take them. He LOVES to give partial credit on quizzes and exams and also offers a large amount of extra credit. You can tell he loves to teach and is passionate about his job. Attendance is not required but is helpful and he gets frustrated when no one shows up for class.

Lots of extra credit and an easy grader. Every exam and quiz had bonus questions. Exams, including the final, are NOT cumulative. Talk to Dr. Balboula if you're having issues and he'll actually help you. He is very quiet so try to sit close to the front, but otherwise very straight to the point and doesn't waste time with small details.

Very slow lectures which get a bit redundant if anyone asks him to repeat information more than once, but he really seems to care about everyone doing well and is by far the most lenient grader grader in AnSci I have ever heard of. Labs are interesting, and assignments and exams are super easy and very clear what you should study if you go to class

Dr. Balboula is one of the best AnSci professors I've had, especially in upper level courses. He simplifies concepts and repeats complex topics if we ask. He genuinely wants his students to learn and succeed in his class. The written assignments are only based on participation. What's on the quizzes is on the exam, and no trick questions!

Dr. Balboula is an amazing professor who you can tell really loves what he does. It was really refreshing to take his course and be reminded that learning can be fun. I came into the course with no care for reproduction and came out really considering it as a potential career choice. Take this course if you can!

Amazing professor. His tests were all written, which was great because if you hit key points even if you didn't know everything you'd get decent grades in the course. Made it really easy to learn and would print his slides for everyone before class. The labs were always interesting and he cared most about understanding rather than memorization

Dr. Balboua is the most amazing and caring professor I have experienced at Mizzou! He really does care about his students and just wants you to understand. If you are struggling on a quiz ask him about the question and he will help you out a lot! He offers 2 extra credit writing assignments that will bump your grade up a lot! Make sure you study!

I really enjoyed taking this class with Dr. G. She's an involved professor who is clearly passionate about what she teaches. She helped me get involved w research at the university and was one of the first academic connections I made at Mizzou. There is a fair amount of reading required for this course, but IMO not unreasonable.

Dr. Guhlincozzi's class is what made me declare a WGST major! Discussions in her class were amazing, and her research focus of feminist geography is so interesting. She is also funny, approachable, and listens to her students.
Doesn't seem to have a grasp on what she's teaching, I would 100% stay away from this course if you value your sanity

Dr. Guhlincozzi was excited about Feminist Geography and had decent lectures. However, the weekly quizzes you took were insanely difficult and based entirely on unclear academic journals. They were only 4-5 questions but took between 30 minutes to an hour to complete. The written final was also insane and took 3.5 hours to complete 15 questions.

Prof is nice but she does not understand that this class is an ELECTIVE. It took more effort than my major classes. You take a quiz every which which takes you over an hour to do and are expected to read 20+ pages of academic journals. Don't take it thinking it'll be an easy A because you're an woman. If you don't learn by reading, don't take.

She is nice but her class is bad. This class took more effort/time than my core classes because we had to read 20+ pages of academic readings and had a quiz every week that would take me around 2 hours. She was sometimes late to class and would easily get off topic. She didn't explain concepts well enough. Projects were time consuming and not fun.

Aidah is my favorite professor at Mizzou so far! She is extremely kind and super fun to work with. She gives great critiques in class and it is not hard to be successful in this class. The only downside is you only get 3 unexcused absences. Do the weekly reflections and go to the plays, and you'll do great!!

Nice.
Likes math.
Good vibes.

He's a little shy but a very nice guy, made math understandable. He wears fun shirts. My personal favorite is his "Hot Salami" shirt. He's always thankful to those who come to class and has a good grasp at the classroom level of understanding. I would recommend taking this course with him.

Aidan was a great instructor. The course material is fairly easy when it comes to mathematics and he does a decent job at teaching it. Overall just focus and show up to class and you'll do fine in this course. He has office hours as well if you are struggling.
Dr. Li is a bit eccentric but a really cool professor. He's very knowledgeable and passionate about astronomy, which means you learn a lot but sometimes in a meandering way. Super easy grader.

I took Astrobiology (4102) with Dr. Li. Definitely the easiest class I will ever take in college, I could have easily gotten an A in this class in high school. Dr. Li is a great guy who is a lot of fun to talk to and makes his lectures very interesting while encouraging conversation. Homework is completion graded, and exams were HW problems.

Li is knowledgeable about his field. He knows its difficult and doesnt demand much. He handed out answers for homework, just so we could rework the problems quickly. The midterm was open note, though the final was closed. Not a difficult class, but meandering and occasionally confusing if youre expecting a clear progression of topics.

Hands down the easiest class to pass. He's very hard to understand. I think I opened my textbook once, but you need the online codes to do the labs (which he didn't explain at all). I only went to class when he handed out "homework" and on quiz days. FYI, the homework is the quiz and he gives you the answers to the homework...

Aigen Li was the best teacher I had! He assigned homework early in the week. Then he'd give us ALL  the answers to the homework before it was due. We would take a quiz over the homework and the questions were very similar. Then after the quiz he would collect the homework. The tests were a combination all the quizzes. IF you didnt get an A you suck

I took this class because it was four credits and counted towards my physical science credit. I could NOT understand him no matter how hard I tried. Didn't feel like any of his lectures were relevant. All the labs he just thrusted upon us at the VERY end of the semester without explaining a one of them. Quizzes were easy. Attendance was infrequent.

Easy course. Although he is somewhat hard to understand, if you do the work required it is easy to get an A grade. Textbook was hardly ever used, and all in class lecture notes were put online (therefore I hardly ever went). To people who are not interested in Astronomy or let alone science, this will be the most dry class of your life.

Seemed like a nice guy but cant understand anything he says because of his accent. Class has no organization, no refrence, the textbook wont really help. Do not take this class. One of the worst classes i have had at Mizzou.

She is one of the best professors I have had at Mizzou. She gave me extension on assignments and allowed resubmissions.. She is very caring and cares about students mental health.She is very understanding and kind professor and also teaches her subject well, you can tell she know well what she teaching.Take her class, you won't regret.
Very flexible with due dates and late assignment submissions.

She understands everything you are going through. Never forces you to work on something you don't like, or affects your mental health. If you have ADHD or you prefer to work individually, she allows even everyone is working in groups. She gives the best rubric ever, so you never miss even a point.

Ainsley Kelly is an amazing English teacher. As long as you show up to class and get your work done, this class should be a breeze. She has super clear grading criteria for essays and assignments. She is also very forgiving if you miss the due date by a day. Overall an amazing learning experience in her classroom.

Assignments had unclear criteria and very little instruction.1 of the assignments is to build your own website with no prior knowledge or instruction! Not fun. Not really a tough grader, thankfully! Very accessible but still not great with instructions. Quiz every week, none proctored. Last week had an overwhelming number of assignments.
I can tell he's passionate about what he teaches but he constantly rambles all class and it's so hard to retain any information. I still did decent because he grades relatively easily.

This is the best, most caring professor at Mizzou. Dr Gibson is very evidently educated and intelligent in philosophy and intellectual thought behind the founding era. The class is engaging and fun. You walk away from the semester understanding the background thought of so much. 
No homework, seminar style, two 500 word essays, and 2 exams.

Gibby is truly awesome! Taken two classes with him and have yet to get tired of him. He does love to talk quite a lot during his lectures but its all information that helps with his papers. He is a very relaxed grader and offers a ton of feedback on your papers. In both classes I've had with him there is a group project but it is not too difficult.

Even though this is only a 2000 level class, don't take it if you're not well-versed in political journalism/commentary. Even though he claims to be open-minded, Gibson has a bad habit of taking points off of assignments if your views don't directly align with his. He also doesn't respond to emails, and his critiques on papers are barely legible.

Professor Gibson has by far been the highlight of my time in college. Be sure to really pay attention to his lectures because that is where the papers will come from. He truly loves his students and what he is teaching and it is obvious. He does tend to ramble and go off topic, however he offers very deep insights to all of the topics he teaches.

The highlight of my semester fr. I know very few people who are half as knowledgeable and intelligent as Prof Gibson. He's so passionate about his field and about helping students engage critically with democracy-related subjects. I always looked forward to his lectures, and how he related them back to student experiences.

Literally one of my favorite professors ever. Super sweet and gives great feedback. Just make sure to listen, take notes, and participate in lecture. It will help you immensely during essays, especially for the midterm and final. He was really good at pulling out deeper analysis from students through his questions. Wish I had more classes with him.

One of the kindest male professors ever. He cares so much about his students and genuinely wants to hear from everyone. He pays attention and is so extremely educated. Show up to class and participate. Take notes during his lectures in your own words that you'll understand later. It will help you with the papers. LISTEN TO HIM.

This class was by far the hardest class I've ever had to take, but if you ask if for help and show that you are truly trying and doing your best, he will see that and do what he can to help. It is very important to go to the extra study sessions and ask him for extra help. He notices those things and it is so very worth it in the end.

Don't get me wrong this course is difficult. I struggled with a lot of the unit material. But when I expressed my worries with Dr.Parrish he helped me, and actually cared. He is the only reason I ended this class as strong as I did. Truly one of the best professors I have had at Mizzou!

Hands down, the hardest class I've taken at Mizzou. I had all A's up to this point, but I got Ds and Fs on the first two tests after attending all classes and office hours and spending my weekends outside of class studying. You get one dropped exam, but the course is exam-heavy. However, the prof is very caring, and because of his help, I passed.

Well this sucks to write because I actually like the guy a lot, but I would not wish taking this course online upon my worst enemy. If you have a job over summer or have trouble will online lectures do NOT take this class. It is very lecture intensive and many days will have you watching nearly 2 hours of lectures, and that's before note taking.

Took for 3202 and 4204. 3202 sucked--but due to Hanft, not him. 4204 has been a ton of fun. He's a good lecturer, though often has tangents, and wants everyone to learn. However, not in a gatekeeping sort of way. He respects grades as things for scholarships, etc., so doesn't try to aim for a class average GPA of 3.0 or any crap like that.
Very accessible outside of class, gives great lectures. Exams are difficult, but you won't have much homework and the homework grades boost your grade a lot.

Class was difficult. The lectures while fine were unhelpful. Tests and lecture materials didn't align. Tests were comprised of questions that had never been covered or expected students to make rash assumptions about the material. Funny guy, but class was dense and he didn't know what to focus on enough.

Highly recommend going to office hours as Dr. Parrish is very personable and reviews everything lectured about. He is pretty funny and overall a great lecturer! The course has some difficult content as there is a lot thrown at you, but I am so glad I had Dr. Parrish for it!

He is extremely kind, intelligent, and eager to have a good conversation about the subject during class. Some of the assignments felt daunting, but the level of preparation that he helps you achieve makes it feel significantly more manageable. If you have questions or ever just want to talk to him, he seems happy to meet.

He's a great guy. He is so smart and his enthusiasm and love for his work are infectious. However, the class set-up is not the best. Unattainable amounts of reading expected. Grading requirements were unclear (no rubrics, no feedback, etc.), and the work/grades were all packed in the second half of the semester (midterm, 2 papers, and a final).

Dr. Reichadrt has gotta be the best professor at Mizzou. He does everything in his power to support his students. Offers so much extra credit its crazy if you end with anything lower than an A. Took the honors version and it was the best decision. I am not by any means a history person, but his engaging lectures turned me into one.

I really enjoyed Dr. Reichardt's class! We had a small group, but he made history very approachable. One downside is his very late grading (most assignments, including the midterm, were graded the day before final grades were due).

I really enjoyed Professor Reichardt but it was a little bit of a tougher class. Nothing too bad but a lot of points came from essays and most of the readings were difficult to write from. He does offer a decent amount of extra credit which can really save your grade. He does lecture fast and doesn't always get through all the info.

Lectures were really long and he never got thru all of the info in one class, so I always was missing info for assignments. Lots of papers worth 200+ points with no rubrics. Just a lot of work for a gen ed history class, I had to put in more time for this class than ones for my major

I wasn't in the honors section so I had a TA grade all of my assignments, so I can't say anything on that part. That being said, I enjoyed the lectures he gave. The homework on InQuisitive was a little annoying, but not too bad overall.

Professor Reichardt was great. He was very well-educated and his booklist combined with his lecturing was an insanely valuable resource that I don't think I'll find in many other history courses. His unique approach to education with combining discussion and scholarly reading from incredible sources has helped me greatly with other history classes

Koldobskiy is great, but only if your learning style is to dive straight into examples. He rarely spent any significant amount of time on concepts in class, forcing me to learn a lot from the textbook. The general difficulty of calc III along with his teaching style made this class a struggle for me.
an awesome professor, he made sure that you understood what he was lecturing on and he had a nice flow that was easy to follow. if you just do the assigned homework then you'll be fine.
She is great! Alex is fun and cares about her students, and it's easy to succeed in her class!

Professor Socarides is hands down one of the best teachers I have ever had. She is super nice and her lectures are informative, and you can tell she really cares about her students. If you get a chance to take a class with her, do it!
loved her.

Not a bad professor, but seems very overbearing at times. You'll have to do group work with her, sadly, but its more along the lines of facilitating discussion than putting projects together. Other than that, the papers she makes you write are so short and so easy you have no excuse to get anything other than an A.
Great teacher, do the readings, show up for class, go to her for help on your papers if you need it and your golden

She is a great teacher, always wanting her students to do well. She is continuously learning as well as teaching and she strives to find out more so she can teach more. Very likable and enthusiastic, not to mention funny and adorable.
She's a great professor. She cares about her students and she is very helpful. Love her class.
She is my favorite professor I have ever had - she is smart, interesting, approachable and a great teacher. I highly recommend her!
Dr. Otis is super passionate about her work and is always willing to help you succeed!!

Professor Lewis's course in death grief and loss was very interesting however her teaching styles made it difficult to enjoy. Her rubrics had not been very clear for assignments leading people to miss points for things that they where unaware of. Lewis was open to zoom calls and meetings but never really addressed the concern that was brought up.

She is the sweetest, best, most caring person ever!!! I LOVE HER!! Super easy class, all quizzes were online and only a few participation things graded. She also offered extra credit and gave lots of points back on quizzes. Shes super into what shes taching and it shows and makes it so much more interesting. Shes is amazing TAKE HER CLASSES!!

Very kind and really wants his students to succeed. Things can be disorganized but he is very accessible and always willing to clear things up and make accommodations. Super funny with infectious passion for engineering.

Dr. Ali's lectures are a little slow, but he is extremely easy to work with and very caring. He's also very passionate about helping students, and is an extremely knowledgeable advisor for capstone projects.

He's the worst professor I've ever had. He's got a ridiculous attendance policy and then will send a TA to teach when he doesn't want to. On the plus side all of our midterms were online. It's like he knows he bad at his job so he lets us take most of the exams online. His handwriting can be illegible. I want to give a shoutout to Wayne the TA.

Dr. Sichani is perhaps the most disorganized and disrespectful professor at the university. Lectures were incredibly messy & information on the slides often was wrong. It was clear that he did not plan his lectures ahead of time. Practice problems were made up on the spot & not helpful. He clearly did not communicate with his TAs. Labs were helpful

Dr. Ali is a good lecturer, but paired with his very difficult to read handwriting and the fact that everything came from the textbook, it was hard to really take the class serious. The textbook and other resources would explain the concepts better than him. One of his TA's, Wayne, was also a very good aide for the class. Avoid if possible.

A very weird experience.

I want to give positives, because it's clear Dr. Sichani cares, but a lack of organization and chaotic teaching style make it very difficult to learn. The course concepts are simple, but he makes them feel more difficult. 5 minutes of YT taught me more than 10 lectures unfortunately.

Great guy, lenient grading, horrid TAs

If you have a pulse, you'll get an A in the class. However, if you actually want to learn something, his lectures are unorganized and his TAs are never around. Try to follow along with channels like "UConn HKN" to learn each topic and "Electrical and Electronics Engineering" to get good at solving problems quickly.

This professor is the worst I have ever had. You'll get an A in this class if you do ANY work at all but you won't learn anything. He assigns homework WAY above the expectations for a typical circuits 1 class, can't explain concepts well, grades very slowly, and has borderline unreadable handwriting. Nice guy, but shouldn't teach. TAs are bad too.

She graded all of our exams, and unfortunately, I find it strange how I received the same grade on two different exams. She was a very tough grader on essays, even if you have all of your facts right, she will still find something wrong about it if she doesn't have the same viewpoint.
Amazing class would take again!!

Attendance is required but you don't get points unless you participate in during class, which would be fine if there wasn't 30+ people trying to fit their thoughts into a 50 minute class.Her grading system makes no sense, they are supposed to be 60% of the grade but effect your grade less then participation. When I asked about it she gave attitude.

Alice was a nice TA, however, she graded the essay portion of the exam extremely hard. I am typically good at writing as well and I found that she took points off for very minute things. It was unfair as I heard other people with different TAs doing so much better in this course and felt it was easy as well. Not an easy A class, should've been.

The course doesn't have a textbook, rather Alicia sends out readings weekly, similarly to her other courses. She gives a lot of feedback, but is a very nice grader, and she makes sure everyone in her class is heard and a part of the conversation. Easily one of my favorite professors at Mizzou, I had her in two of my other courses, 3150 and 3160.
One of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had. Please take a class with her if you get the chance, you wont regret it.

Alicia is the best Spanish professor I've had during my time here at Mizzou. She makes every lecture fun, wants to get to know every student and facilitates great conversation. She is understanding and is accessible outside of the classroom as well. Fairly easy grader, but you have to put in the work. I highly recommend this class!

Alicia is the best Spanish professor I have ever had. There is a lot of homework, but that is how you learn Spanish. If you don't care about learning the language, then don't take Alicia's class. But if you do, you will learn so much from her. She is super caring and easy going. I loved getting to be in her class.

The sweetest Spanish professor I have ever had. She would randomly call on people but she didn't single anyone out and understood if you didn't understand the question. I wanted to take my next Spanish class with her but the section is full :(

Amazing! I loved taking Spanish with Alicia! She really helped me improve my Spanish grammar. Reading the textbook really hopes as we focus on exercises based on the readings in class. Overall, she gives good feedback and makes sure everyone is putting in effort.

Super funny and always happy. She gave lots of pity points on tests and essays. Forced lots of class participation. She did everything she could to give you a good grade. However, I'm a mech. engineering degree and this one class had more homework than all my other classes combined. It was at least 7 pages of notes almost every night.

Alicia is great! She may seem intimidating at first, but she is very caring and also super funny. She gives good feedback on assignments, and is a relatively easy grader in my opinion. Come to class prepared for the compositions, it will make them so much easier.
Very understanding, approachable, and reasonable prof. Felt bad skipping her classes. Taught us a lot of ethics and how crucial teamwork is with clear communication. Responds very fast to email.
Very understanding, approachable, and reasonable prof. Felt bad skipping her classes. Taught us a lot of ethics and how crucial teamwork is with clear communication. Responds very fast to email.

She doesn't respond to emails, the TA's working under her have no available contact info on their canvas page, there's no explanation for how to access the readings needed for the weekly group discussions, and none of the work I've submitted has been graded. I don't know how I'm going to even pass at this point.

I expected to learn anything about Emily Dickinson. Not so. 99% of the lectures were anecdotes about Barnstone's own experience studying Dickinson, or hour long, ridiculously niche tangents about one minute detail at the expense of everything else. Punctuated by trite, pseudofeminist rants. One can tell she's more a fangirl than a scholar.

It's nearly the end of the semester and she has no grades in at all, she only answers emails on her personal email, and I feel like I am wasting my time. Not to mention, for my workshop she did not even read my work yet still forced the workshop to happen. Just very unprofessional, but I guess it's an easy A. (I don't even know my grade, though).

I can't recommend her enough. She understands that life happens, things get turned in late. She meets you where you are and her feedback made me a much better writer. She won't force you to share in class, but leaves the floor open for anyone that wants to. We learn about poets, but most of this class is just generating poems. No exams. 10/10 prof.

You definitely have to keep up with the lectures/read the textbook to do well, but she is a caring professor. The good things are, that she teaches at a slow pace, and gives rather easy and simple midterms. Also, there are polls every class for attendance.

Worst professor I've ever had. She is rarely prepared for class, her iPad is always dying during class. Her examples are hard to follow, and she teaches like her students are getting their phd's in econ. It is very hard to understand her. DO NOT take a class with her.
Alexia was an amazing professor. With all of the work you have to do in J2150 she is definitely an amazing professor. You get the chance to resubmit all your work which is super helpful.

Senora Placeres is AMAZING! I have never felt like I understood or enjoyed Spanish before taking her class. She made it fun and enjoyable in a way no other professor has before. She came to class everyday so positive and genuinely cared about your understanding of the content. She is the best Spanish professor I've ever had.
She's just the best. There isn't much more to say than that. She makes the environment very comfortable even if you don't know what you're doing. I wish I could have her for every spanish class ever

She was very helpful in helping out every student and knew their name within the first 1-2 months. Class could be scary at times because she randomly calls on students, but it does engage everyone in the room, as much as I disliked it. She's very easy to reach outside of class and is always understanding and talks you through wrong answers.

Professor Placeres is a genuinely pleasant person. She facilitates the learning of her students by not chiding them or deducting points in ways other professors would. At the end of the day, she cares about your learning, do her a favor and care for your own performance and she will be a great aid to have.

I understand that the Spanish department is mainly controlled by the director, but I did find this to be the most difficult I have had to get a good grade and connect with a professor. If you are doing poorly she thinks you are lazy and doesn't offer sympathy. She rolled her eyes and scoffed in class. Spanish is hard; she doesn't make it easier.

She was so kind and took the time to help and/or get to know each student. She would encourage, but not force participation from every student and meet them where they were at. The course itself is pretty content and test heavy, but she prepares you well.

She's very kind and quickly learns everyone's names. She forces class participation in a good way and always gives constructive feedback. She supports a lighthearted mood and laughs at her own little mistakes.

She was my favorite professor this semester by far! She is so caring and wants you to understand and love Spanish and Spanish/Latin American culture as much as she does. Even though I won't have a class taught by her next semester, I am very excited to see her out and get the chance to say hi to her again. She's just a wonderful woman all around.
Text books are awful and quizzes are impossible. Health Science courses shouldn't be this cryptic and difficult. Do not take this class.

The material is actually pretty difficult but he gives an ungraded practice quiz before every exam that is very similar to the actual exam, so use it to study. His lectures are pretty hard to pay attention to, but anyone can pass this class with a relatively low amount of effort if you know where to look. Watch out for the final, its kind of hard.

exams are very easy, they are basically a copy of the study guide he gives us. I found most of my learning came from the homework. Lectures are brutal, they are very boring and he has horrible handwriting so it makes it hard to follow along. He can be intimidating but talking one-on-one with him he is helpful and accommodating.

Dr. Tsoi is really kind and has a good understanding of diff eq but the lectures came directly from the textbook so they could be hard to follow at points (textbook isn't great). He does give out a very helpful review packet for the exams and usually draws the exam problems directly from it. Homework can be challenging but does help you learn

The homework was difficult, but the exams and the final were straightforward and based on the lectures. He teaches straight out of the textbook and is not a very engaging professor. He didn't take the time to get to know his students, and his class was exam-weighted. He gave good review packets before exams that were similar to the exams.

Not much homework. Textbook is the worst diff eq textbook out there. Teaches straight from the book, not worth going to class. Saving grace is that exams were extremely straightforward and he was very caring when responding to emails. Learn whole course on YT from Dr. Trefor Bazett and it's easy A. I rate Tsoi high because of the easy exams.

We did the same things over and over each lecture like how to determine if a number is prime or composite (non prime) for over 4 lectures. Each and every lecture is like a summary of the first two introductory paragraphs of the book but in poorly spoken English. 95% of the homework you will NOT be taught in class. Exams covered lecture material.
canvas website had almost no information, felt like we did the same things in class everyday for weeks without new learning

Tsoi teaches right out of the textbook, so there is no need to go to class. He "took attendance" at each class but it never counted for credit. Homework is optional and if you do it and are on the edge of a grade, he will bump you up. Quizzes and Exams were straight from the textbook but changed the numbers. Easy A if you are good at memorizing.

He is one of the best, well-spoken teachers on campus. He explains points thoroughly and he makes interesting points. He makes everyone feel comfortable, even if they have differing opinions about sociological standpoints. You can tell he is well-educated, and is eager to pass along his knowledge to those who want it. SAGrader homework, easy tests.
He's very comfortable in front of a crowd and does a very good job explaining what he needs to and getting people to participate.

Homework is online and you can complete it until you get a 100%. 3 exams, no final. Have one big paper but I emailed him mine, he gave me corrections, and ended up getting an A. Easy A class if you go to class, do click points, and fill out the study guides.

Reading the book may not be necessary but it helps if you need more clarification or just to make sure you get an A. There are clicker points everyday which is the only reason I went although the class is pretty interesting but the powerpoints are online anyway. Assignments you can just take things directly from the book. Def recommend this class

Pretty good teacher. His class wasn't bad, just long to sit through. Clickers count as attendanceparticipation points. Assignments not hard (i got 100% on all of them). LOTS OF EXTRA CREDIT. 3 tests not final. I got a C on every test and still got a A in the class. Take his class.

Allison is a great professor. She cares about her students and their success. She will post mini lessons and encourage learning outside of mini lessons as well. You will actually learn from her lessons and the content she posts. Definitely study for the exams as they are a bit challenging. Wish she taught other courses so I could take her again!

Dr.Meyer is one of the easier professors in animal sciences. Favorite professor so far. He is very funny and chill and as long as you participate, class is fun. Mr. Tiwari is understanding if you have circumstances that call for an extended deadline. You basically get out what you put into his class and I would suggest putting in all you can.
Alok was a great professor. Participate and ask questions and you'll be fine. He truly is incredibly understanding and wants you to succeed.
Not an open minded professor; always had comments and was always docking, no matter what.

This was a great class to take! Very informative and relatively easy. Prof. Rose is super nice and very helpful if you need to reach out although she can take a little while to respond sometimes. You do have to read research papers which can be tough but she really eases you into it. Definitely recommend!

Professor Rose is great! There are quite a few writing assignments over the articles you read for the class, but she gives you time in class to go through each one and really understand it before you write the paper. The material is interesting, and the grading is pretty easy, as long as you do the work.
awesome professor! super nice and easy to approach! always willing to stay after class or meet up to help with whatever you need.  Really easy and interesting! Amazing capstone!!

She reminds me of a kindergarten teacher, but not in a patronizing way at all - just caring and informative, although quiet.  Her research is very interesting, the class was fun, and she's pretty open students presenting their own views and ideas or discussions.
Be ready to take notes, she is a very fast talker, and that's not just how she lectures, she is the same in her conversations.  Be attentive, and take good notes, and you will be fine.

She's a terrific teacher, and she does interesting research centered on children's friendships.  I loved her class (so did my non-psych major friends), and she's a caring, interesting, and dedicated teacher!

took this online event planning class as an upper-level area course for my major. we were thrown into a semester-long group project, having to meet virtually, even when our schedules  didn't align. we also had to meet with a community partner, which felt like an unpaid internship in a career field i wasn't pursuing. overall, communication lacked.

I've taken a couple classes with Amanda and always enjoy them. She can be a little strict with late/missing assignments, just communicate ahead of time and you'll be fine. Big presentation at the end of the semester, start early. She's a little intense with questions, but it's to help your final submission be great. Will happily take again.

I previously left an amazing review for her, however having her for more classes, my original rating does not reflect her current teaching. She is nice, her low level courses are easy. Higher level courses are horrible. Everyone dreads presentations with her. She will tear into you. She rarely responds to emails and provides little feedback.
Excellent teacher who cares about the subject and her students. Easy to talk to outside of class. Attendance through iClicker. Tests were open-book and open-note.

Dr. Alexander is by far and away the worst professor I have ever had at Mizzou.  She is a horrible communicator.  Gives no guidance on the semester long group project.  You also for some reason have to volunteer for 24 hours at a “community partner”.  Stay far away from this class if possible.
the easiest class i have ever taken. all homework assignments and exams were on quizlet. attendance does count for a grade

awesome professor! super nice and easy to approach! always willing to stay after class or meet up to help with whatever you need.  Really easy and interesting! Amazing capstone!!

shes perfect
She is not very genuine. And she treats us like little kids. She is over the top in an unauthentic way that feels forced. And her lectures are mostly repeats. I just cringed the entire time.

Dr. PH was truly a delight. I recommend her to everyone. She is emotionally intelligent, caring, and wants to see us succeed. The other review for this class is a gross misrepresentation of Dr. PH.
This professor is so disorganized. did not understand why I felt like I was in elementary school in so many ways, other than the way we are graded.

She is beyond nice, she seems to try and go  out of her way to try and make sure that everyone understands. She responds back to emails very quick. She is very nice as well. I cannot believe Dr. Durbak's rating is so low. She is an amazing professor with the know-how and the passion for her students. THERES A REASON SHE WON THE KEMPER FELLOW!! The best professor in BIO_SCI and its not close
Yappaholic!!!

Take this class

She loves to involve her students in what she's teaching and won't lecture at you the whole time. Fun group activities in class. Exams are online open note, few assignments. Final project she is STRICT about the use of AI and has strict guidelines. She is very nice, and very acedemic.

I adore Professor Elkhalid! She made contemporary theory so much fun at UARK and I want to have her again for another class. Amnee is GREAT! This was her first semester at the University of Arkansas and she was fabulous. She's extremely kind and cares for her students. Amnee is a great professor because she's always super excited about the material that she's teaching, even if the material itself isn't super exciting. She's also a fair grader and you should do fine if you follow the rubric.

Amnee is amazing!! I would highly recommend having her as an instructor. Awesome learning environment and this course was one of the most "real life" application classes I have taken in college. She is so kind and organized too.

Most of your grade is determined by attendance and speeches. If you miss more than three classes Amnee reduces your grade by a letter grade. She is a super cool professor that makes the class feel personal and also making it know that she cares greatly about the subject as well as her students.

Amnee is an awesome teacher!! She's easy to talk to and cares about her students. I learned SO much from her! Best teacher ever. Granted, it was a super easy class, but she was amazing.

I was genuinely kind of suprised to see many bad reviews. I thought that she really put in a lot of effort and was quite involved which a lot of professors aren't. As long as you do the work, I can not imagine why you would be getting anything less than an A in this class.

She took 10 points of an essay bc i called it a PHOTO instead of a SNIPPET and when i emailed her very kindly asking why i lost points, she literally called me by the wrong name, so she has standards she cant even hold herself to.

If you can, avoid taking ANY classes with Amy Simons. She takes things from level 1 to 100 all the time. It seemed like her goal was for us to fail her class. J2100 is a beast, but Amy made it less challenging for me. The feedback she gave on my papers really help improved my overall writing skills. Amy is literally the sweetest! She's super cool and very willing to help out her students as much as she can. I loved her class, she makes everything very fun and even though there is a lot to do, definitely worth it.

Writing intensive course, and yes it's intense. Professor Enderle is easy to work with though. Enderle is a very bubbly and joyful professor. She acts like she wants to be in class and is understanding. This class and organic chem are my heaviest workload classes this semester. Which is ridiculous. I mean it's an entry-level PUBLIC SPEAKING CLASS, it should not be this much work. Amy makes this class so much more difficult than necessary. She gives a bunch of ridiculous busy work, and her quizzes are so much harder than the exams. This class should be an easy A, but she makes it so much more difficult and time consuming than it needs to be.

Amy is so funny and she makes class quite interesting.  Speech is simple if you don't have a problem giving speeches in front of a class.  Take this class if you can talk purty and need a random elective.

Amy is such a bubbly and happy person, and she makes speech completely bearable. You have to take quizzes, but you always get a notecard. She grades pretty hard on your first speech. When you improve she notices and will give you better grades. STUDY for the tests. If you do, you're golden.
She is super hard grader and she's literally crazy.  It takes her two weeks to get things graded
Very fun teacher and easy going. Not too much work required. Quizzes and test can be a little tough but on quizzes you get to use a note card. Makes you feel very comfortable when giving a speech.

Dr. Petry covered the Swine section in BAP II; you must attend the lecture to learn what will be on the exams and quizzes. She cares and values students time. If you communicate with her, she can help out with anything! The group projects helped me gain confidence in working collaboratively and taught me the importance of asking for help when needed.

Dr. Petry is such a kind person who is truly interested in what she is teaching and it shows. Group work is heavy in her classroom so come prepared to work with others and share your ideas! Dr. Petry is a great teacher who truly cares about her students. Projects are detailed, but if you stay on top of them and check in with her before they're due, you'll get full credit. Dr. Petry expects a lot from her students, but her expectations are never out of touch with reality. It is a hard class but her test questions basically come right off the notes. TAKE THE OPTIONAL FINAL. Dr. Knopps is genuinely the nicest director I have ever had. You can tell she really cares about her students, and absolutely no one could do as good of a job as she does.

Dr. Knopps is very passionate about music as a whole and she makes marching band feel very special and not so much as a class. She does a great job managing an ensemble this large. It was an ensemble so there isn't a lot to say. Expectations were pretty clear but use of rehearsal time was questionable at times. Truly THE BEST band director in the land. Dr. Knopps cares so much for M2. She so frequently advocates for her students, and makes an effort to know all 350+ of us. I would highly reccomend doing band with Dr.Knopps.  She cares alot about the band and their health and she truely does show that on the way she welcomes everyone to M2.  She truely does make the band seem more like a family.

very nice guy cares about his students but the lecture slides are often bear and lot of what he says is on quizzes and tests but the concept itself is briefly mentioned on a slide so keep in mind you will have to look into the text book or type every word he says. props to him as lot of content but hard to know what to be grasping for quizzes/test

This class was honestly pretty difficult. A lot of people talk about how awful of a teacher Dr. C i think he was incredible. Best teacher I have EVER had. Very interesting man.Grades fair, overall GREAT teacher

Prof. Mori is one of my favorite teachers at Mizzou! She's super nice, explains things well and her classes are really enjoyable! Great class!!! She really loves this material.
Best teacher of all time!

Very fun and cool

Still working on a book he started over 27 years ago and got years of funding. Just can't get motivated to finish anything.

Andre is very scatter-headed at times but the class is pretty easy. The lectures were pretty thought provoking and the discussion section wasn't too bad. Show up to class and the exams are very easy.

Not an introductory course nor taught in an introductory manner: the concepts have considerable depth and rightfully so. I thought he was a terrible prof
interesting and helpful

Tough grader and not really good with tech. Pretty old-school, but provides feedback on assignments. There's definitely a decent amount of work outside class but it wasn't a huge overload. She's a very nice woman but when it comes to teaching she's just not a very good at it. She is actually the sweetest woman ever on earth. I had her freshmen year and she still stops to talk to me as a Junior. Definitely a harder grader but she's willing to work with you to do good. She is very good at NOT teaching. Heiss is such a sweet lady! J1300 is a fairly boring class to be quite honest, but she tries to make it fun and engage with you. The class is not at all hard, and she is very willing to work with you all the way through the semester

Heiss is wonderful! If you come to this class, you WILL succeed.  All of the assignments, except for a few will all be completed during class time. Dr. Pavlichenko is an extremely average professor. May times in my Calc II lecture we were behind the other class, then we became behind on the homework assignments. Okay. I took this professor at Missouri S&T and this was his first semester here and first semester teaching Calc3. But he was not good. Lectures were confusing and not really useful. Andrei is a visiting prof at S&T. I had to read out of the textbook a lot.

I have Andrei for Calc 3 at S&T and he is a really good teacher, some people might find that his lectures don't cater to their own preferred learning style, but I think Andrei does an excellent job of teaching and you can tell he knows what he is doing.

Very likeable guy. Engages with the class and is always available to answer questions and help when you aren't getting a concept. All of his assignments are really easy but it's the amount he gives you per week that “count” for a grade but it's only graded for completion with a check mark instead of an actual letter, so they don't even help your grade. this guy grades sueor generously but the class is built such that you have to parcipate bc he makes some of the assignments interacting w your classmates and he does actually grade these. hes super chill and forgiving, also super chill and straighforward assignments.

As long as you stay caught up you will do fine. I hate writing more than anything and got a 95 on the first paper. His expectations are reasonable. He has lots of really cool stories and is very nice. There is homework but mostly discussions and easy grading. There is extra credit to make up for missed attendance too.

He is amazing. He knows his stuff and really enjoys what he does. I would 100% take a course taught by him again. The homework can be a fair bit but he makes the rest of the class enjoyable, balancing it out.

WORST class ever. I have so many negative things to say about it, but honestly one of the worst parts was how extra credit was given out for dressing up at movie screenings (Example : cowboy). We are talking +20 points which could boost you almost an entire letter grade. Alot of people arent willing to dress up in silly costumes for extra points.

Prof Kazakov's class was disorganized and unhelpful. Assignments lacked guidance, and feedback was vague. He seemed unprepared and uninterested in engaging with students. It felt more like I was teaching myself than learning from a professor. Would not recommend his courses.

A very realistic and entertaining teacher. Show up because there's an attendance grade but if you watch all the free movie screenings you'll be fine if you miss a few classes. The guy is great. Funny, reasonable, cares about the subject but doesn't expect every student to be a film nerd. Class has a really chill atmosphere but there's still a clear understanding that this isn't a blow off class. He's not a super strict grader and he's understanding if you have genuine reasons for things to be late or miss class.
He is one of my favorite professors I have ever had in class. I would highly recommend taking his class as youll gain so much out of it.
He is absolutely amazing and very easy to get along with. cracks a lot of jokes, but you can tell he's stressed out.

Dr. Meng was an amazing professor and taught the class what he wanted us to learn, and expected us to know for his tests. Almost a complete opposite of Dr. Bompadre's physics I. He taught the class so well, I am under the impression phys 2 is easier than phys 1.
Very easy class. Andrew is awesome
its hard to get a bad grade in his class. way easier than physics 1

I would not recommend taking this class unless you absolutely have to. The only grades in this class are 5 out of 6 exams and bonus points received for attendance. I think Prof. Clarke has a passion for his subject, but he does a bad job communicating. It's an introductory class and he makes it seem like we should know everything that he's been studying for 35+ years. He speaks down to everyone like they are dumb. Not particularly difficult. Show up to class and take notes and you're pretty much guaranteed to have a good grade in the class. very passionate and qualified teacher (CFP)

Super friendly with great vibes and happy to see his students.

Passionate about what he lectures but as a non-business major the content is extremely boring but easy.
