He is AMAZING! I love showing up to class and always get a good smile from the lectures. Grading isn't bad the homework is a little heavy but if you know what you are doing it goes by pretty fast, and its all online you get to retake the questions unlimited times until you get it right. I would attend lectures whether its mandatory or not!!

Classes can feel quite long, however Professor Zumwalt always tries to make lectures interesting and interactive. He encourages questions and explains them in a way that doesn't make you feel stupid. The assignments can be very long but are easy. On tests you're allowed to use notes, one sheet front and back. Overall informative class.

Lectured very fast and gave a lot of homework. On average HW would take me roughly an hour to an hour and a half to complete. On another note, the exams were very easy. The first one was online and open notes, and the final was only over the second part of the semester and we were allowed one sheet of paper, front and back.

Hard to judge the difficulty of his class. Lots of homework, but easy homework. Tests can be hard, if you get the material, you will get most everything, but you will have to do some critical thinking for the in-class writing. "If p then q" etc was easy to get but the class starts to get a little more abstract. Lovely person, overexplains sometimes

Had this professor for Philosophy for section 4210. He doesn't make sense at all. Constantly goes on rambles and monologues. He has specific criteria for assignments and says that he didn't ask for it when you specifically follow instructions.

He talks at the class the entire time. When someone asks a question, he interrupts them and doesn't let them finish asking the question. He does not respect students' time and lets us out even 10 minutes late most days. I don't see how he is allowed to teach undergraduates. There is no possible way to retain anything he says during class. Horrible.

Took Dr. Melnyk's "Philosophy of Science" in fall '99. So long ago now that Mizzou's course numbering system has changed, and the original course number, which I think was 300-something, is obsolete, but this RMP page is among the top hits upon Googling his name, so I thought I would chime in: 

Just take a course with him and thank me later...

Many of the complaints I've heard about Prof. Melnyk are usually due to people not taking his class seriously, rather than any problem on Melnyk's part.  His lectures are dry, but he never goes on tangents unrelated to what he's talking about.  He's very specific and very detailed.  He can be a tough grader but is not the worst I've had.

He's clearly knowledgeable, which leads to him having a tendency to ramble on about tangents that are barely even related to the actual topic of the lecture. He also spends a lot of time going on about the same things over and over again.

The actual class is not difficult as long as you physically show up and complete your homework assignments.

Melnyk's course on logic was interesting. Many are turned off by the less metaphysical and more mathematic nature of the class material, but I found it to be worthwhile. He is slow and unclear during lectures, but he truly does care for his students. He was a favorable grader. Understand that his class focuses on argument validity not ethics.

I took 1200H with Professor Melnyk. If you are a decent writer, and put a little effort forth in the class, you will get an A. Additionally, his curve makes it difficult to get below a B. Overall, he's a good guy even though his lectures are boring, and has a British accent which is fun.
PLNTS3225 Plant Breeding & Genetics. You'll learn way more than you want to know about soybeans but good class. He grades kinda hard.
i took him spring sem, i could not for the life of me figure out his writing style and how exactly how to write for him. his feedback is horrendous and not helpful. do not take.

If you want the professor to pat you on the back and shake your hand after every half-hearted insipid insight, don't take Hoberek. If you want to have actual conversations with a dude who knows his stuff, DO IT

While I do respect him very much for being extremely enthusiastic and knowledgable on the topic, he made this class WAY too hard. I took this thinking it would be a more fun alternative to other writing credits, but it ended up being so much work. He's an extremely hard grader and made it very difficult to get good grades no matter how much I tried
This was a comic book class. Interesting material, though the content was not my favorite. He is brilliant and will help IF YOU ASK FOR IT.

He's a really good professor. He seems genuinely enthusiastic about post-modern literature and brought up a lot of really interesting, useful, and relevant information. I learned a lot from him and I thought he was excellent.

This class is not a cakewalk. Andrew has very clear cut expectations of what he wants in this class. Random pop quizzes over the reading, mandatory attendance, and close reading make the class difficult. He is not an easy grader. He does, however, teach some pretty quality material. If you want a challenge and to really learn something, take him.

The class is harder than it should be. The way we have to pull a meaning out of every little thing in a graphic novel is ridiculous. You can make something up, and as long as you can explain it, it counts as a "good" observation. Also, I once counted the amount of times he used the word "like" when it was unnecessary. Once it hit 70 I gave up.

much harder than expected.  You will be expected to do very close readings of text.  He also expects everyone to participate.  If you don't raise your hand he will call on you, especially for questions most people don't the answers to.  plus he has a bunch of earings, looks like the boss from BBC the office

Drew's a king. Everyone I knew in that class loved him. We even got together in our GroupMe at the end of the semester to write him a note telling him how much we appreciated his class. He is very kind and understanding and actually cares about your learning. I ran into him on campus the other day and it was deadass like meeting a celebrity.

Drew is my favorite instructor. He was understanding of our circumstances and the stress we were under as freshmen during COVID. His lectures were always interesting and he has a lot of knowledge to share. He left his assignments open, never took off points for late work, and gave great feedback. 10/10 would recommend taking any of his classes.

Prof. Amidei was a fantastic professor. His lectures were interesting, his discussions were fun, and his grading criteria was clear. If you participate, watch the films, and attend lecture, you're sure to learn some cool stuff and have a good time. He is caring, super funny, and has a real love for teaching this class. HIGHLY recommend his class!

He is humorous & personable. He makes his grading clear. What I dont like is how he assigns a long reading assignment every class. Your grade is basically determined by how well you can discuss the text next class. He also makes snarky comments & remarks about your writing and thoughts which isnt encouraging & makes you feel like a bad writer.

I attended Drew's classes not because they were mandatory, but because they were enjoyable and helpful! He made his grading expectations very clear from day 1, which I appreciated, and I felt that all of his homework assignments, which were mostly readings that we would later discuss, were purposeful. His personality was my favorite part of class.

Drew was an awesome teacher! I learned so much this semester that I will be able to carry forth into the future. He does not just give you information to spit back out during a test or in an essay; he teaches you HOW to become a smarter reader and find meaning in the details. I'm truly going to miss this class next year & the humor that he brings.

Dr. Meng was an amazing professor and taught the class what he wanted us to learn, and expected us to know for his tests. Almost a complete opposite of Dr. Bompadre's physics I. He taught the class so well, I am under the impression phys 2 is easier than phys 1.
Very easy class. Andrew is awesome
its hard to get a bad grade in his class. way easier than physics 1

Dr. Meng's course on electron microscopy and microanalysis was fantastic. He teaches clearly. I feel he went into just the right amount of technical detail, and it was comprehensible to undergrads. Some quantum mechanics background was definitely helpful. We got to operate real electron microscopes as part of a class project. We saw atomic columns!

Actual class was PA 1000 but did not have as a class selection. Awesome professor. Lots of examples and course content to make sure students can connect it to real life. Assignments are straight forward and clear instructions for rubric. Only a couple writing assignments and optional rewrites for higher grades available. Really enjoyed this class/
Angie is wonderful. Great human. Great teacher.

Dr. Hull is truly wonderful. She creates a positive learning space where all student can share their experiences; she's very flexible, considerate, and focused on real world application of what she teaches. The work load seems daunting at first, but don't let that scare you. She'll make sure that you're keeping up and gaining practical knowledge.
Probably one of the best teachers Ive ever had. Flexible with deadlines and learned a lot.

The class can be a drag at times, especially if you take the afternoon timeslot. Her lectures are at best tolerable, at worst agonizing. I was fine putting up with this course, as it's a prerequisite to the more advanced photo classes. Not the worst experience ever, but certainly plenty to improve on.
critiques.

Angela is very understanding and accomodating. Assignments are not very focused on technical aspects of photography, but expectations are clear. The course is engaging overall.

A nice teacher who was easy to talk to. All assignments were laid out with specific grading points. If you do the work, you will get a good grade. Critiques are long and you are required to find the hidden meaning behind others work. It was a little too much at times because not every piece has a super meaningful background.Overall nice class.

Really light grader, you can be given an A for taking a photo of a toothbrush on a toilet as long as there's some “deeper meaning” behind it. Doesn't really know a lot about photography and the assignments are not based on technical skill but if you can stand around and “critique” people's half-ass attempts at photography. Really boring class.

This teacher ruined photography for me, I will never take another art class at this school. Giving a decent compliment is beyond her, providing feedback on work is non-existent, and she does not tell you your grade until the end of the semester. do everything perfectly, get a B (it says in the syllabus); teacher doesn't know much about cameras (could never help with anything technical); you also don't know your grade until finals week and no feedback is provided

Both a professor who cares about your well-being and a fantastic educator. I came in with a lot of experience on the instrument and private instruction, but I still learn new things every lesson that help bring my playing to the next level. He can be mean but only in an endearing way.
Takes students out to eat and is hilarious. His aura will skyrocket your tuba playing.
Manzo is probly the bets professor I have ever had. He will help you out whenever you need it, as long as your not stupid, or late to your classes.

Very devoted to his students - his students' success is his biggest priority. Will give you the shirt off his back if you ask, but he won't want the shirt back as it will be "germy" He yells a bit, but only when you don't do what you're supposed to.

Angelo Manzo is an a$$hole. He knows it, and he's proud of it. That's what I love about him, that and he's an excellent teacher. If you're in a bind, he'll help you out too. Just do what he expects you to do and you'll be in good shape. Great guy.

Anika Edwards is a great professor for this class! She gives grades back in a timely manner and adds feedback to all of her grades. She is a very fair grader. The only downside to this class is it is homework heavy, but this also means there are a lot of opportunities for grades. Very relevant and useful information discussed in the class.

She is very lenient and she truly cares for her students. She is easily contacted outside of class and is willing to offer extensions. She understands that you have work outside of her class and that you have your own personal life. You do not need an "excused" absence to receive a grade for the day, there is only a short makeup assignment.

Professor Hatjakes is super caring and understanding! She was a super fast grader, and she frequently provided encouraging and individualized feedback. Her class was also an easy A as long as you did the work and communicated with her about late work and absences. I would 100% recommend her, especially for creative writing!
She is so nice and as long as you tell her you're missing class, it is ok

Professor Hatjakes is super flexible and extremely nice. She cares about her students and makes English a lot better than past English classes I have taken. As long as you write your papers and use her feedback, you will do great. She is an absolutely amazing professor!
shes amazing. she is so flexible with everything. put in minimum, effort and you will get an a .

Dr. Fett is fantastic! Mizzou is lucky to have her. Despite being new to the university, you can't tell, the care and preparedness she puts in and outside this class is evident in the material. Though the class is emotionally heavy, she handles it with sensitivity and a trauma-informed approach. Her feedback is always thoughtful and edifying.
Very lax, understanding, gives good feedback

Professor Wehrwein is very nice, however, doesn't really teach you. she gives you multiple assignments and after spending 6 hours in class working on it expects you to spend 10 more hours out of class. this will only get you an 85 on projects. also, the supplies are 300 dollars and you will never use them again

Anna's classes are her reading off of a PowerPoint quickly. Each day is a new topic and every night there is hw on the reading. She rarely responds to emails and is difficult to reach. I took 3 of her classes and she still didn't know my name after 3 years. (She emailed me asking why I wasn't in class even though I asked her a question in class)

Valiavska is a great professor, feel like she is often misunderstood as a strict professor but she really just cares & wants you to care about what you are learning. She tries to connect w/ her students by using current events in her lectures. The home/classwork can seems tedious, but the papers/project help prepare you for the real world.

Very slow grader. Doesn't respond to emails. Yell's at students who are in class complaining about the student's who don't come to class. Nothing happens during class other than her reading off the PowerPoint resulting in her not going into detail about what concepts mean. I wouldn't recommend anyone to her class ever. Not approachable either.

Assigns a midterm which covers 6 chapters in a book, along with outside readings, exam is 250 points, 23% of the grade in the class, without giving study guide. Class is like a military academy in Russia. Slow grader. In class she goes extremely fast, and doesn't do anything but read whats off the powerpoint. Would NOT recommend her to anyone.

I took this class as a requirement, and I thought I was not the biggest fan of Shakespeare. However, she made this course so fun and got me to love the subject! I learned so much, and she is so passionate and knowledgeable about the material. I have such a good time taking her course, and I would definitely recommend any of her courses!

While I have no doubt the professor is knowledgeable about literature, I would not recommend taking her class if you are not an english major. The lectures were interesting, but she nitpicked through all my papers and finally accused me of plagiarism at the end of the semester, which I did not do. I'm too much of an idiot to plagiarize.

Anne is a genuine person who is extremely flexible and always willing to meet a student half-way. She makes sure that assignments are communicated clearly and everyone is on the same page. If you need help, she will go to any lengths.

Dr. Myers is such a great teacher. Her lectures make 17th-century British literature interesting, which is saying something. She genuinely cares about all of her students and is always willing to help. Best professor I've ever had.
Dr. Myers is a very caring person who will work with you on anything you need help with. She is so approachable and makes learning about dull topics interesting.

One of the best professors I've ever had; I don't know why she doesn't have a 5.0 rating on here. SUPER nice, very funny, genuinely cares about her students and loves what she teaches. It's an English class, so you have to read a lot and actually MUST read to do well on the quizzes, but she is a very fair grader and always available to help.

If you do the readings, you will do well on the quizzes and tests.  All the quizzes and tests include extra credit questions that are easy.  Overall, the class is a lot of fact recall, but the readings are very interesting, and class discussions are too.  Her feedback on papers isn't particularly helpful though, and she grades papers a bit harshly.
Clear grading, the readings kinda suck but you can get away with not reading everything.

Dr. Stanton is a great professor who understands art history doesnt come easy to most. She does a great down at breaking down the material and fostering class participation even in an asynchronous setting. I would definitely take her class again!

Stanton is super nice but she didn't teach very much because it was an online course. Weekly notes take a lot of reading articles (my notes ranged to 20+ pages/week). Lots of extra credit opportunities on homework, essays, and other stuff. Two exams and weekly assignments, with a final project. Tests and homework are open note.

Prof. Stanton is super passionate about art and did a great job this past semester (Fall 2020) and was really helpful in making sure everyone was doing okay with online learning. I struggled with the semester but I still ended up with an A- because of her help and extra credit. A super interesting class and it would've been even better in person.

I love professor Stanton, I have now had her for two classes and I have enjoyed both of them! This most recent class was online so it was not as enjoyable as my first one was. Professor Stanton always offers extra credit opportunities and she is very entertaining during class!
Professor Stanton was always understanding if you miss class or forgot to turn in an assignment. She provides tons of extra credit and it would be hard to fail her class.

Professor Stanton is a wonderful woman. She's very accommodating and approachable if anyone needs extra help. I think she is very obviously passionate about the topic and wants us to gain a valuable understanding of it as well. There's a sizable group project that is terrible but she mentioned letting some people work alone if desired.

Stanton is very knowledgable about the art pieces and is obviously loves art history. She is enthusiastic but it can be difficult to get good notes during her lecturing so I often have to reinforce information on specific pieces after lecture from the book.

Stanton is very nice, and enthusiastic about her subject--however, I find that her lectures tend to bounce around and are pretty disorganized. I can't always determine which piece/work she's referring to, place, time, etc. It's hard to take notes in this class unless you write down everything and try your best to organize after class.
Had her last year, feel bad for everyone in her class this year. Drop while you can, she's a devil witch
loved service learning, hated her.

Truly an evil woman. Failed me for being sick twice, but cancelled class multiple times for her own allergies. Acts so loving & philanthropic, but couldn't care less about students. Hates opinions other than her own. Makes you read 1 terrible book every week, volunteer 30+ hours, and essays she won't accept 1 second late.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. Stone cold, has no sympathy or human recognition for students.  There are no slip ups allowed- and even week you're expected to read a (sh*tty) novel, volunteer 35 hours, + perfect attendance. She failed me after I did all that. Even if you're interested in Service Learning, avoid AnneMarie at all costs.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. The class required reading 1 horrible novel every week, 35 volunteer hours, and perfect attendance- no slip ups allowed. She was stone cold, views herself as a saint, & has no sympathy or human recognition for any of her students. Even if you're interested in this course, avoid Anne Marie at all costs.

Dr. Foley crammed 5 books and a kajillion papers into a semester. Not to mention you'll spend 20-30 hours "serving the community" and only receive 3 credit hours for the course. Dr. Foley kind of irritated me- she interrupt students answering questions she asks, and she didn't put much effort into giving feedback at all. I did enjoy the material.

She will not work with her students, so be prepared to do things Foleys way and without any leeway. Its Foleys way or the Highway. Even if youre a great writer, she will find reasons to not give you the grade you deserve. I made an A in Foleys class and I had to work hard for it, and she still didnt give all of the points I believed I deserve

Professor Foley is no doubt one of the greatest people I have had the luxury of meeting. She truly cares about everyone at the University of Missouri. I did not like her class however, as it requires lots of reading and writing papers over the readings. I am not much of a reader and wouldn't recommend it to people who do not like to read.
She was a lot of fun and was very engaged in class. Her assignments created the projects. Would take again!!!

Professor Trinh isn't really a professor as she is more of a student, but she would mostly just go off and say random things in class. She assigned homework every day which was usually useless and pointless. She was a harsh grader on essays. On one assignment she gave the class a guide to follow, but following it got me a bad grade.
Good teacher! Explains everything so well during his lectures.
Great professor for someone who is not great at understanding math whatsoever. Goes slow and takes his time.

His lectures were amazing, he made all the tests very easy, he gives practice tests before the exams and that practice materials are incredibly helpful, he is nice and a good person.He made the math easy in his class.
His lectures were good, but when we needed help he wasn't very willing to actually help? He kind of just told us good luck and do better.

I was really nervous about taking this class but having Mr. Cairatti as my teacher really made this one of my favorite classes to attend. He explains everything so well in his lectures and was very kind to everyone all semester. I would 10/10 take any math class if he was the teacher.
I liked his class.

Anthony is a real inspiration. His love for math and teaching makes his class a truly exceptional experience. I could listen to him explain the mysteries of Mandelbrot sets for hours. I also appreciate his honest views of Pythagoras. Thanks Anthony, and please continue to bring your protractor to RL.
very fair teacher. great person outside of teaching.

Professor assigns work with no clear guidelines and then will grade harshly for work. With unclear rubrics and short assignment descriptions this professor has unreasonable expectations that one should read his mind

Dr. Vatterott teaches in a relatable way to help keep students active and listening. Very different than a normal lecture based class with discussion points. Lots of group projects and in class participation as well as stepping outside of your comfort zone and getting to meet lots of real companies and people in the business world.

Dr. Vatterott is an entertaining professor. I learned a lot of real word sales skills through active participation. Make sure you are ready to participate and spend time on this class outside of normal hours. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

Vatterott brings the energy to his class. He ties in personal stories with what we are learning which makes the topics stick better. He brings in different companies in class to help you network and learn about different career opportunities. I was not looking for an internship or job, but I could see this being very helpful to those who are.

Professor Vatterot's class isn't your typical lecture style class where the student listens and takes notes. It is a very interactive class, prompting students to get out of the comfort zones through role plays and other collaborative exercises. Another great part of the class was the exposure to companies and networking through company class talks

Professor Vatterott's class is very different then your average take notes class. He brings in company's every week that will help you with your future endeavors whether that be an internship or job. You are given role plays to present in front of the class which will help you in your future sales positions after college.
He wants all of his students to succeed, so expect to be pushed. He also gives great advice on job searching, and about life in general. His classes are never boring!

Dr. Vatterott makes sure that his students understand the sales process in a very structured format which helps you excel rapidly. He's also a very good contact to reach out to regarding class material, future job opportunities, or everyday life.
Attendance matters, lots of group work, lots of extra credit opportunities, many companies talked to us in class, learned a lot from his lectures/talks

Dr. Heese is not a very captivating professor and is very disorganized. Not just on her student side of canvas, which is v messy, but also on the study guide that so many students rely on to get a good grade in this class. Honestly she could use some tech lessons to set up canvas and create more accurate study material.

Her teaching skills are lacking, and she has no respect! When it's exam time, I'm writing for the whole 50 minutes, ending up with hand cramps, and I still can't finish in time. She loves making you write essays for every single question, and she seems to enjoy throwing the same question at you multiple times, just mixing up the words a little.

Dr. Heese isn't a bad professor, just a bad lecturer. Lectures were long and rambling and I often found myself searching for the point she was trying to make. This is saved by very specific study guides that are provided in advance. Fill out the study guides and you'll do fine, but be prepared to scratch your head while you do.

The only complaints I have for Dr. Heese is that she does not clearly explain what she expects when we are to answer short answer questions on exams. She is very particular about phrasing on quizzes and exams. The homework for this course is over topics that are NOT thoroughly discussed in class and is not graded based on completion.

Dr. Heese is a great person, but not the best professor. She is not able to go in depth with her lectures, only knowing what appears on the slides and when asked to go a bit further, she will simply say "I don't know" or "that's a great question." If it is not about her research, she is not very helpful. It's terrible for exams.
Did not respond to emails, unfair grading, and made in person group projects for an online course. Would not recommend
Made comments about the side of political party she does not agree with. Hard grader! Does not answer emails. I would not take any class with her.
She doesn't know how to give proper feedback and also doesn't respond to emails. Other than that thought, I'd recommend… not!
He takes way too long to grade assignments.

I had a summer course with Dr. Castro over the summer and he was straightforward about grading and criteria expected on papers/assignments. He is very funny and always cracks jokes during lecture/discussion that will keep the student engaged.

Fairly easy course that counts for both a humanities and diversity credit. Assignments are mostly just weekly readings/discussion posts, although there were also two essays, a presentation, and two "cultural experience reports" we had to write. Nothing too difficult, though. Prof Chaiwanichsiri was also always available for questions via email.

Knowledgable but talks at you for most of class. Patronizing and often blatantly disrespectful to students. Assumes student time revolves around her and never gives a direct answer to a question. Assigns hundreds of pages of reading per class and will require that you buy 10+ books. Really wanted to love this class but regret taking.

Dr. Langley so clearly cares about her students and the material she is teaching. Yes, you have to work for it but that's how college should be anyway. I ended the class with over 100 percent. Do your work and show up to class. It's worth it and she's awesome.

Really condescending. Treats students like they're 5 years old. Wastes a lot of class time rambling on about how we shouldn't waste class time. 50+ pages of reading per night. Participation in discussions is mandatory. Gets off topic a lot and rambles on about nothing. Don't take a class with her, you'll regret it.

Awesome professor. She is very clear about what she's looking for so if you read the syllabusrequirements then there is no reason for you not to get an acceptable grade. Ive taken her class online & 1 n person, she knows what she's talking about. She might delve deep into the conversation but id rather do that than only read textbooks & lecture

She never returned a single grade throughout the class, so you were left wondering what your grade was until you got it, and most of us were not amused. She also speaks on a soapbox about a lot of things, and is usually late to class. Avoid.

This was a great class for me. She talk a lot and often went to deep into discussion of topics, but overall she is a great teacher. Make sure you NEVER mess up her format or deadline requirements or you will be screwed!! Enjoy her class!! And make sure you participate.

Hands down, the absolute BEST Professor I've had in my college LIFE! Her syllabus is crystal clear, this woman is thorough and intelligent! I believe only the STRONG will survive in her class, and the WEAK ones who only want a degree are exposed from the little effort that they put into the work. She gives extra credit, so how can 1 not get an A?

She's awful. I don't think there's a better word to describe her. She lectures on her own soap box, she grades impossibly hard (and half of her comments are opinion), and she thinks she's outstanding. Avoid this class at all possible cost--the reading material is interesting but this class is impossible and dreadful, all thanks to Dr. Langley.
Mr. Quintaneiro is a very charming man and a very passionate scholar. His "Intro to Bioethics" class is incredibly easy, and his lectures are interesting.

Terrible teacher. Made students write 5-6 page papers over books that were 1000 pages. Lectures consist of him just reading off the slides and talking in the most monotone boring voice and not even adding anything to the slides. Grades tough on the test along with his terrible TA.

Mr. Gruber is such a kind hearted person who truly cares about his students. Yes his lectures are boring and long but you don't have to go to get a good grade. No tests or quizzes, only a 1-2 page essay every week and he doesn't grade too hard. I wouldn't take this class for fun but definitely not bad.

Professor Gruber is a graduate student who needs a lot of work to make him a better professor. His lessons are far from engaging and are extremely boring. All he does is stand at the front of the room and talk, hardly allowing any student to talk with him. Most students don't even understand what he is saying. At least the work isn't too hard.

This class was a struggle, I struggled to understand the content and really didn't understand much of what he was lecturing on. If you really like philosophy, you probably will be fine but the articles were extremely difficult to understand. However, Gruber is a very nice guy and understanding, you can tell he cares about his students' well being.

This is just a very hard class and I think he does the best he can. You read articles and then on the exams you write essays about them. Not the worst but not the best. Really nice guy though that is down to earth

As a professor hes a really down to earth person and a great guy. The class as a whole is a tough one because all the grades are tests and quizzes. All the tests are over 3 argument articles that are a very tough read.
Did not explain anything and every class is a lecture. Better right your notes fast because he talks as his way of notes and then the exams are nothing like what is in your notes.

Dr. Fried is an amazing professor and person! She is very caring and understanding. I took WGST 2005 with her and absolutely loved it! Turn in your stuff on time, participate in class, and read the readings and you'll do well in her class.

Fried is really kind and very understanding.Very approachable if you need help with assignments or the readings.The reading is required to engage in class and participation is a decent chunk of the grade.Would recommend for Fried but didn't love the class material, it was a bit boring at times.Lectures can also be pretty dull if ppl don't engage

One of the nicest professors I have ever had. She is super caring and understanding towards her students. There was a lot of reading, but the readings were always really insightful and I use the knowledge I have from those readings in my other classes. The class I took (WGST-2005) was organized really well too.

She is a pretty good English teacher for ENG1000. You will pass her class no problem. There are 4 papers nothing awful. Just make sure you do the work and you'll get an A. There is 1 group project that is a 10-13 page essay, so make sure you pick good group members
I loved her class. She really cares about her students, and gives really good feedback to make you a better writer.

Took this as a summer class and it didn't feel rushed at all. We were given plenty of time to do the work and readings. Papers were mostly "informal" but still took effort. I was never confused about what the prof wanted from us. She was very understanding and willing to work with me when I was having difficulties.

Ariel is super chill and personal. the class is smaller, maybe 25 people in it. She is fantastic about communication as far as papers and assignments go. She gives fantastic feedback and really cares about the student learning to write at a collegiate level. the reading sometimes feel a little pointless but she makes up for that with good lectures

It was Suits first time teaching when I took his class. It is a 3 credit class that should be a 5 credit class. Suits does not know how to teach such a basic course. He often gets confused and will write or say the wrong things. This class was extremely difficult especially if science does not come naturally to you. Only take this class if required

This lady sucks... She doesn't care at all for her students and even if you try to come to her office hours to ask questions she will make you feel belittled and stupid for not understanding the content. Her tests are completely different from what we learned in class. If you miss class she is unwilling to work with you.

She doesn't care about you or your grade. There were 2 assignments and 4 exams. Went to office hours numerous times to try to ask questions and study better, and then did worse on the test that I studied for than the 1st one that I winged. On top of that the wording of her tests is extremely difficult and she is a tough grader. Just don't do it.

Dr. Givens is passionate about her work but the structure of the course made the information meaningless. Lectures were short and did not go in-depth. Honestly, I did not learn much. The most interesting material comes from classmates' presentations. Too tough of a grader in my opinion, but lax on due dates. Approachable, but this class was a mess.
Dr. Givens is great and wonderful. She is doing amazing research and lectures very passionately. However, she is a tough grader.

Dr. Givens is a very knowledgable and passionate individual. Dr. Givens' lectures are very entertaining because she knows how to have fun. I'm thankful for the content we discuss in this class and the book choice. Dr. Givens gives very useful feedback on assignments that truly teach individuals how to sharpen their skills.

I took Dr. Isby's SOC 101 course through MACC, although it was not listed. She is a very intense grader, with a rubric that goes into the 100th decimal place, discussion posts 6.35/10 for example. Super late getting graded stuff back, but when it comes back late, she seems to just give full credit as a "completion" grade. would not take again.

Ashley Isby is very kind, she made sure that all of her students got exactly what the needed from the class. She's always available whenever you need her. Personally, she's been my favorite instructor i've ever had!

DO NOT TAKE ANY OF HER CLASSES!!! She is the worst professor I have EVER had. She is the worst at getting back to students and she takes 6 months to grade assignments. On top of that, she assigns projects every single week and the instructions are not clear at all. AVOID HER CLASS AT ALL COSTS!!! If there was a 0 I would give her a 0.

Her main downsides seem to be based in organization, typos on tests are common, grades can take a while to come out, but I don't think it's because she's lazy, she definitely cares and works hard. There isn't too much homework, although there was a group project, and she is easy to contact and often willing to work with you
Stay away. Biased professor and takes forever to grade. Strict on grading and brings her political views into assignments.
i dont want to be mean lol

she had a lot of bad feedback on here and I am unsure why. I took her social inequalities class online and didn't really love my first two essay scores so i just met with her before submitting the others and she was so helpful, informative, and i ended up doing a lot better once i started doing that. just show you want to learn and she is 5/5

I like sociology and was so disappointed with this class. Isby does not know how to manage a lecture hall full of college students. She treats her classes like children, has a nonsensical participation system, and is unclear on grading criteria. Her tests are long reading quizzes riddled with errors. Sometimes in lecture we'd get through one slide.

Class is incredibly easy but Dr.Anderson makes it unnecessarily convoluted. Her grading is incredibly weird, you can answer questions in every class and get a 6/10 for participation with no explanation. Felt like I learned more about Taylor Swift than anything, if it wasn't a requirement I would have dropped it within the first two weeks
The worst class I have ever taken in fourteen years of schooling

this class felt like a poor use of my time. she will give you a zero on an assignment if you mess up the smallest detail. most in class work is brainless and feels like i could be doing anything else better
all of the readings for this class are about taylor swift. it's an easy A but Dr. anderson makes it a cortisol spike

Dr. Anderson takes a introductory English class and makes it entirely about Taylor Swift. Her lectures are boring and unengaging. She's a pretty easy grader on papers, but assignments if you do one think incorrectly you lose credit for the entire assignment. I would take this class with another instructor.

Ashley is very kind and willing to work with you, however I felt like I was in hs again taking this class. She gives okay feedback, and grades fairly. I did not improve as a writer in this class. Lecture is VERY boring and the in class activities are childish and feel arbitrary. If you show up and make a moderate effort you'll be fine
don't take this class with here

I felt like I was in high school again. She would make you stay in class for work time—if you left or weren't there, you would be penalized. The lectures are long, and almost all of them are on slides. She is a nice person and gives good feedback, but I would recommend choosing a different professor.
The exams are timed, unclear of criteria, and she grades heavy. The lectures she records and posts online are basically useless because the audio cuts out every 30 seconds. would not recommend

Dr. Groh is really interesting to listen to. She loves what she studies and knows a lot about it. She is a tough grader though, and will tell you right off the bat that her tests are hard, which is not a quality that you love to see in a teacher. If you don't love psych though, I would say this class is not worth it, it'll just be a B on your GPA.

Pretty easy class. You get extra credit by showing up to class using the clicker. Textbook reading requested (but wont hurt if you don't do it). I cram the night before, skim the text book on occasion and get good grades. Only 2 writing assignments, just one pagers.

Excellent professor. Lays out expectations in the syllabus and reverts back to it to provide clarity and assignment reminders.  Classic developmental psychology class, overall very educated, wise woman!

Very clear grading criteria. She did a good job of making sure everything in the class (lectures, readings, assignments, and tests) are all very cohesive. If you go to class, print out the lectures, and read you will get an A. You could tell she was passionate about the subject throughout all her lectures.

Dr. Groh is a very nice lady with clear expectations. You will have to do a fair amount of work to pass or get a good grade, but nothing too difficult or unreasonable. Records attendance via participation with clickers in class, which accounts for 10% of your grade. Posts her slides online, and assigns 8 quizzes and 2 papers throughout semester.

Dr. Groh is very knowledgable and clearly passionate about what she does. The class is not hard by any means if you show up to class and simply go through your lecture notes to study before exams. Only 4 exams, no midterms or finals, and a few online quizzes. She puts lecture slides on blackboard if you do miss a class so it's not hard to catch up.

Very knowledgable and capable professor, but I did bust my ass to get a good grade. Taken as an easy "GPA booster" but ended up being the class I studied the most for. Read the assigned chapters BEFORE class! Gives you a heads up before in class quizzes over the readings so go to every lecture. Gave extra credit options as well which was nice.
very relevant course for the current times!!! highly recommend for anyone interested in the social side of education
She cares

Worst professor Ive ever had. We are almost done with the semester, and I am waiting on 12 assignments to be graded. Readings are repetitive and unnecessary. Would not take this Professor again, shes very irritable at times and hard to work with. Also has a no email policy, so good luck if you have a question.

This class is one of the best I have ever taken at Mizzou. Dr. Lester is a delight to work with and shows up to every class with a positive attitude and genuine excitement for what she is teaching. The class is lecture-heavy, with many turn-and-talk discussions and group activities. TAKE NOTES!! And read the textbook because it will be on exams.

I always look forward to class with Dr. Lester! She is so passionate about what she teaches and really makes the class engaging. It is a hard class, and a lot of information, however she is so willing to help whenever needed! She also is very supportive and provides great feedback! 100% would take any class she teaches again if I have the chance.

Dr. Lester is one of my favorite professors I have had. Each and every class she comes in so happy and excited to teach, and you can tell that she really cares about what she is lecturing. She connects everything into real life scenarios and makes her lectures so interesting. Would absolutely recommend her, and her Intimate Relationships class.

Lester was very difficult and her class about took me down.. So many assignments but only ten points given her tests are very hard as well.. and she gives you little to study from. She also goes till the VERY end of class and does to many clickers you can't keep up. Her ta Karen Talley is awful and horrible at her job and is a pain to go to.

Course-long paper prompt is chosen too early before enough information is learned. Despite focusing on a narrow prompt, the professor insists on note-taking for unrelated lectures. Instructions are vague, yet grading is strict, with points lost for minor details that are not said. Avoid this class; the online section is a much better use of time.

HDFS 2400W with Dr. Lester has been one of the worst classes I have taken. The essays assigned for the class often make no sense and not much time is given to write. The examples provided are awful and the rubrics for essays are confusing. Although she is really passionate about the field, you should take the online section if you have the chance.
There's a lot of extra assignments I feel that there is no need to be done. There is a lot of content in this class I feel very overwhelmed.

I took Dr. Lester for my HDFS 2400 Writing Intensive course. She offered a live zoom of her lectures, which a lot of kids used, however, her lectures were super interesting and fun to listen to. She truly is passionate about what she teaches and makes the content interesting! The big paper you have is no joke, but she offers lots of help!

Good class and prof to learn about linguistics and a different aspect of Spanish language not considered in other courses. It is a hw heavy class, with reading and practice exercises due most classes. Extra credit opportunity, hw revisions, and a fairly generous grader. Only two exams; midterm and final (which covers the second 1/2 of course).
High workload, but also, don't overthink. Do the work, do your best, and ask for help when needed. He's open to feedback and is incredibly kind and accommodating if you communicate your needs.

profe alcazar is amazing. he is kind and really wants you to do well in his class. he knows so much about these topics and has really helped me improve in my spanish skills. i wish he could teach me for the rest of my classes. there is a lot of homework but it is pretty easy to do. grades are very fair and you can improve after an assignment.

By far the best Spanish class I've taken at Mizzou. Topic was very interesting, and Prof. Alcazar gave great feedback. I knew exactly what I had to work on and how I could improve. I learned a lot from him and saw a major improvement in my speaking skills.

Since the pandemic, Prof. Alcazar moved all of his classes online. While the course content was both dry and difficult to understand, his lenient deadlines and grading offset it. He also gave us the chance to revise our homework to get full credit. His lectures are pretty rushed and monotone, but usually the linguistics topics were interesting.

The course is clear and easy to follow. He has a set schedule that cycles through three different interactive lecture types; all of which are engaging and a light workload. There's homework for each class, but it comes from the textbook and it's not very much. He's very laid back and approachable. My best professor this semester.

Second time taking his class, I will say that during the pandemic he has changed. This class used to be a capstone, so lots of homework. Still dry as usual, but gives good feedback. He is a lenient grader, so if you put some effort in, you will at least get a 80% on homework. Sometimes he recycles material (puts homework questions on tests).

Asier was the best professor I've had yet; he is kind, caring, and intelligent. He gives 110% in teaching, and I learned how to speak Spanish much better in this course. Homework due before every class that will probably take you an hour- make a GroupMe with your class. Zooms are optional attendance- you can watch the recordings later.

Dr.Harcharras is by far the best calc III prof. She clearly cares a lot about the content and is always happy to explain topics in more detail or help in any way she can. Exams are fair and she allows note cards for each exam, and provides plenty of practice material. Absolutely recommend her for Calc 3 and Calc 2

Great professor. Had her for calculus 3. Her lectures are full of information so don't miss them, but she does have the material on canvas. As long as you attend and do homework, you'll be fine. If you do struggle, she has accessible office hours or can be flexible for your schedule. She is very good at teaching the material.
She is very nice and easy to work with. Always responded to emails and provided excelent study materials for exams.

Lectures felt slow but honestly are helpful if you miss a day because she'll go over everything from the previous lecture before new material. Tons of practice problems. Go to review sessions before exams, super helpful. Sit close to the front because sometimes her mic doesn't pick up her voice and she uses the chalkboard a lot.

The lectures are poorly paced, spending most of class on an easy topic and then the last 10 min on the hard part. Luckily the slides are easy to learn from on your own and she posts A LOT of practice resources online.
The tests are formatted well. You get a note card, and they look exactly like the practices.
Probably the best calc II option at MU.
Moves way too fast. Reads off of slides and writes on that little board that you need to be at the front to read
Very hard to understand her and she just over-explains things and runs out of time.

She is a very sweet lady who I really enjoy as a person, but her lecture style sometimes felt like a 50 minute sorta monotone rambling of difficult, high-level math concepts. I genuinely almost fell asleep every class. If you talk to her outside of class for help she is great, overall not terrible.
Shes ok but will give bad grades just because she doesnt like your answers, not because they arent correct. Really annoying and unprofessional.
super nice person but a boring lecturer and VERY unclear/difficult grader

She is a very nice person who cares about her students but I wouldn't recommend her class to anyone. As other reviewers have said, she's a very unclear and unnecessarily hard grader. The lectures were also very boring.

EXTREMELY hard grader. She does not go into detail about what is expected from us on our assignments and then grades them extremely harshly. There are no exams in this class and just papers and projects. Her lectures are all over the place and do not relate to our projects/assignments.
Great personality, very hard grader

I really enjoyed taking this class with Astrid. She was knowledgable about the topic, and made class interesting and relatable. That being said her tests are impossibly hard! She expects you to do way too much in the time allowed for the exam. If you take her classes be prepared to work for it!

I have mixed feelings about Astrid. Her class was interesting at times, other times it was insanely boring. Her quizzes are almost impossible to get a good grade on, and her exams were so difficult. she's an extremely hard grader. I like her as a person and she was nice but i think she makes this class unnecessarily difficult

She cares about some students, not all. If you're not one of her favorites, she is not  welcoming nor friendly to go to for explanation, and etc. She has a very thick accent and it is very distracting. It was too difficult to keep up with her fast pace lectures and powerpoint slides, while trying to figure out what words she was even trying to say.

Dr. Sakis is very nice and loves to answer questions whether that's in lecture or in office hours. He's always looking to help his students. That said, the course is very fast paced and so are the lectures, which focus heavily on proofs. Exams are hard, but you can do well on them if you do all the problem sets. Grade curve at the end is generous

He is not good at lecturing, only going over definitions and proofs. Your grade is determined by 3 exams, and there is no homework or practice exams, only some problem sets with solutions that are difficult to understand or read. The class is extremely difficult on its own, but he doesn't make it any easier. You have to teach yourself the material.

Dr. Sakis's class was the toughest that I had this semester. That being said, I really enjoyed having him as a teacher. He is a bit intimidating in lecture, but he is very nice and helpful in office hours. His lectures could be a bit confusing at times, but he is always willing to answer questions. His tests were difficult, but he genuinely cares .
Nice guy.

Audra is a very caring and nice person. Her background is not journalism but she knows the material well that is needed for this class. The class is not difficult but you have a lot of homework each week and in-class assignments for each class. The larger assignments are not too difficult just time-consuming. There are no tests which is nice.

Professor Landini's lectures were very boring to sit through, however you only had to attend about half of the lectures to get full attendance points. He cared about his students and was available outside of class. He posted the lecture slides and the homework/quizzes were all online and pretty easy. It is a low commitment course.

Class was very discussion based and student led He will jump in I'm necessary to keep the conversation flowing in the right direction. Just be willing to share some opinion or thought on the reading. And be prepared to step out and have fun with the roll playing exercise at the end of the semester. Overall he is a professor that is there to help.

This class is almost entirely discussion based save for the final two weeks being a historical role play experiment. What this means is that you need to read and and speak in class. While there are essays that he will grade mercifully, you really only need to convince him that you are participating erego he is just there to help YOU do the work.

2 lecture days and 1 discussion day each week. Lectures are fine, he tends to go fast, so take pictures and just pay attention to the key terms. Don't join the honors discussion class unless you are ok with doing historical roleplays. I hated them, but whatever floats your boat.

While his lectures could be more engaging, you can tell he really does care about his students and enjoys teaching. Very passionate, great sense of humor. The class is pretty easy if you pay attention and study. I do wish the tests were slightly less weighted but other than that, great professor and a great course!

I cannot say I enjoyed his class at all. It was boring and he didn't give engaging lectures. I didn't speak to him once and he seemed to lean somewhat unfairly on his TAs to do everything for everyone but the Honors students, who he personally worked with. He gave bad vibes generally and I never heard anyone besides him talk in the class.

He'll either take ages on one slide or flip through five in thirty seconds, and he doesn't post slides so be ready to take pictures of them. He's monotonous and boring, although to his credit he posts the definitions you need to know for the tests, but I've heard post civil war profs are better so just save yourself the trouble and take that.

Assigned reading can be initially over whelming, but Dr. Stewart does a great job of breaking down the readings in class. The class is almost entirely discussion based, and Dr. Stewart can be a bit hands off at times. However, he frequently jumps in and adds good humor to the discussion.

Prof. Stewart is a good person and is alway available to help you outside of class. Having said that, this was a difficult course so be prepared to be challenged if you want to do well. H2100 is a discussion based class and you will be expected to do a lot of reading and a lot of talking, as well. I learned a lot though and I stayed engaged!

Ayleen is really nice. I just didn't love her a lecturer. Also sometimes I think she makes students feel dumb for not understanding something the first time. There is a lot of reading in this class and a lot of podcasts/films you have to watch. Make sure you're strategic about your studying. If you go to class and put in some effort you'll be fine.

Ayleen definitely cares about what she's teaching and you can tell that she's passionate about it. However, her teachings style isn't the best in my opinion. She takes 20 minutes to say something that could be said in 2. Also, the tests are more about memorizing the readings/podcasts than anything else. If you go to class, you'll probably get an A.

She's a really sweet person but a horrible teacher. She will make side notes during lectures that will be on the tests, and the only grades for the class were tests that were incredibly hard. She will expect you to memorize every slide and every word.

Attendance is mandatory but she just reads from the slides without giving anything else. I took this class because I thought it would be a fun, chill way to get a science credit, but it was so boring and poorly structured.
Do not recommend this class at all. The teachers voice is very annoying and the lectures are extremely boring. Be ready to memorize almost everything even the stuff you don't think is important.

She knew her info, mostly. She blamed the class for lab samples being placed in the incubator incorrectly when it was her TA, was rude when answering questions, told us about a group project 1 week before the last day, & gave us a quiz after stop day. Her exams & lab assignments were also unnecessarily specific & difficult for a 2000-level course.
Do not take this class or this professor, she doesn't know what she is talking about, is not good with technology, and it is honestly really boring.

She is a really sweet person, but the assignments are very unclear. Although there are only a couple, I ended up having to rewrite one of the essays because the directions were very unclear. You are expected to memorize almost all the information given to you on the slides, including which dishes come from which country and how to make them.

Dr. Mustapha is among the most intelligent professors I've ever had. Her exams are difficult but they prepared me for upper-level STEM courses. There's a curve at the end of the semester so don't panic over a bad grade. She did class recordings which were convenient if we were absent. Despite dense textbooks and PowerPoints, she was very invested.

Do not take her class!!! I mean it, the lectures are over an hour long and her voice is so annoying and she is just plain mean. Ask her any question and she will make you feel stupid and humiliate you. There's only 3 tests and most of your grade is "participation points" where half the time the technology doesn't work and she doesn't care.

Dr. Greenwood is a good professor. He definitely cares about his students, and the weight of the assignments I really liked. However his exams were very difficult, and his study guides aren't helpful whatsoever. The group project was kind of bad too, but he is a nice guy.
Good lectures, annoying group project that felt really detached from the rest of class and 4 difficult tests.

Dr. Greenwood is great. I really enjoyed his lectures, he makes the content interesting. Hated the group project, would have been much more enjoyable to do it individually. His exams are very hard and study guides aren't particularly helpful, but if you find a study method that works for you then you will do fine.

Horrendous class, great professor. I feel like Keith did his best to make class interesting and give us the information needed to pass. I went abroad for two weeks in the semester and he was one of the few professors I had that communicated with me and made sure I didn't fall behind in his class. He was super chill and I really enjoyed his efforts.
Nice professor with difficult exams that will make or break your grade.

The tests in this class are incredibly difficult for J-School tests, very detailed! Not a lot of other assignments so how you do on the tests really makes or breaks your grade. He is a good professor but tough grader.

Great professor! I was shocked to see any negative reviews. While the class is not the most exciting, he really cares about his students and tries to make it fun for everyone. I would definitely take a class with him again!

Gives really good lectures that are interesting- don't worry about being bored in a history lecture. He is fun! There's a semester-long group project and 4 tests and a weekly discussion board, but that's it. Easy but interesting class!

The entire class was only graded on 3 tests that were so un-necessarily difficult. I had to withdraw from this course because no matter how much I studied for the exams, I was performing poorly. I knew others who did the same. I'm re-enrolled in this course currently and took it online just so I wouldn't have to take it with him again.
The lectures lacked clarity. I did not find the course helpful or worth the time.

Dr. Park is obviously very intelligent, but this course was completely inaccessible to undergraduates. His tests are extremely difficult, and those are the only things you are graded on. He is by far the most difficult professor I have ever had, exam-wise. Do not take if you aren't prepared to dedicate more time to this class than you expect.
Not an enjoyable professor and is very strict. Tried to get an absence settled with him because I was sick and he never responded to my emails.

20+ page paper that he grades extremely harshly. 10 page final exam. Do not take this class if you aren't prepared to write. Dr. Park is very helpful during office hours and encourages students to participate during class. She's really good, but don't forget about assignments

I don't even know if this guy is alive. Everything is graded by canvas and online. The class is extremely easy and doesn't require much effort. The lectures and content are pretty enjoyable if you have interest in the field.

Dr. Deng taught this class online, which I think limited potential to clear up any problems students had during the lecture, but as for the actual content of the class, it is enjoyable and a good introduction to Environmental Engineering.

I did not like this professor, none of the class knew their grade until the end of the semester. Furthermore, the lectures were long and there was no enfasis put on any of the information. This made studying for the tests very hard. The labs were very good, however these were put on by the TA's not the teacher.

He's a bottom tier teacher who isn't the most coherent speaker - yet you can still learn a lot in CV 3200. The labs/site visits helped to visualize what we were be learning in class. He's not a bad guy, and has plenty of opportunities for extra credit by attending research seminars that are actually interesting. If you work hard you'll be fine.
Very kind man but has no business being in the classroom.

I had Barbara for two semesters for honors German and I absolutely loved her as a professor. She is really invested in helping you learn the content. It can get a bit stressful with the pace and calling on in class, but just be sure you're keeping up with the material.

Professor Molar was a great professor, she really helped me to understand and learn German. She was very understanding if I forgot to turn in an assignment or if I couldn't make it to class. Would take a class with her again.
Best professor I've had in college. Actually cared about me and my success. Very thankful that she made learning German possible.

Barbara is baeeee. She's super cute and really knows what she's talking about. If you get a chance to take German with her do it! If you put in the effort, she will make sure you do well. P.S she gives bonus points at the end of the semester based on participation so speak up in class!

She was honestly the best professor that I had while I was at Mizzou. I was lucky to have had her. I have had several years of both French and Spanish. Barbara made German the first foreign language that I actually took an interest in! (:

I feel extremely lucky to have had Barbara as my teacher for 2 semesters of German. She is seriously the greatest person; beautiful inside and out, she's kind, funny, and will meet one-on-one if you would like extra help. She is Hungarian, but is very well-versed in both English and German! She makes learning German fun and gave great study guides!
Barbara is awesome! She is super sweet. I am so lucky to have had her as my teacher for both German one and German two. She makes it understandable and she is ALWAYS available for help.

She is the BEST teacher that I have ever had. (: Sounds cliché but she makes learning fun. When we use an odd American word in class she gives us a chance to try to explain. It's like she is learning with the class which makes it more interesting. She is one of the nicest people that I have ever met. Plus I'm actually learning German.
She is awesome. She makes class fun and interesting and has great advice for future teachers.
Barri was awesome! She is passionate about education and wants you to be, too! Take this class, you wont regret it.

Best prof ever! If you have to take LTC 1100..make sure you take it with Barri!! She is so entertaining and totally passionate in what she teaches! I would recommend her to anyone! Make sure you take it with her! No tests, hardly any homework!
She was a very fun teacher who really took the time to prepare an interesting class. She made material, which could have been boring, interesting and fun.

He seems like he phones in most of his lectures. Talk a bit, show some video that's related, keep going. It's hard to stay awake listening to them. Tests were a breeze, though. Pro Tip: Never go to class, and only attend the Zoom.

Worst professor I have ever seen at Mizzou. The class is participation based, so if you do work you get an A. But he is lazy, doesn't teach you how to do the LSAT but rather just throws drills at you with no explanation, seems like he plans lecture when he rolls out of bed, doesn't provide or take feedback. Save money and invest in a prep course.

Hospitality Law has been one of my favorite classes I have taken in college so far. Professor Langford is a very nice professor and his lectures are very clear and easy to follow. I would definitely recommend taking notes during the lectures because a lot of things he says are word for word on the tests. Very interesting course materials

Took his Ag Law course last semester. Very knowledgeable about the course topics as a former lawyer. However he was really monotone and boring at times. He works another job but even still he comes off as lazy. Tests and quizzes were among the easiest I had to take in college. Offers extra credit but you probably won't need it.

Professor Langford is a retired lawyer and he makes his lectures as interesting as you can make the material taught. This class is a lot of fun and if you watch the panopto videos and study at least an hour or two before the exam you will pass. Highly recommend this class!
Langford is a really great guy, I would take from him again.
Best teacher and class ever, even if you don't have an interest in law, this class is amazing and will make you interested in law.
I loved having him as a professor! One of the best teachers I've ever had, and I learned so much! He is also super understanding and easy to reach.
One of my favorite professors my freshman year. If you have any interest in law I would strongly recommend taking law-1100 with Trachtenberg.

Professor Trachtenberg is good at not making lectures to repetitive and makes it easy to engage.  There is an assignment between each class but they are much better than reading multiple chapters in a text book per week.  He brings a very good variety of speakers.  If you are considering a career in law this is a great class and professor.

Enjoyed his class so much and learned a lot!  10/10 recommend this course with him.  Lots of participation homework with big papers due every other week, but is very forgiving with late work and resubmissions.

Amazing class and professor and, despite having a lot of homework in the class, I highly enjoyed taking it. Overall, it provided a great outlook on many types of law. A great course to take if you're considering Law School.
Great teacher clearly cares about his students. Clear about what is expected he is very helpful. Just read! and go to class you will be fine.

his voice makes me so mad i actually can't listen to it. his voice cracks every 5 seconds and he says "Okay!" for every other sentence. impossible to focus on the videos when his voice is the only thing i can focus on
Very nice guy and will offer help when needed. As long as you go to class and do homework and study, you will get a fine grade!

I had Benjamin for MATH1400, not 0110, but it won't let me select that course :(
Benjamin is a great instructor. He makes the content understandable, explains topics thoroughly, and does lots of practice problems so you can see how the concepts work. There's weekly homework but it's not long, and the quizzes/tests are very similar to the homework.

MATH 0110 is a basic math class, and Benjamin does a great job teaching the concepts of it. I struggled with math for years, but he is an excellent instructor and helped me get my highest grade in a math class since middle school!

All you do is write 5 long papers for the entire semester. (5-10 pages of writing per paper) He grades easily and fairly if you just have no mistakes and meet the requirements. No homework at all. No real tests that you have to study for. No lectures, just audios you can listen to. Easy A if you're good at writing. I ended with a literal 100%.

Dr. Knapp is super laid back and a great guy. He is extremely knowledge about what he teaches. As long as you do the lab reports and what you discuss makes sense, he will grade you very fairly. I would highly recommend him!
Dr. Knapp is an awesome professor. He takes attendance and there are occasional pop quizzes so just show up and you can have an easy A. Tests are over almost exactly what was presented in class.
He's somewhat of a tough grader. I though it was incredibly easy and interesting but I ended up with a B (probably because of the final)

Interesting information, eye opening. Relaxed teacher, but no phones. Easy going, not tedious work, not much homework. Occasional reading assignments. Tests are not scantron, essays, multiple choice, truefalse, and short answer.

Professor Knapp knows a lot about forestry and natural resources. He has random quizzes so it is smart to show up for class. Not a lot of grades. Tests aren't too hard but you need to know basically everything from the notes. Overall good teacher

Easily my favorite teacher. He takes the most difficult concepts and makes them easy to understand. Very down to earth and makes sure that you understand everything. I definitely recommend taking a class with him.

BEST PSYCH TEACHER YET!  He knows his stuff but is super chill and laid back.  He swears sometimes during lecture which makes him even more relatable to. Easy to work with.  Cute in a high-IQ stoner kind of way.  I was freaking out about taking this class but he made it awesome.  He's pretty flexible on tests. Always has review sessions.

Prof. Kim has a good personality and he is very understanding. He also gave good feedback when I talked to him about assignments before submitting. He is always willing to help with assignments. Dr. Kim is very kind and I can imagine him improving in time.

Dr. Stone was very welcoming and made an easy transition into college. Attendance was very important for daily in-class activities and notes on lecture. You can walk away from this class with multiple basil plants and maybe African violets, would definitely recommend.

Class is pretty easy as long as you pay attention and study. The content isn't difficult to digest, but can seem off-topic at times. Class is structured around small groups and there is a lot of busy work during class, which attendance is part of your grade.

Dr. Stone is the greatest! She is so kind, smart, and funny. If you come to lecture and use the study resources given to you, you will do great. She wants each and every student to succeed. Dr. Stone is a very smart and enthusiastic professor who cares very deeply about her subject. The tests are very difficult to understand. She uses AI to write them, and student made questions. This class is very group-heavy, and if you don't have good teammates, be ready to do everything.

Bethany Stone was an excellent professor. She breaks things down well, and really only focuses on necessary topics that you can connect with other topics in later classes. Bethany is very considerate of your time, and is willing to work with you if you can't make a deadline. 
I didn't love the group project, but that was more because of the group.

Aside from the semester long project with strangers and a random lecture about AI in place of an exam review, I have really enjoyed Dr. Stone's class. She is kind and grades fairly, plus she is extremely understanding when her students are unable to attend class or submit an assignment on time for unexpected reasons. I would definitely recommend!

He cares about the students. Great professor, he's always there to help. Seems like a very genuine professor who loves math and teaching it. Highly recommend him.

Dr. Banks is an awesome professor! By far the best math professor I've ever had. Managed to make the material not seem too intimidating and is always cracking jokes. awful....
