Really, really nice professor. There are only 4 assignments though including the final each worth 100 points. They're all really easy, but make sure you do well!

Great professor who obviously cares about the content. Very interactive class periods and makes everyone feel heard and understood in their views. Material could be viewed as political and touchy subjects but she navigates it super well. Inspirational and cool, she makes me rethink not being a criminal justice major.

Dr. Barrett was the second professor in insect pest management. His lectures were full of information, and some of it was very helpful. However, the information was overwhelming when it came time for the exam. Overall, he was a good professor, though.

Dr. Barrett was probably the best professor I've had my whole time at college! He was clear, slow, and organized. He was always prepared and his lectures were outlined nicely. His tests were pretty easy if you studied. He fosters discussion and admits when he doesn't know the answer to something- then he tells us the answer when he finds out. A++
this guy......THIS guy. He is kinda spicy. I loved his passion and enthusiasm for bugs. Casual fridays were the best when he wore socks and sandals, yeah. HE s got great charisma.
For an Intro class this is a pretty hard class, he throws a lot of useless info at you. Study definitions for test and you should be fine.

Entomology 3710.  His class isnt that hard, you must pay attention and learn ALL the definitions he throws at you during lecture because they will be on the test.  Go to him for help if needed he is willing to work with students who ask.  Overall class isnt that bad just make sure you study a lot for his test, alot.
Great person, who really enjoys teaching and making sure that your better your self for your career as an engineer. Very respectable and loved going to his office hours, to hear his stories.
One of the best professors at MU

This man is my hero. I didn't like hydrology at all, but he has made me really understand why it is important and how it affects everything we do. The homework are hard, but if you work hard and go to office hours he helps out a lot. Definitely recommend!
I didn't think I needed this class, but it was required.  Bryan showed why we needed Hydrology, and connected it to my structures specialty.

I needed a 4000-level poli sci class for my major and after reading other reviews on here, I decided to take his peacekeeping class. Cannot stress enough how happy I am I did! Professor Reeder is hilarious and engaging, always answers questions and communicates, and his tests are about actually LEARNING the content. 15/10, would take again!!

Dr. Reeder was a wonderful professor. This was my first PoliSci class, so I was a bit nervous and unsure whether or not I would go forward with the subject. His class was not easy and was heavy with readings, but everything was manageable yet challenging! I declared a PoliSci grad minor after this course! :)
Dr. Reeder was great. Easy on the eyes and really kind to students. Have taken three classes from him and wish there were more I could take.
Great professor. Loves what he teaches about, and would definitely take his class again.

This class requires a fair amount of work, but the topic was nothing like other Mizzou classes offer so it was really refreshing. Reeder is so nice, wants you to succeed, and care about the world. He is SO helpful and will even point you in the right direction if you are struggling. I appreciated the humor in his lectures, since they could be long

Overall, I really enjoyed Reeders online class. I can tell he would be even better in person! It helps that the topic is super interesting. Only complaint is that the grading was pretty tough, especially considering there really arent any lower level classes students could have taken before this one on the subject.

Professor Reeder is a gem. His classes make you care about the world and makes you question your own place in the world. He is so funny, so caring, and so approachable. I wish I could go to college again just to major in political science to spend more time with him.

Reeder is an amazing professor. He is intelligent, attractive and easy to ask questions to. Make sure the teaching assistant is good or grading might be a problem. But he did a good job handing problems. I would take this class again and again because lectures are so good.

This class only has weekly quizzes, lab reports, and the final practical and exam. The content of the products portion is not hard, but it is a lot of memorization. Your grade is dependent of how you do on the finals. There is extra credit opporotunities and Dr. Wiegand is an engaging professor.

His classes are like a fever dream and always a joy to listen to. Once you take one class that he teaches you are always trying to take another. Wiegand does have a lot of other responsibilities outside of teaching so he can be hard to track down, but he is always willing to spend time with you if you manage to find him.
Good class

Definitely my favorite professor. 
His material can be difficult but he teaches it so well it makes it easier. 
He is funny, respected, and very approachable. 
Don't let any of his courses scare you, he'll make sure you do great!

Overall, it is a pretty boring class, but not too hard. Lecture is good, but a different person teaches the labs and those are terrible. Poorly run and is all over the place. Weekly quizzes are super easy. Only have a final exam which was kind of difficult. Lab practical was difficult due to the professor of that portion. Pretty average class.

Truly cares about his students and their learning. He's also really respectful of time, and won't continue to lecture just because there's time left when he finishes material. Overall, it's a pretty easy class but he makes it fun, and you'll definitely enjoy him
One of my absolute favorite professors. Very clear grading and great lectures. Cares about his students. Wish he taught all my classes.
Dr. Wiegand is a wonderful professor.
she's incredible, she genuinely cares so much about your success and i've never been so engaged by english coursework in my life.

Professor Caitlyn teaches boldly, warmly, and with joyful intensity. The quote by Eden Southworth: ‘It's a great deal too pleasant to be mad, and I'll stay so', shows how she embraces the beautiful madness of literature and invites her students into it. Once that passion hits the room, it sets off a chain reaction - her energy feels almost nuclear.

Professor Caitlyn is a really good teacher. You learn a lot and class is pretty chill. When the projector decides to act up, she just laughs and treats it like her misbehaving dog Whiskey, which always gets everyone cracking up. She's super fair with grading, and her office has so many plants it feels like a mini jungle. Definitely would recommend.

Awful at speaking english and comprehending. Shows up extremely unprepared for class and most days gives up doing her job teaching if she cannot figure out how to turn on the projector. Clearly has no work experience in the engineering field. Save your money and enroll in a class where the teacher can speak and write english.
Loved Chindris but hated Calc 2. He was an amazing professor and although the class was very difficult, I enjoyed going to class because he is quite funny and loves his job and students.

Very kind and genuinely cared for all the students. The tests and homework could be hard, but he gives lots of hints and help if you actually go to class. 
I don't understand how people could've passed this is they didn't go to class, but it's pretty easy if you do.

Dr. Chindris is a brilliant professor. He is super nice and caring and will help out the best he can. Calc II is super hard but he makes it passable. His study guides are exactly like the exams. He also grades the exams really nicely. My TA was pretty difficult and graded hard and I thought that the quizzes were harder than the exams. HW weekly.

Dr. Chindris is one of my favorite professors. I found that I often came into class stressed about classes and tests, but I was calmer when I left. He often made an effort in the first minute or so of class to talk to us about random things. While lecturing he checked in with us often to make sure we understood and answered any questions.

He is a great lecturer, always ready to help a student with any question they have, and gives very fair exams based on study guides. Easy to understand. Calc II is a lot of work, but he makes it manageable.

I loved this guy. I was so nervous for Calc 3 because it was my first college math class. He explained things so well and never had any surprises on the test. The homework is an easy grade booster and also has relevant practice problems, unlike some other math teacher's homework.

I enjoyed having this professor. Calc 3 was the hardest of the calculus courses (in my experience) and I do not think I would have done as well with another professor. The exams are fairly similar to the test reviews so make sure you study those well! He also allows a notecard for the cumulative final.

Great teacher. I had him for Calc 3. The notes are on canvas but it helps a lot more to go to class so he can explain it more. Also drops lowest 2 homework and quiz grades. Quizzes and exams arent difficult. Exams + final often follow the structure of the study guides he gives out with answers. Homework can take awhile sometimes. Highly recommend.
Very easy. Four exams where you watch a movie and relate it to concepts in class. There's weekly homework, which was annoying, but overall really easy. She's also funny and brings her dogs sometimes.

I loved Professor Korasick! She was a super easy grader, but her lectures were so interesting that it was difficult to zone out. She has a huge personality and encourages students to link course material to life outside of class, which I really liked. She may seem like a bit much at first, but she really is a great professor with a lot to offer.
You do not need to attend lectures to do fine in this class. Her lectures are mostly off-topic anyway. If you stay on top of the bi-weekly homework assignments you will be fine.

She's defiantly an interesting one, you won't meet another professor like her. The class was easy, a little underwhelming though. It takes a long time to get grades back and her lectures don't make a lot of sense. Tests are really just a takehome assignment, super easy. This class is very easy just a little annoying.
The lectures in this course dont cover the text book material very well. There is not much structure the the weekly lectures making reading the textbook necessary to learn the actual content.

Didn't grade assignments until the very end of the semester so I wasn't aware I was failing her class until finals week. Her grading criteria is very unclear, even after being in contact with her multiple times regarding rubrics and such.

don't need to come to class. the majority of the grade is based on concept id assignments which she grades really hard on but there are only 4 of those the whole semester so other than that the class is really easy.

This is my second time having her as a professor, and she is very self-aware and funny. She doesn't bombard her students with a lot of notes and makes the class more conversational. She helps us go into more depth about the things happening in our world while applying them to the concepts we learn in class to them.

She was open to suggestion on ways to improve the class.  The quizzes were tricky but the written assignments were clear.  She seemed to grade fair and grades were posted timely.  She seemed to enjoy her job and teaching students.

Awful history teacher. She is a feminist whose studies include feminism so it's the majority of what she talks about while skipping over major world events. Her test are super-specific and are random little things you must remember rather than big picture. Lectures are awful and her slides suck. Overall take with anyone else

This class was super difficult--I would definitely discourage anyone from taking one of her courses. First, my TA has cancelled class last minute, come in late, and didn't even login to his own office hours. I find this incredibly frustrating. Next, Professor Kelley assigns SO much work--around four hours per week and rarely offers feedback!

I have never been assigned this much work in my entire life. She assigns up to two hour lectures a week, which would be fine if she didn't follow it up with a two hour quiz that isn't even worth a lot and a 30 minute map exercise. Plus a discussion on top of that. Plus a ton of reading from the textbook. She keeps these assignments midterm week too

I had the chance to stumble upon her Success Seminar on accident, and took it for an elective credit. She was one of the most insightful and genuinely helpful professors I have had at this school. The class is definitely participation-heavy, but she makes everything so clear that you show up and do your work and it's an easy A.

Carla is the best. You're going to have to participate and actually try, but it's a language class no duh. You don't learn a whole new language by skipping anyways. There is homework every night, but it helps prepare you for the test where it's less stress that way. She is pretty forgiving with the grades and wants you to learn but also succeed.

Carla is one of the best professors I've ever had, she truly cares about her students and loves what she does! Attendance is mandatory and there is daily homework, but the textbooks are free and if you show up and do the work, it is nearly impossible to get a bad grade. I genuinely enjoy this class and highly recommend taking her!

One of the best professors I have ever had! She makes learning Italian easy and instills confidence in all of her students. There is daily homework but it helps with the understanding of the material. As long as you show up to class every day and ask questions when you're confused it should be an easy A-B course. She is accessible outside of class

best professor I have had in college. She is specific in what it is she wants/needs from you in the class for you to get a good grade (& it really is not much.) She is passionate & is always willing to offer help, it is not hard to succeed in this class at all. She is also the most caring prof I've had and cares about your well being & offers help.

carley is fantastic! she knows what she's talking about, the example stories we read were interesting, and the way she structured her class really helped me developed my own skill at writing. the focus on group workshops did wonders to help me get over my fear of sharing my writing with others.
Carley is super helpful and will help you improve your creative writing skills! Not a very difficult class, just has a consistent moderate workload.

Dr. Sinclair is a good English professor to have for gen eds. We did have reading and occasional pop quizzes but she did warn beforehand. Only four essays the entire semester and she actually gives good feedback. She also had workshops where you could peer review and work on the essay in class.

Dr. Conklin is actually one of the nicest and most incredible professors I have had the pleasure of having. She is incredibly knowledgeable, and genuinely cares about her classes. If you don't take a course with her, you're missing out. I am the #1 Conklin fan, take her course, do the reading, and care about your essay and you will do fine.

Dr. Conklin is one of the nicest, most enthusiastic people I've ever met in my life. She cares deeply about her students and their success in and out of class. Prepare, she can be a bit of a tough grader. Also, pro tip: TAKE NOTES DURING DISCUSSIONS! Even if it's stuff your classmates say. She models her lessons and tests after that.

She tends to go off subject, a lot, and time management is not one of her best skills, but Dr. Conklin is a wonderful, wonderful professor. It's incredibly obvious she cares about you and your learning, she wants to see you succeed in and out of the classroom. She's also brilliant so she'll usually have the answer. 11/10 recommend.

Dr. Conklin is incredibly enthusiastic about this class and comes in every day excited to teach.  She is willing to meet with you if you have questions and she takes student feedback very seriously.  She's also just a genuinely nice person who really wants her students to succeed.

Knowledgeable professor that is caring for his students and accessible outside of class hours. Attendance is not required but his test come directly from his lecture. He does not try to trick you with complicated problems and just wants you to understand the base material but gives you the ability to expand your knowledge if you wish.

He is hard to understand sometimes, and his notes don't end up making a lot of sense to me. I love the way he does his tests and the review. The class isn't hard to get a good grade in if you show up and do the review to get ready for the test. He is a very funny guy so that made classes fun. At times it seemed like I was teaching myself.

I had him in Math 4100 and also for Math 3000 which are very different courses but he sturctures them the same. His personality is really funny and he'll talk about concepts from multiple perspectives. The tests come from the lectures which are based on the notes that he also posts. If you go to class and have interest in the topic you will pass.
He never tries to trick you on tests, which was much appreciated. If you show up to class and take notes, and study what will be on the exams, you should get an A.

Amazing professor for any math class. Never tries trick you, & doesn't test you on previous math classes material (i.e. calc 2 & 3). Very funny lecturer and is very accommodating to homework and even test dates. As long as you pay attention in class and do the assignments, and practice exams (like the test) you will get an A.
favorite math class at mizzou, very nice, and good at answering questions

He is a great guy. He really cares about how you do in his class and he will literally beg the class to come to office hours. He is very accesible outside of class and he wont make you feel stupid for asking questions. He is also funny which makes the lectures enjoyable. 10/10 would take again.

I am a math major, I've received an A+ in Calc 1. Carlo is a cool guy, tells really funny jokes, but he teaches on a WHOLE different level than what I believe Calc 2 students should be at. His tests are really hard, and so are his "extra" assignments. If you're on the fence between Calc 2 and Calc 2 Honors take the non-honors.

Carlos is so funny and patient and is really good at getting students out of their shells. My speaking and comfortability with Spanish improved so much. His grading system is pretty generous and he clearly cares a lot about giving intentional and helpful feedback. The class is definitely participation heavy and I learned a lot.

Harsh and difficult. Went abroad for two weeks and made it impossible for me to catch up. Had me take two exams four days apart despite getting back to US four days before. If you plan on going abroad or missing at least a week, don't take Spanish. They really do not care about anything outside of their class and will not corporate with you at all.
Great professor. Wants you to do well in his class and is always willing to help.

I changed my professor from a much more difficult one to Carlos. He was great. So caring of students, very funny, and compassionate. Always willing to help and make sure students succeed. DO NOT SKIP CLASS. He is very good at grading assignments, tests, and compositions fairly.

This is a challenging class, but Mendez was great. He's super funny in lectures, and is always happy to explain something multiple times if you don't understand. Participation definitely matters, but he's awesome at encouraging different people to get involved in the class discussion. Class is fully in Spanish, but it really helps with practicing.

Don't make the mistake I did: GO TO CLASS! Your grade can definitely take a toll if you don't. He's a pretty harsh grader, but justifiably so. He does not speak English, but don't be afraid of that. He speaks in a way so that everyone can understand him. Otherwise, he's pretty funny and makes class entertaining.

Carlos is hilarious! His lectures are never boring and you learn a lot. The honors part is an additional at-home composition, an at-home oral final, and reading a short book in class at the last week of the semester. He definitely grades tests strictly but they're manageable as long as you study. Online homework is due three times a week

Entire class is taught in Spanish, so be prepared for that. Online homework is a lot of work too. If you take notes on the tenses in class and study the culture for each country that applies to the exam then you should be fine. He isn't the best at explaining things if you ask questions and he grades really tough, but I really enjoyed having him.

I had Carlos for my Civil Engineering Legal Issues course (online). He was great, very engaging with students and passionate about work. The exams are a little harder than expected, but the rest of the coursework is very straightforward.

Teaches online courses. Ive taken three classes with him at this point and its always pretty good. The lectures are pretty easy to understand and the material is usually not too complex, but its almost always interesting. Exams are notorious for being worded very strangely but they are not actually too bad. Overall great.

Dr. Sun is a professor that expects student to know a fair amount of material but is sloppy on presenting the material. The first test is a unexpectingly vague/ open ended  question and asks your opinion on a design. overall you need to review it.

I had Carlos for my Civil Engineering Legal Issues course (online). He was great, very engaging with students and passionate about work. The exams are a little harder than expected, but the rest of the coursework is very straightforward.

Teaches online courses. Ive taken three classes with him at this point and its always pretty good. The lectures are pretty easy to understand and the material is usually not too complex, but its almost always interesting. Exams are notorious for being worded very strangely but they are not actually too bad. Overall great.

Dr. Sun is a professor that expects student to know a fair amount of material but is sloppy on presenting the material. The first test is a unexpectingly vague/ open ended  question and asks your opinion on a design. overall you need to review it.

Professor Wexler was very good at explaining concepts. He was clear on what to expect on the exams (in class/practice problems very similar). His lectures were recorded, so missing class wasn't a big deal. As long as you do the discussion problems and go to the review before the exams you will be fine.

Dr.Wexler was a good prof. He gave practice exams that were extremely similar to the real ones. Gave plenty of examples in class for the homework and exam questions. Plus he was clear about grading. Loved that the exams weren't weighted heavily. 5 exams, 10% each. He gave you notes to fill out during class as well. Hate physics but he made it good.

This course will pick up covering basic 2d kinematics identical if not easier than high school level physics. Only difficult exam was 3. It was unexpectedly hard compared to the sample exams and included a very unorthodox problem we were not familiar with. Be careful and study hard for that exam. The other 4 are easy A+ if you practice throughly.

This was probably the hardest class I ever took as an engineer so far and took an insane amount of work, but it seemed that the tas and Dr wexler wanted the students to succeed. I had to read the textbook alot but I found the lecture slides were also necessary. This course is insanely fast paced and he taught it well for what it's worth.

Very entertaining professor. You must pay attention in every lecture or you will fall behind. This class was definitely my most difficult, but it wasn't impossible to succeed. Carlos is very funny and you will find his lectures entertaining!

Dr. Wexler is a great guy who is a lot of fun to talk to. He is clearly very knowledgeable about electronics and is always willing to help. However, it seems he thinks the material is more intuitive than it is, and there are times where his explanations can come off a little condescending. 4050 is conceptually quite difficult, but graded easily.

Wexler's nearly a complete non-factor, you're not going to learn most of the material by showing up to lecture, but from quizzes, labs, and homeworks. He will zoom and post his lectures online, if you do find value in his lectures. Class is challenging but easy to get good grade in due to the weight of labs, quizzes and homework

Prof Wexler is very passionate about physics and makes the lectures enjoyable to watch. The class is really hard and fast-paced so it is important to study outside of class. Read before lectures and go to discussions.
He talks extremely fast and flips the page before you can even write the equation down.

Taking a class with this professor is miserable. The expectations for papers are incredibly vague and no examples are given. Grading is biased. When asking questions, responses are rude and not helpful. Some of the questions on the quizzes have multiple correct answers so it's a matter of guessing what she's thinking. Wish I would have checked here

Carol is one of the worst professors I have ever had. SW7720 is only out of 100 points total, so any slip up can cost you a letter grade. Group project IN GRAD SCHOOL ONLINE is a bit much.. Disrespectful and EXTREMELY critical at grading papers. Quizzes were reasonable and you can take them twice. Avoid her at all costs for your own sanity.

She was clear in her written expectations around when she would be available to respond or meet with us. I appreciated that we could take the weekly online tests twice. Very biased and inconsistent in her grading of papers. Honestly felt like she was trying to weed us out of the program. It's very clear that she primarily operates as SSW Director.

Hands down the worst professor I have ever had. She is a narcissist who puts assignment instructions in multiple places, changes them frequently, then denies doing so. I did not feel supported in any way. In fact, this instructor is the singular reason I will walk away from this program and my passion.

Unethical, uncaring and rude professor. Grades without justification and valid reasoning. Can be very unprofessional at times if she thinks she is right on something. Avoid at all costs if possible not worth the stress

Carol is the only professor in the department that I didn't enjoy. Virtually universally disliked among students. I did well in her class but still felt her grading was erratic and opinion based. Her ego is huge and her lectures are boring. You could read the assigned book and never attend a lecture and get more out of it than I did this class.

Carol is literally the worst professor in the department. She is unapproachable, grades based on what she thinks is correct rather than considering that ethical decision making is fluid and may have multiple acceptable courses of action. She gives you the majority of your grades and feedback after course evaluations are due. Do not take her.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER!! Grades unfairly and with unreasonable expectations. Rude. Elitist. No empathy. Does not care that you are an adult with a life outside of school. If anyone has a choice whether or not to take a class with her, DO NOT.
The class was okay, but it was very confusion to understand the structure and the material.

I spent way too much time in office hours to receive no helpful feedback and no matter what grade I got I was told to come to office hours DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS unless you are incredibly bored because it will take up so much time to get an A
So confusing and not very helpful. She gives too much reading and little time to complete. She isn't really caring about the students. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!

Dr. Brock is very sweet and cares about her students. She provides many opportunities of extra credit and office hours to get help on things. The class was difficult and had lots of work even outside of class but if you take the time to do it you will be just fine.
Just don't do it worst experience I've had in any class so far

Dr. Brock, if you are reading this please take these comments personally. Please stop pandering to your students during class time. Also learn how to grade papers other than just claiming everything as "overstatements." Also stop picking favorites in class. I did not miss a single class and you picked me out in class more times than I can count.

I am currently taking this class, and this might be the most unclear instructor I have had so far at Mizzou. This class has way too much reading for the time she gives us, and no matter what, every assignment has to be the way she wants it, or its wrong. Her feedback on the papers you have to write is very unclear, leaving you to guess what to fix.

So so many readings to do before each class. I understand this is a writing intensive course but it's so much work for a 2000 level class. She's a nice woman but her expectations are so high. She does give opportunities for extra credit but it doesn't matter with how bad the grading scale is. Her instructions aren't always clear either.

Prof. Waldbuesser is great and cares a lot about her students. She'll gladly help you develop the main speeches you need to write for the class. If you show effort, you'll do well regardless of skill.
Dr. Orbann is absolutely amazing. She is so supportive of her students and wants everyone to succeed. Participation really matters but there are so many opportunities for it. I loved her class!
Dr. Orbann is a very caring teacher who makes an effort to connect with her students. She gives very clear feedback and her class is well organized.

Dr. Orbann is very caring and is willing to help if you are having a hard time in her class. There aren't many assignments, but they are worth a lot of points. She's very into using AI to help generate ideas and likes group assignments. She is very nice, although her lectures are somewhat boring. The material isn't half bad.

Super easy class. Attendance does not matter, exams are online and open note, and projects are not worth a lot of points. The lectures can be pretty boring but Dr. Orbann makes them interesting and tries to be engaging with the class. She is so nice and understanding. I would definitely take a class from her again!

Absolutely loved Dr. Orbann's lectures! Even though the content is not super exciting, she stays engaged with her students and makes it easy to understand! Also, she is the most knowledgeable and up to date on the topics she teaches of any professor I know. Definitely my best professor yet at Miz!

Lectures are boring unless health care systems & insurance interest you. Need to understand material to do well on tests. A few group projects, short papers, presentations. TA grades everything. Orbann cares about updating her presentations, uses lots of graphs & a few videos. She's trying, and it's not the worst class. I kind of liked it.

Professor Orbann presented information about insurance and health care in the most interesting way you can. The course content is dry but she does a good job of keeping students engaged. There are 10 reading responses, a film review, a group project, 1 midterm (which is the only test), and the final is a debate on health reform.

She's very enthusiastic about her lectures and makes them interesting. Also was an easy A if you paid attention to the lectures and did well on the quizzes. Never had exams, just homeworks and online quizzes. Class covered a lot of common sense so just sit back and enjoy the A. MUST go to class though-attendance and participation points are given.
I just love her, she is my favorite

Dr. Kalton makes it known that she cares about all of her students. Her lectures were some of the highlights of my week. Her lectures are so engaging and she approaches every topic with so much compassion.

One of the best psych professors I've had at Mizzou Yes attendance is taken but it's easy points and she offers a decent amount of extra credit, and even offers extra credit for not missing any of the labs. Dr. Kalton truly cares about students and is willing to meet to discuss any issues you may be having.

Such a fun professor! She offers extra credit opportunities, and quizzes and case studies can be checked for accuracy before submission. Her class is easy if you show up and participate in her entertaining lectures you'll love going to. She plays music, hands out goodies, and just enjoys getting to know her students. Can't recommend her enough!

Dr. Kalton is the sweetest! She plays music and hands out goodies, loves talking to students and getting to know them. Her class is very easy if you show up to her fun lectures and pay attention. She also has numerous opportunities for extra credit, and you can check your answers on all of your quizzes and case studies. Can't recommend her enough!

Very funny and enthusiastic! Loved going to class, she would play music and usually give out candy to everyone. She loves to get to know you personally and truly loves her job. If you see this Dr. Ellis we love you !!!

She is my favorite teacher of all time! She is very enthusiastic, plays music when you come into class, she keeps the class upbeat and makes it so exciting. She is very caring and always tells us that we can come to her if we need anything at all. I really enjoy going to her class and I honestly hated the times I had to miss.

I don't rate professors a lot but she is truly amazing. Attendance is important because it is graded, but I love her lecture so much that I don't mind. She truly cares about each student and makes lectures actually interesting, which is so hard to find in a professor. I would take her again without hesitation
Lectures can seem cumbersome at time but Professor Duncan is really nice and you can tell how dedicated she is towards the subject and her students.

Reading quizzes 3 times a week online . In the study guide, she said they would help us on tests. Later, she told us that the quizzes wouldn't be beneficial for helping us study for tests. Hard tests, boring readings and unhelpful reading quizzes. Synagogue visit was fun but i don't see how it helped anyone understand ancient Judaism.

While there are a lot of papers and quizzes, the course is really effective in teaching the material. Plus she makes the lectures engaging and really engaged with students who ask questions and engage with the topics.
Carrie Duncan is my favorite professor. She is very clear and very helpful. If you want a teacher for a Religious Studies class, then Carrie Duncan is for you!

Professor Duncan was clear at the beginning of class that it would require work and effort to get a good grade. As a professor, she's extremely helpful, wonderfully engaging and always enthusiastic. Couldn't recommend her any more.

Content is interesting and Dr. Frisby really cares about it. She gives out tons of easy extra credit, which is the only reason I kept an A.

Dr. Frisby I an AMAZING professor. She is real and cares about her students. She wants you to learn and loves feedback. She gave so many extra credit opportunities, that if you're failing this class or have under a B it's your own fault. She LOVES what she does and you can tell. If this woman could be my grandma it would make my life.

I'll start off by saying I took her J2000 class years ago, and we still talk about how bad it was. Disorganized doesn't cover it. She claimed to "research" what she taught. She played a scene from a Spike Lee movie and claimed it was a real racist insurance commercial from the South, and that was only the tip of the iceberg.
Professor Frisby is amazing. I don't know about her other class but her J2000 lectures are of absolutely high quality and absolutely inspirational.

Generally speaking, had zero interaction with him due to the online nature of the course. As long as you read the PowerPoints, exams are extremely easy. No curveball questions, all answers come straight from what you learn in the class. There are like 8 discussion boards, two essays, and 3 exams, so the workload wasn't that bad at all.
Class is made up of a few tests, (open note, two attempts) a paper and a presentation. There's not much to worry about in this class.

SSC1150 is an easy A if you turn everything in and show up. Make sure to stay on top of homework on canvas as they don't announce it before hand. Go to every class; each absence is 20% off of participation grade.
Dr. Fitch has a great sense of humor and cares about his students. I am a big fan!
Great, very intelligent guy, difficult class, but necessary and important.

Dr. Terry leads an excellent discussion every class. Readings are heavy and necessary, but also fulfilling and will change how you view constitutional democracy. If you are willing to put the time and effort in, constitutional debates with Dr. Terry will be one of the most influential courses you take in the Kinder Institute

Class is boring, but required for journalism. Dami was fine, uninteresting. I did anything except take notes during the lecture. Heavily emphasis on participation, in-class participation every day that contributes to your grade. Tests are open-note and easy
Dami was super monotone and boring. The class was super easy and boring. Attendance was required. Class felt like a huge waste of time
Not sure why people like this guy. He does not care about students in my experience, the class was annoyingly easy and he is just kinda douchey
MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR EVER. He cares about students so much and clearly loves what he does.

Dr. Hall is very passionate about sustainability and it shows in his teaching style. There are 3 tests, 3 assignments, and iclicker questions that make up your grade, with only one or two extra credit opportunities. He's a funny guy and will make you want to come to the lecture. 10/10 would take another class from him (I am next semester).
Do not recommend. Not as 'great' as they say.
Dr. Hall was fine, although he was not great at responding to emails about missed classes & making up work. Not outstanding, but not bad.

LOVE THIS GUY! So kind and smart, wonderful class. It's clear he loves teaching and he loves environmental science. He's the best. I took it during covid so it was probably easier but it was not hard at all but still very educational.

I loved Dr. Hall's class on sustainability. He is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had, and he was always knowledgeable and enthusiastic. He is always well prepared for class, leads great discussions, and the reflections and finals are so easy. If I could take every class he offered, I would. Just make sure to participate in class!

Dr. Hall was amazing! He is super enthusiastic and it's clear that he's genuinely passionate about what he teaches. As long as you show up and pay attention well, you'll do fine. The lectures are interesting and he explains topics clearly. Even with 2 in person classes this semester, this one online was easily my favorite.

While Damon was only my professor for a FIG course, I had many meaningful conversations with him that helped me find my footing during my first semester at Mizzou. I heavily recommend him as either a FIG or J-1300 professor simply by how kind, caring and interested in his students well being that he seems to be.

I actually took Kiesow's Audience and Innovation Capstone, (it would not allow me to select it, here.) He is probably my favorite professor at Mizzou. Not only did his class provide amazing experience for my resume, but he also took time during class to help me figure out how to get a job/write a resume. Highly recommend knowing him!!!
TOUGH GRADERRRRRRRRRRR!
The class is lots of work, but he helps keep it manageable. If an assignment is confusing/challenging, he will work with you as long as you communicate!

Kiesow is such a nice professor! He truly wants to help you as much as he can. He always asks us how were doing and is willing to stay after class for an hour to answer questions. The class isnt hard except for the big profile story.

I took Exercise Science Careers with Dan which is a one credit course and there were two exams in the class. Both of them took up a large portion of the grade, and there were many irrelevant questions that were very broad and nonspecific. Overall, it was a simple class but the exams were unnecessarily difficult and arguably unfair at times.

I'm taking an online class, so maybe that's why my experience has been different, but it's been awful. He doesn't accept any late work at all, yet drops assignments randomly. There's no calendar, so it's completely random. The slides he posts are barely thrown together and have a lot of mistakes. He doesn't seem to care about this course at all.

This was my second class with Dr. Smith. The lecture material was very similar to his first class, even though the topics were different. His exams are more difficult than you would expect, so make sure to study. Totally possible to get an A, though!

Dr. Smith is a well respected professor in the NEP department. I really enjoyed this class. However, the exams are much harder than I was expecting, so be prepared to study. If you come to class and work hard, then you can get a good grade.
If you have had one of his classes, you have had them all. But very easy A and very good professor! Super cool guy and really helpful. Definitely recommend his classes.
Very straight forward guy, weekly quizzes are kind of tough but the tests are exactly what was on the quizzes so its easy to boost your grade there.
Very strict grader, and exams were "proof" heavy. He refused to curve one of our exams when the average was 59%. Lectures are awkwardly formatted with his handwritten "fill in the blank" notes.

Aside from his handwritten lecture slides being a tad lengthy or messy at times, I have zero complaints about Dan. Lectures, homework, and exams were straightforward and reasonable. He provided practice problems that were exactly like those I found on the exam. And he's a down-to-earth guy. College classes don't get much better than that.

I have never struggled with any class before. Keeping many biases aside, if you recognize or have a gut feeling that you should drop the class the first week, do it. This teacher only taught proofs of calculus concepts and rarely did any actual problems. Homeworks/exams not like the lecture at all, and i learned more from youtube videos then them.

He's awful. Terrible. He's a nice guy but is terrible at his job. He doesn't know how to explain things in an easy way to understand. The lecture notes don't line up with the homework AT ALL and the homework is insanely hard. The tests are identical to the practice tests though. Overall, stupid hard homework, bad explanations, no bueno.

This professor always answered my emails in a timely manner. I did multiple zooms with him and he explained the content well and walked me through tough problems. If you're willing to work hard, he'll help you and make sure you're prepared for the exams. It's tough content to get, but he's a great teacher. Plus I took it online.

His homework and questions does not match up with the lecture. he uses another professors lectures and its hard to match what is taught, to the level of difficulty of the questions on the homework and exams. we also have to pay to take exams online for every one do not take the online class.

I took Edidin for calculus 3. The homework and quizzes are mild. I would suggest going to office hours and asking him questions about his review exams - he is very willing to help. The material is dense so make sure to study everything. The difficulty of this class shouldn't come as a surprise considering you had to take calculus 2 to get here.

Edidin is a solid calc 2 prof. He knows what he's talking about and is eager to answer questions. Your grade is based on weekly quizzes, weekly webassign hw, and exams. He gives reviews for exams that are typically harder than the exam itself and prepare you well. Ask a lot of questions and you'll do fine. Watch out for the series section.

Do not take her online literacy class. She is 100% not accessible and grades way harder than any intro class should. the topics are so insanely boring and I have to hire a tutor to finish the class. Yup. on top of paying for it I have to pay someone to help me. This is coming from a sophomore who passed the act reading with flying colors.

Nice person, but not a great teacher. She was unclear and poorly delivered information. Many classes she attempted to facilitate a conversation but failed to do so because she was not well respected by the class. In her defense, out of the MANY readings, only three were of any good. Grades harshly based on personal opinion of the text. Not ideal.
Dana is nice, but she is not organized
She grades very very hard and is a bit on the meaner side.

Probably the most immature teacher at Mizzou. She yells and makes students feel dumb when she disagrees with them. Didn't grade assignments for 10 weeks - no exaggeration. I didn't know if I had an A or a D. Mandatory class MWF but also a mandatory film each Monday from 7-10pm. If you have to take the class, it's fine but I wouldn't if not needed.

Dana is a young and spirited individual. You're required to watch films weekly and then answer a few questions about them. There is a textbook that you should read. Rather than having exams you have essays. I suck at writing, but still did good in the class. Dana is not a tough grader, just make sure to interpret films and explain your reasonings.

Weston is such a sweet lady who truly cares about her students. But, tests are EXTREMELY difficult & there's no allowed equation cheat sheets, also her TAs give graded 1 quiz every week which is draining. Lectures are hard to follow due to a funky lecture style and her very hard to read cursive handwriting that the lectures are based off of.

For the love of all things good and holy don't take Calc 2 with Dr Weston. Her notes are all handwritten with lots of mathematical shorthand you have to learn at the start of the semester on top of the course material. Also, her TA gave quizzes every week that were so toughly graded you would be lucky to get a C. DON'T DO IT ITS NOT WORTH IT!!!!!!!

All notes in cursive with strange shorthand notation that is tough to decipher; does not allow notecards/ cheat sheets for exams which makes it very difficult. Tough grader and bad lectures (watch professor Leonard on YouTube instead). I also took this class at 8am which made it tougher but I would not at all recommend taking her.

Isn't wise for teachers to interrupt kids asking questions. Doing so felt insulting to her, having a response of "you should know this! You gonna wait til the night before the exam to learn it? A week? Two weeks? No!" She goes over notes taken from the book, but expects students to understand how she interprets it. Office hours didn't help.

She was nice but not a very good teacher, she seemed like she did not know what she was really talking about and made lectures hard to keep up with. It did not help that her assistant gave quizzes every week that were impossible for no reason. Westons grading on the exams were tough but fair.

Her lectures and notes were definitely hard to understand, but I found that watching other professors lectures on youtube and reading the textbook to be an easy way to prepare for her lectures. Her tests are very fair and she gives a lot of credit on the exams as long as you show your work and use the correct notation. She's a very silly lady.

This class will have you rethinking your entire major. There is homework and a quiz every week along with a lecture everyday. There are four total exams that account for a majority of your grade. She curves the tests at the end of the semester by around 5%. She is a bad at teaching as she only has one style but she cares about the students.

This class is extremely difficult, but she does her best to talk us through everything. I found her notes difficult to understand, same with lectures, and instead the review days seemed to be the best way for me to learn. She's very nice and gave us plenty of review material for the exams, which there are a lot of.

Spoltore is the GOAT. I found his class to be very entertaining when discussion was active, not so much when it was quiet. With this being said, discussion made up a big part of the class. Attendance isn't necessary, and you can do the HW without it, but his in-class commentary is great. Dane is very caring and hilarious. Absolutely recommend. 5/5.

Dane is super nice and a chill professor. He unfortunately takes forever to grade and doesn't always give feedback. Sometimes the assignment will not be posted on time. He does accept late work. The syllabus does not have any deadlines, but the project outlines will. It was not a hard class; there were only 3 full papers and then a revision paper.

This instructor was so disorganized. The syllabus provided at the beginning of the semester didn't have any due dates. Modules weren't updated regularly and major assignments were frequently posted a few days before the due date. He provided no feedback and graded without a rubric. This class was easy, but frustrating and a complete waste of time.

He was okay, work was easy to complete. A lot of in-class peer work which didn't do anything and was pointless. He takes FOREVER to grade, like, after finals week all my assignments were finally graded. "conferences" are unnecessary to go to, all he talks about during the conference, is all on the notes he left on your paper. Fine professor
Professor Spoltore (Dane) is very kind and he is a great instructor. He is just a graduate student and I think he's doing better than a lot of my other professors. Great guy and a great class.
Hes a really nice prof and really young. The class isnt hard at all and he accepts stuff late. Id take him again, its definitely my most relaxed class this semester.

Sipe is an unreliable professor and is often arrogant and mean. He accuses students of cheating when their written French is different from their spoken French, gives very little information about assignments, grades late, and is extremely passive aggressive in communication. He expects a lot from his students but doesn't put a lot in himself.

He was easily my favorite professor of the semester. I had prior experience in French, but he made my desire to continue even greater. I mean, he literally skateboarded for all of us. Doesn't get much cooler than that.

Monsieur Sipe is fantastic! He has a strong passion for the French language, and it really shows. He genuinely wants his students to do well, and will do a lot to help you succeed. The VHL textbook assignments are a pain, but they do help you learn. If you show genuine interest in learning French and participate, you'll have an amazing time.

Sipe is such a great professor. He will definitely call you out if you're not participating but it's only because he cares about helping his students improve. As far as grading papers he gives good corrections and for speaking exams he picks out a mistake and has you correct it. If he likes you he *might* let you talk in English occasionally.

He's a good teacher, passionate about what he teaches, and genuinely wants his students to do well. The only thing I really have is that he's very disorganized and doesn't like to take responsibility when he forgets things. He can be intense one on one; he is not afraid to single people out. But on the other hand, he's a really nice, positive guy.
Dan Sipe is an amazing teacher! He really cares about his students and takes the time to help. Ask him what "nosebox" means for extra credit.
Dr. Sipe was one of my favorite French professors!

professor sipe is a great professor! he can be kind of intense one on one (i once balled uncontrollably in his office) but he genuinely believes all his students can succeed with out any excuses. he pushes you out of your comfort zone sometimes but only enough to challange you which is what sets him apart from other teachers.
He's pretty average. He's absolutely not clear about grading criteria. About 80% of your grade is based only on two papers and he was very picky. I would never take him again.

He is fun and young so he tries really hard to relate to his students. His class is mostly papers and little assignments. CHECK CANVAS often because sometimes he will post small assignments without telling you in class. Show up to class because attendance and participation is worth a third of your grade in the end.

This was his first semester teaching. Lectures were not good. We were either in class for 15 mins or the entire time. There was no consistency. He just read the slides and never did examples in class. Studying was extremely difficult and HW was even a pain. Half the time he had to give us the answers because he realized how absurd they were.

All exams are short answer or essay based. The class was called Yoga and Meditation in the Modern World and we did Yoga Nidra on Fridays so we all fell asleep during the meditation practice. You only can miss 4 classes before it effects your grade.

A great professor! We had great guest speakers, and he is clearly knowledgeable and passionate about criminal justice. We had one assignment and (open-book, open-note) quiz per week. He follows the textbook very clearly. Any questions you ask will be answered kindly.

He is an amazing professor and person overall! He is there for your success and he brings in guests to help better inform us on real life examples!! If i could have him as a professor again I totally would and recommend this class to everyone!

This course is relatively really easy! Attendance is "required" since he does random attendance check assignments, but you can sometimes predict when he is doing them and he does excuse 3 of them. His exams and lectures are easy, but he does tend to talk a lot during lectures about other topics. Overall recommend this professor though!

I loved him so much. Attendance is technically mandatory but he only takes attendance 16 times throughout the semester and we met 3 times a week, also some of them get dropped so missing 1 or 2 isn't a big deal. He taught almost directly from the textbook and exams were online so it was super easy to get an A. Only complaint is he talks A LOT.

Dan is an awesome professor. I encourage all to read about his background and how he currently serves the people of Columbia. This is a very people oriented class and Dan really takes the time to talk a lot about the justice system and how to understand it better...he is my favorite professor I have had at Mizzou. I had him jun/sen years.

Criminal Justice was THE easiest class I've ever taken. He teacher verbatim from the book so missing a class is no big deal. Attendance is technically mandatory but he rarely took attendance. The assignment answers were also verbatim from the book, so I barely went or studied and still did very well. He's SO boring but its worth it for the easy A.

Loved Hanneken! Only complaint is that his lectures could be shorter. He likes to talk a lottttttt. But he is a great professor who is passionate about his work. His assignments aren't worth a lot of points, but they're not difficult and he isn't a tough grader either. He took attendance almost every class.

Mr. Hanneken is very passionate about social work and criminal justice. He goes off on tangents, but they're very engaging and allow for a more human perspective. There are no tests, just 25-point quizzes, and the quizzes are online, open-book, and very easy. He takes attendance with random in-class assignments but they're only worth 3 points

Daniel was a great TA. He worked out many questions during the recitation. He is good at calculus. Although, it's sometimes difficult to understand some of the later topics in this class. It's not bcs of him, it's more about the material. I took calc when I was in highschool. I could say that Daniel was better than my previous teacher!

Instructor was very knowledgeable on this subject. He taught it in a way that a non-math person like me could understand the subject. go to his review session. The topics on the test were clearly emphasized in class to help prepare for it better. He was great at explaining concepts in an easy manner. oh, one more, His english was perfect.
I could never understand anything he was saying because of his accent. He never made any sense and wasn't good at explaining things. Don't take from him
Great professor. Very succinct and insightful lectures and assigned relevant reading materials. Grades were fair and she gave good feedback.

I have nothing positive to say about her. She takes a long time to grade, often talks about unrelated topics during class, and accused me of using AI when I did not. She is a poor grader and takes everything too seriously. will drop your grade for the smallest thing. do not take her unless you have to

Where do i begin. Dr Adams started out the course saying not everyone will get an A.. like hello? She is incredibly disorganized and the lectures genuinely have nothing to do with what we are reading in our textbooks or the assignments. You have one excused absence and then it's half a letter grade gone. She takes forever to grade too.. Good luck!
She goes over all assignements during office hours. The tests are very close to the homework assignements.
Very hard because it is online statistics. The professor is nice and helpful. She does not accept late assignments.

Graded mostly by discussion boards that are worth 1 or 2 points, so you better not miss one or two of them, or your grade will suffer. She won't tell you about the upcoming projects or have any form of communication throughout the class. Had a paper due Monday after a long weekend that I didn't know about until later in the week.
Dr. Crespy is kind and sweet but also very passionate about acting. I learned a ton in his class!

If you are ready to learn and grow and work- TAKE HIS CLASS. I found myself exhausted at trying to do my best in his class, but I never seemed to mind. He's one of those teachers you really want to do well for and want to learn from. And he wants to teach and for you to learn-- and you will. Couldn't recommend more.
SETS THE RECORD FOR SENDING THE MOST EMAIL IN ONE SEMESTER EVER.... so much that it goes straight to junk mail now...
This class was very easy, there is a lot of extra credit so an A isn't out of reach.

Dr. Crespy's class was incredibly easy.  Everything was online, and you didn't really need to go to class to do well.  Although, some of the material on the exams were just from the lectures.  Dr. Crespy is a very very nice professor and very helpful if you don't understand something.  Only sad thing is that he won't be teaching this class anymore.

this class was hella easy. I think i went to class like 3 times.  my friend literally stopped going to class in september and got a B in the class. All tests are online and you can use your book to look up all the answers. this aside, crespy is passionate about theatre and an excellent teacher. the only problem is motivating yourself to go to class

Cletzer may be a QUACK, but he is a pretty good guy overall. Sometimes he is too smart for his own good, so if you need something rexplained or an assignment adjusted, just ask him. He is a rambler and talks fast during lectures, but provides good info. Class is pretty good as long as your assigned small group and TA is not horrible.

You'll easily get an A if you do all of the homework. There are weekly reading journals that cover 15+ pages of scholarly reading. Every class period involves group work. Don't take this class if you're busy.
Cletzer is such a fun professor. He really works hard to help every one and is very respectful in terms of feedback. Really awesome guy, 10/10 would take again
He's a super nice guy and very funny, I enjoyed his class. It is very test and lecture heavy but nothing unbearable. I'd say it's not easy but if you put in the work you'll be fine.

I would not take this class with this professor. I looked it up later and he has the lowest grade distribution out of all of the professors that teach this class. He does IClickers but they are random and you will never know when they are. Your entire grade is based off of iclickers at random and tests. Take this class with anyone else.

He gives way too much info. There are no study guides and says that any content can be on the tests. It is too much information to cover, too many reading assignments to keep track of, and test averages are not great. Usually C averages for the class on tests.

Lectures are entertaining and you learn a lot. Exams are very very hard and if you dont memorize pretty much everything you are probably out of luck. Wish there was opportunities to raise your grade through other things like a project or something else

Attendance isn't 'mandatory', but if you miss a lecture you will not be able to pass an exam as well as losing very grade heavy iclicker points. Extremely unorganized class, only canvas posts are in syllabus. He makes lectures entertaining at least, but exams are difficult to study for because of an abundance of information and no study guide.

Tests are majority of your grade. Go to class! Write everything down. Statistics will be on tests. Read the books and articles assigned. He seems like a pretty chill guy but he's an alright professor. Class could be organized better. I feel like he could use things other than exams to gauge learning. Mentioned that and gave reccs in my course eval.

Dr. Ruggeri does a really good job with lectures and keeps them interesting. Make sure you write down EVERYTHING from the slides as that is the majority of the material for the exams. There's a lot to read and no study guides. I recommend using quizlet to study for tests.

Go to class!!! It's literally like 80% of your grade and he makes attendance weigh more than exam scores!!! He's a nice teacher but I wish the class had more structure. He'll say something won't be on the exam and then it ends up on the exam. There's also no study guide, no clear direction on what or how to study. Won't respond fast but yea he's ok

Due to corona, we had to switch to online mode. Despite that he went above and beyond. He made us participate, & turn in assignments online easily. He also does a good job explaining the stories we read. Very charismatic, and fun. If you need more time or have a personal thing happening, he is very understanding and helps you.

Took his advanced convo class and LOVED it! All we did was talk everyday and usually that can be awful but he has us talk about really cool/controversial topics like identity, abortion, terrorism, the future, and a bunch others. I really enjoyed the class, and the only homework was a 2-3 page reading every now and then and a group project.
Do NOT take him.

He is a really good professor! Take notes. Don't copy the slide show word for word, he posts it on canvas. Take note of the iClicker questions and answers, there will be some on the exams. Complete the entire study guide yourself. You get a better understanding and can find the little things in the reading that he will put in the exams.

Education Majors are Idiots. That is mainly my only comment. Dr. Bergin is clear of his expectations to read the textbook, and many of the exam questions come from that. Rubrics are clear, discussion posts are easy to score well, and the tests are all multiple choice and EASY.
Knows what he is talking about, makes classes interesting. Very informative, definitely feel more prepared to be an educator after taking his course.

Doctor Bergin's class is not hard in regards to material, his class is just insanely boring and hard to pay attention. The textbook is written by him and contains things that are definitely not backed by science. He mentions race, gender, and SES very oddly, its almost uncomfortable. His lectures are a mess and I think he makes up half the info.
I said lecture heavy, because he talks to us but everything he says to us comes straight from the book.

Dr. Bergin is a horrible professor that structures his class poorly. He requires mandatory attendance but barely talks about anything relevant during the lectures. The entire exam is taken from the text book (which he wrote himself) and he expects you to basically just learn from reading the text book while he himself teaches you nothing.

I would not recommend this class to anyone. The teacher is what made this class so bad. Half the time he did not know what he was talking about and you would ask questions and he would not know how to answer. The book you have to use, he wrote and it is all over the place and does not flow what so ever. The Professor is very monotone and boring.

Guess work on exams will get you around a 65% if you've taken similar classes before. If you watched animal planet for ONE DAY you could pass this class without trying. I leave every day angry that I wasted money on this class. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Geary is a nice guy, but he gives no outline of things to study for tests. There is no homework but that means your grade is strictly test scores. If you don't go to class or read the book, you will definitely fail.

Dr. Geary is a decent professor - knowledgeable, willing to answer questions - but borders on strange/offensive sometimes. Psych 4440 was a dream class, though, with no homework, just tests grades, and extra credit for showing up to class the class after every test. He is condescending and thinks he is funny, but is generally offensive. Gives you a ton of information and virtually no guidance on studying for tests. I dreaded going to his class and left in a rage many days. I will not take any of his classes again
He is an incredible professor and is entertaining/informative. Tests are pretty hard though. Covers a lot of material and there is little guidance as to what specifics to look for while studying.
Really interesting class and the professor definitely knows what he's talking about, I mean he literally wrote the book. Very challenging but worthwhile

This class is very interesting. It focuses on the evolutionary differences between the sexes. The textbook is a dense read, but it supplements the class very well. His power points were easy to follow. If you take notes, read the book, and study you will do fine. His exams aren't tricky. Multiple choice, T/F, and 5 points of extra credit. No final.

He is one of my favorite professors at Mizzou. The course is not hard, read two books, a group presentation on one, and a book report on the other. Talks about current topics and makes the class relevant.
Does not follow a syllabus. Does not teach published course description. Won't help you outside of class. Cannot teach the material. No textbook. Creates class as he goes.

Meyer estalishes no clear curriculum. He does not follow the course book. He teaches what what he wants. He does not follow the course description. Professor Meyer doesnt put much effort into teaching the course from the textbook. His strategy of teaching with a textbook is random and jumps around topics. David is one of the smartest teachers I have ever had. With that being said, he did not care about our class.
