He reads off the powerpoint slides, but takes attendance every class. Sits in back during presentations w/ pics of students & docs participation points if he sees you on your phone or not paying attention.

I love Don! He clearly loves what he does and is very knowledgeable. Lectures got long, but so does any lecture that's 75 minutes. If you study the book vocab, put in effort for the two group projects, show up to class and pay attention to the main ideas you'll do well.

Don is one of the BEST professors at Mizzou.  I've taken multiple classes w him and have enjoyed every one. He's extremely helpful, funny, and really wants all of his students to succeed. He does take attendance every lecture so missing class isn't really an option but he makes it fun. Tests are easy as long as you study the slides he puts on BB!

Don is very helpful and cares about the development of the student. I utilized his office hours and I saw my test scores improve by a couple points each time. He also will really help out your group during the group projects as long as you take advantage of his availability.

Really enjoyed class with Don Meyer. He is so laid back and understanding, and truly wants to get to know his students. We had multiple projects throughout this course and he would go out of his way to e-mail his students his advice and feedback without us asking. Class was interesting and exams weren't bad as long as you go to class!

Donald Meyer AKA Don, is one of the best teachers I've had. I think that he only teaches Retail Marketing 4250 at Mizzou but he does it well and he loves his job. He is so interested in his students and is one of the most understanding guys I've met. Take his class. It's fun and brings the best out of people.

This class is not what it claims to be. “Learning, Teaching, and Curriculum” doesn't match the content at all. Instead of learning about teaching or curriculum, we spent 15 weeks talking about identity. It was required, or I would've dropped it. Easy A, but misleading—this class should be renamed DEI.

Dr. Alonzo is passionate about education and cares about all her students. The material is pretty easy and she's good at explaining it. You're assigned a group of 3-4 people at the beginning of the year and you do three group presentations with them but they're not very hard if you split up the work evenly. Attendance is mandatory so go to class
Dr. Yoon is a very kind and understanding professor. The lectures aren't always the most interesting, but his humor helps make it bearable. He also prepares the students very well for exams. 10/10

I really enjoy Dr. Yoon. He is a very considerate professor with a true passion for teaching. The lectures are a bit lengthy when online because it's a 2 1/2 hour long course. However, he does a great job preparing you for the exams. Exams are open note and he provides a lot of assistance. Very understanding and enjoyable. I suggest Dr. Yoon.

You will succeed by adopting a self pace method. All info needed for tests are on his powerpoints (recorded & uploaded lectures to canvas). Very helpful & easy to reach out via email. He is very nice and gives study guides for tests. Tests are open note and you have a couple of days to complete the tests. Grades come from Group Projects & Tests.

Dr. Yoon was one of my favorite professors at Mizzou! He's nice and funny. He doesn't give a ton of work. He also wants you to learn the material. The tests are easy because he gives a study guide with the answers on them. He's a fair grader. He takes attendance, but it wasn't factored into our final grade. He lectures a lot, but they're on Canvas.
Yoon is an incredibly smart person. Always willing to help. He is very passionate! However, use your cohort as a reference, because it helps to process with other people.

I really like Yoon's class but at times it can be a bit boring. It is a really easy class as far as assignments go with only a few tests and projects. Attendance is not mandantory and the textbook is not needed. If you don't understand something, ask him! He is such a nice guy and is extremely smart. He is always willing to help!
Reads directly off the powerpoint without giving any explanation for what he's reading. Lots of group assignments.
Expect to do a fair amount of work, but the time in class is fun. She gives great feedback on every assignment.

I just don't get why her rating is so low. She is very friendly, and by far the most honest professor I had when it comes to expectations over the assignments. The only problem I had with her was reaching her outside of class because for some reason she doesn't check her email at all. But even so, she gave me lots of career advice and support!

She was very clear about class expectations and always made sure we knew how to contact her for questions. Timely responses too! She is VERY big on participation, so not the best class if you're quiet. Just go to class and do the work and you'll get an A!
1200 is a discussion class and Donna is a good leader of discussions. Very easy class and she makes it pretty easy. Lots of feedback on everything.

Professor Kosztin might be one of the best professors I have ever had. Her lectures are amazing, everything is super organized and well planned, and she gives lots of practice problems for exams. This was probably my best experience with a class in a lecture hall because of how well organized she is.

Super easy teacher. Had lots of great illustrations in lecture. She went through notes fast but uploaded her notes so you could download and print off the lecture notes with the illustrations. Tests were exactly like the practice exams. Discussion was actually helpful. Also uploads her lectures so you can watch it if you missed it.

My favorite part of the class is that the grades are weighted: 30% homework, 30% labs, 30% exams, 10% quizzes. You have 5 try's on each homework question, exams are open book, labs are straight forward and easy to complete. There is also no exams worth huge % of your grade. I would highly recommend to anyone looking for online physics.

I am so glad I took this class over the summer. There was so much that I had to learn and I'm glad that I had time to just focus on physics. Everything for this class was online and there was a lot to do per week, but I liked the number of questions we had to do because it helped me learn and be prepared for the exams.

I wish I would've taken this professor during an in-person class instead of an eight-week online course. I feel like she is a great professor but because of the hurried manner of the online course, I didn't get a great feel for her. I will say, the course is organized and structured and she goes above and beyond to help her students.

This is a time consuming class, but definitely way better than the other physics courses in person. The homework takes forever, but you eventually get the hang of it. This class has a ton of assignments due every week but you get more than one chance on quizzes, homework problems and even the tests. It is easy to do well but have to put the time in

I took 2760 as a distance student but Kosztin is a great professor. Her lecture videos are helpful (but I watch them faster than 1x because she talks a little slow). The setup of the class is easy follow. Just know, if you get behind it will be very hard to catch up.

Dr. Kosztin is fantastic. Her lectures are short and to the point. She is very nice and will answer any questions you may have. She gives thorough feedback on the labs. There was a quiz, homework, and lab due almost every week. There were 7 exams, each usually about 4 questions.

I have never disliked a professor before, and Atuhura is very kind, passionate and generous, but she is not a good lecturer. She jumps from topic to topic so quickly that I can't follow her at all. Incredibly unclear in her expectations. Also if she learns your name be ready to be cold called on every single day. No joke, all the time.

She offered to take everyone in my class out to lunch and I was the only one who took her up on the offer. She paid for my meal, asked about my mental health (the day after election day), and asked if I had any questions about my assignments. She cares a lot about her students in and out of class.

Dr. Atuhura is very considerate; she is always approachable and understanding regarding outside circumstances. Unfortunately, this class was based on participation, something that Dr. Atuhura struggled to incentivize. Maybe a different group would have been able to create better discussion.

While she may call on you randomly, she is a very easy professor to communicate with and you know what is expected of you when you join the class. she repeatedly asks if anything can be changed with the class and the way it is ran, she also poses great discussions.

Attendance is taken daily. While the assignments are necessarily difficult (content-wise), professor Atuhura lacks personal communication skills. Students often feel uncomfortable in her classroom as her tone is very demeaning especially if you do not answer the question asked in the exact way she wants it answered. I rarely dislike professors.

My grievances: she proves formulas then expects us to apply them with no examples, which is not teaching. She made mistakes nearly every lesson and excused it by claiming it was intentional. This cost me exam points. She also wastes 10–15 minutes setting up and runs over every class. Not a good professor.

didnt lecture until the end of the semester, used borrowed notes, we did super long homework for hours, and exam averages were really low. she was nice, gave some extra credit, but if she'd lecture from the start, it would've helped a lot. nice person, VERY tough class. might be good in calc 1-3, but def wouldnt recommend for differential equations

- weekly if not more hw assignments that take 4+ hrs each
- difficult exams with low averages
- in class notes do not prepare you
- lecture style consists of group work and then students presenting the work on the board (dont take if you like actual lectures). After answer was provided we would just move on
- final project on top of final exam

Dr. Ghoreishi is an amazing professor. She truly cares about her students. We were offered over 30 points of extra credit throughout the semester. She cares more about the students actually learning the material than the grades received on exams. Go to her office hours if you're feeling lost!! She is incredibly kind and caring.

I took calc 3 last semester with Dorsa. She was an amazing teacher, caring, tough and inspirational. I always looked at math as course I have to memorize the formulas and pass but after I took calculus with Dorsa, I got a totally different concept from a math class. I loved her classes! if you every get a chance, take a course with her.

I took calculus 3 with Ms. Dorsa. She is by far the best math teacher I have had in college. The class is hard but she makes it so easy to understand. She loves math and it projects on her lectures. I was lucky to have her for Calc 3!!

Somehow makes a 3 credit hour class take more time to complete all of the work and study effectively for than the 5 credit hour and comparatively harder calculus 2 class before it. Does not explain everything you will need during class, so be ready to teach some material to yourself. Also gives the most useless "group work study guide" ever.

Dorsa is a great teacher. She has a good understanding of the material and explains to us both the mathematical, formulaic components of what we were learning along with the three-dimensional, applicable part of the course. Slides are always good to have for studying outside of class. If you get a chance, take Calc 3 with her.

This class was very easy. Make sure to attend lectures because he doesn't post his slides. Lectures and assignments are easy. Make sure to read the books. Tests are easy and online. Dr. Hurt is constantly telling dad jokes. An easy A.

Dr. Hurt is one of the best professors I have had. He makes you well aware of what is expected very early on. Lectures are important for tests, but they are entertaining. I would take any of his courses if you have space for an elective.

Dr. Hurt is just so amazing with us the students. This is one of my favorite classes of the semester because he is very engaging with students, has a lot of dad jokes about geography that will make you laugh, and he gives a lot of extra credits. You do need textbooks but those are short novels to read, I will pick his class again if I could

Dr. Hurt was an engaging teacher. The honors component was tied to the TA led discussions, so the quality varies by TA. The lectures are not honors. Notes are not posted on canvas, but that doesn't matter much because he is very easy to follow. Course content seemed to just be whatever he wanted, but it was interesting. Good class for an easy Gened

Geography 1100H was 2 lectures + discussion with TAs leading the discussion section. Because of that, my only interactions with Dr. Hurt were during lecture classes, which were very funny. The tests are online and outside of class, with test material coming directly from lecture and the different books we were required to read.
Immensely enjoyed having Dr. Hurt as a professor. He makes geography interesting and fun, something I didn't think was possible.

You'll do good on the exams by taking notes in class and just reading the books. Make sure you stay on track with the reading goals the TA's give you, it's hard to keep up once you fall behind. Other than that Dr. Hurt was great and his lectures were always entertaining.

For GEOG 1100 you have a lecture section and a discussion section run by a TA. His lectures are a little boring but easy to follow and have lots of dad jokes. There are three open note exams throughout the semester. I skimmed the books for the answers (all book questions are on canvas). Easy credit -go to lecture bc he gives out extra credit here
I love Doug. He is so helpful. Really makes you understand what you are learning is willing to help you as long as you participate and be active in his class.

Available before and after class and by appointment. He cares about each student and takes the time to get to know you. He is good at reading students faces and knows when to slow down or keep going and is always encouraging students to question him and the material. He is a phenomenal teacher and a great role model for future teachers!

Doug was fair grading, funny, and a great teacher. He simplified material so it was easy to understand. Before every exam, he would have a review session where he stayed for over two hours helping all his students personally. If you have the option to take Doug, take him!

I am not a science person, so I was intimidated coming into this class. However, Doug was always available to help whenever we needed it. We had a small class so he constantly took our feedback of when to have our tests. He makes the class fun and loves to make dad jokes. Even if you don't know the answer, give it a try because he loves that.

I had Chandrasekhar for this class, & she was awful, unavailable, and gave no direction on what to study for tests, quizzes, and the final. Doug was there the entire way to make sure his class and my class were prepared and knew what to study. He truly cares about the students. I wish so badly I had taken his section. Amazing guy with a big heart.

This has been one of the best classes i have ever taken at Mizzou. Physics is not an easy topic but Doug teaches it in a way that is fun and interesting. He explains everything and is more than willing to help anyone at any time. The class is really fast-paced which is my only complaint but amazing class overall

Doug was one of the best teachers I have had in a while. I am an elementary education student and this was a mandatory class for me. He let me take quizzes in advance if I knew I couldn't make it to class, he let one girl be exempt from her work because of family issues and he is funny. He is an all around good guy and we all respect him.
I love Doug. He is so helpful. Really makes you understand what you are learning is willing to help you as long as you participate and be active in his class.

Available before and after class and by appointment. He cares about each student and takes the time to get to know you. He is good at reading students faces and knows when to slow down or keep going and is always encouraging students to question him and the material. He is a phenomenal teacher and a great role model for future teachers!

Doug was fair grading, funny, and a great teacher. He simplified material so it was easy to understand. Before every exam, he would have a review session where he stayed for over two hours helping all his students personally. If you have the option to take Doug, take him!

I am not a science person, so I was intimidated coming into this class. However, Doug was always available to help whenever we needed it. We had a small class so he constantly took our feedback of when to have our tests. He makes the class fun and loves to make dad jokes. Even if you don't know the answer, give it a try because he loves that.

I had Chandrasekhar for this class, & she was awful, unavailable, and gave no direction on what to study for tests, quizzes, and the final. Doug was there the entire way to make sure his class and my class were prepared and knew what to study. He truly cares about the students. I wish so badly I had taken his section. Amazing guy with a big heart.

This has been one of the best classes i have ever taken at Mizzou. Physics is not an easy topic but Doug teaches it in a way that is fun and interesting. He explains everything and is more than willing to help anyone at any time. The class is really fast-paced which is my only complaint but amazing class overall

Doug was one of the best teachers I have had in a while. I am an elementary education student and this was a mandatory class for me. He let me take quizzes in advance if I knew I couldn't make it to class, he let one girl be exempt from her work because of family issues and he is funny. He is an all around good guy and we all respect him.

Love this guy. Very helpful outside of class and genuinely wants to see his students succeed. You don't even need to go to every class just make sure to review his content on Canvas before the exam. I would do it all the night before and I was just fine. One of the best professors at Mizzou hands down.

Dr. Rudy is great! Lectures were exactly what you needed to know for exams. Class was in-person, but you had the option to complete the entire course online with the exception of tests. Tests were extremely easy and almost always curved so you got extra points. Extremely nice and understanding professor.
I took HDFS 2300, and the lectures were easy to understand, and tests were a little hard, so be ready to stud,y but otherwise he is a super sweet professor who genuinely cares about his students.
Super easy class. Would recommend taking this class if possible.

He was good so long as his attendance remains to be not required because he is really bad at lecturing. He talks slow, quiet, dull, and stutters between most of his words. There are at least 4 assignments worth 3 points or less due/week. Everything except "Term Tests" (exams) are online which is nice, and the class content was interesting at least.

He is so kind and cares to teach the information. He uploads all of his lectures for the week so you can either attend class or do it online. I preferred doing both in case he added anything in person. All together, very sweet professor and absolutely would take again.

Dr. Rudy was great. I took the class in person but only went to class for the tests. I did watch every lecture posted, which is why I secured the grade I did. Not a huge time commitment, and it's pretty interesting information. Study your notes for the tests and you will have no problem!

You can tell how much Professor Rudy truly cares about the information he is teaching; class can be done fully online. He is a lovely man who works with students to ensure they understand class lectures and expectations. I would recommend this class to anyone due to the versatile subjectmatter and content!!!
Cares a lot and breaks it down well setting you up for future math classes
Just an amazing prof. Enough said.

Dr. Belt is an amazing professor. The practice tests were very similar to the actual tests and were super helpful. He also allows for a notecard with notes on all the exams. He's responsive to emails and has even sent me a video in response to a question I had.

Dr. Belt is definitely a professor that you want to have for all of your calculus classes.  I have had him for Calc 1, 2, and 3, and it was definitely worth it.  You can tell he loves what he does based off how well he teaches calculus. He is the GOAT

Do the practice tests and you're good. Discussions and iClicker questions will be on the test. The tests are like 70% of your overall grade. He is a really good teacher if you pay attention and go to the classes. If you miss a few, then you will have some trouble catching back up. He teaches the content very quickly.
Honestly one of the best teachers I've had. He has a very dry sense of humor but it comes out really funny. Always willing to help, and grades very fairly.
One of the best math professors I have had to teach this course. Highly recommend.

I am writing this review after taking Calc 2 and Calc 3. Professor Belt used so much visualizations in his lectures and it took me 2 semesters to realize how good I had it. Professor Belt is my best professor thus far

Dzhambul is personable, sharp-witted, and knowledgable. It is easy to follow his intuitive coursework and class direction over a term. He is on-time and prepared, respectful and patient, and knows how to reign in the class to bridge individual and collective learning. I would say he excels in fostering a conducive learning environment. Just show up

One of the best professors I've personally ever had! Jambul cares so much about his students and genuinely wants them to succeed. By the end of just one semester you'll be able to speak basic Russian. Mizzou is so lucky to have Jambul. Take his class!

He is an amazing professor. I am seriously considering pursuing a Russian minor based on the sole fact that he is the teacher. The more you get to know him, the better class will be. He makes Russian fun to learn, even if there is a good amount of homework. The tests can be quite tough if you don't do the homework, so keep up and ask questions!
Amazing instructor!!! Would 100% take the course again!

He is very nice and genuinely cares about his students. Tries to make learning Russian fun with videos, activities, and jokes. There is a lot of homework, but it's understandable for a language class. Be mindful that he does tend to cold-call on people, which can be daunting, but if you studied and are prepared, it is not bad. Overall a great time

Jambul is a fantastic professor, one of the best I've ever had. He genuinely reignited my desire to learn and inspired me to pursue a Russian degree. He is an asset to Mizzou, and his presence at Mizzou raises its quality as a learning institution.
Jambul is the best professor that I've had at Mizzou. I cannot say enough great things about him and his classes.
He is our prophet, our priest, our king. Joseph Smith was not one tenth the revelator he is. His teaching is like unto the discovery of a third tablet at Sinai.

I took Spanish 2100 and the class was heavily guided by the online textbook/assignments. Regardless, I enjoyed lectures by Professor Medina. He is very clear over what material will be tested, with tests on paper and in-person. Attendance is taken at the beginning of each class, and there are makeup assignments when you do miss class.

I hate the Mizzou Spanish department, but Eduardo is the best teacher Ive had. The class is tough, exams are hard, but that is the coordinator. Eduardo is definitely a confusing teacher but he is hilarious and does want you to succeed. My favorite memories were him talking bad on the department. If you do have to take SPAN2100, he makes it bearable

Professor Rodriguez truly cares about his students success and wellbeing and will help you as much as you need. You can tell he loves the Spanish language and is passionate about teaching. Very fair grading and a very understanding person all around. Highly recommend his classes.

GO TO CLASS! If five people are missing from the class, there's a pop-quiz (20% of your overall grade). Overall, Medina is an amazing professor when it comes to explaining concepts + structures extremely well. He isn't super cheerful and clearly hates being in Missouri 24/7 but he's honestly hilarious about it.

Prof. Rodriguez is a fantastic professor who cares deeply for his students and does his very best to ensure they truly learn the language (his native tongue, but you'd never know his English is better than mine). The syllabus for 1100 requires attendance so he kinda strict on that front & there's lots of hw, but I'd ultimately recommend him.
Dr. Avery is great! She's very approachable during office hours, even for an online class. She's so cool I want to be her when I grow up.

I'm writing this to hopefully warn some people about SOCIOL3000. It's an engaged learning course and the entire class is a group project. This would be fine but the prof is extremely disorganized and expects students to have extensive background knowledge. She also got extremely defensive (almost hostile) when concerns about the class were raised.

She is an amazing professor! I took the course online, there was 1-2 video lectures each week and a discussion. There was two exams over the lecture content and a couple of easy projects. The course was organized and very clear about the expectations. She always worked with me if I had any problems, it is obvious that she cares about her students.

Easiest class. She gives you 2 weeks to do hardly any work, and the material is so simple, you definitely already know it. Occasionally, one week you'll get two 20-min lectures that you can watch on double speed and knock out assignments real fast. Dr. Avery doesn't do much for the class at all. This class is a joke.

Criminology is a fun and easy class. If youre interested in the topic and need an easy A, this is the class for you. Tests make up the majority of your grade, but if you know the lecture then they are the easiest tests ever. Only 10 attendances are accounted for, but they are crucial. She doesnt seem very confident in her teaching or material.

She is a very boring lecturer. She does not use a mic and does not project her voice. Very disorganized in speaking and thought. I think her exams were all very poorly worded and written. It was required to do volunteering service hours, which was rewarding, but she had no idea what was going on with that for the entire semester.
elaine was always very kind to me and knowledgeable about everything we talked about during class. she was especially helpful when it came to the cardiac lectures!!
The rudest professor at Mizzou. Be ready for her to make fun of you and criticize your character for minimal mistakes.

Calc II is very challenging, but she moves too fast and is hard to reach for help. She skips key details yet focuses on less important ones, which makes topics more confusing. She often pauses class for minor noises or side conversations. Homework is extremely difficult, leaving students more lost than helped

Calculus 2 is a very difficult class, no matter the professor. Elena has done her best to teach us what she has learned in her time at college. Given that, the averages were very low, and the class was weighted very fairly. I would see if another professor is open before signing up, but she is very knowledgeable in her field. The exams are not easy
Lectures are not good. Does not explain stuff in class at all. Very inconsistent with new material. Does not use a mic in lecture.

Not a good professor, also says that we're all doing bad and not learning because of “the acoustics in the room”. 
Seems like a nice person I guess but not a good professor.
I like this professor.

Frequently lectures will derail into lengthy proofs, but fear not because she makes the tests relatively easy for the variety of content covered. Test reviews are close to identical to the exams themselves, if you cover those problems and are well versed with them you will have literally zero difficulty getting triple digit scores.
She makes a lot of mistakes and goes into pointless textbook stuff, but she curves hard, so it's not that bad. Lectures aren't that useful, definitely attend recitations though.

I found her to be a very caring professor. She was always ready to help students after class and during office hours. Im not even a math or engineering major and did just fine; test curves are generous, and if you complete and understand the reviews (which are just harder versions of the test), you're golden. I promise, the class is not that scary.

Eliot is so freaking nice! You can tell that he really wants his students to succeed. He is always willing to slow down and cater to his audience. Make sure to do your homework!! Also, don't stress about attendance if you miss a day; he usually forgets to record it.

I liked Eliot because he made math fun. He lectures kind of fast but you just have to let him know and he'll slow down. He asked for input a lot and tailored a lot of lectures to what we needed. There's quizzes every Friday but that's for every math1100 class but he'll usually tell you what questions will be on it or what to study.

Dr. Glick is phenomenal. She is so helpful when approached with questions and she truly cares about her students, which isnt common at a university. She offers a ton of extra credit and goes out of her way to ensure that her students succeed. :)
She's a difficult grader and will take off one or two points on every assignment without explanation.

Phenomenal professor. Her gender freedom class was my favorite class ever. Unfortunately, it had to all be done online this semester due to the pandemic, but Dr. Glick made it as accessible and easy as she possibly could. Her lectures were very engaging and she facilitated class discussion so well. Would definitely recommend her class!

Glick is a very nice professor, but if you don't agree with her, say what she wants you to say, or interpret the text in her way, then you WILL lose points. Her grading criteria is shoddy and she lets her personal opinions get in the way a lot. She does seem to care about the topics, but it isn't worth the exchange when it's her way or the highway.

She was constantly taking off points if I wouldn't say exactly what she wanted to hear in the discussions. It was seriously every week she would find something new to count off for. You will have to read a lot of various articles, books, and watch different videos. Not that hard of a class, she's just extremely picky.

Dr. Glick really knows her stuff, which is admirable, but there is seriously so much reading. It's a little ridiculous for an entry class into gender studies. Also, she can make you feel a little dumb, not on purpose, but just because of the looks she sometimes gives and how much she knows about the subject. It made me not want to participate.

Love this professor! Totally devoted to literature, well versed in the field, and is super compassionate about both the subjects she teaches and her students. Discussions are a blast, and welcoming for everyone to join in and speak up. Class was so fun that we arranged an after-semester get together for pizza to chat and say our farewells.

Dr. Glick was knowledgeable in LGBT+ issues but lacked in other areas. Papers were graded inconsistently and not returned in a timely manner. The final had topics that were never discussed in class. While she claimed the classroom was a safe space, I often found her judgmental to people who may not have been aware of every LGBT+ term.

I loved Ms. Broaddus, this is an easy class and she understands that not everybody is going to major in English, she completely understands if you need an extension and will grant one to you on any papers. Attendance isn't necessarily mandatory, but she does take it into account at the end of the semester.
Right off the bat she had a great vibe. She is very understanding and accepts late work. You can tell she really cares for all of her students.
One of the most sweet and caring TAs I've ever had, and is sooo understanding.

I had Ms. Broaddus in a small, honors class, so we had discussions every time we met, and she did a great job asking stimulating, challenging, thought-provoking questions about the piece of literature we were studying. For each essay, we turn in a first draft, do peer review, and that helps our final draft be much stronger.

Besides being so obviously knowledgeable about literature, Ms. Broaddus has an incredible sense of style and her wit, humor, and graceful bearing are all difficult to ignore.  A great instructor whom I highly recommend!  She is challenging but so remarkable and kind that you really don't mind it!

I took Mme Ramey's French 1100 and 1200 classes and REALLY enjoyed them!You learn so much with her and she's also funny, helpful,and sweet! She makes jokes and gives you some french culture info and really makes the class more than just learning the language. She's also extremely helpful when you go to her office hours& she cares about her students

Since she's a TA she is operating under guidelines from a co-ordinator. She's energetic and clearly loves what she teaches. She is approachable and willing to help. I think she provided a great foundation for me going on into higher levels. I highly recommend her! Just pay attention and participate!!
She is nice and fun but assumes her students know more than they do in an intro class
Very fun,cool and helpful.  Make sure you pay attention and don't be afraid to ask questions!
Mme Ramey is an excellent teacher! If you go to her office hours she will be a much easier grader on your tests/quizzes/essays. She's also a lot of fun!
Great prof. She is down to earth and knowledgeable. Lectures aren't required to attend, but sometimes she gives you extra credit for attending.

She does a great job at setting personal boundaries and delivering feedback in a way that isn't soul-crushing. Her critiques are harsh, no doubt about it, but she's preparing you for on camera work, with a much larger audience ready to aim and fire away at your skills. She's endearingly awkward in class but very sweet outside of it! Good advice.

Frogge is really helpful and understanding. The technology in the lab is awful, but if you're taking B2, you probably figured that out in B1. If you're late to lecture she won't let you take the daily quizzes, which are 20 % of your grade. She is the worst professor i've ever had. Very unprofessional in manner she speaks to students. Very condescending. Doesn't give positive feedback, she gaslights students into thinking that she can teach but they cant learn. Grading is unfair and leaves no room for error.

This professor will make you regret even asking for help. She'd rather insult your intelligence than actually do her job as a teacher and help.Her class is nothing but busy work. Dont bother asking for help if you havent watched every second of her lectures because she'd rather waste her time yelling at you than helping.

This is one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Over 4 hours of mandatory lectures a week to watch. Most assignments were 5-7 page papers, single-spaced, and worth 48 points max. Spending 8+ hours on a paper worth so little is such a slap in the face that it shows the professor clearly doesn't value her student's time. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
never again. no clue how I got a good grade because it was so hard and so horrible. 0/10

This class is a nightmare, the professor is unhelpful and if you ask for help she will belittle you. I spent an hour and a half in a zoom call where she spent the entire time making me feel like a bad student. I would recommend literally any other professor for this class before I would recommend her.

Dannecker is the least helpful professor I've ever had throughout my time here. The Canvas page is quite literally unreadable and the most unorganized thing I've ever dealt with. She grades the toughest I've ever seen and gives the most confusing instructions. Lectures consist of about 10 40 minute videos a week, where nothing is explained at all.

Canvas page is a mess, lectures are long and she speaks very slowly, if you ask for help she will point you to her lectures where it will give you little to no info, just irritating person/class overall and so much more. I don't write reviews on professors but don't take this class if you want to have a good semester.
Easiest prof ever only four real grades but if you try she will give you an A
I absolutely loved her. I recommended her to all of my friends. Truly one of the most caring and best professors I have ever had
She is amazing

She is really sweet and caring! While you do get some attendance points, it does not impact your grade significantly. She literally said that if you're sick, DO NOT COME, so she cares way more about your well-being than you attending class. If she taught other classes here, I would take them again, every time.
Amazing Teacher

This class was honestly so easy if you just wrote the papers. She would give our class extra credit for just showing proof you submitted your paper to the writing center. It was super easy, definitely recommend it for an easy A.

Erin is so amazing and you can tell she genuinely cares about each student. There is no homework and you only write 4 easy papers throughout the semester. This was my easiest class and I never felt stressed about it. She also loves her cats so be prepared to see many pictures of them.
Honestly a great and easy English 1,000 teacher. She shows that she cares and understands sometimes if you aren't able to make it to class if you email her ahead of time.

This professor truly cares about her student's success in and out of the classroom. She went out of her way to help students understand coding and the coursework material. She is the gem of the Statistics department. She follows the textbook closely in her lecture material. Encourages collaboration.

Gives great lectures. Makes students responsible for their learning and is readily available to help if you pay attention and comment in class. Also brings in material specific to each student outside of the class to apply material to. Very good course for developing working skills.

Erin is pretty knowledgeable. For this class she seemed to follow the book for her lecture formats, but she also explained things well. The tests are hard but she is very accessible for extra help, and friendly too as long as you show you're willing to work to figure stuff out. A favorite teacher of mine.

Dr. Holmes is caring and understanding, but she took incredibly long to grade and occasionally class was cancelled because the homework was never uploaded. I was unsure of my standing in the class due to the lateness, thankfully she didn't grade harshly. Despite that, she facilitated really interesting discussions and it was a really fun class.

Her lectures are good and you NEED to go because wile the slides are posted they often have no words on them. Her biggest issues was how LONG it took to get grades back.
Honors: write 2 papers on people from class and 2 papers from lectures given by people at Jesse. Then revise 1 from each section. 2-3 pages, very easy.

Professor Holmes is a great person and great lecturer. While it took her a while to get grades back sometimes, she was very fair in her grading and offers a ton of opportunities to earn an A in the class. The best 1100 professor I have known at Mizzou.

I have had this professor twice and loved her so much. She is my favorite history professor and ensures students can work with their emotional health while maintaining an education. If you struggle in her classes, most likely you don't understand how history works or how to survive college. Maybe you should return to reading Magic Tree House books.

I love Dr. Holmes. She is my favorite professor ever, she is relatable, understanding, cool, honest, funny, and one of the most brilliant people that I have ever met. When I grow up, I want to be like her. There is never a dull moment in her class. Her classes are as easy as you want them to be, if you show up and do the work you will get an A.
wonderful professor, seriously so understanding about personal life issues and stress. educational and great topics in classes

This lady never grades anything the semester is about to be over and I have 0 grades in grade book. She is extremely late on posting material and I would not recommend this class unless you want your grade to be NA the whole semester.

She is a great person. Genuinely cares about mental health, wants to talk during office hours, passionate. She can rapid fire explain something, but if you're not paying close attention it sometimes goes through one ear and out the other. If you like history and understand it fairly well, she would be great for you. If not, discussion helps a lot.

Very passionate about the subject and wants to help students in their future careers as much as possible. Makes an effort to get to know every student and is very willing to give whatever help is needed, and adjusts the course as the semester goes on to fit the pace of class and not feel rushed. Has a lot of knowledge to share.

Does not actually teach how to work through problems. Instead, she teaches the broad concepts and how they pertain to psychology, will maybe go through one problem, and expects you to figure the rest out yourself. She also used the same example problem for almost every single concept, and often makes rude or insensitive comments.

The most unorganized professor I have ever seen in my entire college career. I could of done a better job. I would schedule meetings with her and she would forget. I registered, enrolled, and paid for an in person class. Class was supposed to be in person but we never met in person not once. The TA did all of the grading, she never graded anything

Etti is a nice professor who cares about her students' wellbeing, but this class is a mess. Easy A if you show up & turn in work, but the most unorganized class I have ever taken. Due dates are posted wrong or not posted at all. Instructions are unclear, especially for final project. Much time wasted talking in circles and irrelevant guest speakers

This is the MOST disorganized class I have ever been in. It's not even close, it's actually shocking how disorganized it is. Canvas was not up till halfway through the semester, and all the due dates were wrong and were never changed. If you want to email her for anything, 9/10 times she will not answer.

I did not think that Etti was that great of a teacher. The canvas site was put up late and was never updated with due dates. I had no idea what I was supposed to be doing during my group presentation because there were never any guidelines sent out about the project. She also picked movies that were old and somewhat outdated. I would not recommend.

Etti is an incredible human being who genuinely cares about increasing cross-cultural awareness for her students. Attendance is mandatory--even when you think she does not count attendance, she does! My main complaint is she's extremely disorganized so you never know when due dates are or where you stand in the class.

Etti is a wonderful woman that is caring and respectful to everyone. As long as you show up and do your work (which is minimal) this class is an easy A and is pretty fun when not discussing sensitive subjects. That being said, she is very disorganized and due dates/instructions are not always clear.

Etti is sweet, but there are issues. She graded all assignments of the semester the weekend after finals, and gave me the same score on everything - clearly she didn't actually read any of my homework. There are no rubrics or clear schedules for the class. It's an easy class but if you need organization - not the class for you.

Etti is hands down the best professor I have ever had. I cried when her class ended. She cares about her students more than any professor at any university and works with you so you can get the best possible grade in her class. Her class isn't on canvas, so being in class is important. She gives you dates and lots of time for assignments.
Amazing professor with engaging lectures. Makes it very easy to learn Korean even as a complete beginner.
Take korean!!!!!!
Eunyoung is the best professor I've had. She's kind, funny and amazing at teaching. I feel like I've learned so much thanks to her.
She's literally so amazing and a great professor!

Professor Choi is an awesome professor. Do not miss the opportunity to take this class! She helps everyone succeed, is kind, caring, and very funny. I love her class. She makes sure goals are achievable, and you are having a good time while feeling like you're learning. She knows what she's doing, great professor.
I wouldnt want anyone else teaching me Korean!
She is so kind and very caring. I had her spring 2020 and Fall 2020 and she was so flexible. Really great teacher

She was the most caring and sweet professor I've ever had. I ended the class with a 99.5%, that's how easy and simple it is. She grades you on content but also effort. Gave great feedback on my assignments and how I could improve. There are no exams, but 3 papers that are pretty enjoyable. Weekly quizzes and discussion boards tho.

The kindest, most lovely professor ever. This was her first year teaching and she was fabulous. She sets clear standards and I can actually say I have learned a lot. She is so kind and compassionate and makes you feel like she genuinely cares about you, even though it was an online course. The class does take work but it is easy if you just do it.
Avoid her at all costs.

Harsh grader, very dense course load but was self-paced. A LOT of required readings and media to watch, very dense but few assignments, all papers and a proctored final that the study guide did not adequately prepare us for. Took the class with a friend and we both agreed this is not a 2000 level course, we have had easier 4000 level courses.
This was a paper-heavy class, with not very many assignments, but they weren't too difficult, and there were no outside readings, only short lectures. Content was interesting

Her feedback is inconsistent, unclear and often downright rude and unprofessional. She should consider professional development and interpersonal skills before continuing online classes. I would skip this professor, because you will get an A one day and a D the next, and she will provide no valuable feedback as to why she gives the grades she gives

She didn't start grading the homework until week 4. It was then she said my work was "trying too hard" and I was "acting smart". She told me to answer like I'm telling a child. When I did, my grades came back still failing with her saying it was "too basic". Does not answer questions in emails. Super biased and condescending. She should not teach.

Probably one of the worst professors I've ever had. The class is based off of reading articles and writing weekly assignments that would've been a lot easier if she would've offered better help instead of telling you you're wrong without stating why. Also very rude on multiple occasions and never felt comfortable enough to ask for help.
So basically the worst professor I have ever had. Very rude. Very inconsiderate. Gave terrible feedback whenever I tried to do better. Nothing you say will be correct to her!

Unorganized class. Can be disrespectful to students. Not much instruction was given at the beginning of the course except for the syllabus. Will take off points on major assignments without giving feedback. The course itself was very bias. When asking a question, isn't helpful but then will later grade harshly even though she didn't help to begin

I would have loved this class- with a better professor. Her lectures are disjointed and hard to follow, but you'll still have to show up because she gives randomized quizzes. Her assignments are unclear and she can be rude sometimes. People told me to switch out of her section before I took the class, and I didn't listen, which I now regret.

She expects you to read a lot, but most WGST classes do. She gives pop quizzes that are either attendance based, group work, or individual. She does not do powerpoints, so you have to consistently pay attention to get notes. Her homework is based off the notes you take in class.

Super intelligent and insightful, but unfortunately tends to be unorganized sometimes, making note-taking a challenge. Her energetic, welcoming personality and passion for the topics made the class worth taking nonetheless. She puts a ton of emphasis on class participation, and sometimes does pop quizzes, so attendance is crucial.
She has no idea how to teach a class. She is way too lenient I don't even know what the point of that class was.

She's a nice professor, but her lectures are awkward and disorganized. Don't rely on the syllabus. She admits she falls behind on content. We had only one discussion post despite them being listed as weekly, and the exam was all essays, not multiple choice/short answer like it was stated. Few chances to earn points and grading is very slow.

Dr. Rais was an easy grader, who rarely assigned projects; but liked to assign a decent amount of reading.Throughout the entirety of the semester, I never felt like I could challenge any of the statements made, which turned me off. No professor should teach as if all things in the textbook are inherently fact, and she did. Wouldn't take again.

Reading the textbook and being engaged in class is super important to get the most out of class. Professor Rais is incredibly caring and always open to feedback--she always asks students for their feedback so speak up! There are few grades so make sure you put time into her assignments. Class isn't required but she'll respect you if you show up.

She was extremely kind and welcoming but her class lectures were a tad hard to sit through as she was a bit unorganized. In the syllabus she stated there would be assignments every week but we only had 3/4 grades put in by the time she posted the final exam. The slides were not always the m sot helpful. Get the book for the final.

I feel bad because she is really nice and made my class a breeze but HOLY... she rarely assigned stuff and her classes felt so unbelivably optional. If you want an easy class go for it but I wanted to learn way more.

Professor Rais is exceptionally pleasant. Her lectures prove engaging, and she provides ample chances for participation. She is accommodating in various aspects, such as attendance and deadlines. So, I strongly endorse taking her class.
She was a bit hard to listen to throughout lectures, not the most organized and lots of time was spent on figuring out how to work things. Very nice but not paced well.

What he asks for and what he wants aren't always the same. When asked a question, he rarely answers what was asked. His talks are ridiculous: rambles on about semi-related things, is unclear about important concepts, etc.

I did not like his teaching style. He jumps around way too much and is very confusing. He repeats himself a lot saying how he smart and humble he is. These are the only two lines I remember from his class. Did not learn much at all.

he's very nice, smart and humbled. really liked the capstone course. besides, i was considering to apply for mba after a couple of years. i requested a meeting with Dr S and he spent 2 hours helping me with gmat questions. idk any prof other than Dr S who would do that for a student. in short, amazing guy and teacher.

I really loved his course and teaching. I think the person (very clear is the same one from the writing) is talking about someone else. He never talked about him, treats students fairly, cares about students. Exam was hard but his curve was super generous. Nobody I know got below B.
Do not take this professor. He is so unorganized and lost and doesn't tell you what he expects from you. He hasn't taught me much other than about himself. I was so willing to learn.

Too arrogant and isn't very clear or helpful. From his boring lectures, he already expects you to understand all the concepts. Rather than helping, he'll ridicule and chastise you for not knowing. It's hard to tell whether he's using constructive criticism, or just too mean and arrogant.

Professor Felipe is a great teacher who really cares about his students and always finds time to talk when requested. Not a fan of the capstone course because it is more like a finance course? but the prof's attitude and passion to teach is remarkable. Plus, he helped me with case questions for my consulting interview.
Best professor I had at Mizzou. The complaints below are false. How can a prof treat students badly if the classes were pre-recorded?

This is a difficult class but it would be difficult with any professor. In my opinion Dr. Fritschi is a very knowledgable instructor who has great lecture slides and is genuinely interesting to listen to. It will require studying to get an A in his class but the information is valuable and it is possible with class attendance and decent studying.
Save yourself.

The worst professor that I have had at Mizzou. Started the semester by saying in the first class “this class is really boring, I don't really like teaching it”. The most monotone person I have ever heard speak. Took two months a piece to grade the first tests. Didn't grade the quizzes for at least a month as well. Didn't respond to emails.
each persons test is different- different questions for each person. they aren't different orders but different questions. stupid hard

Alvear is one of the best professors I have had during my time at Mizzou. His lectures are entertaining and he makes it easy for his students to succeed in his class. Definitely recommend! Very nice guy.
good
Super nice guy but the final is impossible
She is really sweet and I enjoyed her as a person a lot but her class was ver difficult and hard to follow. It also tended to be boring.
This professor was very big on participation, even for an online class. Makes you work super hard, not a lot of time for other classes.
Very tough grader. Stingey, even on participation, but definitely willing to help on larger projects such as research papers.

One of the best professors I have had at Mizzou, she has high expectations for work- meaning you have to put forth effort. Class was overall easy 7 reading responses and 4 tests. She really knows her stuff, and is helpful if you are confused, she can also be funny. Work load was perfect, just short stories- take her!!

He is a nice guy and an engaging lecturer but often fairly disorganized. His exams are hard but he curves them a lot. He is not super flexible or accommodating to students (especially with late assignments or missing class) and can be kind of a "gotcha" professor at times. He will like you more if you go on the Colorado field trip.

Paco is obviously very knowledgable about all the things he teaches but it makes it hard for him to tell when other people can't understand the subject matter. He is not very well organized and may take a while to respond to communication. He's brilliant, but a very disorganized teacher, he posts the slides but they don't make any sense.

This class was FAR more difficult than I anticipated. Paco is a fun, interesting person but lectures were hard to follow. Tests were unnecessarily difficult and hard to prepare for, but there is a generous curve. I found the lecture skeletal outlines and recorded lectures helped with test prep, and I recommend taking physics before this class.

Paco is a sweet, caring, funny guy. He is very willing to help you if you ask for it. He's passionate about geology. Only thing is he loses his train of thought and it can be hard to follow his lectures. This class is really difficult, so take easier classes when you end up taking it.

Paco is a sweet professor who is very clearly in love with geology and teaching. I oftentimes struggled to follow through with his lectures and had to resort to the online "textbook" that he replaced with the traditional textbook. I do appreciate the notion of wanting to save his students some cash, but the online replacement was subpar at best.

I love Paco for his personality but this class is DIFFICULT. If you are an Environmental Science student who is required to take this course I HIGHLY recommend taking PHYSICS AND SOILS FIRST. You will much better understand a lot of the content. Paco is caring but this class isn't easy & he's not great at lecturing. You will need to study a lot.

If you have not taken physics or calculus yet I would recommend doing so. A lot of the homework and a few exam questions involve math and physics that he expects you to know even though physics isn't a requirement for the course. You can get by without it but you'll likely struggle with the math/physics topics. His office hours are helpful though.
Funny but disorganized. Extremely accessible outside of class and replies quickly to emails.

Dr. Palermo is one of the most understanding professors I've ever had. He cares a lot about his students and the subject he teaches. For this class, he had us sign up to do service work in the community (although this was cut short due to COVID-19) which not only looks good on a resume, but it's fun, too! I can't recommend this class highly enough!

I genuinely enjoyed going to his class even though it was a 9 am. He is kind of hard to understand at times, but the stuff he teaches is interesting. He did very well with switching to online courses because of covid. His review lectures on the day before exams were very helpful & everything from the review was on the exam.

Professor Palermo really cares about his students and the subject that he teaches which makes the class more enjoyable. Some classes he teaches involve a lot of information but if you go to his office hours even once to review I can almost guarantee you'll preform better on exam day.

Very good teacher and has a review class before the exams and he gives you the option to print off the lecture slides for the review class. Bring them to class and take extra notes of what he says! His review slides are everything that is on the test! No need to go to class but recommend going to the review class!

I don't know what all the complaining is about. The lectures last as long as they are supposed to. Some times he even let's us out early. If you don't like spending time in class and/or are expecting a show to keep you entertained in class, don't come to college. I found his lectures interesting. He explained things well. He is a fair grader.
His syllabus is very vague which isn't a good sign. He drags on his lectures and will have you feeling like you have been in there for hours and it's only been 10 minutes.
He is a great teacher.
Worst class ever! he is very inconsistent on grading and his lectures are very long and drag on.

He never seemed very warm or connected to the students. Grading was wildly inconsistent; first few weeks, we got 100s, then we got 70s out of nowhere. I didn't really learn anything in class, and one time we spent the entire class watching this bizarre animated film that didn't seem to connect to anything. Would not recommend this professor.

Talented at what he does, but has an ego problem. In a less than a 10 person class, he didn't learn our names. Even after meeting out of class. The basic lack of respect for students does not foster a welcoming environment. When students are spending sometimes up to 15-20 hours a week creating art for his class, the least he can do is learn names

He's very talented and passionate, but the amount of disorganization in the class makes it frustrating. There is very, very little actual instructional time and he instead uses class time to give extremely rushed and hard to follow adobe tutorials. His canvas modules are insanely cluttered and it's very easy to miss assignments.

The whole class is about creating a full campaign, be prepared to work in a team! Frank is a ton of fun, though I rated a 4/5 because I wish he would slow down on his Adobe tutorials. I also wish the group work was divided more clearly, being the art director is fun but you'll do all the work. Other than that, this class is fun for creatives!
Did not answer emails. During March of 2020 straight up did not contract students from March 15 - April 1 and would not reply to emails.

This class is a portfolio builder. I took it during COVID so it was via Zoom. Frank gave minimal feedback, but when he gives it he will rip your work apart. He doesn't use Canvas, NEVER answers emails, and told us our grades for the first time 12 weeks in. If you want to become a better designer, take this class. He's a great designer, okay prof.
He speeds through lectures which is nice in the sense that you wont be there the full 75 minutes, but hard to copy down all the definitions in time. Tests are medium. Design lab is fun but long.

He's extremely knowledgable, but he seemed more interested in lecturing about random artists instead of teaching us how to design. Plus, the design part of the lab was extremely frustrating: Most of the class didn't know what they were doing, there was only one TA, and there wasn't enough time to finish assignments.
Awesome teacher. Difficult class.

I've had Professor Bereskin for Financial Investments, and he's one of the nicest and most supportive professors at Mizzou. He makes tough finance topics more enjoyable with his jokes and friendly style. He gives great advice, sees the best in his students, and wants everyone to succeed. Exams are hard, so attendance matters if you want to do well!

I took investments with Professor Bereskin last semester. The course was challenging, but he was knowledgeable and passionate about this subject. Great guy, very approachable, and he made class fun and worth going to by looking at real-world topics. If you want a good grade in this course you have to attend every single lecture.

Fried enjoys us students and our discussions were very interesting, but he was a tough grader. Be prepared to write intuitive and thoughtful papers, if you do not, your grade will fall. Fortunately, Fried is willing to provide some guidance if you want to make high grades. Also, be sure to participate in class, your grade will thank you.

The coordinator of the class chose a lot of boring books, but he made them interesting and fun. No busy work and few essays, although he is a tough grader and you have to earn your grade. Participation is a big deal, and simply showing up to class won't cut it. But if you engage and spend time on the assignments, you'll get an A.

Amazing professor. Knowledgeable, cares about his students, grades fairly, and will actually work with you to become a better writer. Participating in class is important, but he makes it comfortable to do so. I would definitely recommend taking any class that he teaches.

Really great guy. Very understanding and supportive of students. The class was a lot of work, but he was very laid back. Willing to work with students on final grades. Encourages a LOT of participation but nothing uncomfortable. A lot of group work. If you're lucky, like i was, you'll have a great group and have a blast.
This was a fun class. Knowing the material is necessary. He is enthusiastic and passionate about what he teaches. I really love his colorful wardrobe.

I absolutely love Fried. He is a great discussion leader and really lets his students decide where the conversation is going. He is all for creative assignments, and does not grade harshly on papers. He's wicked smart and all in all just a cool guy.

Very easy class, however, extremely disappointing. Going into the course this was the most excited I have ever been to take a class, Literature of Baseball, how amazing does that sound. Well, the class isn't exciting at all. Its him talking for an hour. He progressively grades easier and easier throughout the semester. FYI Do the papers don't read

He loves baseball and literature. Nice guy, pretty geeky but he's extremely intelligent. Come to class, read everything assigned (or at least know parts of it) and you'll do fine. There are 10 250 word prompts that are worth 5 points each.

Dr. Yao is a really nice guy and helps out a lot outside of class. I would often email him for homework help at 11pm the night of the due date and he would still respond and help out. Lectures are a bit rough as far as retaining information and this class is lot of just learning by failure, but Dr. Yao is extremely helpful along with his TA Samuel.

I had no experience with coding before this class, and he made it easy to learn. It actually helped me to decide on my track. He answers emails almost right away and is super helpful if you encounter any questions about assignments. Make sure to read assigned readings and pay attention in class, and you're good to go.

I was definitely very hesitant to take this class online, but it turned out well! Dr. Yao is very responsive to emails and I would highly recommend asking him (or the tas) any homework questions you might have! I did not have any programming experience before this class, so I did get the textbook. It was definitely helpful to explain some concepts.

Pretty good class for an online programming course. Didn't have any MATLAB knowledge before taking this class and I did fine. Homework is very important for your grade, he and his TA's both give good feedback if things are incorrect. 3 exams, usually pull questions from the quizzes he gives. Not a bad class, do well on the homework.

For an online set up, this class is very easy to stay motivated. There are multiple lecture videos per week, but each are less than 10 minutes and are very easy to understand. There were only very few times where I was lost on how to do something. Assignments and tests follow what have been taught in lectures. Very nice professor.

This man is so nice and always willing to help you understand the material! The lectures were recorded which was nice. He helped me discover an interest in programming, which I knew nothing about before taking this class.

Was a really nice guy and took the time to make sure you really understand every step of the coding process. He wanted me to succeed and would take as much time out of his schedule to help me when I needed. Tests weren't terribly difficult but not the easiest either.

While the class might've been easier if I had some previous experience in coding, there were very few times I knew what I was actually doing. I constantly felt lost during the class and the explanation he gave as to why things were done this specific way were very minimal. If it weren't for my other classmates I 100% would've failed this class >:(

The class was overall super unorganized and there didn't seem to be a plan most days. Also, since it's a writing class, the grading was pretty subjective. However, it was always a good time, Dr. Baker is a great guy. Super easy class (considering it's a 3000 level chem class).

Funniest professor I have had at Mizzou. The content can be pretty boring, but his humor and enthusiasm makes it bearable. He really knows how to relate to his students and the class was structured with a quiz after each class that was online. Hardest part about this class was the lab, but they are manageable. Highly recommend for your chem minor.

easy grader, but won't respond to emails for a few days. all assignments were given to us at the beginning of the semester with the due dates. he doesn't put grades in often so you might be waiting till the end of the semester for most of them. it was in covid era so we didn't even have class, just a paper due every week. 2 pages max

Quant lab is hard, but the lectures with Baker are super easy. He gives you major hints every class about what questions will be on the test, and as long as you pay attention to those and do the practice problems in the book, you'll do just fine.

Very nice, personable guy who clearly cares about the class and enjoys our time together. His teaching style is mostly just running through problems together as a class. Pretty hard grader and gives out a good amount of work but if you want to learn he's a great professor for it.
Lectures are mainly pointless, but all exams come from the labs. If you go to the labs and make a good binder for the open note and you will be fine.
He is excellent professor.Understandable and caring professor in our university
Great teacher, you'll learn a quite a bit.  And I agree with the positive comments above.
No Comments

Prof. Solbrekken was about as good as a prof can get for teaching a subject I really didn't look forward to!  We did one project in particular that was VERY cool and fun.  Very clear, helpful, and an extra is that he's a really nice guy.
Prof. Solbrekken really cares about his students and is an excellent lecturer.  You can tell that he really likes his job and he works hard at it.  I learned a lot from his class.

He was a nice person, but not the best teacher. Expectations for assignments were unclear. Would skip through the lecture slides and tell us that we can look at them later. Told us we should not email him because he probably won't see it. I left class feeling like I did not learn anything.
Nice guy but terrible class. Everything is based on his opinion and he likes to get mad when people don't respond in class. He has good intentions but not the most convenient class to be in.

My favorite professor I've ever had at my time at Mizzou, he was so passionate about the class and more than willing to learn from students which I thought was so personable and amazing. I was actually so upset when the class was over, after we finished our final he fist bumped or shook hands with every single student- I LOVED HIM

Professor Daryl is the best professor I've had at Trulaske. His classes are not only teachable and able to be applied to real-world situations, but he makes them fun.
