He's really brilliant during discussion and always keeps the material interesting.
Wonderful Professor, very passionate about his subject matter and the success of his students. Very fun class!!

The class content was interesting and fun to learn about but Dr. Carlisle doesnt make it very excited. I honestly thought this class wouldve been so much more fun. Shes a fine professor its just a little boring considering how fun the class could have been.

Dr. Carlisle held only a few (7) live zooms which she didn't take attendance, and the rest were online lectures. The vet school supplied the textbook but you don't really need it. The quizzes are super easy and you can keep taking them until you get 100% as long as its in the window its open. The exams aren't too bad. She cares a lot about the sub

Professor Perez Anzaldo is a great professor. She's one of the best Spanish professors at Mizzou and I would recommend any who is taking a Spanish class to take one of her classes. Most of the class consists of reading and presenting, but she's not tough on speaking errors. I would look for her for any higher level Spanish course, she's great.

I had Prof Perez-Anzaldo a few times. She assigned a lot of reading, but that's expected for a literature course. Her lectures were both energetic and interactive since it was mostly discussion based. Outside of class, she was both caring and flexible. The in-person essay exams can be intimidating, but she usually hinted the questions in advance.

While she was nice, she can be intimidating when being serious. I once had to participate after a group meeting and struggled to give an answer and she said "no participation  cheating". After she said that I was less motivated to participate. Tests are essay based, lots of hard challenging readings. Lots of discussion homework. Class was okay.

Very philosophical. Good if you're interested in neurology. Heavy on the readings which can be difficult but every lecture goes over questions we have. Quizzes in every class but they're super easy and open note. One midterm and one final which just reuse questions from weekly quizzes. Dr. Piccinini is very passionate about this course!

Guang did a good job keeping the class organized and did well coordinating papers we needed to write, but his lectures were so bad I cannot explain them with words. He was so boring and basically just talked to the white board. He taught intro to modern physics, which is super interesting. He did not make it interesting.

If you complete all the work assigned, it is virtually impossible to fail the class. He is very intelligent and knows the content, but his lectures are sometimes quite boring and made purely of slideshows. There are two papers assigned throughout the semester, both 12 pages long but graded very generously. I liked his class overall!

Quizzes are solely one of what is talked about in the lecture. The wording of the quiz questions is not clear and most of the time they are multiple answers. She does expect you to do your research but this is very helpful in understanding the material. She challenges students to think differently. Overall, I enjoyed the class.

I took a 4 week version of this class and it was great! Material felt very approachable and well paced for such a short class. Really well organized, clear guidelines, and no busy work. Super interesting content as well. She's clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about her field and work. Would definitely reccommend this class and prof.

I love Gwen! They're a great professor and you can tell they care a lot about their students. This class is really easy and they offer extra credit. You pick a theme to work with all semester and end up creating a digital project (podcast, e-chapter, etc.) about what you researched. Grades ONLY by if you met requirements, allowing more freedom.

One of my favorite teachers this semester. If you show up to class, do the readings, and put in the effort, you will do really well in this class. Papers are long but easy; again, you just have to put in the work. Would 100% take again.

A GREAT teacher. Extremely passionate on the subject. Is always there for questions or concerns. Gave a ton of extra credit. She was always prepared with explanations for the topics that were relevant and informative. I would recommend to do the readings but they aren't necessary to pass. Overall, she was a great teacher that I recommend.

Dr Horstman is overall a good professor to have, she makes lectures interesting. Tests are open notes however, they are questions you have to think about. My recommendation for the tests is to actually complete the study guide and then during the tests you can command + F from your notes, study guide, and the textbook.

Great teacher, but you only have about 10 things total to turn in that will really make or break your grade. Grading also takes an EXTREMELY long time. Did not grade half of discussions posts until end of semester, first half was graded after half semester was done. Very important papers take about 2 1/2 months to 3 months to grade.

personally, I like the professor but hate the class content. The method research are to difficult to me but the professor is really interesting and care about all students. I think she makes the class easier because of her vivid speech and teaching. I would recommend her class to my friends.

Haley is a great professor! You definitely have to work for your grade, but she is available for help if you need it. Her lectures were interesting, but most of the test material came from the textbook, because in class we ran out of time a lot.

Haley is definitely one of my favorite professors at MU. She's really fun and her lectures are usually pretty interesting. Make sure to go to class as much as possible and take good notes because she doesn't post notes online. Her tests aren't too difficult, but you definitely need to study for them.

Haley is a really great teacher and is very entertaining to learn from. Her lectures are easy going and fun, however there are a lot of notes you need to take because they are not put online. Go to class and get there on time. Study hard and pay attention. Not an easy A but really cool class.

Great guy, always eager to answer any questions inside and outside of class. Focuses a lot on proofs and theorems in class. If you do the practice exams and attend office hours sometimes, you will do well in his class.
Very organized lectures. Exam reviews are usually ten times harder than the actual exams. Lots of practice opportunities. Soft spoken.

Decent teacher I would say. I ended with a C+ in his class I couldn't understand his lectures very good so I just taught myself how to do everything with youtube videos and with Chat gbt giving me lots of practice problems. He does give a lot of partial points as well.

Very fair grader and good at explaining the lectures once you get accustomed to the accent. Exams are very similar to the reviews given the week prior. The final was very challenging and the reason I didn"t get the grade I want, but the rest of the class is one of the easiest Calc's at Mizzou.
Was a little difficult at first to get used to the pace of lecture, but taught the content very clearly and understandable from about week three on.
Probably one of the best math professors I had, the first thing I noticed at the start of semester was how well he explained how things were derived.

Very kind professor and is always happy to answer anyone's questions in class/outside of class. HIs lectures might put you to sleep but he asks questions sometimes to keep class engaged. Grades very fairly on the exams, which helps because of how hard the content is. Just need to know the concepts well to score decently on the exams. gpt the hw

Han knows the content, but has a difficult time teaching it. I often had to try to learn the content by myself on the homework. There was only one homework assignment per week, but it was lengthy, taking me around 2 hours each week. There is a quiz every Friday, which never was too long. One benefit is that Han gives out lots of partial credit.
One of the best professors you will get to take, but the class is very difficult. Homework and quizzes every week and the exams are very hard.

Dr. Salim loves to crack a joke early in the morning. Super smart guy, he genuinely cares and wants students to learn the material. Exams are very hard. Weekly quizzes 1-2 HW assigned per week. Don't skip lecture and you are expected to worship the textbook. Pretty tough class overall, but the content is what made it unenjoyable not the professor.
Dr. Salim is actually one of the best professors I have ever had. If he could teach all of my classes, that would be awesome. He explains the concepts thoroughly and answers questions very well.

Full disclosure, I took the online version of this course and was completely disappointed...I cannot believe I paid for this class! The reviews I've read on him stated he hates lecturing which was made very evident by his complete absence from any form of procedure or explanation. Sad to see he earns over 200k for this piss poor effort...
Dr. Salim is my favorite professor.

Dr. Salim was a very good professor. He taught clearly and made things very understandable. However, the set up of the class was a little difficult. We had lectures only on Thursdays and homework was always due on Saturday and Sunday nights.
Dr. Salim is a great professor and explains the details very well. You have to work every week to catch up.
Great Professor

I loved having Hanna as a professor. She was super nice and engaging and she is the only professor I've had who does a good job of relating to students. She tries new activities and ideas and clearly cares about how the class feels about things. She even took my class to the Heidelberg after finals and bought us appetizers. I seriously love her.

Nothing that is discussed at in person lectures is related to the work that is actually due for the class. We had weekly reading quizzes and a sociology project (I was in honors section), but never had time to work on this in class. Lectures felt like a waste of my time, and McElduff referred to lectures simply as "added fun."

Hanna was awesome!! I fell in love with sociology while taking her class! She is also so caring and really prioritizes the mental health of her students. She let us pass on up to three assignments, and was super flexible with due dates. No tests, just weekly journal entries, and a final paper. Would love to take another class taught by her!

I loved this class, and Hanna was awesome. Super understanding and reasonable with her expectations. The assigned textbooks for this class are novels instead of regular textbooks, which made it a lot easier to complete the required readings without getting bored. Quizzes were easy as long as you did the readings, and tests were fairly easy as well.

As a student getting a degree in Philosophy Dr. Rubin is probably the most intelligent person in the department. She takes complex concepts and makes them easy to digest and apply. I learned a lot in her class without struggling through a needlessly complex course structure which has been hard to find recently.
Easy class taught in a way that can be easily understood. Super friendly and approachable.

Great lecturer, but refuses to give any information about exams, could study for 20 hours and still get a 60 on the exam, ridiculously difficult for a intro class and does not give the materials to succeed.

The course is front loaded with work due to the main portion of the class being carrer fair prep. The main grade is carrer fair attendence, resume, coverletter, and mock interview. After the carrer fair the class consists of weekly guest speakers and one budgeting assignment. Hannah is amazing and very caring of her students!

She's very passionate about her job, which is admirable. Her grading criteria is not clear at all. Two students could say the same thing in an assignment and it would be marked wrong on one and correct on the other. Overall, very funny, but I think that can take away from lecture sometimes.
Was ok in class, definitely need to study to pass the class. Was very difficult to get a hold of through email. Was very difficult on grading. Was not very gracious about things.

Will call you out for talking in lecture. Easy to reach outside of class if you need help and is reasonable about absences/make up labs. Some people feel she grades unfairly but honestly just study and the exams are straight forward. Clear she is passionate about the subject she teaches and us learning it for a reason.
almost wants you to fail, refuses to make study materials

In her sections of this class, she lectures for the purpose of you deeply understanding the information. She invites students to talk to her at any time and makes it easy to ask her for help or to just talk to her. She understands where we are in life and that we have other things going on. The only thing I didn't like was the pointless packbacks.

Absolutely love Hannah! The animal science courses are a good mix of biology and management. Provides fill-in-the-blank notes for lectures. There are weekly pop quizzes, but I've found they help me study during the week and understand the material. She's very sweet and open to questions during lectures and makes learning very casual and fun.
I had to drop

i took this course (extra-galactic astronomy) last semester and liked it a lot. dr yan was one of the two professors in the department who inspired me the most. his lectures were well organized and he asked deep questions. i also liked it very much that he set aside time in class to work out the past homework problems. he is awesome.

I took his Galactic Astronomy last semester. He is an extremely knowledgeable professor and a caring person. He teaches in the classic way but I did learn a lot, basically what astronomy is really about. Not an easy professor though, and to do well you must come to his lectures. But he would give you many opportunities to make things right.

Missed a few assignments due to family issues after the spring break and thought I'd fail this one. I explained my situations, he was sympathetic and gave extensions. A highly recommended teacher. The class was fun, the lectures were organized nicely through canvas. just did the hw on my phone because i had to travel a lot.

I took this online course instead of a bio class to fulfill the science course requirement. Being a history major I found this course a bit different from what I'd expected. But overall the materials were great and inspiring and I'd recommend it. Dr. Yan was very quick in answering my emails. Had I not forgotten two homework I believe I'd got A.
Absolutely terrible teacher. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. SO BAD SO BAD SO BAD.

All of these reviews are 100% true. One of the online quizzes (worth 75% of grade) closed out before the due date for me, and I had to basically argue with him over email to get him to open it again. Expect no leniency with assignments, even though they are 3/4 of your grade. Very lazy class layout and seems like an excuse to get research funding.

This is the worst teacher I've ever had. His homework answers are not anywhere in the notes, and are not accurate according to legitimate online sources. He can barely speak English in the lectures and skips over important information needed to succeed in Astronomy 1200. Will not ever take a class with this teacher again.
PRACTICAL one of only two professors I've ever had be practical and not teach the dumb academia. teaches you what you need to know and that's why he's the best

Professor Naumann has been one of my favorite professors in college so far. This class was more challenging than some of the other agriculture-based courses, but the information was valuable and applicable in every division of plant science. He clearly explains all concepts. I hope I get to take another of his courses before graduation.

The course and the content were not bad if you were willing to study outside of class. He is a very dry individual, so can be difficult at 8 am. Homework was all online via the textbook, so lots of concepts you are asked to use for homework/quizzes are not even on the test. Use the practice tests because they are VERY similar to the real thing.
Dr. James is an excellent teacher!

He is very effective in a large setting & is very passionate about what he teaches! Yes, he does assign a lot of homwork. However, if you are a bad test taker, like myself, the participation & graded assignments outweigh the exams.
He was easy and chill

He is a very good teacher! if you do not go to class do not plan to get an A or even a B. You will have a bunch of online work to do and this is majority of your grade. I read the book and still did awful on the tests. Go over past exams and you will do fine. If you do your homework, quizzes, and go to classes you should be fine!

Textbook needed for HW, takes Tophat for attendance and participation questions. Very friendly and tries to make the class fun and easy to understand via pop culture and the like. 8 homework assignments, easy points.
He's a such a good guy. He applies economics to some of the most random things, but it helps! And he really cares about his students.
Go to class, do the homework, pay attention and you'll get an A.

Professor Cox is a great teacher and is extremely understanding about deadlines and assignments. We spent most of the semester doing writers workshops and assessing short stories and articles so be prepared to do a fair amount of reading, though she makes sure the work load isnt overwhelming. She gives great advise on publishing and grad school.

She provided a detailed syllabus and follows it closely, tough but fair grader. In class time is spent effectively and she encourages an open discussion classroom setting. She truly wants all of her students to excel and is available for outside class help. She encourages students to think deeper and be better writers.

This class is the reason I am not in JSchool. She claimed I had citation issues worked with me to fix them then claimed to find more and failed me in this class. Avoid her at all cost she has a possibility to ruin your entire college experience

Most unorganized teacher I've had in a while.  At the surface she seems like a good teacher that will offer an easy class with plenty of learning opportunity but then she soon turns into an unorganized mess who does not help with anything.  Took me around a month for feedback on each essay, and she was very late to respond to any questions. AVOID.

These ratings seem unfair at best. Long readings and complex material, sure. However, the lectures were extremely explanative, the expectations were reasonable, and the professor was receptive and accommodating. While the grading was tough, my final grade reflected my level of effort and understanding of the material. Perhaps a bit generously.

Her online course is not as difficult. The quizzes can be difficult, but there are not any tests, so as long as you watch the lectures and read the textbooks, you should do fine. However, some of the pdfs she assigned are very lengthy and hard to get through.

I have never felt so lost in a class before. Her final was truly one of the most difficult exams I have ever taken I cried to myself while taking it. Teaches like we already know everything she is talking about.

The professor didn't seem to care too much about the class. There were weekly quizzes that were doable, but sometimes, she assigned lengthy PDFs along with the long and boring homework. If you do the work, an A is attainable.

Dropped this course after a few weeks. Too much reading to keep up with if you're taking 4 other courses and working. She made it very clear at the start of the course we were not her priority as this was the last undergrad course she was teaching. Didn't respond to emails. Her poor TA.

A is not impossible. Can't give advice for it because I'm still surprised I got one, but, boring lectures and extremely long readings are around 30% of quiz questions per quiz. I had prior knowledge of the subject before taking the class which helped greatly. Recommend that if you need a genuine intro class, please find another 1400 professor.

Dr. Ba is a kind and knowledgeable person. My biggest issue was the quizzes. We had 150-250 pages per week and the questions she asked were not big picture questions, just random facts. Sometimes, I couldn't even find the answers when I reread the text after the quiz. I would take her courses again if she reformatted her quizzes. RIP my 4.0 GPA. :(

She only reads off of the slides. She also believes in dropping a letter grade for each time you don't show up to class after 4 absences. There's quizzes every week that are insanely difficult for no reason. I would not recommend taking this class.

Quick responses and good combination of individual and group work

Minimal effort from Davenport on grading and feedback- received same feedback every week. Easy class, but feels like a waste of money- little to no learning. Assignments are reused from other professors & classes and feel meaningless. Lots of dumb discussion boards and quizzes with answers word for word in textbook. Feels like elementary school.

For this class at least, it is clear priorities for Prof Davenport are elsewhere. Lots of recycled presentations and videos from other sources and professors. Weekly reading of a textbook chapter (granted, fairly interesting stuff), some discussion posts, various other small, doable assignments. Never once interacted with Prof.

If you are looking for an easy class/professor she is not it. Her grading is based on length and proper citations. If you go beyond her selected number of eord choice (i.e., 150 words) she will dock you points. She post questions and you have to answer them thoroughly with 150 words or less, same goes for responding to other classmates work. ��
Genuinely cares about all of her students, their performance in the course, and their overall well being. She goes above and beyond :)
Genuinely loves what shes doing and wants her students to succeed.

Hennkens is a great professor! The class no doubt is very difficult, especially for a 2400 class, so you have to work pretty hard at it. I would suggest writing down all the powerpoint notes, then going through the textbook to practice problems. ATTEND OFFICE HOURS!!! She will get to know you and helps out a lot!

Tests are unnecessarily difficult with failing class averages, no practice tests or practice problems, tests are 60% of grade. She does not help in office hours and is too smart to dumb material down enough to help us understand. Grades on a modified curve but refuses to explain what that means.

Dr. Srinivasan's class is taught much more like an upper level proof-based course than an introductory course. She is a fine instructor for someone who is slightly familiar with the material, but her class will be VERY hard as a first look at matrices. If you are a science/engineering major, consider that the class will not be applied math.

Do not take this instructor. I took her despite the reviews and it was a mistake. Please do not repeat my mistake. She is a nice person, but it will not set you up for success for all the reasons other reviews have listed. Find a way to take it elsewhere, there are better options.
Could have been better.

For someone whose USP is being such a wonderful and kind person, she sure gets very defensive and very rude when questioned about questionable grading practices, at the very least asking to see her grading, and her well known and questionable practice of having many typos and serious mistakes in problem sets and exams.

Wish I would've trusted these reviews & dropped this class when I could. She is a very smart and kind lady, but I feel like I learned nothing in this class. No homework, grades were mostly determined by exams (+ some quizzes worth little points). You have to teach yourself if you want to do well. Received the lowest grade of my life in this class:(

Dr. Srinivasan seems to think that all of her students understand math as quickly as she does. Once she tells you about a topic, she acts as if you fully understand it. Her slides are extremely technical, but you barely have time to time to take notes. She never takes time to explain concepts, yet each test had conceptually-based questions.

Prof Srinivasan is very helpful, but the way she taught the material just did not work. Still not sure if going to lectures was worth it or not. HWs were doable & she'd give plenty of "insights" onto what is/is likely to be on tests. Had some extra credit available too. Also gives plenty partial credit & is very forgiving about arithmetic errors.

Professor Srinivasan is a sweet lady, but she is fundamentally incapable of teaching. She teaches as if everyone has had a proofs-based course and is familiar with linear algebra before. Her slides are as long as the textbook, and she offers no substantive insights to make things more digestible. She is the antithesis of what a professor should be.

His dendrology with lab is ridiculously hard. You're experienced to go find the trees discussed in lab in your own given a map. You need to be able to identify the trees and it's like he goes out of his way to find hardest ones. Also it's unfair because the group with the ta gets it real easy. Nice guy though.
You need to lock IN for Dendro, but Doc really cares about his field and his students, and tries to make it easier on everyone. He is great to learn from.

exams are easy as he allows a cheat sheet- but they go over SO much information. lectures and labs do not correlate at all in terms of what youre learning and when. lab quizzes are like 75%+ of your grade and they are HARD. one bad quiz will drop you a letter grade, guaranteed. be prepared to study like your life depends on it.
Very kind, well-respected, and willing to help students. The class is heavily memorization focused, but very useful. Study throughout the week for lab quizzes and you will do fine.

I am not doing great in Dendrology, but this teacher is so nice and he has emailed me twice saying he wants me to be successful, even offering to take a walk around campus with me to catch up on the tree species. Wish I could do better in class because he deserves good grades! Amazing teacher.
I loved Dr. Stelzer, but dendrology was HARD. Memorizing over 100 trees and their latin names and silvics and twigs was not easy, but flashcards help! Show up and take this class seriously.

This class is fine but the lectures were very monotone (online lectures). The class is mainly graded on labs (80% of your grade) and if you miss one tree in the quiz, its a big hit to the grade. He does do a double points day to make up for the harder labs. He was never in class, the class was mainly taught by TAs. One of our TAs was not good.

This was one of the hardest, yet most rewarding class I have taken in my 3 years at MU. 140+ tree species to memorize and identify in the woods/on campus seems daunting, but Doc and his TAs do a great job of preparing us for our 20 weekly tree ID quizzes!

If you have a heavy schedule DO NOT take this class. Not necessarily difficult but an unreasonable amount of workload. Attendance is now "mandatory" and takes up a solid chunk out of your grade even though lectures are incredibly hard to follow. Your TA will be your make or break. Some can be very tough graders.

No need to attend lectures. However, labs are mandatory and there are weekly lab assignments, some of which are very long and tedious. Practice exams, which are extra credit, are close to the real ones with guides to solutions.

Huy Nguyen is very kind and friendly, and he's very knowledgeable about his field. However, he's extremely difficult to follow in lecture, and the structure of the class means that you'll spend half your week learning almost nothing. Plan for at least 10-12 hours of work per week on this class.
Most of what people complain about on here has nothing to do with him, just based on what TA you have

A lot of people complain about his lectures but he's probably one of the best engineering professors I've had. He actually likes his job and he's easy to follow.
He's also pretty chill when it comes to exams too, he gives opportunities for lots of extra credit and if you just do that then you'll know stuff for the exam.
Very long lab assignments due every week, so plan accordingly. Very long wait for grading as well.

Labs were intense and lectures didn't reflect on labs/exams. Lectures were not mandatory but labs are. You'll have to spend time outside of class to work on lab assignments, and grading was also sketchy and inconsistent (done by different TAs). Big group project at the end too, can make or break your grade. Also a fair amount of extra credit.

I hate to say it but he is really not easy to understand at all. Going to the lectures is pretty much pointless, the quizzes are online and the theory parts of the exams are open note. I feel bad for him because no one was listening during the lectures, but you really don't need to anyway.

If you are thinking of taking this class as an easy A elective DON'T!! The material is really simple but the amount of work for something as simple as hospitality is utterly ridiculous. He is difficult to get a hold of and even when you do get a hold of him you can never get any answers from him. This class makes me want to snap my laptop in half.

We didn't do ANYTHING in class, but he expects you to go because he does TopHat questions over the chapters and if you don't go it will count against you when you realize your bad grade at the end of the semester when he FINALLY puts it in.

Dr. Marshall is a really nice guy and you can tell he enjoys doing his job. He will love you as long as you show up to class and participate. Sometimes he isn't the most clear on directions so make sure you ask questions. He also wasn't the best at getting back to emails in a timely matter so if he doesn't get back to you, go to his office hours.

HORRIBLE!!! Do NOT take any class with Marshall. He has no clue what is ever going on and is clueless on how to use any technology. He is frequently wrong about topics and his exams make no sense/ do not follow anything from his lectures. He does not care about his students or how they do in his class.

Dr. Marshall is not clear on what he wants out of his students. Grades are not uploaded until the end of the semester. He's not clear when you ask him a question through email. This class has been stressful because you are guessing what your grades will be, and the quizzes at the beginning of class are extra credit, so thats good. Test aren't clear

The most unclear teacher I've ever had. He throws a rubric at you and expects that you know what he wants from him without describing it. Also he doesn't update grades so you have no idea how you're doing till it's too late. Test are easy since their online, but he can't even spell the questions or answers right on them. Harder than it should be!

So he's for the most part a good guy just strict and clear on certain things he want's. Attendance is mandatory and there's 2 group projects which he was never clear on what he wanted. He never once updated grades during the semester so you have no idea how you're doing. Test are online, but there were so many spelling errors in the questions.

Does clicker type attendance and if Mizzou wireless isn't working, he doesn't care. Doesn't explain well, doesn't answer questions, e-mail, give feedback, update grades, ect. Hard to get a good grade on exams when words are spelled wrong on every single question. Worst class i've taken so far and don't recommend it to anyone.

I really came to admire him throughout the semester! He has a nuanced worldview that he tries his best to bring to class each day and values diverse points of view. As long as you're engaged, everyone's happy!

He is very clearly a professor that cares deeply about what he is teaching. He is excellent at taking confusing topics and making apply to a students life. While I respect him a lot as a professor, his classes can be difficult depending on the type of class you're in. He is big on participation, but my class wouldn't work with him at all.

Professor Medina is passionate about what he teaches, his classes are somewhat lecture heavy but they are not boring. He poses intriguing questions to students throughout to keep you engaged. Weekly at home quizzes on the readings, very easy even if you didn't fully do the reading and 3 essays with clearly laid out rubric. Overall would take again.
Dr. Medina knew everyone's name by the end of the semester, very easy class no exams and only 3 essays. He encourages everyone get involved in the class by talking about their ideas or experiences.
Your grade is mostly based on the 3 essays, but he is not a super hard grader. Make sure to go to class because attendance determines your grade. Pretty easy class.

Hilda is a good person and outside of class she is very caring and helpful. However, I didn't learn anything new in her class and even though I made an effort to talk and participate every day, I somehow still got terrible participation grades. I don't think my Spanish really got any better. I like her, I did not like her class.

Must keep up with readings and participate or you can't pass (but this is true of most Spanish classes). She seems a little tough at first, took some warming up to her, but by the end our whole class loved her! She has high expectations, but only b/c she truly cares about your learning and improvement. Not hard to do well if you put in the effort.

Hilda has great intentions, but she does not realize how rude she can be at times. This particular class had many students who were avid about Spanish and could actually speak it pretty well. Regardless she still would scold you if you got a question wrong. Also the class structure is confusing so you have to talk to the other students in class.

At the beginning of the semester, I wasn't very fond of her but she really is a cool person. Shes very opinionated but she cares about her students and she loves to teach. The homework problems are the same as test problems and she can tell who did the homework so do it. The vocab can be tough but try and she will reward the effort and dedication.

Easily the worst professor and teacher I have ever had. She makes fun of students when they get answers wrong, even threatening to jump out the window when someone made a grammatical error out loud. She is rude, condescending, and mean. I would NEVER EVER recommend her as a professor. She is HORRIBLE. DO NOT take her class.

One of the worst Spanish teachers I have had. Be ready to work hard everyday in class. She expects a lot from her students and she becomes angry when her expectations aren't met. She is not very clear with what she wants, so most of the time it is a guessing game. Strongly suggest a class GroupMe to discuss what is going on in class.

Hilda is an awesome professor, although she took some time to get used to. She is strict on attendance and participation. Homework every day, but nothing you turn in (but do it because you go over it and that counts as participation). Tests are tough, and essays are not bad. She is very helpful if you take the time to see her. Also very funny!

My favorite Spanish teacher that I have ever had. Although the tests are hard, she does give points to you and tries to boost everyones' grades. She is so nice and really made my decision easy to become a spanish double major.

2200 is very fast-paced and gets into the material on day one. Prepare to struggle if you are given a bad group. Fortunately for me, my group mates were hard-working and collaborative throughout. The peer evaluations are a great way to hold members accountable. Initially disliked the course but found myself liking it toward the end. Prof is kind.

She was super nice and clear with expectations throughout the course, but it felt like way too many projects per week for a 2 credit class. I think she's great for the higher Strat Comm classes--she knows what she's doing--but for J2200 there was a strange mix of projects and busy work in the schedule. 

She did not round my 93.96% up to an A.

Just took my final for this class and was excited to hop on here and brag about her! Attendance is required, but her lectures are always engaging, memorable, and entertaining. If you just want to pass, show up to every class and take decent notes. If you want an A read the textbook! Great class for all directions of strat comm.
Great professor, very engaging classes and lectures. Classwork was relevant and helped me grow in my major.

Prof Higginbotham has some of the best, well-structured lectures I've taken in the J-school. She's always very well prepared for class. Attendance isn't required but I very rarely wanted to skip it because her content was so interesting. The group work can be tedious but that's standard for a strategic communications class. I highly recommend her.

Holly was an amazing professor! Organized and very intelligent. She is my favorite professor I have had so far in the J School. For an online/ async. class, she was very engaging and interesting. Her lectures were clear and included useful examples to help make the concepts understandable. The class is easy, just time-consuming.

Holly was hands down my most organized and clear professor I had during the fall 2020 semester. If you do your work and you end up with a good group for the group projects, then you will do just fine.

Loved Holly soo much, she is the nicest person ever. The class is pretty much all group assignments and quizzes. As long as you have a good group you will get an A. Everything I learned is applicable to my future in PR.

Prof. Lidsky lectures with a passion that kept me both entertained and intrigued throughout the semester. If you care about rhetoric and legal philosophy, I highly recommend that you take this course. No homework to this class, and exams are graded lightly.
Excellent mentor. If you want to attend law school, take this class. Very challenging and sometimes frustrating but he will answer any questions you have and is happy to help.

Love him and hate him. I liked the course content & found it engaging. He assigns papers & law school projects without clear instruction. He thinks he's giving you a ton of guidance but he's not. He openly admits one-on-one to holding certain students to a higher standard. If you disagree with a grade, go talk to him. Rewarding when you succeed.

People on here are pressed because they didn't do well on the 3rd exam. Big deal. You day its like law school then complain when you are preparing. Study harder. I am a bio major... bio. He is the first prof I have ever had to write for. Just use your brains.
Horrible teacher who needs to be fired. You are going to be teaching yourself with this class. Not worth one second of your time.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I cannot stress it enough. Your GPA WILL take a plunge and if you're reading this and still take it you have only yourself to blame, don't say you weren't warned

4 tests, on material that he sometimes never even talks about. The tests are all subjective, he decides how he chooses to grade them after you've already taken it. He mentions something once and takes points off your test if you don't think it applies to the cases and don't write it down. Important to mention the tests are essays which isn't easier

Whoever is reading this, I beg you to take a different class with a different teacher. Don't put yourself through it for a 2000 level course. NOT worth it. Some of these reviews are straight up lying to you, he is a horrible teacher and doesn't actually help you.
Dr. Hua runs a very disorganized class and has very rambling lectures. You may be tempted to take this class because it is 1000 level and multidisciplinary, but it isn't worth it.
Dr. Qin's lectures are painfully boring. He will wait until finals week to assign you an 8-page essay. Do not take this class if you don't have to.

She was an amazing professor; she's incredibly caring, very respected, and clearly knows what she's talking about. The problem comes with the classes schedule, which she did not make. She did the best she could with an awful schedule, but it made the class very difficult. She'll do her best to help. *I took class 1100, but it's not an option*

An incredibly kind and caring woman. There isn't much she wouldn't do for her students. I've taken her Chinese language classes from freshman to senior year. Very lenient grader, flexible and accessible, clear expectations, frequent quizzes/assignments/tests though. Chinese itself is difficult, but it is worth it if you care about the content.
Says attendance is mandatory but it really isn't. Some tests are ridiculously easy and others are very hard. Not always very organized but a nice woman.
Very, very kind lady, understanding and sympathetic towards students. There are assignments and things due nearly every day, but they're not bad. Textbook necessary. Very lenient grader.

She is a very nice lady but is easily confused by questions and is somewhat scatterbrained. She is from China, so clearly she knows a lot about it, which is good. Makes a lot of mistakes on tests but accepts fault and fixes her mistakes. Unorganized and seeming lack of communication with TA. Often late for class & kind of a pushover.

Clearly well-educated on the topics teaching, but not good at articulating the knowledge needed for exams. In a class where the average exam grade hovered around a 50%, it was tough to know if we weren't learning the right things or not being taught the right things.
Fast-paced, math/matlab-heavy. From what I gather, very easy to pass with a C-, very hard to get an A.
Challenging but fair. Homework assignments are long but easy. Make sure you know them by heart for exams.

One of the toughest classes I've taken, but also one of the most rewarding. The material is dense—expect to work hard—but the professor explains everything with clarity. If you put in the time, you'll come out with a grade you're happy about. Expecting a B+.

Dr. Nassar is an infuriating professor. He makes assignments very easy and then absolutely destroys everyone on the exam. He takes no accountability when students do terribly. The averages have been in the 40s. He continues to blame the students instead of reflecting on the idea that the exams should actually cover class material.

Homework and projects are easy. Tests are extremely hard and take too much time. Exam averages are in the 40's with no curve. Mind you, this is a sophomore-junior level class, so none of us in there are dumb. I will say his lectures are fine, but the class kinda stinks :(

Hussein Nassar is the worst professor I've ever suffered under. By his own admission, his exams are only 60% material the class has seen before, putting the class average on every exam in the high 40%'s. Almost every student in the class is on the verge of failing, and he does everything he can to rationalize his choices with no accountability.

He's chill, his lectures are like meh but I think that's just because not many MechE's care about coding so no one participated (also at 8 am). The grading for the class used to be infamously hard but as of Fall 2024 it was very fair and honestly hard to not get at least a B. The TAs are really bad though and didn't know what they were doing.

If you have a heavy schedule DO NOT take this class. Not necessarily difficult but an unreasonable amount of workload. Attendance is now "mandatory" and takes up a solid chunk out of your grade even though lectures are incredibly hard to follow. Your TA will be your make or break. Some can be very tough graders.

No need to attend lectures. However, labs are mandatory and there are weekly lab assignments, some of which are very long and tedious. Practice exams, which are extra credit, are close to the real ones with guides to solutions.

Huy Nguyen is very kind and friendly, and he's very knowledgeable about his field. However, he's extremely difficult to follow in lecture, and the structure of the class means that you'll spend half your week learning almost nothing. Plan for at least 10-12 hours of work per week on this class.
Most of what people complain about on here has nothing to do with him, just based on what TA you have

A lot of people complain about his lectures but he's probably one of the best engineering professors I've had. He actually likes his job and he's easy to follow.
He's also pretty chill when it comes to exams too, he gives opportunities for lots of extra credit and if you just do that then you'll know stuff for the exam.
Very long lab assignments due every week, so plan accordingly. Very long wait for grading as well.

Labs were intense and lectures didn't reflect on labs/exams. Lectures were not mandatory but labs are. You'll have to spend time outside of class to work on lab assignments, and grading was also sketchy and inconsistent (done by different TAs). Big group project at the end too, can make or break your grade. Also a fair amount of extra credit.

I hate to say it but he is really not easy to understand at all. Going to the lectures is pretty much pointless, the quizzes are online and the theory parts of the exams are open note. I feel bad for him because no one was listening during the lectures, but you really don't need to anyway.

She is genuinely one of the best professors I have had. She is very good about responding to emails with any questions you have. The structure of her class is very easy. Does not take a lot of effort/stress to pass this class. Truly the easiest writing intensive I've taken. Would recommend this class for anyone who needs a writing intensive credit.

Everyone told me this class was gonna be super hard, but it's one of the easiest I've taken.There is an attendance question each week plus a couple of assignments. Most of the assignments took like 20 minutes if they weren't for the research paper. She also gives 100% on all assignments and you get to drop 4 so you don't even have to do all of them
DO NOT TAKE!

I honestly don't know why there is so many bad reviews. She has been super nice, and never once was demeaning over zoom meetings discussing my research paper. The workload is not bad, as attendance is as simple as replying on canvas how you are doing. Besides an occasional weekly short assignment, the one research paper is the bulk of the class.

Worst professor ever at MU. Drop the instant you see her as your professor. She makes you do so much nonsense busywork. You can't understand a word she says, and she uses the language barrier to her advantage. She makes EVERYTHING way harder and more confusing then it really needs to be. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR!!!!!
Terrible.
Don't take this with her

Not the easiest class to take, but not difficult either if you keep up with the material.  She is a bit hard to understand due to her Korean accent, and also does go a bit fast on presentations.  Participation is important for in-class discussions.  Exams are also hard if you don't review the material too often.  Does curve grades after finals.

In 3-D materials, Ian was a great professor. The class was getting restructured and he made sure we were happy with the projects he was proposing. He was semi laid back and always made sure to check in with us during our projects. I thoroughly enjoyed having him as a professor.

I have never had a worse professor in my life. He allowed no technology in class, assigned more homework than any 4000 class ive taken and was a horrible teacher. I hope he is never allowed to "teach" aka torture students again

Just a genuine kinda guy. Could sit back and crack open a cold one with him, you know? Does he ramble? Yes. But it's about the journey, not that destination. And, boy, did we go on a journey! Shout out to my man!

He does IClicker and questions throughout class. There are itnquizitives due twice a week but they are pretty easy. His tests are multiple choice. My only complaint is that he doesn't allow technology in class. He does have field trips though to art studios on campus and guest lecturers.
Lectures are hard to sit through. Make sure to attend class as 5% of overall grade will be deducted after 5 absences, sick or otherwise. No study guides and tests are hard to prep for.

Intro to visual arts was unorganized from the start to finish. Lectures were very hard to sit through as they seemed to not get to the point. The iclicker questions were said to be the questions on the exams, but many questions were not or not even out of the textbook itself.

Class was always disorganized & Ian would ramble the entire time. It's difficult to study for the exams as he rambles the entire class period & doesn't provide a helpful study guide. You can study your homework & iClicker questions but you're still going into the exam blind. He provides lecture notes, but then doesn't cover what's on the notes.

Caring professor who is very organized and sets clear expectations. The course includes take-home quizzes and opportunities for extra credit on exams. If you keep up with the material and attend office hours with questions, it's possible to do well. Overall, the professor explains concepts clearly and supports student success.

Content speeds up towards the end of the course, which Ian discloses numerous times in the early weeks of the semester. He is an awesome person which makes it a lot easier to put effort into his course, and if you put in effort you can earn the grade you want. Exams can be tough at times, but are never unfair. Would definitely recommend.

Professor Aberbach was a fine teacher and a great person. He was personable and genuinely seemed to care about his students a lot. Class material speeds and gets tough up at the end of the semester but if you do well enough early on in the semester it will be enough to carry your grade.

This class is a very fast-paced class and it can be very difficult to keep up. However, Dr. Aberbach worked very hard to ensure you could succeed if you put in the work. Weekly take-home quizzes, extra credit on quizzes and exams, always willing to answer questions, generous partial credit, and test questions are tough but fair. Highly recommend!

genuinely, he was the best professor i have ever had. always willing to help with problems, his lectures are great, and the problems on quizzes/exams are difficult but always within the scope of what he has taught you- there are also usually a few bonus points on quizzes/exams. he is very witty and super nice

Great professor. Lecture is pretty good, lecture notes go online, tells you explicitly which concepts will be on a test and which are omitted. Extra credit for take home quizzes & every exam. Exams aren't tricky, either. Also is forgiving with partial credit. You can tell he wants students to succeed. Better experience than calc II for me.

Fine professor. decent explainer. builds in extra credit into quizzes and tests. However, pretty unorganized with his notes and his "exam study guides" are just a canvas announcement saying the units we've covered since the last test, which is not helpful. Though, he does tell you to omit a few of the topics so it's not all bad. overall he was fine

Great Professor to have for Calc 3 compared to other options. He does curve exams and final grades. Notes are fairly organized, yet I don't think he posts them on canvas. Weekly quizzes, but they were online. Usually had extra points built into exams and quizzes. Overall good experience with him.

I took 4580 because I really loved Dr. Gizer in 2510. He's funny and really cares about his students. The class is hard though, I would recommend it for upperclassmen because I was a sophomore and was kind of thrown in head first. However, Dr. Gizer does understand that his material isn't easy to understand, as you're reading lots of research.

He is a very nice guy and the material is interesting and easy to follow. However, exams are poorly worded and confusing. The questions differ significantly from how concepts are explained in lectures, so studying the lectures alone isn't enough—you need strong inference and interpretation skills to do well. Average on exams is usually C's or D's.
Lecture-heavy class, attend them, read the textbook & take notes. Tests are asynchronous, so not hard to get a good grade. Difficult due to the sheer volume of info.

Dr. Gizer is engaging and creates a safe and welcoming learning environment. While lecture heavy, the exams are online and open-notes. Attendance is (kind of?) mandatory, he takes a grade for attendance on iClicker but it's not a very heavy percentage of the grade. Literally if you just show up to class and pay attention you will do great.

Loved having him as a professor and Psych2510 with him is such an easy class. The lectures can feel long sometimes, but the homework isn't difficult and the tests are all open note with one lowest test score being dropped at the end of the semester. Overall, super easy and I'd recommend this class for sure!

Dr. Gizer is very knowledgeable about psychopathology and I learned a lot from his class, but his lectures just drag on forever. He tends to spend a lot of time on each chapter because he puts in so many slides, but most of what you need for tests is from the book. Tests could be challenging, but open note and book so that makes it better.
i love this man so much, his lectures are interesting and entertaining and the homework is easy. tests are open note

Professor Gizer is not very good at lecturing, because his class is an hour and fifteen minutes its very hard to stay engaged. The tests can be difficult, so notes are important, but his slides aren't very in-depth, and you'll need to study the textbook too. On the upside, he is a very nice and approachable guy!

I respect the woman but her class is structured more for graduate students than undergrads who are used to more organization. As a student with a learning disability, I do not recommend her class if you struggle with note-taking because she talks too fast and cannot pronounce English words well.

Dr. Pearce has been publishing her work on feminism for decades before any of her students were even born, and it shows in her lectures. She has the best examples and makes class very enjoyable. As long as you have an interest in whatever topic she is teaching, this class will be a great experience.

This woman is one of the best professors I've ever had the pleasure to have. She would sometimes give two or three hours of reading a night, but I quickly learned that coming to class prepared (and coming to class, period) was the best way to go. Dr. Pearce is sweet, insightful, informed and engaging. She's a must-have for any sociology student.

Dr. Pearce is brilliant.  She is tough and demanding, as one would expect from someone of her intellectual caliber.  Serious students should absolutely take at least one of Dr. Pearce's classes.  You just know that you are sitting in the presence of an intellectual powerhouse with a unique perspective.

This is not a class for the light-hearted. There's a lot of reading, and her teaching method is more classic(mostly lectures, no powerpoint) But it is extremely interesting and she makes the classes enjoyable (and chooses really good books/articles) Grading based on exams, a term paper, and a group project. Highly recommend for serious student

Your average Calc 3 professor. Exams/Quizzes is what makes most of your grade. Also don't forget about the final exam! This is a difficult class so be ready to grind. I don't think he curves too in which he should. He just reads the slides and expects you to know everything. Pretty challenging to communicate with.

Had him for cal 3 in-person and he read from slides from the textbook every lecture. I didn't learn much from this teaching and I wouldn't recommend him as a teacher. 90% of the time he is standing in front of the class reading from the slides that we get on Canvas. Although the homework load was pretty light which is nice, only one a week.

Dr. Verbitsky was a very straightforward professor. He gives you 2 dropped quizzes and 2 dropped homeworks. He definitely understands how difficult the course material for Calc 3 is. All of the tests and quizzes had very straighforward problems which we had either done in our homework, or in class notes. Would recommend him over other Calc 3 profs.

I think Mr. Verbitsky is kind of dropping the ball in a virtual setting. I had him this past semester for 2300 and it was certainly the worst math experience I had in my life. My main problem is that he did not allow you to show your work for partial credit on every problem. He will not slow down in a lecture even if you ask.

He is an older professor and seems to be caught up in teaching in his ways. My least favorite math prof so far. He teaches fast and strictly writes on the board in chalk and does not post any sort of notes online. This makes it hard to follow him when he is talking in class. Definitely be prepared to use your textbook and to teach yourself.

This class was my first experience with college, since I'm actually just a high-schooler that's ahead in math, so I was mildly intimidated at first. But Prof. Verbitsky is very straightforward and teaches difficult concepts clearly. Do your homework -- there is no time to "figure stuff out" on the tests. Quizzes on Fridays. He grades fairly.

If you ever need an extension, just shoot him an email and he is super understanding. His homework is rather intensive and requires compiling all previously learned topics and critical thinking, however if you have any questions he'll answer your emails or meet with you in his office hours to help. He's one of the best professors you'll ever have

Favorite engineering class I have taken so far. Dr. Ozden makes hard concepts easy to understand. Exams are take home. Hw and exams do require a little bit of work but are nowhere near impossible and help you understand material. Dr. Ozden is super nice and will explain things to you in office hours in such a nice way. Highly recommend him.

Long lectures. She's very passionate about WWI but I would only recommend taking this class if you have previous knowledge! Grades were based on 3 assignments so if you bomb one you're screwed. She's a decently tough grader and expects you to include material from all of the weekly assigned readings in your paper. She uploaded the textbook, no cost

I liked professor Karthas, but I found her paper grading to be pretty strict. I do think that if classes had been in person her class would have been much easier and more enjoyable so I do not blame her for my struggling in her class. She is caring and a good professor I just would have liked a little more understanding when she graded things.

Even though my class with Doctor Karthas hasn't finished yet I can definitely say she is my favorite person in Mizzou so far! I am an international student who judges professors very strictly, but Doctor Karthas just blows my mind with her energy, ideas, inspiration and eager to help us to do our best! Love her!:)

Karthas is extremely passionate about the course, which makes her fun to listen to. However, she is a very tough grader and expects her students to know the information forwards and backwards. If you go to class and make an effort to get to know her in office hours, she'll love you. Don't take this class if you're expecting an easy A.

I took Dr. Karthas capstone class on Interwar Paris. She is by far one of my favorite teachers I've ever had. She is so kind and it is obvious that she cares a lot about each of her students. She didn't just teach history, she encouraged discussion and taught critical thinking skills that could be applied to any study. I really enjoyed this class.
Professor Karthas is a pleasure to have for a professor. She is clear in her expectations and provides excellent feedback to her students.

She is one of the most knowledgable teachers I have ever had. That being said, she expects her students to understand the information as well as she does. Her lectures are so detailed that it is hard to get the gist of things. The French Revolution class is a lot more boring that what I read online. She is helpful in office hours though!

One of the best teachers I have ever had.  So nice and accommodating - she is genuinely passionate about her students' learning. Always willing to talk with her students and help them any way she can. Her History of the French Revolution class is one of the coolest, most interesting classes I have taken in college.

I loved Indah she was super nicel. The class itself can be a little challenging and I came in not knowing how to use Adobe and she didn't do much explaining on how to use everything but she was always willing to help. She wanted the best for her students and helped us succeed. She also set up times outside of class for us to meet for extra help.

I had Dr. Segert for two courses last semester and she made it so easy to know what you have to do every week, there are tons of options for extra credit and if you keep up with the work the exams are very simple!

I have had three psych courses with Dr. Segert, she sets you up for success. Watching the lectures and taking notes will give you an A on every exam. There are a few exams, discussion posts, and no final. There are a decent amount of extra credit options which are super easy. I am ending PSYCH 3830 with over 100%. Take her classes if you can!
This class is best if you want to spend majority of your life studying the brain.

Dr. Segert is amazing! Online courses can be difficult, but she sets them up in an extremely helpful way. She lets you drop one quiz, and provides extra credit about every other week. She has office hours set up at frequent times if anyone wants to ask questions, or just chat with her about anything. She's an amazing professor!

I have taken professor Segert for all of the Psych courses I have taken at Mizzou, she always keeps things interesting and I never got bored in her class. My favorite of her classes was Drugs and Behavior I would highly recommend it. Lectures are recorded and test are online. Loved taking her classes, I wish she offered more.

Love Prof. Segert. This is my 2nd class with her. This class is an easy A and a great GPA booster. 6 quizzes, 3 exams (open note), no final! There are optional extra credit assignments. Some of the material can be too in-depth but the lectures were interesting overall. Some lectures are long, but they're interesting enough that it is bearable.

Professor Segert is awesome. I took her online class, and even though her lectures were all videos, she still made it seem as though you're actually in class and actively participating. You can always reach out for help, and she makes sure everyone has a easy opportunity to earn a good grade in her class.

This is now my second class with her and she is the best! I took it completely online and it is an easy A as long as you stay on track with the assignments. Each week is pretty routine and you also learn a lot from her! Love her!!

Professor Gruen is probably the best teacher I have ever had. He makes food science interesting and also lets us know exactly what we will be tested over. Super nice guy and understanding. His class isn't too challenging but isn't too easy. 10/10 would definitely recommend

Took online during summer semester. Hw, labs, and tests were equally weighted so you could do well on everything but tests and still do well in the class. Lectures were recordings that were mostly understandable. TA was mostly available on for help/questions throughout the week. Course was on Canvas, except for hw and exams. Only exams were timed.
Dr. Kosztin and his wife are awesome teachers who make online classes so fun and pretty easy! They are very accessible to help you and want to see you succeed :)
Very demanding, moves quickly. Do your work ahead of time and be ready to study a lot.
Presents material in a way that is easy to learn and study.  Definitely the guy you want teaching you physics.
A pretty cool guy. He does some fun demonstrations in class. Romanian, I think. Short temper though, so definitely don't bring your laptop or let your cell phone go off.
Good teacher.  For the amount of information in the class, I believe he did a very good job at teaching it, although probably not quite as good as his wife.

The course material is somewhat tough, but he doesnt teach it very well. It seemed like I did everything on my own, out of class, which is very irretating. His curve is very good and hes pretty leniant, but he just cant teach very well.

Loved her class. I took Pub Af 4175 - Policy Analysis. Class had only a few assignments so participation was vital. Graded extremely fair and gave detailed feedback. Two discussion boards, a small group project, and one 8-10 pg paper.

50% of class grade was a group project with no clear rubric. Points are deducted based on what the professor imagined in her head she wanted but never actually told the class. Project guidelines were incomplete, vague, and went way beyond what should have been expected for this level of class. Expect to write a 80 page paper worth only 25 points.
Dr. Z is awesome. I took Stat 3500 online this summer. I recommend taking Stat 3500 over the summer if you can.

Dr. Z is okay. I took STAT3500 online and she really just gave a 15 min lecture and expected us to learn the course on our own. However, homework was typically easy and it isn't hard to pass the class if you do well on the homework.

Dr. Zaniletti is an amazing teacher! It is super important to attend all classes or you will fall behind. If you keep up with the content, it is not hard to get As on the exams. Dr. Zaniletti is always prompt at replying to questions via email and will answer your questions even if they're dumb! HIGHLY recommend her-- plus she's entertaining.
She is nice, pretty and she is also the best Prof. in Stat department. Take her class and you will love it.

Genuinely my favorite professor at Mizzou! Can be a hard grader on papers but is very supportive and helpful.
