Super easy class and an interesting professor. He's super passionate about the subject, but the class is very lecture-heavy. Grading is clear and exams are take home and open note.

This class is very interesting and fairly easy. Dr. Monk is very knowledgeable and cares about what he is teaching. Tests are online and open book but can be a little difficult. Most grading categories get a dropped grade. The class material is the most interesting that I have had so far. Attend class and do the work and you will be fine.

Favorite class so far. Uses iClicker for attendance but drops two and also drops lowest test, reading reflection, and in class assignments. Does random in class assignments. Super entertaining and really cares about his subject. It shows in his teaching!

Attend class for iclickers, tests are online so you can take the test based off your notes or with people in your class. He is beyond amazing and this class helped my personal life as well as my GPA. Makes me want a HDFS minor.
THE BEST CLASS EVER! HES GENUINELY SO SWEET!

Doctor Green is unfortunately very lousy when it comes to teaching. In a regular 16 week session, with class twice a week, we are supposed to have 32 class periods. Green cancelled more than half of them and we met maybe 10-14 times. Very sub par grading, as well as teaching style. I would not recommend this teacher.

FINPLN 4483 was a one-hour class. The material was interesting and the class was graded by eight quizzes pass/fail. Many of the quiz questions required outside knowledge and had little or nothing to do with what he lectured about. Also on a couple of occasions I answered correctly but it was still marked wrong. Just be prepared for stuff like that.

I really liked professor Green's personality. He is a fun and entertaining guy.... when he is not teaching the class. Do not get me wrong, I know Personal Finance can be a hard class to teach but he taught almost nothing. I do not know if it is because of the COVID virus, but the whole class was self-taught from the book.

Attendance is not required but highly suggested. Have guided labs that will give visual aid for what you learn in lectures. Tests are hard and do have to study for it, but put in the effort and the class is not overly difficult. He and his TAs do help explain things really well if you ask for it during lab as well. 110% recommend.
Dr. Proffitt was one of my favorite professors at Mizzou! Highly recommend taking him for anatomy :).

You will definitely work in this class. Professor Proffitt is incredibly helpful and intelligent and was very accommodating outside of office hours. You will have to study, this class is challenging. If you work hard though, there's no reason you won't pass. Be prepared to do a lot of outside work.

Professor Endersby is very passionate about what he teaches. However, assignments weren't provided with a rubric leading you to have to blindly tackle papers without really knowing what you were supposed to do. Exams had no study guides either but weren't necessarily hard. Attendance is mandatory but he is lenient on late work and overall kind!
great professor...very knowledgebale and kind
Super good professor beware exams make up majority of your grade

His lectures can get very boring and are simply just reiterations after the first 20 minutes of new content. The class grades consist of a paper, 2 tests, attendance, and a group project. The tests are extremely important as they make up 60% of the course. The first test's mean was around 66%, but it shouldn't be hard if you study. Good person tho.

Endersby is a very sweet, caring and passionate person. He does love this subject. However, it needs work. It is incredibly boring and does not need 16 weeks the way he currently teaches it. He constantly repeats the same topic over and over again with minor variations. It is very easy and does not have really any homework so its a fine elective
really hard in person exams, class grade consists of2 assignments and two very heavy exams. Would not recommend

I will never take one of his classes again. Endersby may have been the one giving the lectures, but the TA deserved the credit for everything else. Class time is wasted, his lectures are boring, and I would use the class time to do other homework (as attendance is required). What he "taught" me I could have learned from a wikipedia article.

Canadian Politics course can get boring with lectures, but he clearly is passionate about the subject. In this instance, there are two tests and one final paper. Some might like this, but it means not a whole lot of cushion. There were no additional assignments to help you understand material either.

Professor Flink is a wonderful teacher who gives great feedback and really cares for your success. This class is a lot of work, difficult, and Flink is a tough grader, but overall I've had a good experience.

Jamie is an awesome teacher! I loved my team in this class. I wish her style of teaching was clearer and that lectures would have been more consistent but overall I would recommend this class to anyone in strat comm and would take a class with her again.

Jamie is a professor who puts in as much work as she asks for. She's so incredibly smart and supportive. I appreciate her for always meeting groups where they're at and helping them out. Be prepared to work a lot in this class. Your group's success depends on everyone doing their role. If the class isn't right for you, drop early in the semester.

This is a really time-consuming, difficult class, so DO NOT take it unless you're willing to put in a LOT of hours outside of class. There are a few major group projects, but you can get some really invaluable work for your portfolio out of it. She was a really good lecturer and knows her stuff. She's a great advertising professional to learn from.

I had her for both 1041 and 3224. She's not as bad as a lot of people say, but there still were issues. Her homework and assigned readings felt excessive for the scope of the class. There was also a language barrier that confused a lot of students. I wasn't a fan of the group setup in 3224, but I understand how most jobs require working in teams.

Dr. Palacios was a good woman, very kind. However, I did not enjoy the setup of the class. It may just be a me thing, but it seemed that the tests and notes/lectures did not match up. Other than that it was not bad. The TA that we had for this particular semester was also a bit harsh. By far just rude and did not seem to help.

Took this online. Point distribution on syllabus did not match up with actual points given on assignments. Examples given in book were not the same as the homework. Material is not extremely difficult but having to teach yourself and apply it on hw can be a challenge. Would recommend this if you need a gen ed econ but not otherwise.

There was almost always a gap in communication between the professor and TA's making it difficult to stay on track in class. The grading procedure for writing the assignments was also very counter intuitive. I would recommend that you avoid taking this course if it isn't a requirement for your major.
If you come to class, you'll be fine. People say her accent is thick, but I understood her just fine. The book is also very helpful. Pop quizzes every week so go to class!
Wrote very few papers, one test and had two group presentations. Almost everyone gets the A if you show up and do your work. Easy class and great for non business writing intensive.

Jamille is an excellent professor. If you had her for Micro/macro econ you probably think she is boring because generally those classes are a bore anyway. She is very knowledgeable and interesting. ASK QUESTIONS! BE POLITE! She is awesome if you get to know her. GO TO CLASS! Duh. O and she's a babe.

Lectures are boring and she has a thick accent so sometimes she is hard to follow. Uses a clicker for attendance but only assigns 10-question weekly quizzes online for homework. Don't miss the quizzes! Exams are essentially the practice questions.
Good luck teaching yourself calc he will not help you and it helps that its online.
This class was online as well as exams. Professor Segert set up great practice exams that would help a ton for the actual exam. Super nice guy and congratulated myself when I did well.

Dr. Segert is a wonderful man. He is a bit eccentric, but nothing that you won't get used to quickly. He cares about students understanding underlying concepts, so he spends a bit more time on proofs than some people like (but not too much). He makes Calc 3 MUCH easier than it could be. If you like math, he's a fantastic choice.

You can really tell Segert knows what he's talking about within 5 minutes of lecture. You can also tell that he doesn't spend a lot of time with people. Still a great teacher. We had a bunch a quizzes but he told us exactly what to study. Read the book. It doesn't matter for tests or quizzes but does for the homework. Go to class.

He's not a horrible teacher; there is only so much one can do in fifty minutes. I appreciate that he allows students to ask questions during lectures. My only warning for this class is to be prepared for self-studying because you most likely won't understand anything that's going during lectures. Read the book and you're golden.

If you love teaching yourself Calc then Segert's class is just for you because you wont be learning much from him this semester.  Good guy, but a very poor teacher who spends way to much time on proofs rather then teaching problems that relate to the homework and tests.

Mr. Segert is an intelligent man but you may find that his lectures are difficult to follow and leave you questioning your knowledge. I would recommend taking a different calc class especially if you are questioning how prepared you are for the class.

Professor Segert is a really nice guy, but his teaching is not so great. He spends most of lecture giving definitions that can be read in the book and that aren't essential to understanding the content. The discussions were EXTREMELY helpful in understanding the material.

The exams are challenging because you have to piece things together. This would be fine and dandy if the class was actually taught like that. Instead I heard a lot of stories and poor explanations. He's a nice enough instructor but does not explain things well in my opinion. Maybe I'm just dumb... (but I did pass the class)

Probably my favorite science professor I had. Exams are conceptual but quizzes are straightforward. This is a class with no shortcuts you need to study everyday. Try to go to his office hours and get to know him he would be a great person to write a letter of rec.

Good luck... this class is hard and will rip you to pieces if you don't read the book. They say it is a "overall concepts" class but you still need to know specific details otherwise you will be lost on test questions.

Dr. Schmidt did an excellent job at teaching.  We had weekly quizzes which were a huge grade booster and the exams were very difficult but we got to take  a copy of the exam home after we took it in class, and get up to 50% more credit on it.  Dr. Schmidt also had offer hours after each class in the cafe.  He's very knowledgeable and helpful.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Mandatory attendance and lectures are boring and useless. Mandatory labs each week too. It is a writing intensive course and time management is critical to succeed in this class. Homework is long and she grades tuff. Only take this class with Dr. Kent if there is no other option.

Jane truly is a gem. She cares about you beyond the classroom and wants you to succeed  as long as you respect her. She gives bonus opportunities, goes over study guides in class, so do not take advantage of how she helps you!! Go to class!! Tests are not easy As, but if you study and meet with her you will do well.
Graded a project four months late that tanked my grade.

Very confusing lectures, she gets off topic a lot, and then adds those random things to the tests. Harsh grader and does not have clear intentions with the projects, tests, or assignments. Good person, but not meant to teach.

Rambles a lot in lectures and often veers off topic. Goes through slides pretty fast and is a little unorganized. Grade is based off exams and a few 100 point assignments, which aren't too hard just heavy. Has a small assignment every day for attendance. Overall very knowledgeable and knows what she's talking about, she's just not for everyone!

The class was harder than expected. Exams were open-note but in person, with questions based on what the professor said ONCE aloud, and not on slides. Attendance was mandatory due to in-class assignments and the grading scale was strict, as only three major projects made up most of the grade, and was graded super harshly by the professor and TAs.

I would take 1,000 more classes from Dr. Lancaster!  She is knowledgeable, comes to class prepared, and really cares about her students.  Writing assignments are reasonable, and solid feedback is given for each one.  When I was going through family struggles, Janna was so kind and compassionate.  I wish all of my professors at Mizzou were like her!

Janna is a great professor. She's passionate about what she does and teaches and it shows. I always get sad when everyone starts packing up early and leaves before she can finish what she's saying. She deserves more respect than that. She is the most wholesome and caring person I think I will ever meet. Highly recommend taking her classes!!!

Amazing teacher! I will be taking as many of her classes as possible. She comes to class with well-prepared lectures and is easy to talk to. Homework is easy as long as you pay attention and take notes.
Boring lectures and is always telling the class to close their computers and phones lol. Easy midterm and final. Projects were kind of fun but sometimes it kind of felt like a high school class.

japheth honestly is just ok. not great. not awful. he takes forever to grade stuff. there is only a midterm, a final, and a 5 page paper due for the whole semester and the only thing that really matters are the discussions bc he grades in attendance. he posts slides on canvas but basically just reads off of those. wouldnt rec. not a fast grader

He has been one of the worst TA I have ever had if you have a chance to switch from him please do, he takes forever to answer any emails and makes excuses about all the work he has to do. if I fail this course because of not knowing my grades in time I would honestly give him most of the credit.

Took this class as a general Ed and my TA Japheth was seriously frustrating. Hes 10/10 the WORST at putting in grades and he makes a LOT of excuses. I currently have NOT ONE grade in canvas. Its Dec 16th. Dont know what my grade is and grade cut offs are tomorrow at 5pm. I just emailed to see what it was. He said I had to wait till 5pm to know...

He never once put in a single grade and complained the entire semester that he didn't know how to work Canvas because it was "broken" when it works for everyone else. We didn't even know our grades until he emailed them to us in November. He also gives way too much info about topics which doesn't help at all when asking a question.

I ab didn't take this class bc of reviews about the difficulty, but im so glad I did. It takes a lot to get me to consistently show up for lecture when attendance isn't graded, but Dr. Schroeder's teaching style was genuinely engaging Tests are challenging but if u make a good cheat sheet and use critical thinking its not hard to get a decent grade

This is not a difficult class, despite the other reviews I'm seeing. The tests are open note, you just have to pay attention during lectures, which are engaging. Dr. Schroeder is fun. Just don't forget to do the weekly quizzes.

Like everyone else critiquing Schroeder on this site, his exams are really difficult. He is a good professor that's clearly dedicated to the subject of communications law, but if you just take care of the weekly quizzes and iclicker outside of class then you shouldn't bother attending his lectures.

Jared Schroeder is one of those professors that kept me wanting to come back to his class. The tests are hard, don't get me wrong, but the class content is interesting and professor Schroeder makes it really engaging. As long as you take notes during lectures, and make a study guide, you will exceed in this class.
Go to class. Schroeder does a great job with the lectures, you just have to set yourself up for success by attending class and taking good notes.

It is so refreshing to take a class with a professor who clearly cares about the material. Dr. Schroeder is such a fantastic lecturer, pulling in real-world examples for all the content. Also, for the 3 tests, just study, bring your notes and prepare to actually apply what you've learned, and they aren't bad at all

I know everyone says that the exams are tough, but I think it's just because the tests are application-based, which I feel better prepares us for real-world application instead of memorizing cases or definitions to just forget after the test. Show up to class, think about the lectures critically, and you shouldn't have a problem.

The professor is funny and nice as can be but his tests are impossible. You can study for hours and write every single word that comes out of his mouth into notes and the test will still be nearly impossible unless you can find out exactly what trick he's playing throughout each of the 50 questions within a 1 hour and 15 minute time frame.

Jared Decker is good at explaining course material and very open to discussion and questions. Lectures are thorough and have lots of real world applications/examples. Daily problems are assigned after lecture and are sometimes difficult with no opportunities to redo and resubmit if you're incorrect.

The exams are online and you have one week to complete them. In addition there are daily problems that go along with lecture. There is an essay at the end of the semester and he throws some extra credit in there.

Last 8 weeks of the semester so lectures are every day but only 20-30 mins. Daily math homework that is either fully correct or wrong. No partial credit. About 80% of the problems are easy. Definitely make friends in the class to compare homework answers (allowed). 2 exams but are fairly easy if you take notes. One final paper but super easy.

I never liked history before this class, but he's an amazing professor. It's also a great honors course—we do a bit more work, but the discussions are the best part. He always clears up my questions and makes things easier to understand. Take this class!

Jarrod was amazing. He is very understanding and gave clear instructions in class. He also cracks dad jokes every now and then. I highly recommend having him as a professor. However, there is a lot of homework and quizzes, but they are all very easy, you just need to show up to class and be honest in your reflection papers.
He is super nice but pretty boring to listen to. He is pretty helpful, but kind of a tough grader. Makes you read a lot, but will help give you the answers you need for everything

Jasim is probably the best professor/ TA I have ever had! Jasim showed a passion and interest in the subject and showed up to class dressed professionally and on time. During his office hours, he wanted to make sure you actually learned the material and was determined to teach it to you through various methods. Overall 10/10. Jasim is brilliant.

Very nice professor! He tells you what is expected of you in this class from day 1. His grading format is different from the norm which he makes it based on how much you grew. Exams are difficult, but he is very accessible and very caring. Getting a cheat sheet is also really helpful. 10/10 professor!

Super fun class, if you're scared because of your experience with chemistry don't be, it so much better. Furrer is a really engaging professor brings in real world problems to keep students engaged. There is opportunities for extra credit which is helpful. Of course the doggies and candy is a huge plus!!

Dr. Furrer is extremely passionate about teaching which made Micro2800 so much fun for me. I'm not usually someone who enjoys science, but Micro was easily my favorite class this semester. He's an easy grader and often gives extra credit/bonus assignments/points, and encourages students to ask questions and challenge themselves. He's AMAZING!!

I LOVE DR FURRER!!! He is an AMAZING professor. The class is challenging and carries a lot of note taking, all outside of class, but I would 100% recommend it to anyone. He gives a lot of extra credit in the lab, and for doing the kahoots in class. He truly is so passionate about what he teaches and I loved this class so much.

Genuinely the greatest man ever. Also the freest class you could take. I got an 86/100 on the final but he gave 15 "free" points for it so I ended up with an 86/85. The lectures take a lot of time and I almost dropped the class after the first section because it was so boring but I'm very happy I stuck with it. Brings dogs to lab and gives candy!
a true king

While this class was very hard and test were intensive, this class was worth it because of Furrer. He genuinely cares about students as an individual and that you are actually learning. He brings his dogs to class and also has a candy cart that he allows his students to pull from. If you have a learning disability make sure you have extended test.

Dr. Furrer WANTS his students to be successful!! I have never had a professor who was as caring and respected in their field as he is! You can tell how much he cares on the topics he teaches as well as your performance in the course.
Don’t ever learn anything in the class. Super boring.

Jason takes the time in class to get to know you. He allows the class to be a safe space for discussion, where all viewpoints can be expressed. The class felt almost therapeutic, and I felt comfortable expressing some things to people I didn't know amazingly well because of how well Jason made us all feel like part of a community.
Jason is hands down the best professor I have ever had. He took time to get to know each student and relate to them on a deeper level. He is very flexible and willing to work with you.
Awesome class and awesome teacher. Easy A if you show up, pay attention, and do the assignments well.

I truly believe he is a nice man. But he treats his adult students as if they are still in high school with strict attendance policy, and long lectures about obvious topics. Teaching style does not reflect the industry or any real working environment I have been in being an industry professional for 3 years now.

The most tedious professor I have ever had- takes attendance way too seriously, does way too much. Lectures are pointless and hard to sit through. I'm exploring the PRST major and he has made me not want to be a PRST major. Talks way too much about himself, literally cannot stand him as a professor but the class is easy.
This guy is an absolute dawg. Cares about what he's teaching and has a lot of background in the field. Highly recommend this guy if you're intrested in the degree!

The work he assigns you is the most tedious, pointless, time consuming things you will ever do in your life. He makes you do journals about YOUR experience at work, and then will take points off for whatever reason he thinks as if he was at the job site. Just get out if it while you can.

Easy class but his work is very outdated would post post links that were old and had templates of professionals in the field that no longer worked for the company he had posted, overall easy class but his work is old and he seems to be very outdated with his knowledge of the industry.
He was very light on grading and pretty funny and easy going. Topics in this class were very simple with minimal homework. I hope to take one of his classes again throughout college.

A very easy class with points for showing up! Professor Young was very passionate, but personally lecture could get boring when it was all stuff that's kind of obvious. If you attend each lecture, you don't necessarily need to read the textbook closely.

His class was very easy and ended with an open note final. It is graded on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory, and doesn't factor into GPA. His lectures do heavily revolve around using iClicker, which he puts a location lock on so you do need to attend class. He was very nice, and was open to answering questions regarding your major after class.

He's an industry professional so he knows what he's talking about. You don't need to be Picasso just do your best and show effort. Caring is the best way to get an A in this class. If you are a film buff get ready for a real conversation. Overall he's a great teacher, and stays after class frequently to help students or just talk about anything.
He's very chill, simply do your work and show effort! He is very easy to talk to about assignments and encourages participation. I would definitely recommend his class!

Dr. Grashuis was a good professor. This semester was the first time he had taught Statistical Analysis, so his lectures were a little sparse, but he was always available outside of class. He sometimes brings in baked goods for people who can answer questions the fastest, so studying is encouraged! 3 tests, weekly homework, 1 group/solo project.

Called Title IX Thelen. Earned it. You don't know what to actually study--just how to listen to him go on about corn. So. Much. Corn. It's his research, so it makes sense, but you will end up crying because corn was discussed instead of whatever insanity goes into making his tests.

Dr. Thelen is clearly knowledgeable, but he tends to skim quickly through slides and read off them verbatim. He is a tough grader, but exam performance tends to improve over the semester. Office hours help if you come in having a basis about the material and questions at the ready.

Overall not a horrible class but a little tough, exams are very specific and account for most of your grade. His lectures are really fast in person with a lot of information on each slide, but posts lectures pre-corded online that are helpful. Readings are really long but helpful. Homework load is light. Attendance not mandatory.

What you get from Dr. Sexton's class is what you put into it. Do the readings and pay attention to the lectures and you'll do just fine. He doesn't grade his own students' work now, but he has TAs (some from  The University of Oxford). 

Dr. Sexton is extremely knowledgeable in 19th century studies. I looked forward to his classes each week.
Learned something new every class. Every history major should take Jay.

Dr. Sexton is a very captivating speaker whose lectures are informed by his vast knowledge base. If you pay attention and keep up on your reading, you will definitely be able to do well in this course. Plus, if you're a history buff, you may receive extra credit if you can answer questions in class pertaining to mid-eighteenth century history.

Professor Sexton is extremely knowledgeable when it comes to the Civil War. I found his lectures to be very interesting, and he was always up for answering questions or repeating information if needed. There is no homework for the course; however, you're expected to stay up to date on your readings, as there are weekly quizzes. GREAT PROFESSOR!!!!!
Genuinely amazing professor!!! His lectures are hilarious and very easy to follow if you do the readings on schedule. Only hard part are the quizzes but they're light work if you show up to class.

Styled the class similarly to an AP History class. Very good at keeping me engaged and interested in the topics being discussed. Genuinely makes the class so much more enjoyable just because he is the professor.

Jay Sexton is an amazing professor. He clearly knows his history well, as he has very in-depth lectures with a lot of interesting stories in the mix. He does not allow technology at all so you have to take hand-written notes but that just makes you pay attention more. He gives a lot of in-class and out-of-class extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Sexton is truly an amazing professor, he is incredibly smart and has an amzing ability to share his kowledge in a fun and informative way. I honestly did very little of the reading, find summaries online and pay attention before quizzes and you will do fine. All tests are in person now, but they went well. Try your best and talk to the TAs!

Rude awakening from the modern read and discuss poli sci experience. 4 tests + attendance with no excuses other than illness. Generous extra credit for lectures is nice, but somewhat necessary. You will need to read every word in every reading, but you'll get a good amount of info for the test from the lectures. He's funny and nice though.

I love Dow! His class is really fun and I enjoyed all of the essay prompts. The discussions are great if people feel like talking, so just get him to like you through talking when he goes quiet and you're basically set. He says essays should be 500 words but doesn't check, so just keep your writing generally concise and you're good.

Dr. Dow is great! He's super funny, has a ton of energy, and really cares about all of his students. He makes what should be a very boring class fun and overall brings a great vibe to class. While his grading can be a little confusing, if you meet with him and discuss what you did wrong, his feedback is very helpful.

Dr. Dow is a nice person, but a difficult professor. The class was graded on 4 exams and attendance, with optional seminars for extra credit. You won't pass the exams without almost perfect attendance or reading the required book. Exam questions also felt abnormally difficult. If you aren't a good test taker, I wouldn't recommend this class.

Super sweet guy, 3 midterms and a final & if you do not read the textbook, you are so incredibly cooked. Visit him for office hours and if you score bad on a test, make sure you see him ASAP for help and he will give you tips on how to do better next time. All and all, he's a great guy, lock in for his class though.

Prof. Dow is a clear instructor. A lot of the work is done in class, and he lectures in a very easy to follow, articulate style. He stays in the intellectual mainstream — you'll read for standard interruption, and very rarely encounter critique of the Founders.

Dr. Dow is a very sweet guy. He also is the most confusing grader in the world. I consistently received the same feedback that I had no thesis regardless of how I moved or phrased it, and eventually resorted to bolding it so he would see where it was. There's a lot of reading, but as long as you pay attention in class its fine- I suggest annotating

Professor Dow's class is intense, but engaging. Attending lectures is a must - he moves quickly, but his passion shines through. Utilize the textbook and study tools like unstuck AI to stay on top of the material. Manage your time well, and you'll do great.

Joe is my favorite teacher I have had ever. A real stickler for attendance and expects students to care. But, if you show that you are ready to work on your photography and push yourself he will make sure you are achieving your best. This class involved a lot of outside of class time so be prepared. I cannot recommend this class enough.

Joe is an amazing photography professor and helped push my photographic skills more than anything else in college. However, you only get out of the class what you put into it. Don't take this class if you aren't serious about making work. Classes are 2.5 hours long and more time is required for shooting/editing outside of class.

Teacher is fair, funny, cares a lot about his students, gives detailed feedback to help students improve, and is very into relevant social issues. Class is a huge time commitment though, so if you're a very busy person already then this isn't the class for you. Grading wise very easy, if you turn in everything you get at least a B

Joe Johnson was (and to this day still is) one of the toughest professors I've ever had. It's not impossible to do well in his class, he very clear on his expectations and sets the bar high. To succeed you need to attend class, participate, do your assignments and be ready to be challenged. If you work hard it will pay off, in and outside of class.

He is a great professor. One of the best at mizzou, but if you take his class you have to be prepared to put in an effort. He only wants people in his class who are willing to put their best foot forward. Having him as a professor has shaped my college career.

Joe's absolutely wonderful. He's highly intelligent, and he brings a lot of great points to the table. He's honest, and he truly cares about each and every one of his student. However, he does not go easy on his students. You most definitely have to put in work for this class. Tough skin is also a good thing to have because critiques can be brutal.

love-hate relationship. Hes passive agressive and brings his political opinions into the classroom too much, but is really smart and helpful when it comes to photography. Believes in students. Expects a lot

Photography is at the center of Joe's heart. He knows and has worked with many renowned photographers. Joe is brutally honest with his students/their work (outright rude sometimes), but usually right despite his harsh critique. Don't take this class if you want an easy A (if you do everything well, you get a B).

I took Archst 4325 (Energy Efficient Building Design) and he was an amazing professor. While the homework assignments were a little lengthy, there were only 3-4 throughout the whole semester. His lectures and quizzes were also not too bad, and you have a couple attempts if you didn't understand on the first one.
Aman is great! He is very strict with his standards, but also very clear about them. Everything he has you do is for a good reason, he has good intentions. He wants you to succeed.
Very good. Started off harsher but accepted criticism and became very sweet.
Her comments on graded work are blunt, but most students still get A's. She's old-school, but you'll actually learn.

Took her for Phil 2482. Guess my last review was too hateful and got taken down. So, I'll give it to you as nice as possible: Intelligent person, abhorrent professor. 10 weeks in: not one grade in the class. Modules posted late every single week. Save yourself the headache and just take it in person.

She graded 200+ assignments less than 12 hrs before grades were due. She also uses her own grading system that is not standard and not listed in the syllabus, really making it difficult to know your grade. She does not post materials in time. She does not respond to emails. Too much work. Never again

PHIL2440 Online

Every week included 1-2hr video lecture, 10 discussion posts, quiz every other week. Course load is heavy for 3 credit hours. Nothing was graded until finals week.

Material itself wasn't hard, but an extremely tough grader. Didn't publish modules on time and wouldn't answer emails in a timely fashion either. We had 2 papers worth 30% of our total grade; neither of which were given a rubric for until after we had submitted the paper, making it impossible to know what she wanted. STAY AWAY FROM HER

Didn't grade anything of mine until the last week of class. We had mandatory 10 discussion boards a week, all worth a whopping 1 point each. Awful at responding to emails- didn't even respond to the ones I sent. Posts material late every week and seems super disorganized. Don't take her if you can help it, she sucks.

Was one of the worst teacher that I have ever had a class with. Does not provide a grading rubric for the papers due which are 30% of the grade. Post assignments late and expects them to be due two days later. At least six discussion posts a week as well. DO NOT take her class.

She is a very good teacher, but she did not provide good resources to succeed in this class. We were assigned work to do, and it was due the very next day. There was tons of homework that was not unrealistic with deadlines. She also only did mp3 files and no visual lectures. I would not take this class with her.

When it comes to Dr. Parsons, I enjoyed her lectures and liked her on that end. But when it came to the discussion section she was irritating. (If possible take a different discussion person for the class, there are multiple TA's). She's a tough grader on the papers and her comments aren't helpful, and good luck if you aren't the best at papers.

Every time I work with Prof Abbott I am reminded why traditionalism kills journalism. She is incredibly difficult to interact with at a base level and comes across as patronizing. Her critiques of stories and pitches are senseless, and she breaks down students until they have no confidence in their abilities despite having quality work.
She is very hands-off as an editor. It is difficult to go to her if there are issues or if you have questions, I have found that I leave frustrated or still confused.

She's very hands-off with the students she edits for. She never clarified her expectations during editing for RW 2 and would try to cut my stories to half their content. She didn't understand that assigning extra sources would make my story take longer and then tried to cut an entire source after telling me to talk to someone else.

Abbott may seem ditzy, but she really knows but she is talking about and I have lots of respect for her. Her class may have little direction and be difficult, but If you go to her outside of class about how to improve, she is very helpful. At the end of the semester, she even published some of our assignments, which was really generous of her.

Several lectures were certainly controversial with several opinionated points that could be found offensive given the seeming lack of evidence to them. Other than that the content of the class was beyond simple and easy, hardly relating to appropriate college journalism at some points.

Professor Porter is very passionate about the topics she teaches, and her lectures are very entertaining. The class is heavy on readings, but they don't matter a ton. Quizzes and tests are pretty easy and it's mandatory attendance twice a week (she will ask a question in class and you will answer it on Canvas).
Professor Porter's lectures are very fun to attend and she brings in a variety of high valued guest speakers. The weekly quizzes are easy if you pay attention in class.

Professor Porter is very intelligent, but I feel the class was incredibly heavy on readings and videos. This typically wouldn't be an issue, but for a student taking 17 credit hours, I didn't always have time for a two hour podcast. Aside from this, Porter is an excellent lecturer and also had compelling guest speakers in class.

By far the easiest journalism class and professor I've had at Mizzou. Although she said things that were questionable at times, she is knowledgable and very kind. Attendance is mandatory, but as long as you show up and do the weekly quizzes this is an easy A.

Professor Porter was great! The class would be better as a smaller class, and the readings were many, but I loved her energy. Professor Porter did a great job handling the difficult task of explaining her lived experience and getting people who can explain what she hasn't experienced and handled people speaking without thinking with grace.

I think Dr. Porter did her best to manage a class with a difficult structure. We had a huge lecture hall with little opportunities to discuss nuanced topics, so discussion usually fell to particularly vocal and often bigoted voices.  Dr. Porter is very intelligent and assigns valuable readings and other materials.

This class was really important but Porter does rely heavy on outside reading and videos. I know she created and found the material but I don't think she was the one that taught the class. She was an easy grader on most things IF you give in-depth answers. The more thoughtful and in-depth you are, the better you'll do on weekly quizzes

Watch out for this guy. On the day your final paper is due, he will change the due date to the day before, and then lie about it. Take screen shots of your due dates so you can prove it later. He seems okay at first, but he will throw you under the bus.

Dr. Firman gets off topic very easily and his lectures don't really have anything to do with the exams. He also grades on pop quizzes & attendance and it's worth 20% of you final grade, so show up to class. He doesn't change the material year to year, so if you can get ahold of old notes/ tests it will be very helpful.

Honestly an easy A capstone course for animal science students. Show up and take notes. All exams, quizzes, and final are open note/open laptop and easy to pass. If he says help is needed at the turkey farm GO HELP. I received 60 points extra credit towards my quiz grades. Lecture doesn't have any prepared notes or structure so be prepared to write
Tells irrelevant stories during valuable class time. In class teachings and even his "study guide" for the test, have very little to do with the actual test.
Dr. Firman is a pretty chill dude and tells pretty cool stories, but the topics discussed and the way the class is structured does not go along with the test.
Horrible class. Only talks about poultry. Would not recommend.

Dr. Firman has a tendency to subtly insult his students. His lectures are long and unorganized. His blackboard page is also very unorganized. He poorly prepared students for exams, with little guidance on areas to focus on. He does manage to make relatively dull topics interesting and has some good stories.

Professor Stilley is really nice and such a genuine person. We had async class but he still offered lectures two times a week that was not mandatory and recorded it to post in order for us still be successful. The work was average, he works through them in his lectures so make sure you attend/watch his lectures to pass.

Prof Stilley was really great and you can tell he really wanted to facilitate a productive class discussion and wanted to be thorough with class material. There are Monday discussions where you only have to participate once (contribute to a part of the discussion) throughout the semester. He's nice to interact with and prompt with email.

Professor Stilley is such a genuinely nice guy. You can tell he cares about his courses content and wants his students to succeed. He welcomes feedback and in class discussion about the topics that are being discussed. The tests & inquizatives are easy if you study and attendance is tracked with iclicker. He gives you three free absences.
This course was very easy. Read the lecture slides and textbook, and you'll do great.

Super chill guy that loves his students and is definitely passionate about psychology. There's not a lot of homework and what there is is super easy. Tests are online, open note, and open book and the lowest test score is dropped at the end of the semester. Attendance isn't mandatory and he posts all the slides after class.

I took him for Marketing 480 online and he was an outstanding teacher! Great lectures, relevant assignments, fair grading, etc. You will have to present a 1 hour group project with 4 other people regarding a company report. Not too hard if you watch his lectures and communicate with your team early on. Would recommend this class!

Lectures were interesting and Dr Johnson is just a really kind and likable guy. Go to class, he has pop quizzes but you basically get an A if you are there. Tests are straight from the lecture notes, if you miss class get notes from someone. It would be hard to do bad in this class.

His lectures aren't *bad*, but he's the most amazingly monotonous speaker I've ever heard. He speaks slowly and is extremely repetitious, which might be useful if he covered any information you hadn't already learned in psych 1000, but... he doesn't. I stopped going to class when I started falling asleep every time I went. Still have an A.

A great professor! Exams are 50 questions, and maybe five questions come out of the book, but the rest are from the study guide. I found the first and third tests to be easier than the second test. The final was literally pulled from the three tests and it was an easy A+. Dropped lowest test score+15 pts easy extra credit. pop quizzes for points.

Very enthusiastic, made sure everyone fully understood, available for help, gave lots of extra credit, he was very interesting and knew what he was talking about. I greatly enjoyed this class, exams were easy and all lecture based, barely have to open your book, open to students' questions and tries to make class fun. definitely take this with him.

By far the best psych prof I have had at the University.   Jeff is very interested in his field, which helps. The best part was that if he didn't know something, he wouldn't just ramble on trying to figure it out;he just said "idk" BUT, next class, he had done his research, and he worked it into lecture.Attend class and use the book as a supplement

Dr. Milyo is fantastic; his class is demanding but fair. Grading is clear, and he knows his content super well. Homework is optional but should always be done, as it looks exactly like the test. He has a dry sense of humor and makes economics interesting. So long as you pay attention, take light notes, and do homework, you'll do just fine.

I found Prof. Milyo's lectures pretty entertaining and found his style of teaching much more engaging than endless powerpoint lectures. But lectures are not recorded though so you NEED to go to every lecture. Also keep up with the optional homework and readings every week, I did so much better when I kept up with it.
Dr. Milyo is great! He's knowledgeable, super funny with great humor, and a prof that really cares about his class.

Dr. Milyo is a great professor who's clearly passionate about the subject. Attend his lectures (which are engaging and funny) and do the "optional" homework, because you will be tested on all of the content. The tests aren't easy, but preparing a detailed cheat sheet can make them much more manageable.

Professor Milyo is very funny and engaging, which I feel a lot of teachers/professors fail to do. Make sure you really understand the graph, either that be putting the exact graph in your notes and understanding what each variable represents and their relationships, or by memorizing the graph. Do the homework not required, but none of them are busy

The class is 300 points spread across 3 exams with no curve. Other than that grading system he is a very funny professor and has very entertaining lectures. If you show up to class every day, take notes, and write a good cheat sheet you will definitely pass. If I didn't lowkey owe him $14 I would definitely take another course with him

Overall good professor, very intelligent. He runs class the 'old-fashioned' way -- chalk on chalkboard, minimal slides, handwritten notes. Hardest part about the class is the grading -- for 1014H, only the tests were in the grade book (and an optional 5 point paper). If you think you can handle it, I'd go for it. Very nice guy once you meet him.

Great prof. that cares about his students. The grade is based on three tests and an extra credit paper. He gives extra credit on all exams. He is open to talk after class or in office hours always. Pay attention because he gives students money, I got 20 dollars.

He is very knowledgable about this topic, but at times it feels like he expects students to have the same level of understanding. This made it hard for people to speak during discussions, because the learning enviornment was not always encouraging. The class content itself is interesting (although we did have to read a lot)
Don't take this class if there's a better alternative option.

I found Dr. Pasley's class very fulfilling. He is clearly passionate and hilarious if you can appreciate dad jokes. Some segments of the class did drag on (1820s MO politics aren't always interesting) but when Pasley reaches a high point, his lectures are phenomenal. His grading is also consistent and fair, assuming you follow deadlines.

he is passionate about what he teaches, I just don't personally care. i never went to class and still got an A. he gives study guides for all 3 tests and the papers are pick your own due date. its lowkey a perfect class if you can stay self motivated.

A lot of people like to hate on Professor Pasley genuinely because they did not put enough effort into the class as they should have. It is clear from the start of the class in the syllabus the weighting of each category and the due dates for papers. Pasley is very knowledgable and it did not seem like he graded too harshly.

his lectures are very boring, gave us two huge papers and the second half of the mid term was a huge paper that took me 4 days to do. i would recommend taking any other history class the only reason i got a b was because he had to curve his midterm. please choose another history class

Don't take this class if you have other options. There are only 2 papers - one 10+ page, one 4-6 page - that are research-heavy. The study guides for the tests are a list of every term from the slides. Tests include: writing a paragraph about 6 different terms, at least 5 map identifications, and 3-4 essay questions (3-4 paragraphs each).

His lectures are hard to pay attention to, his slides have way too many words and are difficult to follow, and the tests are formatted in a strange way. He also does very little to prepare you for tests and it is extremely unclear what you ACTUALLY need to know on exams. There are also essays required in the class that just seemed unnecessary.
This class was so chill. Required.

Dr. Wintemberg is the nicest woman, and professor, I have ever had. If you are in this course, you will get an A. No exams, content is intuitive. There are some lengthier homework assignments, but I didn't even mind because of how much I love Dr. Wintemberg. Class gives good insights into health issues.
Amazing class and amazing professor. Fair grading and learned so much! Could not recommend more! Class attendance is required but the class is interesting so its not bad

Amazing prof. So sweet and cares about all of her students. Class was very easy and manegable. The only thing that sucked was the group project at the end, but even then it was fine. Clearly knowledgable about her field and great lectures.

Very sweet person. She's very helpful and shows how much she cares about teaching and one-on-one she is super nice. I don't like the attendance policy due to how many days you can miss. Her class is interesting and the quizzes/home works are always doable. She gives clear explanations over what to cover for each week and how she can help the class.

Dr. Wintemberg is a good professor and she is very nice. Her slides are posted on canvas which is nice. She does use iclicker for attendance so go to class because attendance counts for points. There are 5 "homework assignments" throughout the semester and no exams. There is a quiz at the end of each week. Make sure to stay on top of things.

She is an amazing professor and cares very much about her students. Most of your grade is in class participation so be ready to go to class! Not too many assignments and quizzes are fairly easy. Would recommend!!
she cares about her students so much. there's extra credit opportunities and projects, but participation makes up a HUGE portion of the grade. i loved her class.
Had to take HS4300 for my major. Pretty easy and straightforward class as long as you read her lectures and watch a few videos per week. She'd give a few extra credits here and there.

I took HLTH_SCI 4300 as a requirement. Read the lecture materials and use them for the quizzes. Most points are from the discussion boards. Midterm and final are similar to quizzes. There are three papers for the class but are not too difficult. Read the material and you will do well in the class.

Intro to Women's Studies with Jenna Pirok was hands down one of my favorite classes in my college career, and was life changing for me.I had barely considered myself a feminist before her course and I came out red hot and ready to fight after getting proper education on women's and black feminism studies. Some reading, discussion boards, and papers

I loved professor Rice, she was understanding and kind. I did notice that the students who talked during lecture or didn't do the readings tended to complain about her as a professor because she requested the same respect she gave. she offers redo's on her essays. Follow the instructions, write like a college student and you'll be fine.

This professor was amazing at giving feedback and always making time for meetings when they were needed. However, this was not an easy course. She definitely makes you work for your grade and it is a very heavy reading course. 99% of this class was probably spent reading and the readings are quite confusing. However, the professor did a good job.

There are lectures every class, but honestly reading the textbook was sufficient for learning the material that would be in the weekly quizzes and even the midterm. The "essay deconstructions" were a little work because of the very broad prompts, but she was very fair with grading, gave good feedback, and was always willing to help students.

Overall I learned a lot from Dr. Ikuta's class on modern political theory and not just material but how to become a better student and engage with assigned texts more. There is a lot of reading for this class and some days the readings have more text than others but I think that comes with the nature of the course. I enjoyed her & the course!

Dr. Ikuta knows her stuff. She's a bit intimidating, but she has definitely made me a better student. The class requires a lot of reading, paying attention, and intelligently participating in discussion. If you aren't going to do the reading or make an effort, don't take her class because you'll regret it.
Probably the nicest teacher at Mizzou. There are iclicker attendance polls every class worth points, but this class should be an easy A and is interesting.

Probably the kindest and most bubbly professor at Mizzou.  This class was very easy, everything was online but the lectures.  Attendance did count for a grade, there were mandatory polls to take but you could do them at home if you timed it right.  I will say her grading was a little hard, mostly because her TA's grade stuff.

Very intelligent professor, who continues to update lessons for students, based on current literature. Some issues with final test having multiple questions over things that we straight up didn't go over or ever learn. Other tests reflected the notes and what we went over. This was the first time something like this happened.

She had really good lectures with specific information that has helped me a lot in the healthcare field. She is also really good about using proper pronouns, which isn't something that I see most teachers do. The class was pretty easy if you read the textbook. You have to come to class because she gives you incomplete notes online.

Not a good professor. Unclear grading. Homework quizzes ALWAYS have grading errors. Even if you get the question right, will be counted wrong. Unclear expectation. Online tests, but very short time period to take them. Would not recommend.

Dr. Bohanek is both a fantastic person and professor. It's clear from her lectures that she loves the material and teaching. Furthermore, her enthusiasm for development and narrative storytelling is infectious. She's exceptionally knowledgeable, personable, and an absolute sweetheart. I can't recommend her classes enough!
Lectures were concise and interesting plus Dr. Bohanek frequently promoted class discussions. The assignments (essays) had consistent expectations and felt do-able.

Lectures were amazing and engaging. They were also balanced with plenty of discussion and learning was very project based and interactive which I appreciated. She created extra opportunities for us that most classes wouldn't and was always asking us our thoughts and opinions. We thought critically about material and learned so much.

Dr. Bohanek is such a sweetheart! She was so passionate about all of her lectures and really seemed to care about engaging everyone in the material. Since it was a general honors course with a lot of different majors/backgrounds, she encouraged everyone to contribute to conversations. Participation and attendance is definitely necessary.

Dr. Bohanek's tests have nothing to do with her lectures. she spends little time on seriously lecturing about the material, instead she uses class time for unrelated videos and reenacting small snippets from the textbook. all test questions are essay questions. she is totally unclear what makes a complete answer. i asked for clarity and shegavenone

This class does require some reading, but Dr. Bohanek is so helpful and if you do the work and put in some effort, youll be fine. Dr. Bohanek and guest speakers made the class super fun and a great way to learn developmental psychology in an engaging way, with a fresh perspective. Exams are written, but its all stuff covered in class (not boring)!

I really liked professor Bohanek's class and she was amazing at helping out students. There are essays every few weeks after guest speakers but they are very easy and help you tie in information from class. Really tries hard to make the material enjoyable and fun to learn, and it's really appreciated.

Dr. Bohanek does not cover material that she tests over. She grades with a bias. I setup many meetings with her to discuss why my grades where not meeting the criteria for a higher score and she failed to give any clear or helpful answer. She doesn't grade tests objectively. She compares answers between students, so corrects answers miss points.

Love, love, love! Excellent and efficient lectures. Connects with her students and is easily reachable outside of class. The assignments correlate with exams and she assigns papers that are easy and fun to write.
Freaking awesome and so leinant! Greatly appreciated all the help and flexability!

Jen is one of the best teachers I've had at Mizzou. Her lectures are informative and her tests are really easy if you've paid attention in class. I had a small class and she provided an open environment where we all felt comfortable and had great discussions. She's relatable and kind and understanding. Every student who has her is SOOO lucky!

I took this for web designing and since it's online it was ok, but making websites was annoying because it breaks on Github. Since I never met that professor in person, I only send emails and comments and she does have some advice. This class is mainly discussion questions and building your website, nothing much. It does have an optional textbook.

Prof. Selin was an excellent teacher. The class was very difficult, but she mentioned how this class would relate to law school. If you're a poly-sci major this course is a must-take. She is a tough grader but it forces you to really soak in the information. Would totally recommend but this course isn't for the lazy/unproductive type.

Terrible. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS! I don't know why MU puts up with this. TOO MUCH READING- Not Practical. 

*My grad class was not available in the RMP dropbox, btw.

Highly miseducated professor. Believes her personal opinions are so well thought out that they can be taught as class worthy content. Teaches the nuances of state government and the judiciary branch blatantly wrong. Grades not posted,No clear content plan or what info is important to focus on. Twice a week, being in her classroom ruined my day.

Prof. Selin was harsh but fair. Her teaching philosophy is to metaphorically "break" students by assigning a lot of homework in order to challenge your world view. She grades relatively quickly and gives good feedback, but be prepared to answer difficult questions in class. Overall I enjoyed her class, but it's not for everyone.

This class was only graded by 3 short answer/long essay exams. The answers and information needed for the exams were clearly lined out in lectures and outside resources were not needed. I think professor Selin graded fairly and quickly, and her lectures were interesting. There were also a lot of extra credit opportunities.

While the course is challenging, she is always willing and able to help. Will work with you one on one and wants you to succeed in this course. The criteria for exams is different but take advantage of office hours and meetings, you will do well. very happy and calming individual and makes you feel heard. Tough isnt a negative in this class

Professor Selin is one of the greatest poli sci professors I've come across! This is not an easy class whatsoever, but if you take advantage of the help she offers, you will be successful. She is tough, but very fair and incredibly knowledgable. If you are serious about poli sci, take this class! If you don't put in the work, you won't do well!
Do not expect a good grade going into this class. The lectures are scrambled and dont represent the test. Lots of reading. Terrible. Dont take if you have another option

She was very passionate about what she taught and her class was fairly easy. Just a couple papers that are lengthy.

OMG HES MY FAVORITE!! Always remembers everyone's names and makes me think about real world problems with myself during lectures

LOVED HIS CHEMISTRY CLASS!!! After taking this class I have debated switching to a chemistry major.   He makes you work for your grade and that is what made it all the more enjoyable. Chemistry is hard, very hard, so the class definitely requires a lot of work. But Dr. Adams help sessions are great to attend and he is good with explaining things. He is a great guy! He has a lot of passion for chemistry and it shows! He also loves to help his students, so don't be afraid to ask for help. I would recommend going to class because the tergrity videos make me fall asleep and do the homework problems!

Dr. Adams works so well with his students. He understands what we deal with and he makes his class interesting. Homework assignment 23 is being worked on now. That is a ton. Ridiculous. His lectures are all over the place and he seems confused a lot. Not the worst, but not the best either.

Halfway through the semester, we are on assignment 15. These are engineering assignments, not easy little humanities HW or something. When told that this is too much, his response was "Yep. I know." Consumed a large amount of time every week for 3 credits. Course is writing intensive, so lots of cover letters, executive summaries and professional reports. If you wait until the week of you will not do well. Its a lot of work. If you try you get a good grade. Test questions are poorly worded and confusing.  Hes chill
Not the easiest class, but he ddefinitely cares about student learning. The amount of work he assigns actually helped me become a better student. Really glad I had him.
Class material is easy. Homeworks are insanely hard and graded even harder. Impossible to get an A on anything. Exams are off the wall questions and stuff never discussed in class.

He is very odd and quirky. Tends to select favorites and talk to them often and give them breaks. Class is not difficult but homework everyday and it is time consuming. Have to write a executive summary and cover sheet for every homework submitted. He is very helpful but is usually pretty busy.

Dr. Tanner is a great professor who explained the topics very well, but some lectures were lengthy in material because of what we were learning, but he made them entertaining and relevant. Hard because of the concept so you have to study a lot. Lecture was him reading and elaborating on slides for an hour straight making it hard to focus. Really enjoyed tanner! Switched to biochem my sophomore year-so I took this primarly freshman based class my 2nd year, and this class really ensured that pursuing biochemistry is what I want to do.
