I know you are reading this Tanner

Dr. Tanner is honestly a great person. You can tell he genuinely enjoys the subject, but sometimes that makes it really hard to understand what he's saying. He goes through lecture slides pretty fast. You get a notecard and he drops one exam including the final. Its gonna be hard, but that's biochem for you:)
Easily accessible outside of class, enthusiastic during lectures, passionate about teaching, and extraordinarily knowledgeable.

He has a passion for teaching this class! I always found the content to be interesting and would recommend it for anyone interested in the content! Grading isn't very clear and could use some work on grading on time. Assignments due in March and April weren't graded until the final weeks of the semester.

His lectures were very thorough, so showing up and taking notes is a must. It's a reading heavy class, but if you're taking a 4000 level history course, what else would you expect? You need a few different text books, but they pay themselves off with how much you use them. I had Hammer of Witches in my backpack at all times.

Lectures were fine, readings manageable, but he would constantly say extremely inappropriate things during class to be “funny” and took like a month and half to grade his assignments. Which is wild, because he doesn't accept any late work. Clearly wants specific answers in his assignments, but words them so vaguely it's hard to know what he wants.

If you do not need to take this class, DO NOT! It is a very hard class for someone who is not interested in the subject at all. Signed up for it since it fit well with my schedule, but I regretted it by week 2. Beware that the tests are huge and are worth 75% of your final grade. History majors would enjoy this more than I did for sure.

3 exams each lasting 5 hours. It is so important to show up for every class and take detailed notes as the questions on the tests directly relate to the lecture outlines he gives you. Overall a very knowledgeable and funny professor who cares a lot about what he's teaching.

The tests are difficult and time-consuming, but this professor is extremely knowledgable and relatable. His lectures were one of the best I heard from a history teacher, and he often sprinkled in fun examples that helped you immerse into Euro History. As long as you show up to class and take detailed notes, you should get an A or B.

Overall, Prof Frymire is a pretty good professor. His lectures are full of useful stuff and he throws in some jokes which makes it easy to engage. He worked with me on deadlines and was pretty forgivable as long as you attend class.

Class was pretty reading heavy, but overall the readings were interesting. Tests were a bit long, all together five hours, but sections can be taken at separate times. Frymire is very chill as long as you do what you are supposed to. Doesn't respond well to slackers.

He is so rude and blatantly talks to you like you are dumb. He gave tests a week apart and I failed cause it was so hard. This is the first time I have failed a test, I always show up and do the reading and he didn't care to help me at all.

Poor Dr. Zemke has such a bad rep. He's an acquired taste, I suppose, or possibly just not for everyone (definitely not for the faint of heart). Personally, I think he's brilliant and kind (if you get to know him), and I enjoyed the classes I took with him.

Terrible professor, not helpful at all.  Seems to enjoy discouraging his students.  Definitely plays favorites and laughs in your face if you mess up.  He told me I would never survive study abroad - moved to Spain and became fluent.  Only grade below a B I got in all of college.

In seven years of undergrad/grad school and above, he was the WORST professor I ever had.  He belittles his students, and should find something else to do.  I'm so glad I'll never have to see him again.

I am not sure if you call him a "professor" He does not know how to teach. Very unorganized, does not explain anything. You pretty much have to work on your own or in a group to learn the concepts. People like him should not be teaching. The worst teacher I've ever had,

Absolutely horrible professor.  It's almost as if he enjoyed making his students feel stupid.  Constantly interrupted students during readings and reply in the most condescending way. Made no attempt to hide laughter aimed towards those who clearly do not understand. Never available for office hours. Avoid like the plague. He really is that bad.
I learned a lot of techniques from this prof. He works hard to make sure students know their material. It helps to show up prepared. Office hours help, a lot.
Very interesting professor, I'm definitaly taking him again. Love the office hours too.

Dr. Morgan is enthusiastic in his lectures but they can be boring at times. 90% of this class is just listening to him talk. We had 7 Assignments over the entire course plus a couple extra credit assignments. The tests are written but the study guides cover everything on the test. Just put a little effort in and you will succeed in this class.

Dr. Morgan is one of the great OG professors at Mizzou. No other teacher will give you that "college" feeling like he does. He is extremely enthusiastic when teaching which makes the lectures very interesting. He is also a great guy and will help you out whenever needed. He is very understanding. However, tests are very hard. Mostly written.

Try your best to avoid this course, it is that awful. Mark Morgan is stuck in the 70s, his lectures are both dated and dumb. He yells in class about nothing, and often his remarks are offensive and NOT RELEVANT. Horrible randomly assigned group assignments, and the hardest tests of my collegiate career. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Morgan gives long and boring lectures. At times you find yourself what to take notes over and what hes even talking about. He made us pay about $15 in rental movies (even though you already pay $900 for this 3 credit hour class). Grades hard on tests, but gives no feedback on what you got wrong. Dont take his class unless you have to.

Dr. Morgan is quirky. Unfortunately, lectures were very, very dull. If you're interested in interpretation, you may be into it but for those taking this class from another major, it's mind-numbing. I literally only went to syllabus week and test days. SO MANY GROUP PROJECTS and not much support if there are issues with your group. Not hard.

Dr. Mark Morgan is a very likable guy on paper. With my interests in the outdoors and fishing, I thought I was going to really like his class. I couldn't be more wrong. He will take the whole entire class period to go over 3 powerpoint slides that make no sense. He ends everything by saying "okay" and "k" which is very annoying. Wish I could saymor

Dr. Morgan is known for old-school approach but does best to appeal to modern trends & topics. You are responsible for your own performance and must turn in assignments on time or your grade will suffer. Attendance is not required but from someone & many other PRT/CAFNR peeps that retook this course, please show up! He uses all 75 minutes each day.

Morgan goes about lectures and moves on. He does poor job of explaining and elaborating exactly what will be on exams. He seems exhausted most of the time. His old-school approach upsets students to the point where attendance decreases. Morgan does not give credit for students that do attend class; SAD! Find another 2750 instructor; thank me later!

John is a great TA! He is smart, helpful, kind, and fun. His recitation lectures are very good. He explained Chem concepts well and always answered our questions, especially when our labs didn't line up with lectures. He answered emails quickly and reminded us of important deadlines. Don't buy the lab notebook. You can rewrite labs in any notebook.

Amazing TA! No better person to take a lab with. He knows what he's talking about and he gives great lectures in recitation. He's always willing to help and willing to answer any and all questions. 10/10 would recommend him.

Your grade won't be kept up to date on Canvas throughout the semester and you won't see why you get the grade you get on the final, so your final grade could be a bit of a mystery. There are quizzes that are nearly identical to the homework problems, and the lectures don't help much so as long as you do the homework you will be relatively okay.
American Lit was a great experience, the readings all felt very intentional and important to themes discussed in that unit, and writing assignments had a great variety

I liked Evelev! I will say, the amount of reading assigned was definitely overwhelming but he was super understanding and did not require us to speak a lot in class. Would recommend him if you are a shy student!

Professor Evelev is a great professor. I saw a lot of comments that say he is dull or confusing. I don't think he is dull if you actually do the readings and engage with them. He cares about the well being of his students. He is a bit of a tough grader on papers, but he gives a lot of constructive feedback. You can also make it up by participating.

Terrible professor. Expects you to read 10+ readings for one exam, all of which can range from 8 pages up to 30+ pages. Then, he gives you an exam where you have to identify quotes from those readings. They're all basically the same quotes, and it's impossible to memorize all of that. Oh, and a paper every other week. Terribly hard grader. Unfair.
n/a

Great professor! His class is a lot of work, but he is willing to help you get through it. He is a very caring professor who offers some valuable information, and I would definitely recommend it if you are up for a challenge!
This professor is open to feedback and willing to give more time on assignments if needed.

Professor Evelev was one of the most caring profs that I've had. He tried so hard to make sure that everyone was engaged and understanding class. Sometimes his expectations were unclear, but all I had to do was reach out for a little bit of help. Would def recommend him- such a nice guy! You def have to read (obviously-its English!) & attend class!

LOVED HIS CHEMISTRY CLASS!!! After taking this class I have debated switching to a chemistry major.   He makes you work for your grade and that is what made it all the more enjoyable.  You have to be willing to do the practice problems several times.  I did very well on his tests and I would accredit it towards doing the book problems 3 times.

Homework is optional but if you don't do it ur guaranteed a fail on the tests. Don't be intimidated by it being an honors course. An A in the class is a 87-100%. His test have 115 pts possible so even if you miss 15 pts you can still get 100%. U dont have to go to class b/c no in class assignments or pop quizzes. A lot of hard work but is doable

It's a pretty hard class. Lots of lecture material, with not too many examples of when and where to use the equations discussed. Practice the homework problems! Very willing to sit with you in office hours and explain things, but sometimes confuses you more. He is a super nice guy, and loves to make jokes which keeps the lectures from being so dry.

Chemistry is hard, very hard, so the class definitely requires a lot of work. But Dr. Adams help sessions are great to attend and he is good with explaining things. IMO he doesn't provide enough practice problems, so that is kind of bad. Content is difficult and he definitely does his job. SOOO HELPFUL!

He is a great guy! He has a lot of passion for chemistry and it shows! He also loves to help his students, so don't be afraid to ask for help. I would recommend going to class because the tergrity videos make me fall asleep and do the homework problems!

Dr. Adams works so well with his students. He understands what we deal with and he makes his class interesting. He is ridiculously smart in his field and he is more than willing to share his knowledge with you. There are plenty of opportunities to get extra help or instruction which are extremely beneficial.

An excellent professor who really cares about his students.  The HW isn't mandatory & the tests have an average of 75-80 with an 87 being an A.  Attendance isn't mandatory but watching the tegrity videos is very useful.  I recommend watching them at 2x speed as Adams speaks a little slow.  He doesn't blow off office hours.

If you have taken chemistry previously and done fairly well, this class will be much easier for you than for someone without chemistry experience. As for Dr. Adams, he is pretty boring. He always posts his lectures to tegrity, so not going to class won't hurt you. There is 10 extra credit points on every test and there is no mandatory homework.

The tests are definitely tricky, but he offers review sessions before each one. He gives plenty of extra credit opportunities and really wants all his students to succeed.  He's pretty kooky at first, but he knows his stuff. Lectures can be hard to follow sometimes, as he just talks for 75 minutes. But he's so beyond nice and loves to tell stories.

Bob is a good guy. He's funny and likes to tell random stories. If you don't understand things, at the review session just ask and he will clarify it for you. The study guides are very complete, study them and you will ace the tests. I only read the books for definitions, probably could have googled.

Bob is, & probably will be, the most memorable professor during my time at Mizzou. His lectures get a little long-winded but he has some tremendous insight. He's also the sweetest old guy you'll ever meet. The exams are a little challenging but he provides a thorough study guide for each one. As long as you review those you're good. DON'T BUY BOOKS
Bob is a wonderful teacher and a wonderful man. I really enjoyed his class. There are a lot of guest lectures too, which was very interesting

John goes by "Bob" and he is the best professor at this school by far. He is laid back, relaxed and made sure no one was stressed out in his class. The books aren't necessary to buy when you can look up all you need to know about them online. If you need a humanities corse credit, take a class with Bob and you won't regret it.

The class was an easy A. However, during lecture no one could follow what he was saying. It was completely confusing and made no sense, but had review sessions where he almost literally gave you answers to the entire test. The class is easy, but don't take if if you actually want to learn.

By far the easiest class I have ever taken. Honestly, as much as I love Flanagan as a person, I feel like this class was a complete waste of time, even though it's an easy A. He spoon feeds you the information if you attend review sessions. After the first testbefore the 2nd, make sure you attend each lecturehave a friend take notes.

Bob is a great guy who really loves his students. He helps you out with anything you need and just an overall interesting guy. Will always make sure his students understand and are doing well. I'd honestly with he was my grandpa... he's that cool.

This class was extremely easy. You just write up a paragraph once a week and make sure you get the group project done, which can be about anything at Mizzou and has virtually no guidelines. However, you do have to suffer through about an hour's worth of Professor Fuenfhausen's lectures (aka his personal life anecdotes)

Basically the class is easy. You have to do discussions and a class assignment each week. But every other week you'll have a quiz shoving 2-3 units into a 25 question quiz. You won't know what's on the quiz because all he says is put the learning objectives into ChatGPT and good luck. Quizzes are hard!

He is not lenient at all. Absolutely my least favorite professor ever. He is not understanding of unfortunate circumstances that students may have. He is what our high school teachers warned us about. He gives too much material at a time and it's hard to get it all under wraps before the tests every week.

I LOVE Professor Huntley, but I hated geology! It's not my major and I needed a science with a lab, so I signed up. This class is SO HARD, especially if this isn't your area of study, but none of that is Prof. Huntley's fault! Both him and the TAs are amazing, always available for help. Just be warned that this class might kick your butt.

This class is basically him talking for an hour 3 times a week and then telling you good luck on the test. There was 5 exams over the semester that each cover a couple topics. There are no study guides. Just random questions over random topics in his PowerPoints. I studied all the PowerPoints very hard and still struggled a lot in this class.

The lectures are great!! He is very sweet and he knows what he is talking about. As long as you are at class and engaging, you'll be fine. Its the labs that were the most difficult! Half of the time they didn't go along with the lectures. The labs were difficult to understand and under explained. But I would blame that on the TA.

I took Prof. John Huntley's class this semester looking to round out my gen ed requirements. I thought the class would be enjoyable yet slightly easy. Not the case at all. Test avg grades were in the 60's and the lab was not in sync with the lectures. Every lab was going in blind and expected to apply concepts. Prof. is a nice guy. Would not take.
Hes all over the place with his slides. Only uses top hat which had failures often resulting in bad grading. 10/10 would not recommend.

Anyone saying Huntley gives bad lectures probably only attended a couple. Huntley gets very engaged, and excited over course content and gives good lectures, utilizing examples. If you show up to lecture and lab, and do the weekly homework assignments, you will do fine in this class, he even gives extra credit occasionally for attending lecture.
Her feedback is precious. Awesome lectures. Hard grading but valuable.
It's not easy to get A from Dr. Moore, but if you want to learn something and get some real training, take her course.

Lectures for the entire period. I was in a class of 12 students for and she never once asked for our input or participation. She consistently showed videos (sometimes 20+ min) during class- waste of students' time. Would not recommend this class with this professor. Extremely boring with repetitive content and a waste of time..

I had this professor for an asynchronous class and it went surprisingly well. The weekly updates and readings were simple enough and you could easily get by with skimming. Seemed very well versed in the topics and you could tell he had plenty of experience. If youre looking for an easy and interesting class this is a good professor!
Mediocre at best is the perfect way to describe him. He is probably very intelligent, but teaching skills....

One of the worst, avoid at all costs. Exams were all trick questions and contained material that was not in the lectures, slides, or supplemental material. He claimed he was going to curve the course grades and then didn't. His lectures are not helpful and he will not help you if you're confused.

Avoid this professor at all costs. He is a very kind person, but is awful at teaching. The exams seem to have many questions that ask about specific details that were barely talked about. If you have to take this class, I would recommend looking at the video links he puts on his power points. They explain things much better and take way less time.

His tests were rough, when he'd have an extremely low average test score he said it was our fault and we should have studied harder
There was a lot of extra credit my semester, but from what I've heard Green hasn't offered it again
His test questions were so specific they should be written, not multiple choice, to give the chance for partial credit

Very hard exams. Made quizzes online for us. Exams are the majority of your grade, unless you attend every lab. Lab was made optional for us but if you went, there was usually a pre-lab quiz and a post lab quiz. If you do well on all of those, and the quizzes, you can fail all the exams and still pass. TALK TO HIM IF YOU ARE STRUGGLING. He's NICE!

Terrible the only way to get points is through exams, quizzes, and the optional labs. The labs have a post and pre lab quiz that sometimes seem impossible to answer. Not helpful at all with questions and will only answer questions if its to his liking.

Dr. Greens class is easily the hardest class Ive had to take at the University. He takes pride in having a lot of gotcha questions that nobody can answer. Many people had near failing grades and he saw no problem with this. Not to mention he curved those with low grades up by around 15% but not people with Bs.

Horrible class. It is obvious that he is a researcher and not a professor. Hardest class in the entire department. Class averages for his exams were always less than 65% and he didn't see anything wrong with that. Hours of studying seem pointless. Very unhelpful with questions. Tests are very hard to understand and do well. 5 exams about 7 quizzes.

By far the easiest class I've taken at Mizzou. Honestly never went to class unless we had a quiz and still got an A. Jon was chill and I could tell he loves math. Really good at using examples to explain problems but if you took math in high school there is no reason you don't get an A.

He is the best!! He made this class so interesting and helped if you were ever confused. The entire class is a semester-long group project, so the group you get the first week is who you will be with.
Wicked smart, incredibly funny, and passionate about the industry. I learned a LOT

I loved this class. It really is an Easy A if you submit everything, I just didn't turn in a few assignments. Weekly discussion post/replies and an assignment, usually a couple page paper with clear guidelines for grading. Professor is very kind. 25 pts extra credit opportunity given once a semester. 
Online and asynchronous- would take again.
Terrible self-centered professor.

Jon is without a doubt the best professor I've had at this school. He comes to class prepared with content students actually care about and can connect with, is very clear on grading criteria, is talkative and caring with students outside of class, and all around is just an excellent instructor and person. He will help with anything and everything.

Jon Stemmle is incredible at what he does, and you can really tell he has a passion for his industry, and for teaching others about it. He was extremely engaging and I never wanted to miss a lecture because I enjoyed the discussions so much. He genuinely cares about the success of his students, which is hard to find sometimes.

Prof Stemmle is the best. I struggled this year with my mental health, and he was so understanding when I showed up to office hours and explained why I had been missing class, and that I needed help. He really cares about his students passing. Lectures were fun when I went. The take home project was not too bad, just put away time for it.

Prof Stemmle has been one of my favorite professors at Mizzou. The one exam was difficult and the take home project is a lot of work, but I didnt do well on the exam and still ended with an A. He is extremely fast at replying to emails and he wants his students to do well. Use him as a resource! He WILL help you, in class and after graduation.

He spelled out the test/essay questions for everyone but beware and DONT put off studying bc there's lots of terms to know. As for class, I didn't go all the time and did ok, going more may have helped though. However, I'm surprised now that I enjoyed his class and what I took from it (not something typical I say about history).
So sad that this was his last semester... I wish I could've had the opportunity to take more of his classes.

Professor Krieckhaus, aka Vanya, was one of the best professors I've had while in college! He truly cares about the topics he teaches and makes the students comfortable asking questions if they have them. He gives current-day examples for lectures and gives a great historical context of Power and Money in the US and around the world!

I left class each day more confused than when I came in. He's definitely very passionate and open to helping students, but you definitely have to be pretty self-sufficient to study and complete assignments because the lectures won't help very much

Nice and understanding person, however his lectures are confusing and full of tangents. He's big on trying to help by being open to questions, however you'll be more confused after you ask. Show up to class and learn how to use the databases. Read the textbook to understand the concepts. Not hard to pass if you have a basic understanding of stats.

The professor is passionate about this class, and it shows! The tests are difficult and make up most of your grade, but he provides a study guide and is very forthcoming about what you should be reviewing. There is almost never homework! Attendance is not graded, but mandatory if you want to have any chance of success on the exams.
Vanya was an amazing professor. His classes are engaging and open your eyes to just how much government effects us each day. would take another class with him in a heartbeat.

I LOVE VANYA! He is by far one of the poli sci department's best professors. His course on "how government works for you" really opened my eyes to just how much government effects us. He also gave us tools and skills to complete tasks (budgets, taxes, etc.) which was awesome that I can apply this in my life. I'd take another class with him.
Half of the time I didn't know what the professor was talking about and Im not sure he did either. Lots of rambling. His exams were god awful and bent me over like someone who dropped the soap.

He is the best!! He made this class so interesting and helped if you were ever confused. The entire class is a semester-long group project, so the group you get the first week is who you will be with.
Wicked smart, incredibly funny, and passionate about the industry. I learned a LOT

I loved this class. It really is an Easy A if you submit everything, I just didn't turn in a few assignments. Weekly discussion post/replies and an assignment, usually a couple page paper with clear guidelines for grading. Professor is very kind. 25 pts extra credit opportunity given once a semester. 
Online and asynchronous- would take again.
Terrible self-centered professor.

Jon is without a doubt the best professor I've had at this school. He comes to class prepared with content students actually care about and can connect with, is very clear on grading criteria, is talkative and caring with students outside of class, and all around is just an excellent instructor and person. He will help with anything and everything.

Jon Stemmle is incredible at what he does, and you can really tell he has a passion for his industry, and for teaching others about it. He was extremely engaging and I never wanted to miss a lecture because I enjoyed the discussions so much. He genuinely cares about the success of his students, which is hard to find sometimes.

Prof Stemmle is the best. I struggled this year with my mental health, and he was so understanding when I showed up to office hours and explained why I had been missing class, and that I needed help. He really cares about his students passing. Lectures were fun when I went. The take home project was not too bad, just put away time for it.

Prof Stemmle has been one of my favorite professors at Mizzou. The one exam was difficult and the take home project is a lot of work, but I didnt do well on the exam and still ended with an A. He is extremely fast at replying to emails and he wants his students to do well. Use him as a resource! He WILL help you, in class and after graduation.

Professor Kim was by far one of the best professors I've experienced. He made me enjoy learning and genuinely cares about students. He was very accessible outside of class and gave detailed feedback on every assignment. Great professor, and I would definitely take his course again.
Fair. Applicable. Can't complain. Just go to class and pay attention.

His lectures are awful, he talks in circles for an hour. He grades harshly and requires you to answer questions in the exact way he wants them answered or else you won't get full points. Doesn't matter if you got the answer right, if you didn't quote his horrible lecture then you get a C. He also changes the syllabus and doesn't announce it.
Attend class!!!! While it isn't mandatory he does give grades for class sometimes. You can only miss 4 classes

He maintains a very structured and strict classroom. He expects no talking and attention for the whole lecture. Lectures are long and require sustained focus. Classroom policies on phone use, talking, and headphones are consistently enforced, and reminders will be given. I would not recommend taking this if you don't have to

Dr. Booker's tests are extremely long (80-100 questions, ~2 hours long) and his lectures are boring and monotonous. However, he is super generous with grading and knows what he's talking about. You can miss around 3 weeks of class and still get a 100% attendance grade, and he drops our lowest exam and 3 of our lowest homeworks. Easy class to pass.

I would for sure take his class again, I had him this recent semester and I had a 95% in his class. The tests are difficult but studying makes it easy. He has many opportunities for extra credit and allows you to miss a good amount of class + a dropped test grade. I felt very comfortable with being able to score high in this class.

Dr. Booker is the worst professor I've had. He lectures in a monotone, reads slides we already have, and tries (and fails) to be funny. In-class questions are mandatory and tests are hard, often unrelated to lecture or book. He does drop the lowest test though. He calls out students for talking. Total waste of time.

Dr. Booker is very nice and this class is very easy but his lectures are incredibly boring. I would take it again though because you can miss a certain amount of days that get dropped, theres no final, and the exams are open note. He will yell at you though if you talk during his lecture.
Dr. Booker is a very good professor. All exams are online, open book, open note, and there is no final. The class is very easy and interesting.

This professor is awesome! The class is an easy A. Mandatory attendance, but open-note exams (all online). He leaves the exams open for 3-4 days, leaving you plenty of time to take it. Probably the easiest psych class you'll ever take. Also posts the notes online to go back and review. Allows three skipped classes per semester. Overall worth it!

Dr. Booker's Developmental Psych class is an easy A. Although attendance is mandatory, lectures are not too bad. The tests are online and open note, he also provides recordings of lectures as well as transcript summaries for each of them so you don't have to re watch them. Extra credit with textbook material as well.
Professor Pellerito is extremely knowledgeable and personable. I'd absolutely recommend her class.

Jordan is in the upper echelon of instructors at Mizzou. She is so genuine and caring, and is always available to her students by phone, email, AND in her office, no matter what they may need her for (help on a tough concept, concerns about college life, etc.). Her feedback was always constructive and helped me grow as a writer. 10/10 recommend!

Jordan Thomas clearly cares about the material and wants students to learn it. He offers a lot of extra credit opportunities and explains material in a way that is thorough and easy to understand. Tests and quizzes are slightly challenging, but fair.

For repro phys the lecture grades are 3 non-comprehensive exams and 6 quizzes. You get one dropped quiz and he averages the rest of the quizes. There are two lab practical exams, 5 reading, and 5 dissucsion assignments. There is an extra credit book worth 25pts and the class is only 500pts. He also gives plenty other extra credit options.

One of my favorite professors at Mizzou. Would highly recommend him as a professor and the classes he teaches. Grading can take a while and don't always get feedback but if you ask you can get feedback. Accommodating when things come up, fun class, and I have memories from this class I will never forget. No textbook required!

One of the best professors, very caring and always hilarious. Dr. Thomas is always willing to talk through topics and work with students to improve their grades. He is one of the sweetest people out there and an amazing human being. Highly recommend taking one of his classes.

I was afraid Professor Butcher would be super strict, but she's so sweet and caring, and made an effort to get to know every student individually. The hardest thing about her class is there are few things in the grade book, so you have to do well on everything in order to get a good grade. Just show up, do the work and you'll pass the class!

She is the hardest grader and the only grades are 3 exams and 1 paper so if you do bad on one your grade will be destroyed. She goes so fast in the lectures where you cant take notes and doesnt put them on canvas. You have to show up to class for attendance and participation grade.

The lectures and in-class activities were rarely beneficial to learning the content, but attendance is mandatory. There is an unrealistic amount of reading. Tests were graded very hard. The only things the class consists of are 3 tests, 1 paper, and attendance/participation, so you have to do very well on those tests to get an A in the class.

Butcher's class was a smaller version of a typically large lecture style class, which was a great alternative. She got to know every student individually which was wonderful, and she really cared about each student. Only complaint is that she didn't enter grades in all semester (you were given tests/papers back and expected to keep track yourself).

Pretty decent, the class is not hard, and barely anyone ever showed up. It's honestly very easy so if you're looking for an easy A or B just be ready to put in effort for the midterm and final. He assigns a weekly 2 page writing which is annoying and talks a ton. Pretty boring but it's nothing horrible.
Overall good professor. He isn't strict when it comes to grading, but you should watch your grammar and punctuation. Very chill and laidback professor and I'd take his class again.

First day of class he told us he didn't believe in grades and if we turned in our assignments (that we always just did in class) you will get an easy A. Our only assignments were free writing during class and was the easiest class I've ever taken
Wasn't really a fan of this guy. He was very unorganized with classes and I began to skip regularly as they were pointless to attend. He is a great, funny guy but not a great professor.
Just make sure to hand in the important assignments i.e. essays and papers and you will surely get an A.

Eng 1000 with Jordi is great and awful. While the classes are incredibly boring and seemingly pointless, attending class isnt mandatory and it is very easy to get an A. Quizzes are worth 60% of your grade, so if you do bad on one, it will be hard to raise your grade. The only things she grades are quizzes, essays, and a few participation points. She takes off points for the simplest mistakes.

Absolutely terrible prof. She does not teach. You are expected to read the textbook in your own time and all you do during class is answer questions. 4 quizzes are 60 percent of your grade. She cares more about you knowing all the irregularities than being able to understand or speak French.

This class was sooooo boring. Wang is a smart woman, and I respect her a lot. But this class made me want to sleep. Like most one reads, the book is okay, but you never want to finish it. Class drags on, and it's on Friday at 2. What a bummer.

She is a nice person for sure, but not the best teacher. Classes are mostly her just talking and the criteria and rubric for papers and classes are very unclear. I would not take this class again because I did not have a good time at all. All be it, the books were interesting to read and I got a good grade.

It was Fiction in Science, which was fine and sounded like fun. I was ready to read decent sci-fi books. The books she chose were dry and horrible. They weren't super difficult to read. We had in-class discussion and she didn't give us ANY good questions to go off of or anything to promote talking. Terrible teacher and made the class bad too.

She's a very nice person, but not a good professor at all. She goes off on a lot of unrelated tangents, and her grading criteria isn't very clear. Very passionate about the subject, but it can be tough to understand her.

Sweet woman, terrible teacher. She knows so much and conveys it so poorly, leaving us students completely lost. Lectures stray drastically from the deigned topic, her grading is strict and unreliable at best, reviews and Midterms cover completely new topics never seen before. She also is completely unprepared for online teaching.

Kind teacher, mildly interesting subject, difficult class. Reading off powerpoints with *critical exam info* injected during lectures is an easy way to create an unengaging 8 am class. The cycle between exams goes as follows: drowsiness ruins concentration>miss key info during lecture>struggle studying>exam at 8 am>poor results.

She's a great teacher, and if she can tell that you put time into the class, she'll help you find the answers if you're struggling. The test study guides are very good - pretty much exactly what will be on the tests. The quizzes were a little harder, but as long as you spend a little time with the Spotify playlist, it's fine.

Dr. Mabary is a very nice woman and she wants you to do well in her class. There is a lot of material to learn and it's very easy to fall behind. She posts her lectures and she posts study guides for all quizzes and tests. As long as you prepare carefully you'll be fine.
Dr. Mabary is lovely!! As long as you ready the anthologies and listen to the music, you will do fine!

This rating is regarding the Music History courses for majors at Mizzou. Dr. Mabary is very knowledgeable about music history, however, I find her lectures super boring. Nearly every time we meet for class, she reads straight off of the powerpoint. The class is already harder to enjoy because what we study is farther in the past in less tangible.

Super nice teacher who cares and offers unlimited extra credit. If you're willing to do the work and don't procrastinate in your studying you'll get an A. A lot of memorization of terms, which can have weird names. Just go to class and do concert reports.

She has such a good attitude and high interest in the subject. Attend all classes, take notes, review notes, and skim the textbook and you will surely pass (and its not even as hard as it sounds). She is very helpful! You will also have to attend outside concerts for grades, but its not too bad.

You can tell she's pasionate about music. She gets so excited and wants her students to be excited as well. You HAVE to go to class and study the listening examples like crazy. The content isnt always interesting, but Mabary's a sweet woman.
Loved her class!

Great professor, lecture heavy classes but incorporated videos and examples to make the topics more relatable and easier to remember. She cares about her students doing well, encourages questions, and takes time to learn everyone's name. Do have to study to do well, tough tests but nothing too bad compared to other courses.

I love this professor. She's so eloquent and engaging. There isn't a lot of work to do either - just 6 worksheet assignments (she drops the lowest grade) and 3 exams (the last exam isn't cumulative). I learned a ton in this class.

I took Human Language with Dr. Goodman and I loved it. It is a tough class though and you definitely have to study. She's the chair of the department, so she's very knowledgeable, but is very approachable and encourage people to email her or come by her office with questions. Her class is worth it, especially if you're a CSD major.
I took the WI Normal Language Development class. Good class. Hard, but very very good!

Really great professor, fairly hard class.  She is extremely knowledegable and knows the answer to pretty much EVERY question.  The material is really interesting,  tests aren't too bad, but they are the only points of the class (other than one paper), so make sure to study for them.  Overall, highly recommended professor and class.

Great professor.  Is always willing to help you better understand and clarify concepts.  However, her classes are not easy.  If you study hard and out a lot of effort into the assignments you will get a good grade.

LOTS of work in this class - two essay tests, plus a transcription project and a proposal spread over the semester in parts.  Very willing to meet with students outside of class to discuss projects/tests/grades.  Awesome woman, great teacher.

Took this class online to count toward my sociology minor and was very pleased with it! I did not spend much time on this class (maybe a couple hours every other week), and I still ended up with an A+. Interesting subject matter. Lots of readings, but his PowerPoints summarize them well. Exams were quite easy! All the writing graded nicely too.
Awesome teacher! Class is definitely a breeze as long as you read. Downside is there's a lot of reading but what is assigned is surprisingly very interesting. I would highly recommend him!!!

He makes the class very easy to get a good grade in, providing plenty of review before tests and homework problems that are nearly identical to test questions. I typically don't enjoy math classes much, but he makes the class as easy as possible for you.

Miller is one of the most chill professors I've had, I really struggled with the material but he would always patiently answer my questions after class and during office hours. if you show that you care about the class he will help out how he can. Would definitely take one his classes again.

Hilariously bad handwriting but otherwise he was fine. The way he explained the concepts seemed a little heterodox at times and I could see how it might be confusing to some. Probably among the easiest math courses Mizzou has to offer overall, though.
Taught the material well, was helpful and responsive in Emails. Should be the standard for professors, but sadly isn't.

For a basic college algebra class, he explained it worse than any of my high school teachers ever did. Tried to make material easy to learn, but instead, ended up over-explaining + complicating the subject. However, he is very nice and all of the homework, quizzes, and tests are easy. Clearly said what was on each test so you knew what to study.

He looks like Peter griffin from family guy. He's more interested in telling you why it works vs how to do it. Has the worst handwriting for a teacher that I've ever seen. Be ready to teach yourself everything.
super clear with his expectations and prepares you well for tests and quizzes. very fair grader.

Professor Miller is a great teacher, he grades fairly and his exams are similar to the homework and lectures. I've gone to a few office hours and he is always available for questions. If you pay attention in the lectures you will do fine.

Also, he's pretty handsome. I'd give a few chili peppers if I could.
Grading is unclear, barely responds to emails, and the class feels unstructured. Most assignments had no rubric, an unclear assignment explanation, and no submission comment explanation.

Dr. Elman's passion for health humanities is evident, but the class lacks clear instructions and structure. Assignments often had vague guidelines, and criteria changed unexpectedly, making it hard to keep up. I valued the class topics, despite Dr. Elman's political views.

This class is a joke and a waste of your time. Syllabus wasn't followed, assignments not graded until the end of the semester, the assignments themselves were busy work and not college level assignments. She also does not follow the rubric she gives your grading. If I could make one wish it would be to go back in time and unenroll from this class.

Dr. Elman care about the success of her students. She is real + direct. She encourages critical thinking about deeper topics. I learned more in her class with 0 exams than my 1st bio class that had an exam every 2 weeks. All healthcare degrees should require health humanities. Assignments were easy if you payed attention to lecture.
My lowest grade last semester simply because she didn't put a single thing in until the day everything was due, I had a zero in there until dec 15
does NOT follow syllabus and grades everhthjng the last day of the semester
Same this everyone else has said about the grading and not organized

The course itself is not difficult, but prof does not follow the syllabus, doesnt enter grades until they are submitted at the end of the semester, grades things LATE, wont reply to emails and occasionally would change classroom locations with no notice, due dates are not clear whatsoever, and she just didnt seem to know what she was doing… ever.
really funny guy; learned lots
He knows what he's talking about, but he doesn't always explain himself or his PowerPoints very well. The class is also pretty hard so that doesn't help.
Lectures were super boring and he talked in circles. Not a super hard class but not interesting at all.

This class is not fun. Dr. Grayer is nice, but you get lost in the lecture a lot, and there isnt too much structure. He grades based off 3 exams (MC & T/F) and 5 journal entries (easy 100%s). His exams are not easy though. Lots of memorization. Overall, not a horrible class if you need a diversity credit, but I would explore other options or profs.

If you do not learn well from just lectures you probably will not like this class. I wish that there was more interactive stuff but he is a good teacher and definitely knows a lot of what he is talking about. The only assignments that we had were writing assignments but they were pretty scattered so that was nice. A lot of dad jokes too haha.
He usually does lectures but has scattered assignments throughout the semester. He has in-person exams, journals, and analytic papers. He is a little quirky, but overall a good professor.

He's a very nice teacher. Loves memes and jokes. He does three exams overall which are decent. He also does journals and analytic papers. He randomly does attendance. I have him for multiple classes and by far he is my favorite professor this semester.

Julien is super awkward and kinda seems like hes on something all the time - but in the best way. He has extremely millennial humor and talks about memes every lecture. Grades are based on 1-2 page papers every few weeks, a couple tests (not hard for me but Im smart) and a 6 page final paper. Pretty easy grader as long as you format stuff right.

He's genuinely just a really nice teacher. He's a native German speaker, so he's good at explaining aspects of the language from the stand-point of not everything you learn from a textbook will be how its spoken in the real world. He cares that you show effort, but he's patient.

This course makes statistics much easier for me to understand. The lessons were clear and organized. The pace worked well. I liked that we always saw how the material related to real engineering problems, so it never felt pointless.

Dr. Kim is arrogant and unhelpful in every sentence. He shows clear enjoyment in embarrassing students in class. His lectures are useless but required. His quizzes and exams are over material we've barely touched. His grading on reports is rude and unconstructive. He is over-reliant on AI and occasionally uses it in grading.
Professor Kim is passionate about challenging students to think critically and apply concepts independently. His lectures encourage active participation, which keeps the class engaging.

Kim does not explain concepts very well, especially the math portion which you need for the quizzes and exams. He'll cold call you in class to ask you something that has nothing to do with lecture and then make fun of your answer in front of the class. Also everyone tends to average about a C-on all the quizzes and he sees no problem w/ it.

Dr. Kim is a fairly nice and energetic guy, but not a gifted professor at all. His class tends to follow the lines of "study for my class 24/7 and maybe you'll pass." He is horrible at explaining concepts and his processes, especially when it comes to his math portions of lectures where he skims over everything you need to know, leaving you lost.

He still has an old-fashioned technique to "study hard" for exams. His interaction with students is fine but sometimes he makes inappropriate comments. My experience with his office hours was not the best, and indifferently gave me a feedback . He knows the subject well but lacks on teaching strategies. I would not take his class again.

Ergonomics was a very interesting class! No homework, but instead there are five big papers due throughout the semester. Focus on these and make them the best you can. Pick a good topic for your project, it will help in the long run. Quizzes every Tuesday, so go to class to know the material. The second exam is the hardest. Great class overall.

Kim is high energy which I like a lot, but this class was just not fun. The homeworks take forever, Chegg will be a necessity for them (will still take 5+ hours). He will call you if you skip class, so go. Content is not very interesting and his slides come straight from the book. Exams were challenging but doable. Lectures were long. Work hard!
Great Teacher. Best teacher at Mizzou.
One of the best instructors I have ever had. Class is fun and very Interesting. Great elective History course.
The best man alive. Definitely take his class, especially if you love law or the Constitution. As long as you listen to the lectures, you'll do well.

I took this class in fall of 2020 and it was fully online due to COVID-19. I was initially nervous but Dr. Dyer's podcast lectures (I listened on Apple podcasts) were really well done. There were no exams for this online class, but weekly quizzes and 3 papers. You need to be good at writing about the Constitution. Overall a great professor.

Very intelligent professor and does a great job of portraying topics in a non-partisan way. Course content is interesting and relevant. Tests are challenging but doable and fair. Overall, great option for a poli sci professor.
Dyer is a good guy. Show up to lecture, take notes, and use the study guide.

Final is 50% of grade. Doesn't activate canvas grading page. Syllabus doesn't have dates and doesn't use slides or powerpoint to stay on topic. Gets off topic easily & spends most of class talking with over-eager students about concepts loosely related to topic. Learned more from the website Oyez & txtbook, but have to go to class for pop quizzes.

Not a loud lecturer, so sit up front. Gives study guides for Exams. The exams are pretty easy, but they lazily do not hand back your exam in class, you have to go to the edge of campus during office hours to get it. When you read the textbook just note the concepts that are brought up. Don't ever worry about reading the "Comparative Perspectives"

Decent lecturer, definitely knows his stuff and keeps you engaged mostly. 2 exams are very easy. The essay was kind of tough, but doable and has a rewrite. Doesn't take attendance but does 10 pop quizzes. Easy if you show up and drops the lowest one.
Amazing teacher and one of my favorite classes so far. He presents the material in a very organized and interesting way and really cares about his students' learning.

This teacher is so nice. Office hours are super helpful and he's willing to answer every question in a way that is easy to understand. He makes sure to ask if there are any questions while going through the practice problems in class after every topic or difficult problem to make sure everyone knows how the answer was found. Would recommend.

this guy is awesome, hes the chillest guy ever and so fun to talk to. tests get graded as such: 1 mistake= earn half credit and 2< mistakes= earn no credit. tests are short, hw quizzes every week, hw is kinda long. but if y'all have any choice of teacher, TAKE THIS GUY YOU WONT REGRET TRUST.

Great teacher for Calc, he didn't have much freedom because it is a 900 person class in sections and coordinator is very strict. You can tell he cares and understands the material well. I would suggest going to class because there is not a recorded lecture. Quizzes every Wednesday, he gave occasional days off if we got ahead of schedule.

Loved him as a person. I just personally had a rough time with Math 1400. I know people who I clicked for and people like me who had to scratch and claw to move on. Overall, he would give extra credit and give you points whenever he could. Very fast lecture style. I would NOT take Math 1400 if it's not required.
Very chill and approachable dude. He taught well enough that I could skip most classes and still get high grades. Very easy, highly recommend. He's super nice, I want to be his best friend.

Always helped and tried to give as many points on the tests. During quiz gave extra credit for writing our favorite song. Easy to understand and good at answering/explaining questions. Maybe don't take the 8 am... wanted to fall asleep in class. (Not because it was boring just because I was tired and didn't want to lock in that early lol)

Overall, he's a great and helpful teacher. Gave effective and easy-to-understand lectures about the subject matter and willing to give help outside of class. I had a few medical issues the semester I had his class but he was always willing to be accommodating. Also, he's just a very kind and fun guy, definitely recommend taking his class.

Great professor, and a super nice guy. Has good office hours to get help. Seems like he does not have much control over the course as their is someone above him controlling everything. 3 exams and a final exam. weekly homework that can suck as sometimes you will have 100 homework questions. also have weekly 2 questions quizzes. Overall good!

Professor Butler is an incredibly tough grader, and there is no way around that. You will have to work very hard to do your best writing and follow his rules. You will read the entire textbook. However, he is a very kind person to interact with online and he will improve your writing skills. If you are not a strong writer, do not take this class.

He makes sure to ask if there are any questions while going through the practice problems in class after every topic or difficult problem to make sure everyone knows how the answer was found. Would recommend.
