Overall good!

The professor is very caring, with his unique spin on teaching. Can be a little quick, but posts the lecture so very helpful. Very helpful when asking questions and makes the class really fun. Wished he taught honors OChem.

First of all, the first class of the semester he started lecture by reading his negative rates on this site and told us all why they were right or wrong. The class can be tough, but Walensky was great. There is a lot of work right before tests and the tests are stressful, but if you sit down and work it is possible. I did enjoy this class.

Even though this class is lecture focused, the lectures fly by with the way he explains the material! This was his first year as a professor and he did great! Study guides are clear cut, grading system is fair, and overall a great class!

Walensky is a good Professor, and if you attend lectures it is clear what questions will be on the exam. Since the class was online, tests were open note and you could use things from Canvas. Due to this there really isn't any reason to do worse than a B-, so you should really learn your way around his canvas. It will save you Alot of trouble.

He's probably one of the most sarcastic teachers I've had, but he does explain throughly what the concepts are. Tests are average you really just need to pay attention in class which can be long. He also gives grade boosts through other assignments (but they can also hurt your grade) so do them early so you don't fall behind.
Dr. Walensky is beyond amazing. His sense of humor makes the class even more enjoyable and he is very helpful when approached with questions. As long as you study the material, its an easy A! :)

I took Dr. Walensky's class during the pandemic, which I thought would be a real challenge. However, I somehow found myself looking forward to a chemistry class (not usually my thing). His jokes provided a break in my hours of online lectures. Tests weren't too hard, and he posted plenty of practices. Highly recommend any class Dr. Walensky teaches

Chem 1330 was the first chem class I actually enjoyed including high school chem. He convinced me to minor in chem and the class is super interesting. It's a bit fast paced and the tests aren't the easiest but they're not hard if you do the practice problems. Super accessible outside of class and generally a great professor.
Really not cut out for virtual learning. Grading was scattered confusing and not transparent. The quality of instruction given had a lot to be left desired.

Sweet woman, definitely not cut out for an online format. I personally struggled in this class because it moved very quickly and Frau Gray didn't really know what she was doing which made it even harder to try to learn. I definitely would not recommend taking her class unless you are confident you can teach yourself a new language.

Dr. Lewis's class structure facilitates a healthy learning environment where all questions are welcome. She frequently asks for feedback on her class and is willing to make changes to the syllabus to support our learning. She's always willing to laugh, joke around, talk, give advice, and have serious conversations with her students!

Dr. Lewis was incredible! Her lectures were detailed and she is very passionate about this class. I missed a lot of school due to illness and she was so accommodating and caring. Course was not easy but not overly difficult. Come prepared for discussion every class. Every professor should be like Dr. Lewis!!!!!!!

Dr. Lewis is a great professor who is passionate about what she teaches. She's patient and understanding of any problems or questions you may have, and is very accommodating in my experience. As long as you watch the lectures and do each weekly assignment, you should have little to no problem doing well in this class.

This is one of the best professors I have had at Mizzou. She is so caring and works so hard to do what is best for each of her students. If you ever have the chance to take her classes, DO IT. Absolutely loved her and her teaching style. Amazing professor. 10/10.

Kamau is one of the best professors I've had at Mizzou- he's extremely kind and caring with his students and understands your course load outside of his class so he's easy about late work or extensions. Lots of the assignments are completed in class, with hands-on experience and feedback from Kamau as well which is super helpful.

As a person, awesome. As a teacher, maybe too chill. Hey, I'm not complaining. I had a tough academic semester, and I liked being able to show up and just chill. However, we had a real slacker class, so it felt like he didn't push us too much. And that's kind of really on us, but kind of sucks for those who want to be pushed.

I took his Cinematography class and he's a very chill professor. You can tell by the feedback that he gives that he knows what he's talking about.. He grades his students fairly so if you put in the work you'll get the grade you want. He starts out every class asking about any new films we've watched, giving us a chance to chill out before class.

I took his Intro to Cinematography, and he was pretty great. He's very laid back, is open to lots of ideas, but not afraid to critique as well. There isn't a ton of lecturing, just class discussion, and working on projects, practicing with equipment. Overall, really good experience and no pressure, just encouragement and good feedback.

Kamau is a very laid back teacher who lectures occasionally.  He gives good feedback and is very encouraging when it comes to student's ideas. I took his intro to cinematography class and he only gives very quick lessons on how to use camera and lights, minimal stuff on how to edit.  Overall, Its a fun class to get some video good projects in.

Professor Seo is a nice guy, and he is accommodating if you talk to him. However, math students may feel unsatisfied with his explanations. Pop quizzes also make you show up every day because your grade will suffer otherwise.

Seo is a kind professor, but most of the time in lectures I have no idea what I'm even learning about, even taking notes the night before. The concepts are so abstract, and there's a lot so you really have no idea what is important to have remembered, exams can be hard. Not to mentioned he gives pop quizzes, so you have to attend class.
Make sure to take good notes, exams rely heavily on understanding the homeworks so make sure you understand them. Lets you have cheat sheets on the exams which helps a lot.

Seo was thrown into this class without prep so I will cut some slack. He has neat writing and works out a lot of examples on the board in class. However, his lectures were VERY slow and hard to sit through. There are 10 homeworks, 2 midterms, and a final. Read the book, it helps! He is a nice, lenient guy, but could definitely use more preparation.

Professor Starnes was a good professor, but lacked feedback from students. The whole semester you work on a group project, with no clear instructions.  There are 2 extra credit opportunities during the semester. She also takes foreverrrrrr to grade.

Starnes is a great human. She facilitated a classroom that was so lively, and one that I actively looked forward to in my days. I've made friends in that class that will hopefully last for a long time. The textbook reading sucks, but it is easily doable in 20 minutes if you commit to it. Presentations aren't bad and are loosely graded.  Highly reco

Public speaking can be overwhelming, but with Starnes the course is truly refreshing. Starnes is a great teacher and goes above the call of duty. I learned so much about communication and public speaking! Starnes truly cares about students and their success. Highly recommend. Be prepared to learn, and grow your public speaking skills.
Told me to submit assignments one way, then told me that it was against the syllabus, then was confused when I showed her the email she sent me giving the directions I followed.

Kara is a great professor. She really cares about students, but you have to show up and put in the work. She's going to help you out more if you try to establish a relationship with her. She cares and wants to help you be successful. Can be a tough grader at times, but gives good feedback on assignments. Take 4824 with her - it was a great class.
SHE IS AMAZING!

Very helpful course. Weekly newsroom shifts in 4824 let us put everything into practice to build experience and portfolio. Lots of guest speakers to build networking opportunities. Somewhat project heavy with lots of long-term assignments, but she is very helpful throughout the semester.
Extremely tough grader, gives vague instructions and will deduct points if the rubric is not followed exactly how she wants it to be. Does not respond well to emails

She would take points off from assignments and claim that I hadn't followed the rubric. What she would take points off for were not reflective of my work and her claims were not consistent with the contents of the rubric. This is a 1 credit hour online class with minimal work and minimal instruction and yet the grading was difficult.

she gave a lot of extra credit and gave good instructions about the assignments, the class content was little bit disorganized but still there was nothing too dfficult and assignments didn't take much time to do

I think prof. Edgerson is a good professor. I communicated with her few times and she responded within hours. She was respectful and understanding in her responses. The course was easy and she also gave a lot of extra credit opportunities, which was. great. I think she just expects studnets to pay attention to rubric and wants to see quality work.

Dr. Mitchell is incredibly kind and class is super relaxed. 3 papers for the whole semester. Class is very discussion heavy so you should participate, but you do not have to. You can get away without doing any of the reading.
This class made me want to slam my forehead into the back of a porcupine.

Professor Gangloff is a nice and caring individual that has a lot of enthusiasm for her job. However, the class itself seems pointless for juniors and should probably be a freshman level class. Projects include interview practice, creating a resume, learning to be professional etc. Lots of homework/projects that are time consuming but easy.
She is a great professor and truly wants to help you learn the material

Lots of busy work, but she goes out of her way to help you and make the class easier. You are required to volunteer for this class, but she makes it up by cancelling classes to give you more time. Show up and skim the chapters before the quizzes and you should get an easy A.

The best professor I have had. She is an awesome professor who truly cares about your success. She has prepared me for a career in agricultural safety and health. Would recommend students to take her online class.

Enjoyed this class. Everything is online. Well organized and laid out. Easy to read and understand. Instructor wants her students to succeed so she is willing to help you out! I would definitely take this class again.

Great professor! I took AGSM 4020 as a psych student, without ever taking an AG related class in my life and still got an A+. Just do the work. Her assignments have a lot of videos and reading materials, but just take the time to do them (and write about them) and you'll get an A+ too.

I took this class for fun! I got behind in this online class and Professor Karen was willing to work with me. She cares about her students and wants them to be successful. Shes takes agricultural safety and health seriously; which its a bad thing. Take this online class and you can expect to get an A!

Professor Funkenbusch cares about students. Great teacher that knows how to teach. Understands that life happens and is willing to work with you. Has high for students in this class. If you read the lecture materials, follow directions, do the discussions on time and try on weekly quizzes you will do well in this class.

Online class. Weekly reading with an assignment. Also have weekly discussions based off reading materials, internet sites or video clips. I enjoyed the weekly discussions. Very fair professor who is willing to help you out. Enjoyed the class and would recommend it to others.

Professor Funkenbusch is amazing.  I'm not an Agri major, but I highly considered it after her class.  She is a wealth of information, and is more than willing to help you in anyway possible.  If you put forth the effort you should have no problem getting a great grade!  I would recommend her to anyone, and would definitely take her again!

Easily my favorite professor. Detailed feedback, super encouraging. Plenty of room for creativity! There were some suggested readings but they were not mandatory. Grading was based on quizzes and assignments and was done reasonably timely, unless she had other things going on at the time; if so, she will say as much. She wants students  to succeed!

Okay, it's obvious she is being review bombed due to her recent tweet re: the fires in California (Jan '25)
So Imma be truthful.

Karen is a solid teacher, her classes were straight forward and she is good to talk to, whether you agree with her politics or not. she is an open mind and mouth, and I think that is important for growing minds.
Spent most of our time watching YouTube videos, and not actually learning. Lots of pop quizzes, and she can be inappropriate
Yuck for the class

Very judgmental and actually did not hide that she enjoys someone struggling because of differing beliefs.

I was very pleased that I did not suffer like other commenters about having to see "too much skin", I have enough leather at home.

I took British Literature: Black and Asian Studies. The one thing I appreciate is that she extended the due date to multiple assignments. My complaint is long response times to my emails, many quizzes and journals for the books we would read, and only watching youtube videos.

Very nice woman but I wouldn't take this class unless you want to be told how to think regarding politics (which should never be the objective of any teacher), and sit around and watch videos all class after taking a pop quiz over the extensive amount of reading.

She spent each class confused and was extremely vague. She often completely mixed up characters and stories. She told our class that we would be doing a research paper and then later seemed confused and told us that we shouldn't need to do outside research for the papers. She also made inappropriate jokes when we read stories about sexual abuse.

I thought this class could be interesting, but no.  The books were good, the teaching was terrible.  This was a Women's Writers class turned anit-Iraq and anti-Bush class.  Regardless of your opinion, it's not literature.  Furthermore, I saw way too much of inappropriate parts of her body in class (accidentally, of course).  Ditto to above remarks.

Professor Rodriguez is a very nice and caring professor. With that being said, she is a very difficult grader, but does provide feedback. I'm not sure if it was because it was her first year teaching this class, but she was also always unclear about directions on projects and would leave out important details and then critique students.

I loved this class. The subject matter was actually information that I would use outside of class in a personal context like when making investment decisions or checking out a company I want to work for. There wasn't too much homework and she is super fair.
Man hater. Inequitable grading standards. No clarity of task or purpose. Inability to provide specific guidance with unreasonable expectations. Avoid this instructor.

Dr. Adams is fantastic! I was extremely nervous about joining a college choir ensemble, but after the first day with her, all my worries were gone. She makes everyone feel comfortable and important. If you are questioning participating in choir, do it. I promise it is wonderful! (I am not a music major either and I love it)

Dr.Adams is the best choir teacher I've ever had. She cares about each member as an individual and knows everyone's name (about 70 ppl) by the second or third week. She's new, but her style of teaching is well-refined and confident. The grad/doc students each get to direct a song and she's good at instructing them while not neglecting the class

Definitely my favorite professor in terms of personality. Very talkative, and he makes it very difficult for you to leave his office until he thinks you fully understand a concept. Problem is that he loves his proofs too much, so expect long homework assignments with nothing but proofs from your lecture notes to help you.

Dr. Hammond is a great professor. His tests are pretty tough but he never asks something you can't answer, rather something that makes you think in a different way. The homework, while long, will save your grade. Make sure you get as many points as you can on the homework and don't be afraid to ask him for help! He'll gladly guide you if you ask.

hilarious, good natured guy. Favorite professor in terms of personality. he likes to get a little too into explaining where equations come from rather than giving helpful examples in class. If you come to his office he's not going to let you leave easily until he thinks you understand the concept you're asking about which could be good or bad.

Karthik is an amazing professor, you can truly tell he cares about what he teaches. You do have to read a couple books and there are readings online for most lectures. You get out what you put in, but he's really good at working with you if you're struggling!

Dr. Panchanathan's anthropology course was extremely educational and engaging. He gives hilarious and consistently interesting lectures, and assignments are mentioned well in advance. If possible, please take a course with Dr. Panchanathan!
I absolutely loved this professor! He made the class very interesting, and everything he talked about was on the exam, no surprises!

Professor Panchanathan's anthropology course was an excellent view into other cultures that allowed me to see beyond what I thought was normal. He also gave fantastic lectures that drew me in and excited my desire to learn.

His lectures are fun and entertaining but his tests are difficult but it's manageable if you study enough or manage to create a study group to nail the tests. If you are falling behind, Karthik offers extra credit for his students. It's not an easy A but his lectures and the pacing makes up for it! He also listens to our concerns and feedback!

He is a great professor who clearly cares about what he does. Offers a lot of extra credit. The classes are fun to attend despite being a lecture hall. His exams and book reports can be challenging, but if you put in enough effort, an A is easy to get.

He is a great professor and person! But this class is NOT AN EASY A!! The exams are the hardest tests I've ever taken. But he offers a lot of support and extra credit. He is a great professor, but this class itself is just insanely hard. If you just need a humanities credit and don't have an interest in anthropology, another class would be better.
He is actually so approachable and reasonable. Lots of opportunities for extra credit.

The ONLY grades are 8 papers, and two tests (midterm and final). This is extremely annoying, but she's an easy grader and I got 100% on all of the papers. There are no actual video lectures, just youtube videos, the textbook, and written "lectures", so this class just seems like a waste of money. Take it if you must.
I enjoyed class with Professor Kelley. She's sort of an odd person, but in a good way. She is very caring and inclusive to her students.

She was a super nice professor. Had 4 papers during the semester but not more than 1000 words or usually less than 3 pages. Is there to help during conferences and office hours? 
The one confusing thing is grading, she does something called "ungrading" and its where you will grade yourself at the end of the semester.
Super chill and fun. She interacts with the material well and deeply.

No exams but lots of writing assignments. This class felt extremely unorganized. She would post the description for assignments the day they were due, or would post the wrong description. Didn't keep up on grading so I didn't know my grade going into final paper. This is supposed to Religion AND STEM but it felt like a repeat of general religion.

This professor makes an easy class. However, my religious studies class had very little religion mentioned. It was an anti-white, anti-male class where she blatantly and outspokenly practiced "reverse racism" (racism against white people) and "reverse sexism" (sexism against men). If you would rather be indoctrinated than actually learn, go for it.

This was a great option to take as my >2000 level humanities course. It was only 8 weeks long and insanely easy. There were only around 10 assignments for the entire semester, and none of them took more than an hour. There are also no exams.
The class content was interesting and Kate Kelley had a lot of insight. There was a lot of homework, and she expected a lot of thought. Tough but interesting.

Kate has a real passion for world literature, and you can tell. She's great at facilitating discussion and squeezing every last bit of analysis out of her students. The constant group mini-projects can be a little grating, but her curriculum is otherwise super lenient. Lots of extra credit. Do well on most of your essays and you'll ace this class.

Lots of reading which can be tough at times but she was very helpful and always willing to talk through issues. She's super chill and a perfect mix between lenient enough to keep you calm and collected but still presenting challenging and thought provoking assignments/texts

I had covid and a family relative passed and she would not fix my attendance. I was literally grieving and emailed her she never answered. Also made it very clear she didn't like me even after me explaining why I had been struggling and not came to class.

This class's structure was quite difficult at first, but drastically became easier. The textbook was not actually needed. Plant Structure and Function could easily be passed with minimal studying/reading. Make sure to go to the labs! The labs were easy; it felt like we were back at a high school level, but they were points-heavy and harshly graded.
I loved her class. She's very good at explaining and making her class fun. I really did enjoy learning about all of the wines and viticulture.

I genuinely loved this class, even if some of the lectures were pretty boring. Dr. Hagely clearly cares so much about plants and her love for them is definitely infectious. The class had a lot of interesting/unconventional projects, which was cool. One of the coolest professors I've had. Niche questions about the readings are on quizzes, be warned.

Good teacher and makes the class fun, even bringing in a super cool wine expert. I wish her slides had a little more info on them but overall pretty good and she will post the slides too. Grades are only based off attendance (randomly & at tastings), a midterm, and a final though, so beware. I wish there was a small assignment or 2 to boost grades

Dr. Hagley is a very caring Professor, and a wonderful lady. However, I do feel like she is restricted by the massive lecture nature of the class ie. it seems as if she just reads slides and can barely answer questions in a decisive way. Beware of the Midterm and Finals! While the Wine is great and the guest lecturer is fantastic, the finals suck!

In a smaller course setting, she did a wonderful job of introducing interesting materials and allowing for discussion. There were many readings that varied a lot by length. However, she was very understanding, and with explanation I never had any difficulties with late assignments. If you participate, you'll have a great time!
So disorganized and can barely hear her talk in lectures
No technology allowed, sped through notes during lecture which has no definitions of any terms, reads off a script, canvas page has no grades or dates. Very disorganized. Save yourself

She doesn't allow technology in lectures, making note-taking harder. Her Canvas page is disorganized, with no clear due dates and grades split across 2 different Canvas pages, so it's difficult to track progress. Staying organized is challenging. I recommend choosing a different professor if possible.
Very helpful, class was easy to follow.

Kate is the best teacher I have ever had in college. You can tell she cares about her students' success and she will spend the entire class helping you with everything you need help with without ever making you feel like you're bothering her or asking too much. She also creates tutorials and sends helpful resources if she sees people struggling.

Weaponized my childhood trauma to make me accept the heaviest assignments surrounding death and abuse. Wouldn't let me stop when it was impacting me negatively. Abuses power over students regularly.

Her lectures are okay. I wish she had more recent experience out in the real reporting world. She makes you feel stupid often, and cannot take the criticism she constantly gives. Get ready to like you don't even have an editor if you're on her beat. But she talks a big game that she hasn't really played. Tread lightly and get out.
My unique experience with Katherine Reed includes mind-numbingly boring lectures wherein Reed brags about herself and essentially belittles her students.

She can be a bit intimidating but it's part of her personality. She gives great lectures and is someone you want on your side if you ever have a problem in the j-school. Didn't have her as my section editor so I can't speak to her that way.

Katherine works differently from most professors. The key is trying everything you can think before asking her questions. Anticipate what she will ask. She was absolutely one of my favorite professors and I learned more from her than I did in any other course in college. She's not that intimidating if you talk to her.

Katherine, like all of the other comments have said, is slightly intimidating. But she does have a lot of knowledge to give her students, and she cares about them. If she can tell you are trying hard, and taking assignments, she will be very supportive and encouraging. Great teacher.
She's tough and doesn't take crap from anyone. Great lecture professor. If she's your Missourian editor, get on her good side and you'll be fine.

If you get her as your Missourian editor, just switch editors if you are able to. She is hard and unhelpful and can even be downright mean and embarass you in front of the entire newsroom. Not one to mess with and not one to work with. Avoid her. Scary.

Class can be painful if no one participates, and there is quite a lot of discussion. The essays aren't particularly difficult, but can be a burden if you procrastinate. I can't say I learned much in this class but it wasn't a bad experience. She's a graduate student. She's not out looking to hurt your GPA, just try and you'll do perfectly good.

Ms. Buckley was an amazing instructor. She gives amazing feedback on assignments and makes the class enjoyable. There is a lot of group participation required, so be prepared for that. Attendance is not mandatory but, there is a lot of in-class assignments that are for a completion grade. She tries to include every learning type in the curriculum.

Kathy Kiely is the worst professor in the world. Avoid her section at all cost you will genuinely regret being in the class. She's a tough grader and takes weeks to even grade portfolio assignments. I don't know how her old self is allowed to keep teaching.

While it is true that 4180 is a "weed out" class in the J-School, Kathy makes it fun. Her feedback is very good, and if you put in effort, she will take note. She's honest with you, which is really useful and and she cares about her students. Do well with Kathy and you'll be on track to success in the newsroom. She's a sweetheart!

Professor Kiely has a deep well of knowledge about the history of journalism and challenges students to think critically about the free speech barriers they face in our current technological landscape. She gives detailed feedback and loves to talk to students who are passionate about the work. Her class was one of my favorites in college by far.

The sweetest, smartest woman. If you are nice, ask good questions, show a real interest, do Portfolio Revisions for J4180, and show that you care about getting a good experience out of the class, she'll give you a good grade that reflects that. Don't be afraid of her honesty, she's just showing students what its like to work in a real newsroom.

The best professor I have had by far. She has such an in depth knowledge of journalism that you will learn something just from being in the same room as her. 4180 is not an easy class regardless of the professor you have, but she is always accessible if you need help and genuinely wants you to succeed in the class. Could not recommend her more.

Something about her always rubbed me the wrong way. Some of my group members were genuinely terrified of her because she could be so mean. Even if you have to take the class at 8 am, AVOID her section of 4180, she was truly a nightmare. I've heard she's a nice enough person, but being a successful journalist does NOT mean you should be teaching it.
Tough grader but I love her so much!
She is professional in journalism as well as humorous in taking classes.

She was a good professor and obviously knew what she was talking about. However, her lectures are extremely borning and if you have trouble paying attention in lectures this definitely isn't the teacher for you. She reads directly off of the slides for the whole class. The tests are not bad if you study but there is a lot of content to memorize.

Dr. Newton is very enthusiastic about genetics. She knows her stuff, however, she is not great at getting material across. The class is very powerpoint heavy with 50-80 slides per lecture. The ample amount of slides and information makes it hard to study for exams, which by the way, are the only things that go toward your grade.

Kathy is very nice, but she is a terrible professor. Her lectures and slides are disorganized and she spends too much time discussing people rather than concepts. My best advice would be to go to lecture and recitation for the bonus points. Read the textbook (I prefered the alternate tb personally) and do any practice problems/old exams available

Awful professor. She is crazy and changes exams at the last minute to make them more difficult. The extra credit means nothing and it doesn't help your grade at all. Avoid taking her for genetics and choose ANYONE else! She rambles on about pointless topics in her lectures and you do not learn anything. She is extremely hard to pay attention to.

This professor went through a crazy amount of information in every 75 minute class period and gave little to no indication of what would be on the tests. There is a cumulative final which is just the absolute worst. I stopped going to lecture and used the book to teach myself the entire course. Don't take this class.

She rushes through lectures and goes through an average of 70 slides in 50 minutes every class which makes it impossible to retain any information. Tests are impossible unless this is the one and only class you are taking. She vaguely explains everything but the test are so in-depth. Save yourself.

Dr. Newton is a really great professor and uses real-world examples of advances in modern science to emphasize the concepts discussed in lecture. Really fun teacher, and exams are really straight forward. Lecture notes are very useful for studying for exams.

Dr. Newton is a great person. She is very caring and if you put in the effort she rewarded you with extra help. Some of her questions were tricky but she never actually meant for them to be. If you take the class I highly recommend you get to know her!
Professor Miller is tough. Be prepared to work really hard and learn a lot, but you'll do well if you put in the effort.
Simply put, she lies about how she grades. I've maintained a 4.0 through every class except hers, because she arbitrarily changed how she grades mid course.
Way too much research required, at moments it felt unnecessary. Did not have enough guidance throughout and there was a constant lack of communication between all students and the professor.

Dr. Trauth is a very sweet person, and if you ask for help, she will help you. However, hydrology (fund. of water resource eng.), was one of the hardest courses I have ever taken. The material itself is not difficult to learn, but there is little time in class where there are examples & no textbook. 75% of class went to TA for help on weekly HW.

If I had to choose between taking this class again and getting an incurable case of syphilis, I would choose syphilis every (insert curse) time. Kathleen thinks she's stuff because shes a civil engineer that couldn't cut her teeth in actual work and decided to come back and torture freshmen in her FIG with weekly assignments and due dates.
Professor Miller is tough. Be prepared to work really hard and learn a lot, but you'll do well if you put in the effort.
Simply put, she lies about how she grades. I've maintained a 4.0 through every class except hers, because she arbitrarily changed how she grades mid course.

I took her a couple of semesters ago for my freshmen year. She was really cool as a person but hard to like as a professor. She grades so toughly and I felt like if I didn't please her as a person I wouldn't get a good grade. Offered a lot of help for the papers but if you don't ask for help it's a toss-up if you did good or not on the paper.

She is a nice person, but she never put work into actually being a teacher. She is horrible at responding to emails and half the time would never join a zoom call that was scheduled for questions. She goes MIA for weeks at a time. Takes forever to grade a paper. I scheduled a zoom appointment with her and she never showed up. Good luck with her.

A little on the odd side, but super sweet if you get on her good side. I made an effort to write my papers about topics I knew she would respect/be interested in, so she always gave me really good grades. If you take her class seriously and meet with her before turning in papers, you will get an A.

For over half of the semester, there was only ever one assignment graded for us to see. There was one guy I knew that didnt get anything back until the end of semester. Lectures were boring and unhelpful. Office hours were pointless. If you enjoy not knowing what your grade is until December and doing 3 overly difficult papers, this ones for you.

She's a nice person but she grades so harshly. According to her grade distribution she gives out lots of A's yet I do not know anyone in the class with an A. I haven't skipped one class, actively participate and turn in everything on time yet I have a B. I had an A the entire sem until she put in an essay that I even revised based off her comments

Throughout the entire semester the expectations were unclear but I still had an A. Then in the the last 2 weeks of school she put all major things in and it dropped me a ton. Only English 1000 teacher that makes you write a 10 page paper. I missed two classes, 30% in attendance. Her response when I talked to her was that grades are non-negotiable.

There are no strict guidelines on attendance except that it is essential that you are there for every single one. A skipped class and an excused class are treated as the same thing and she grades really harshly. Students who didn't miss one class and actively participated got low Bs in the category and there was no explanation as to why.

She is super kind and caring. You can tell she loves teaching and her students. Show up to class, the textbook isn't even that important. She just wants to make sure you are getting something out of class. Highly recommend!
She co-taught with Mr. Pinto and I thought they were phenomenal. She is so involved in everything she does and she really just wants everyone to succeed.
She's pretty cool, and the co-instructors were alright. Just show up, really. Don't buy the books, it's not really worth it.

This is an online course that requires LOTS of time. Each week you need to complete about 20 assignments and an exam on Sunday nights, but it isn't hard work just very time consuming and you have endless attempts for the assignments only. You can work ahead of time too since she unlocks weeks worth of work in advance.

I took this class online, and it was very easy. There is one unit per week (approximately 15 in total), and it takes about an hour to complete. All assignments are multiple choice or matching with unlimited checks, including each unit test. Would highly recommend this class!

Unfair grading system and not clear with homework instructions. I wouldn't take another class of hers again. 

I wasn't given access to an assignment and when I told her I was docked points for it. She was rude when I reached out about it and was unreasonable too. Her instructions are also not clear and she typically doesn't follow her own rubric.

I took it online and it was a very easy A. Every week there were about 15 assignments, but they were very easy and only took about an hour to complete. Quizlet and Google will become your life and savior. She was very caring with weekly check-in emails. Great course overall.

I don't know the professor well but that is good because I could do the course asynchronously with no problems! There are a lot of assignments but they are not very difficult if you utilize the textbooks. Great course for future work!

Overall good content, grades a bit tough and sometimes takes off points for reasons that seem iffy. We had a journal prompt each week which was 250 words, but was graded complete/incomplete and not worth any points even if you completed. You failed if incomplete. Irritating to produce quality work and find out I could have done the bare minimum.

This class is basically done entirely on Cengage, so she does not really teach that much, but all due dates and required materials are clearly outlined and given to you at the beginning of the semester. If you ever have questions or need assistance she is more than willing to help. Overall, a very interesting class that teaches you a lot!

A lot of discussion boards, but it makes for easy points. In the beginning of the semester I mixed up the due date for initial discussion board posts for the due date of discussion board responses, but that was my fault. She provided feedback for assignments and graded fairly. The class was very well organized and I enjoyed her teaching style.

Where do I begin? This course is terrible. 3 required books for the class, none show up on booklist, and 2 weren't in the bookstore. You absolutely can not miss 7 classes (even though it is a pandemic) or you basically fail. Yes, attendance is being REQUIRED DURING A PANDEMIC. Absolutely useless information and a terrible course I recommend to zero

Kat's audience strategy is a great course and she is a great professor. I took this course for my career path, but it is a specialty course so I would totally recommend for all. It is very group-project heavy as you help a client with their goals. She grades the practice presentation very tough but it's to set you up to prefect your final.

This course was difficult, but I felt very supported by Kat. She strives to help all of her students, and while feedback is slow, there's over 100 students and only a couple graders! I really appreciated how much effort she put into our work being published, and while she is harsh, she really does care about your success.

Does not work well with students (especially female students for some reason) and is incredibly defensive over criticism. Not a fan of this professor, would not recommend whatever section of 4180 she's teaching.

Kat is a great instructor, especially if you are willing to meet her halfway and put in the work to improve. The organization of the class leaves something to be desired, but she will go the extra mile to help you succeed if you INDICATE AHEAD OF TIME that you are struggling. She's very approachable and wants you to succeed. Go to office hours!!!

Worst professor I've ever had. She asked someone to start over on a two week long project a mere three hours before the deadline, she doesn't turn in feedback for your first draft until the night before it's due, and she will count you off points for changes that SHE made. She's never even been a reporter. Avoid her at all costs.

Truly one of the worst professors I have ever had. My first project I had approved by multiple editors, classmates, and another professor. When I showed it to her, she chopped and screwed it substantially, sucked all the life out of it, and gave me a 52%. She shows zero regard for her students and her well being. Avoid her at all cost.

Kat was really harsh about grading late work, would give edits at the last possible minute, scored half the class really low (favoritism), constantly stressed students out and would not give clear directions. She would give feedback that drastically altered assignments a couple hours before deadline and padded the class with mind numbing speakers.

Such a sweetheart, but as of December 11th she has only graded ONE assignment from the first week. She reallyyyyyy needs to grade more efficiently. Readings are incredibly dense but I had good class discussions. The class honestly became a family despite the difficult readings and lack of grading.

Kathryn was nice but literally took 2 months to grade things. By the time a paper was done, it was finals week and I didn't know how to improve my last two papers that were already due. The feedback is also confusing. Solely on the way she grades and the fact that it takes forever, I wouldn't take her again
I fell behind in this class for personal reasons. Dr. Kat was extremely understanding and super flexible.

I have never felt passionately enough about a course to write a review but this class was awful. For an entry level sociology course the workload was insane. Every week was somehow worse than the last and no matter how good your work is or how much time you spent on it you will not get an A. She is a really tough grader, doesn't respond to emails.

I took SOC 4240. She's passionate and loves student discussion, but very slow with grading. Weekly reading quizzes were easy, and journal assignments were every few weeks. Midterm was multiple choice with a couple short answer. Not too bad. Random attendance checks with 5 freebies. Loved her, but the grading delays were frustrating.

The papers you have to read are nothing short of esoteric. If that's not bad enough, then you have to compare 2 of them. Weekly. 100% should be writing intensive. 
Other than that, she's pretty engaging during lectures. Class was interesting as well. The papers really suck the fun out of it.

Posted the final assignment the Thursday OF finals week. Does not respond to emails and has graded three assignments total (it's finals week). Although this course was relatively easy week to week, Kat's lack of communication and complete off-hands method of teaching for the first 7 weeks made it incredibly difficult to know what was expected.

She is nice and helpful with feedback. However the directions on a lot of her assignments were confusing and vaguely worded. This class is also writing and reading heavy compared to many other 1000 level courses. There are 4 essays (the last one being a 6-page group essay) with 1 page-long reading response every week and discussion every week.

I'm gonna miss her. Thermo 1 was a pain but she made it manageable and I even found myself enjoying it in my bettter moments. I'm sure the new Thermo 1 prof is wonderful, though. Thank you for your work, Dr. Myers.
Best professor ever. Very smart and great at teaching. Also super funny.

I don't know if she realizes that she is teaching a gen-ed that most people do not want to take and are actually forced into by state law. She lectures as if she just wants to hear herself talk and seems fundamentally uncapable of understanding how to teach in a way that reaches students. There are too many readings and tests basically every week.

Probably my most favorite discussion section I have ever had at Miz. She was totally understanding when we had things come up, and I feel like she actually wanted to connect with the members of my class. I had her spring semester my Freshman year, and she really set the standards high for the rest of my discussion sections!!!

Professor Sullivan is one of my favorite professors. He is incredibly nice and he genuinely cares about your well-being. He talks about his life a lot which is really nice because he feels more like a genuine human being rather than just a professor. He doesn't check homework for accuracy just asks that you do it. Pay attention to Truth Tables.
Professor Sullivan is great and was my favorite professor. He makes the class interesting and easy to understand. If you have to take a Philosophy class definitely take it with Aaron.

He is the funniest professor ever. He doesnt mind in you skip class. There homework and quizzes but you cant fail the quiz and he doesnt check homework. He is absolutely hilarious and nice. Not difficult at all and the work was easy to understand.

best intro philosophy prof anyone could ask for, is very attentive to student's needs if something comes up and tries to explain concepts as best he can. Tests are straightforward and exactly what was taught in class

Best ethics class ever! Super fun, not stressful, relevant, and Sullivan is super nice! Only 3 tests and a few pop quizzes he grades generously. Just read the assignment or watch black mirror and discuss!
dope philosophy teacher that cares about his students and their knowledge about philosophy

Professor Sullivan is the absolute best. Love his class. He is very caring and gives extensions when you need them. While there isn't really a penalty for missing class, I highly recommend you go as it helps on the tests (which are entirely multiple choice). The lectures are also really interesting. Half the homework is watching Black Mirror.

Prof Sullivan's class was always interesting. He always expanded on questions and didn't make anyone feel bad about asking too many. He was respectful of different perspectives. He had a few pop quizzes to incentives us to come to class, but if you missed a class/ quiz he would let you retake it if you asked. Tests were online which was nice.

He was really good at providing examples of performances, but was very vague on assignments. Was told to write reflections on things discussed in class and reflections on plays we were required to see. I assumed they were the same thing but he told me the play reflection was too short. Easy grading, no need to read the textbook, no formal quiz/test

He was very caring and respectful. He told some of the most amazing stories Ive experienced. He was very excellent at getting everyone ready for class and cared deeply about our participation. It was obvious he was enjoying the class and so were we.

He's a great caring and respectable person. However, as a teacher, he's horrible at everything: doesn't reply to emails even when you send in 10+ emails, doesn't know how to use Canvas for grading, rarely goes to office hours, etc.

Participation and going to see the plays is my best advice to anyone taking this class. The essays aren't hard because he's a super easy grader. Don't expect to not have to perform stuff in front of your classmates though!

Your going to have to go see productions and write two page papers on them. You write papers frequently, but it isn't an English class. He's not a hard grader at all. I enjoyed his class. As long as you try and participate your good. He's not good at replying to emails , so send multiple.  You get to play games

I have loved this class! Would be impossible to do well on exams if skipped lectures, but attendance isn't for points, and vague notes are posted on Canvas. Read 3 books and write a paper on one. Exams are short answer, but you pick your questions to answer. Super nice guy, and interesting material!
He is such a good professor, and is willing to work with you on due dates. He genuinely cares about what you have going on. Genuinely a good guy, and is definitely worth taking his class.
Was my TA. Nice guy but graded it way too harshly for a required course. Is a PhD student and very smart but he has to understand not all of us are getting a PhD in history...

One of the worst grading systems I've experienced. Attendance and homework hold no weight, while every exam requires at least a 75 to pass. No test scores are dropped, regardless of circumstances. The grading feels unrealistic and lacks understanding for students who struggle or face personal issues. I wish there were other professor option
Quizzes were 90% of our grade. 90. I believe that was way too much especially since none are dropped. He also wasn't very understanding with when I was in the hospital and was rude about it.

Dr. Ries is a good lecturer and his slides are straightforward. There's a 10 question homework every week/every other week. There are quizzes 1-2x a month, but they're short (12 questions) and reflect the homework. There are no exams or finals (but there are 2 cumulative quizzes). Textbook is optional, but he posts the key terms from each chapter.

I took this course online, and had taken stats in high school so I was kind of familiar with everything already so I ended up just throwing on the Panopto lectures and doing other things. Course will be easy if you know how to use the equation sheet to your advantage.
If you go to lectures and do the homework you will do good in the class. He is very accessible outside of class and wants all his students to succeed.

85% of the grades in this class are quizzes, so once you get a bad grade you're cooked for the semester. I got a 66 on my first quiz, and a 75 on my second, then proceeded to get all 100's and 92's and still didn't pull out an A despite turning in all the homework. Teacher is super monotone, but other than that he's kind of funny.

He was, overall, an outstanding professor. The tests are worth 80% of your grade. I did badly on our first test and have been playing catch-up ever since. I feel as though he should make an exception like other professors, and drop the worst grade since it is so test-heavy. Overall, he teaches the material really well.

This class is hell. Do not take this class if you are a bad test taker. 80% of your grade is based of quizzes that are 12 questions and you only have 30 minutes to do it. He is also extremely rude when you email him and he makes absolutely zero exceptions no matter what.

I think Larry is an overall great professor. He goes over the readings very effectively in class (our class was discussion based so doing the readings was important) and tries to facilitate discussion. He gives very in depth feedback on essays, which can feel daunting but is very helpful. He obviously cares about his work and his students.

Prof. Svabek taught 1/3 of my online POL_SC1100 class. He did a good job explaining concepts and seems unbiased. The class is overall easy and boring due to the online lectures and ultimately useless discussion section. Weekly online quizzes that I recommend you do while watching the lecture. 4 online exams and an online final, all multiple choice.

The class is graded by very few things (3 essays and attendance) but the criterion is extremely clear. The classes feel more like insightful discussions than lectures and are amazing. He cares a lot about his students and how well they understand the concepts. I would definitely recommend him for any of his classes.

The amount of time you have to spend on discussion boards in order to get full points is ridiculous. She sent out an example of a good discussion board post that was closer to the length of an essay. You HAVE to do the readings to do well. I did well in the class, but wasnt expecting to have to spend as much time on it as my hardcore STEM classes.

Class itself is very interesting and enjoyable, and would recommend her for that alone. Dr. Rosenberg is a pretty love-her-or-hate-her type of professor, and while I enjoy how raw and honest she is, her style won't appeal to everyone. Just be sure to actually participate and do the readings if you want to succeed.

Worst professor I've ever had. Makes you participate and then yells at you or tries to belittle you if your opinion is not EXACTLY like hers. I was anxious every day before class because I knew she would gaslight one of her students and you never knew when it was going to be you. Makes her political opinion very clear. Better just pretend to agree.

This class was my hardest class for the semester and I am Pre-Med. This is because the professor talks in circles and has abstract connections that make no sense. She is rude, condescending, unprofessional and she politicized everything. Did not learn anything about what I was supposed to. AWFUL learning environment. So distracting.

I absolutely adore Dr. Rosenberg. I took her Dying in the West World class and she was so amazing and very clear/concise. She truly wants her students to succeed and is very reasonable. I'm taking another one of her classes this semester as an elective just because I liked her so much the first time. Definitely recommend anything she teaches!

I was optimistic at the beginning of this class. I like professors who are honest, raw, and passionate about their subjects. However, Dr. Rosenberg is rude, condescending, and will often try to belittle you in front of your peers. I have a pretty tough exterior and even I was taken aback by how toxic she was in class. Distracted from learning.

I love Dr. Rosenberg! This class was interesting and heartbreaking  WELL worth taking. Other reviews say she talks over class discussions, but while sometimes she does get excited and blurt over people, she is always adding useful, helpful information. She is challenging, funny and a great professor. My favorite prof at Mizzou so far!

I enjoyed this class and Dr. Rosenberg is very funny, kind, and interesting. We talked about social norms/politics/racism/sexism throughout history, and it was all so interesting. You have to read EVERYTHING. You end up reading 2-3 books worth of material and then use it for 5 papers throughout the semester. It was hard, but worth it.

Prof Manion is one of my favorite professors. He expects you to participate, but nothing about his class is difficult if you do the reading. He tells you everything expects. He is funny, easy to talk to, and understands. I'm only upset he isn't teaching a class I signed up for anymore. 10/10 would take again!!

I had Lee Manion last semester as a freshman for Honors Epic Destinies. He's amazing and the quintessential college professor. I cannot recommend him enough! He was so funny and engaging. Discussions are mostly student-led. I read 1/4 of the texts, but I still got a 100% in the class. If you participate in class and take notes you'll be fine.

LOVE THIS PROF! Very kind & flexible. His lectures are entertaining, engaging, and funny (which is hard to do in a middle-age-English course) He leaves amazing feedback on essays and grades very fair. The only issue I have is that the grade has been locked on canvas the entire semester. However, the accessibility of the canvas page makes up for it

He's one of the best professor's I've had at this school. His lectures are funny and he's great at putting complex ideas in a simple way the class can understand. He always has an interesting perspective on the reading we do (although there is A LOT of reading). He's accessible outside of class and really personable too.

She is one of the most caring professors I have had at Mizzou! The tests are straight forward and open note. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches and shows that. Her class is extremely engaging and easy. I definitely recommend her has a professor

Kind and cares deeply about her subject. Class was all lectures and notes with no homework. Lectures are detailed and easy to understand. There are random one-question attendance quizzes. Biggest criticism is that on the 4 tests we took, I got 3 As and one C. The C dropped my grade by 6%, so the tests are weighted heavily; it wasn't even the final.

Neier is the most preachy professor I've ever had. Class includes constant reminders that students should be 'learners, not just finishers'. Content quizzes are open notes and questions come from the lectures/materials. She claims students should spend 9 hours a week JUST on her course, which is insane bc there is 0 writing or discussion posts.

This class all sounds made up, and she repeats everything she says, which is essentially a whole lot of nothing. I can't complain because the online class is really not much work. But we have 4 online quizzes which are just annoying. She pulls from like 15+ sources, gives too similar of answers, and writes dumb questions.

Professor Neier has never taught in a classroom herself, but she sure has a lot to say about how we should teach. This class was so hard to sit through, she talked about the same thing over and over again. What could be said in 5 minutes, took her over an hour to cover. Take this class online, or with someone else to save your sanity and time

This class was extremely easy but I really wish I took it online. Professor Neier talked in circles the entire class. 
The content is easy to understand, but I always left class irritable because I felt like I had just wasted an hour and 15 minutes of my time. All of this info could be googled and found online in less time.

Professor Neier's class was kinda intolerable. She talks in circles the entire class and NEVER gets through the slides. I almost fall asleep every. single. time. She is very outgoing and passionate however, I don't think I learned anything. All of the info given can easily be accessed online and is base level. She is lowkey passive aggressive. ew.
Very kind and helpful!

This prof is probably the coldest human in the music school. Not in a good way. He loves to make students cry and will blatantly insult your intellect and tear down your self esteem. Please go to any other college for saxophone majors. I promise he's not worth it and the studio is extremely toxic because of this! beware and good luck.

"Prof" is so great. I am very glad that I switched from clarinet because he has helped me improve so much since I've been here. He is a very good instructor. 9.9/10 would recommend. And he buys you pizza every semester!
Positives: great saxophonist, teacher, and karaoke'er. Negatives: could be taller.

He is very helpful and offers a lot of ways to bring your grade up with study sessions and extra credit.  He sometimes goes through the notes a little fast, but he has a lot of material to cover in a short amount of time to do it in.(He offers the notes on webct when he is done with the material)
Did I stutter or something?  Studio class is a blast

He does a great job with teaching tha class as best he can.  I know its not all that interesting, but he magnifies whatever there is.  Also very dedicated, has a ton of study sessions,  and extra credit opprotunities.
He really opened my eyes when he helped me realize that I wasn't playing Mozart.
Great teacher! Great guy! Sucks at taboo.
easy
He's the bee's knees

Doc is awesome. He's genuinely interested in what he teaches, and it shows in his enthusiasm and how well and thoroughly he explains things. He really cares about students' learning and is always willing to help if you need it. He's also a great advisor. He and his administrative assistant, Sandy are really great at what they do.
Great professor! very clear and fun, class is very hands on.
One on the best instuctors I've ever had.
Great professor
Great professor! He gives outrageous amounts of extra credit for almost no effort. This class is an easy A if you show up. He is also super caring about you and your grade.

I loved Leonardo. He gives you every opportunity to succeed and he gives you plenty of chances to earn extra credit. If you do your homework, you should earn an A. I would absolutely recommend Leonardo, to any person, he is not only a great teacher but he is great guy all around. I had a great time taking his class.

There are 6 exams plus a final which is a lot but Leonardo is really understanding and let's you make up work and exams.  There is a lot of online homework but it's not hard and actually helps you learn a lot.  If you think you're ever falling behind just contact him and he will help you.  He really wants students to succeed.

I LOVE MARVIN! He can be kind of rude at times but if you go to class and study hard, you will be just fine. His lectures are actually pretty engaging and interesting to listen to. He's hilarious. You get graded by like 3-4 exams but if you really study and go to class, you'll pull out with at least a B.

Great professor. I respected the way he conducted class, and felt that I had learned more because of it. You must do all assigned readings, know everything he has said in his lectures, and then some, to do well. I would not say I am blessed in this subject, but with a solid work ethic, I got an A.

If you are good at memorization and have an interest in politics, you will be fine. However, if you are looking for an easily passable class without doing work, you will fail. He is very tough and you have to study heavily for the exams. There is a lot of information and it takes a lot of dedication to get through the semester.
To reiterate a former post, Overby gets a lot of hate that he doesn't deserve. He will make you work for your grade, and he will make you smarter.
Great teacher overall you will learn a lot if you attend the classes, the whole class is based on four tests, take good notes, review the notes very well before the test and you'll be alright

His lectures are pretty interesting and he's good at keeping you engaged on a boring topic. The reading is not really necessary but be prepared to miss a few test questions if you don't do it (he assigns like 50 something pages a week, not worth it). Overall, he's a good professor if you try in class and study hard for exams.

This is one of the worst classes that I have ever taken. Do not take this class. The professor is rude and will use profanity throughout the class. The exams contain so much material that it's ridiculous. He will not let you withdraw with an F. He does not care what you are going through.

Professor Overby is one of the best teachers that I have had at Mizzou. He does make you work for your grade, but he has a wealth of knowledge that you should take advantage of. This class is very interesting.
Really lovely professor! She is very kind and gives amazing feedback, you can tell she really loves what she does. All of the TAs are also amazing.

I really enjoyed this class! Most of our lectures ended up being online which was nice. Labs were fun and easy. The TAs ran the lab portion but when I interacted with Lesleighan, she was very nice. Arrangement grading is fair and you get feedback. If you need an honors course credit, take this class as honors. All you have to do is write a paper.

Lesleighan is one of the kindest and most qualified professors I've encountered in my college career thus far. She is extremely knowledgable and her experience in the field is apparent in her familiarity with class subjects. She is very sweet and gives off big mom energy.
Class was entirely run by TAs, but the one time I had to talk to her she was sweet. Easy A though.

I love Lesleighan! I have taken her classes a couple of times just because I really enjoyed her as my professor! I have recommended her classes to all of my friends at MIZZOU. She is very sweet, Her class is the sole reason I get up for my 8 A.M.
I loved this class. It was so fun and out of my comfort zone. Mrs. Cravens and her TAs were simply spectacular.

Not only is Lesleighan great, but the TAs are too! Such a positive and encouraging atmosphere! There are "signature assignments" due every Sunday that include a picture of your floral arrangement and 3 questions about the lecture. They are pretty easy if you listen in lecture and in the lab. The TAs are also quick to respond if you email for help!

I love Lesleighan so much, I recommend taking all of her classes. She makes having an 8am class worth it. She is very knowledgeable about her field and she is a breath of fresh air. Best professor that I have had so far. If you need a gpa booster take this class, you will learn so much and may decide that this is the field you want to work in.

He doesn't understand how to use technology and often spends a chunk of class time trying to get his computer to work. Also, he cancels class a lot or lets the class out early. He is a genius and has a very broad vocabulary which can sometimes make it hard to understand him. It is very easy to get by in this class by doing minimal work.

This is my second time having him as a professor but with the Film History class and the only difference with this class and Film 1800 is that he grades slightly harder and asks more obscure questions on quizzes. He's always open to student's feedback about quizzes or projects, and he's always great to have a casual conversation with about films.

Please give him a chance- even though he may not be used to using the technology portion of the class, if you truly apply yourself you'll learn a lot about film. He's a brilliant and funny guy. A walking encyclopedia of film knowledge. Put in an effort and he'll love you!

Stowers is a person who knows about the topic of Film studies and you could probably have a really good conversation about it over lunch but not during a lecture.  He likes to ramble on and I never really learned a lot of concrete things from his lectures.  His tests are sometimes unreasonable but you can easily debate yourself some points back.

Sam rambles and can be confusing and sometimes I get secondhand embarrassment for him, but he's great once you find his genius, like someone said. I did this class as honors by contract, so I got to know him even better, and he really is brilliant and very knowledgeable about film. Be patient and watch the films, and you'll get a good grade.

Professor Stowers is a great, and he likes what he does. Although he speaks with his eyes closed and can be unorganized, he will help you. Give him a chance early on when it seems like the class is going nowhere. As long as you show that you care, you will do great and learn a lot. He has lots of knowledge and he also lets out class early a lot.

One of my favorite professors at Mizzou. First couple weeks i thought he was crazy because he doesn't talk with his eyes open, and is kinda all over the place. He lets you redo papers until you get the grade you want. Once you realize how genius he is you will find him fascinating

He is one of the better English teachers at Mizzou. He is very nice, smart, and understanding. Sometimes you will learn more by his conferences than in class. I wasn't a good writer in high school but because of him I am better. Take his English class because he is helpful and not too strenuous like some of the others.

He's an amazing professor who is available outside of class. In his office hours he will go above and beyond to help you figure out the information. Unfortunately, you need to go to class to really understand the info, which I was not able to do due to athletics and traveling. He's so accommodating and I would highly recommend him as a professor.

Go to labs, do your reports, you will easily pass the class. If you have questions, skip asking Phil, he will make you feel stupid, belittle you, and might answer your question. Nice one minute, demeaning the next. Go to your TA with questions. Lectures aren't mandatory, but he gives away a lot of post lab/mechanisms so might help you out.

Phil is great. His recitation is more geared towards medical students, but that honestly got me more interested since it wasn't as related to my major. He can be intense (military background) but that doesn't make him mean or rude. He has high expectations which is good considering this can be a dangerous lab and you work with strong chemicals.

Phil is quite nice at times and at other times you have to walk on eggshells around him. Barks out orders like you're in the military and is rude at times, while goes out of his way to help you at other times. Is extremely unclear with mechanisms in prelabs. TA grading varies. Communication with lab report content is average at best.

A lot of people think Phil is really mean, but if you go to his office hours, he's super helpful and caring. He wants you to understand the material, and will work with you. His final required you to remember things from other classes, which is good measure of comprehension. If you're in Orgo II, you should be able to do a limiting reagent anyway

Phil is not necessarily a bad teacher, but can be rude and tough to listen to. However, recitation is very helpful; he gives you half the info you need to do well on lab reports, so you definitely want to attend his lectures! A lot better one-on-one. Will often give back points if you think your lab TA graded unfairly. Take his final seriously!

Took Chem1100 over the summer. The class was small so it was easy to ask questions and most of us were not science majors. Open note quizzes everyday but Monday. He dropped our lowest test grade and the final was optional. If you have to take a lab Asanka teaches it, take it with her she's the best! Very easy to get at least a B in this class.

Silverman seems nice sometimes but can be pretty strict or "snappy" other times. Same goes for your TA - some are helpful while some will criticize every question you might ask. The lab reports take a good chunk of your time every week but if you do them right it's easy to get a good grade. Beware of the final exam, it's much harder than expected!

Shi Jie's lectures are very well organized and sometimes quite funny. The course is mostly statistical mechanics, so brush up on your probability and prepare to do lots of integrals. The tests weren't hard, except for the final, which was hard but graded fairly. Our TA slacked on grading homeworks, so everyone who did the work got like 100% on it.

Shi - Jie is undoubtedly the best lecturer I have ever had. Thermodynamics is not a trivial subject, however there was never a point where I was not following what he was doing on the board. Shi - Jie will prepare you very well for each exam. Homeworks are conceptually difficult, however unless you don't answer a question you will get a 100%.

I have had this professor for Introduction to Quantum Mechanics and Thermodynamics. There is a homework assignment that is due biweekly, and some of these problems can be difficult, so these may take some time. However, the textbooks, lecture notes, and videos on his canvas page are very helpful for all of these. Clear on what is on exams as well.

I have had this professor for thermodynamics as well (4120) and he acts same in both. Best professor I've ever had. He teaches from the textbook in a creative way, so you can always re read sections if you do not understand. He also posts videos of him solving problems, step by step, which is very helpful. Consistent grader with good feedback.

Lectures are well-paced. Sometimes tests on things that he said in class that aren't in the textbook, but you could probably reason to them if you have time. Exams aren't toughly graded, but they will take all the time you have in class - make sure you know content! Homework isn't long but is /difficult/. Professor is very available outside class.
Exam questions were all related to the material discussed. Still difficult, but more than willing to help and go the extra distance if you put in the effort.

Shi Jie is great. I took Thermodynamics last semester and after taking one look at the book, thought I was going to fail. I ended up with an A. If you pay attention and study hard, then you will pass. He was always willing to clarify, and had some quite elegant explanations for some concepts.

He is the most coherent teacher in the physics department.  His classes my run a little long on occasion, but its worth not feeling completely lost at the end of class. Best physics teach I have ever had.
Excellent Professor, helps make Mandarin more applicable and accessible.
52167 is Chinese 1100! I also am currently taking Chinese 1200 primarily with her, and she's great here too! Learning Chinese gets easier :)

She is a great professor! She's very caring and will support you through learning Chinese. She's a bit timid, but super sweet. She wants to make sure that you understand what you're learning - questions are appreciated. The assignments are all useful and the coursework is manageable. She's fantastic and always accessible outside of class!

Great person, and she loves being an anthropologist, not best professor. Doesn't give work the whole grade rests on three exams. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she doesn't post detailed slides (there are times when it will be a blank slide with a photo and no context). She only gives you information on the slides by word, so you must go to class.
Take this class!! such a great and experienced teacher. Only grades based on exams (no homework) so just study. attendance is not required but her lectures are so good youll want to come to class.

Libby (of course) is amazing. She claims that this class will be harder than anything you've ever done. It was not nearly as hard as she says. Just go to class and study. This class, compared to her other ones though, is a much more independent type of study. You will have to stay focused, just use the time they give you! Ask questions!

libby i know u read these ratings so i just want to say that ily and u have been one of my favorite professors ever. literally u are the coolest person ever and i want to be you some day but that can't happen so i'm gonna have to settle with being myself. oh well. really hope i can take more classes w/ u in the future!! ok goodbye

omg LOVE Dr. Cowgill. Amazing lectures and always has some interesting facts she throws out. Never a dull moment in class. Don't rely on lecture slides, the majority of the exam comes from her mouth, not the slides. I would go back and study harder and differently. My people who don't take good notes by only hearing may need to start practicing.
Absolutely loved this class and would love to take another with Dr. Cowgill.

I definitely recommend this class. Dr. Cowgill is really funny and explains things really well. She doesn't give homework, your grade is based on the tests. If you attend class, you'll be fine. Do not rely on the slides alone, they don't give you all the information you need to do well on the tests. Highly recommend reviewing notes after lectures.

EXACTLY LIKE ABBY FROM NCIS! I had the honor of having libby for an intro anthro class that I was randomly put in as an elective. I wasn't looking forward to this class b/c I knew nothing about anthro and thought it was the study of dirt or sum... Lemme tell u I fell in LOVE with anthro after this class! Libby made every day so fun & interesting!!

One of the best professors I have had at my time at Mizzou, very organized, excited about material, good orator, and just all around a good person. She genuinely made me love economics again because I was shown how it is actually applied in a real world scenario, like healthcare markets, in so many different ways. TAKE THE CLASS.

I am a senior in college, and Liisa Laine is one of very few professors I've had in my undergrad that genuinely made me feel inspired, smart, and excited about economics. She does a phenomenal job at making complex topics digestible, and her lectures feel like those which you see in movies. I wish I could've taken her again.

Dr. Laine is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about health economics. She makes it clear on what she expects for different types of questions. Tests are 75% of your grade and are based off the homework and slides. Lectures prepare you well for the homework and then subsequently the test. Expect to defend your answer not just true/false.

Won't even write out practice problems herself. She just zooms through them on presentations. Ludicrous amount of homework every week. Labs are complete busy work. Take it online if you can because half of the class doesn't finish in-person exams in the given time(which is completely preventable if she'd just expand it).

You are better off teaching yourself the material over anything she can teach you. All of her lectures are rambling nonsense that waste everyone's time. An hour for an exam that a normal prof would give 90 minutes for. I can confidently say I have learned nothing from her, all of the physics I have learned are from the TA or self taught. NEVER TAKE

Take the class asynchronously and don't watch the lectures. Instead, use that time to understand the homework. I learned more gaining through the homework problems. I thought discussion was useful as well. I would recommend going. Labs were super easy. Use old exams to study. She is nice, but get ready to teach yourself. Canvas page is also a mess.

Take the class asynchronously and don't watch the lectures. Instead use that time to go over the homework. I learned more from the homework and the discussions. Go to the discussions they are helpful. Also make sure to go over the practice exams. Labs were super easy. She is really nice, but can't teach. Get ready to teach yourself.
take the class somewhere else and save your sanity

Pretty hard for a 1000 level class, she's very hard to understand at sometimes, and lots and lots of homework. HW represents the exams pretty well so they're pretty predictable. You will spend lots and lots of time outside of class trying to understand the material. Exams way too short for all of the content on it.

Anyone who says this class was insanely hard just didn't keep up with the homework. You are assigned a maximum of 4 assignments per week all of which are self explanatory if you do the problems she goes over in lecture. The key to getting an A in this class is literally just doing the homework every week since her exams use the same problems.

This course was at best, bad. I am a 3.9 GPA and a hard worker, yet a B was all I could pull. The lectures were incredibly difficult to understand -- it took me half of the semester to understand her speaking. There is at a minimum,10 hours of homework a week and the exams are much too short for the amount of problems. Avoid if you can!
Lots of reading. More hands-on than most other history courses. Very well-respected professor; the only con would be that not everything was engaging.

Dr. Santoro is an amazing professor and leads some awesome discussions with students taking the spotlight. Loved talking with her outside of class about various historical topics.
