I can tell she loves her work and talking with students, and even though I'm not a history major or anything adjacent really I wish I could take more classes with her.

Dr. Santoro is a really nice and caring person, but as a professor was not for me. Be expected to read a minimum of like 20 pages every day for her class. There aren't many grades in this class, so be make sure you do the readings and participate a lot in class. Even when there are assignments expect to not know what you are being graded on.

Dr. Santoro is a really nice and caring person, but as a professor was not for me. Be expected to read a minimum of like 20 pages every day for her class usually it was even more than that because there were multiple readings. The bulk of your grade is participation, so if you are in a class full of people who talk a lot, good luck getting points.

Dr. Sowers is possibly one of the best professors at MU. I have NEVER had a professor be so amazing at giving lectures. She makes material easy to understand; she is extremely passionate about what she teaches, and that passion makes an imprint on the students. If I had Sowers teaching all of my classes, I would pass every class with an EASY A
BEST professor on campus! Very knowledgeable and always willing to help her students. Puts you out of your comfort zone to actually learn something.
The best professor I have had. She is an amazing professor and truly cares about your success. She has prepared me more for my career in one class than I have received in any others.

100 percent easily the best professor on campus and CAFNR is lucky to have someone as talented and caring as Professor Sowers. I have taken two of her classes and getting ready to take a third next year and I have to say that she has really helped me become an impressive individual when it comes to placing myself in front of future employers.

Professor Sowers is the best professor I have had while at Mizzou. She cares about students and is the first one to lend a hand in times of struggle. She allows you to come into her office and ask questions before tests as well as lets you know what you personally need to work on. By far the best class and professor I have taken at Mizzou!

Professor Sowers is one of the most amazing teachers I have had in my 4 years of college! Her class was so beneficial for my post-grad endeavors and I will take these tools into my work life forever. You definitely have to put time and effort into it, but she grades fairly and you will actually learn and retain the material.

Fundamentals of communication was the most challenging and MOST REWARDING class I have taken yet at Mizzou. Sowers is absolutely incredible. Everyone should have her as a teacher. She cares about you as an individual and wants to see you succeed.
Linda Sowers is the absolute BEST professor I have ever had. After taking two of her classes, I can truly say that she is incredible and is really trying to help students get a job in the future.

Amazing professor who certainly knows what she's and is passionate about what she's teaching. Class is not very challenging: 5 homework assignments that each take a few hours to do, 5 discussion posts, one exam, and one big project at the end. As long as you watch the lecture videos on pace you'll be fine.

Class was super interesting! Teaches both concepts and math for things in our solar system (i.e. Hohmann transfers and flybys). Lectures were a bit dry, but after I made myself sit down and listen to them, I learned a lot. Hearing about her experiences in the space shuttle program was also super neat!

The way she runs the class can make you want to terror your hair out. The homework assignment are every other week and are "50 questions" but with the multiple parts of each question it can very well turn out to be 200. On top of that there are multiple tries for each question but you lose half the points if you get it wrong. Have to put the workin
Lectures are dry. You can get a B if you don all the homework and submit all the labs. Multiple choice quizzes and exams.

She's an astronaut which is very cool but her lectures are super dull. do the readings and do the homework and go to class. i really like astronomy but didn't love this class because she didn't make it interesting. cool topics but not a great lecturer.

ALL power points from lectures are posted on Canvas for this class, so you only need to show up for clicker points, 5% of your grade. I only opened the book a handful of times, lectures and book material overlap. You get to use 2 pages of notes for the mid term and final, which is a godsend, and the final was curved extremely nicely for my class.

LInda is such a sweet lady and genuinely cares about all of her students. She is very passionate about this class because she used to work for NASA. Her slides are hard to take notes off of sometimes. The labs are very interesting. As long as you stay on top of your homework and notes, you'll do just fine. (You have to work for a good grade!)
Way to hard for a introduction course. Super hard Test. Crazy amounts of homework. Not recommended. Must study very long hours for quizzes and test.
Lots of writing and reading. Accessible outside of class, and the material ties back to all the writing. Thoroughly enjoyed the class.

If you want a professor who respects students, do not take any classes taught by Dr. Reeder. She changes due dates genuinely every other class period. It seems like it is impossible for her to be prepared. She offers no actual helpful feedback while simultaneously not providing any rubrics, which makes understanding grades nearly impossible. Avoid!

Wowza. Linda is interesting. The lectures seem to be thrown together randomly and they never really add up. I like history but this class is a snooze fest. The midterm was intolerable and made me rethink sanity. She is passionate about history but teaching is not her strong suit. I could never reach the TA and communication was never a priority.
We read a LOT in her class. Be prepared to be reading a ton and preparing for participation. She is participating heavy, as well as writing intensive heavy. Tough grader for sure.

The class project is basically your whole grade, but there are weekly reading quizzes on several books. You have to read around 100 pages every week, sometimes more plus research for the project and write a bibliography and historiography. Really unorganized class!! Nothing gets done in class and youre just expected to know what to do

Lecture-based classes that consisted of Professor Reeder rambling on about non-applicable tangents every few slides or so. Never got through an entire presentation due to this. Attendance is not mandatory because she or the TAs will give you the questions/answers to the test in the discussion section. Loved European History but would not recommend.

She wants you to succeed, so that's good. Often gets confused when lecturing, and will explain simple things in too much detail, and the big things not enough.  For example, for World War 2 she said "then the war happened," and then discussion about reconstruction began.  Grading can be interesting as well, changed quiz grades with 1 week left.

I was really excited for this class. The content sounded exciting - Mafia: Myth and Reality, but her lectures are really boring and hard to follow. There is little organization and she goes on crazy tangents while talking. She does grade pretty easily and she's a nice lady; she also knows the content really well, just has a hard time conveying it.
His questions are unfair and he doesnt know what hes doing. Dont take him unless you want to make an easy class super difficult
Super easy class and super sweet teacher who grades super easy

Lectures are just her going on tangents you can barely hear. She doesn't seem to know how to setup iclicker or canvas. Never checks for understanding. Will look at iclicker questions where majority of the class got it wrong and just move on without explaining or teaching why we were wrong. It's all group work & you never know when anything is due.

Lovely lady. If you put in the effort, you will walk away from this class knowing more Italian than from years of high school classes. She is fair and understanding with assignments, and goes above and beyond to make class engaging and fun every day. She's enthusiastic, and more than anything wants to see you succeed. Lisa is the best!

Great teacher, helps a lot, will give you the highest grade she can. tests are hard tho and there is a lot of information to learn, it is very dense, has lots of HW, but she is extremely helpful if u have a question and will even let you re-do a section of the test if you bomb it, and also gives detailed study guides for all tests, plus no final.

Lisa was a first year teacher when I had her. She is very caring of her students, and truly wants everyone to learn. In this class, she teaches about all the regions of Italy and lots of cultural aspects, which is a nice addition to learning the language. This class is easy if you do the homework and pay attention during lecture. I highly recommend
Don't like her as a person but the class so ridiculously easy and there isn't an exam or textbook
Gives support through good vibes and good intentions rather than material support. Lacking in empathy.

I had the opportunity to fall upon Dr. Scheese's class on accident, but I am glad I did so. She not only makes the lectures super entertaining, but allows student participation so it doesn't feel boring. The class is quite participation based, but show up and do your work and it's an easy A. Recommend her classes 10/10!
Don't like her as a person but the class so ridiculously easy and there isn't an exam or textbook
Great professor! Very enthusiastic and encourages student participation. Lots of memorization for the class, but relatively easy exams.
She is a good professor. Gives a lot of room for improvement and offers many opportunities to improve your grade.

Professor Bauer is very kind and constantly offers information and resources to help her students succeed outside of class. She made sure her class was accessible to everyone. She also seemed to have a lot of experience outside of Mizzou, which I thought was cool!

Professor Bauer is a very kind individual that clearly cares about her students. She provided so many resources to everyone that she had no obligation to. Attendance is not mandatory after you reach a certain number of points for in class activities.

I took Forensic Psychology online to complete my minor, and it was very straightforward and easy.  Weekly discussion posts and 4 exams total, lowest one gets dropped. Dr. Bauer and the TA's were very approachable for questions or help.  Interesting content and an easy A.

While learning about research methods may not be the most interesting topic Dr. Bauer manages to make it interesting. She keeps you engages in lectures. Dr. Bauer is also the nicest professor I have had. She is always willing to talk and cares about her students.
I loved this professor and how caring she was. The lectures were a little boring but not bad, they could just feel a little bit long. Overall, I would love to take her class again.

Dr. Bauer is nice and cares about her students, but the course is boring. Presentations are usually close to 100 slides long and there's a lot of redundant content. The assignments are exactly the same every single week - even the discussion questions. If you want to be interested and engaged with the material, take Psych1000 with someone else.

worst class ever. she assigns articles, and the classes are entirely led by her asking questions about the articles and students are expected to teach her class for her based on their answers. she doesnt even provide notes. why would anyone take notes based on what a student is saying vs the professor? i dont understand what she expects form us

I have taken several courses with Dr. Sattenspiel and have gotten to work with her on a few occasions. Her classes are challenging at times, but as long you are an engaged student you will do fine. She is INCREDIBLY intelligent in her field, super willing to help you, and is HIGHLY respected within her community! My favorite professor ever!

One of the more interesting Anthro professors I've had so far. The subject matter was completely fascinating and Dr. Sattenspiel was very knowledgable. Grades come from two (at times challenging) tests and three short papers.  If you're any good at writing, this class is an easy A. You probably won't even need the textbooks.

I took Human Biological Variation with Dr. Sattenspiel. This is not an easy course but her lectures are insightful with clear descriptions. I'm NOT an anthro major and did well in the class. She's always available to help, an awesome professor overall. No tests or quizes, only short essays!

For Anthro majors, she is wonderful. She is very knowledgeable and cares about her students. She is an odd person but still a good teacher and a good advisor. I doubt if she is comfortable teaching an intro class and may seem like a grouch but she is really a kind person.

I do not understand the other comments posted here.  They seem like the angry comments of whiny adolescents who would rather have grades handed to them than to actually learn something for themselves.  Dr. Sattenspiel is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about her teaching.  She is a highly regarded, well-respected, member of her field.

The class was semi-interesting, although she spends much too much time on her actual studies which aren't always that interesting.  Make sure to write everything down, she sometimes asks silly questions on tests.  Tests are super easy as she gives the questions to you before the test.  The books are helpful.  The TAs are generally of little help.

Dr. Sattenspiel is a very established researcher within her field, most of these comments come from an Intro class, which for most teachers is not their speciality. She shines in her Plagues and People class, because that is her speciality and for what she is respected. Besides, what teacher thrives on teaching intro classes?
I loved loved loved frick! Shes the best professor i've ever had in the j-school and I still think about her and her class often when I walk by her classroom. HIGHLY recommend this class!!

Frick is an actual journalist that is still writing/working in journalism which you can't say for all journalism profs. She is amazing. Frick is an easy grader, makes class enjoyable by creating a playful/chill environment and tries to make required work fun. I would take her again and recommend her to any J school student

Class is pretty easy if you keep up with homework and attend class regularly. He does talk pretty fast and isn't the best at time-management (you might end up needing to consult the textbook over stuff he goes over at the end). Grade consists of tests, which are online and open note, and homework, which is online.
Does not treat you with respect. He knows the content but awful professor.
He asked a kid if our test was easy, after he responded saying no he proceeded to laugh in his face about how hard it was. Literally prides himself on the difficulty of his exams.
Horrible.

Definitely one of the hardest classes you'll take if you aren't an economics major. That being said, unlike most of the classes at Mizzou, you actually have to work for an A in this one. He is incredibly knowledgeable and if you can force yourself to listen to his lectures, you'll learn a lot about the stuff that happens every day in our economy.

If you show up to class on a regular basis you should be fine. He'll occasionally give out xc just for showing up (he likes to give extra clicker questions and points on Fridays as well). As for exams, so long as you study the practice exams and the hw you should be fine.

This is by far one of the most challenging courses I have taken at Mizzou, but also one of the most rewarding.  A lot of people complain about this course- they're just unwilling to work for their grade and will be in for a sorry shock when they hit the real world. Dr. Thomas is a phenomenal professor with tons of knowledge that is very important!

Dr. Thomas is a phenomenal professor. His class was extremely challenging but very rewarding. Dr. Thomas really cares that you comprehend the material- it is very important stuff! He has a deep knowledge of economics and passion for finance. Incredibly smart guy who deserves much more credit.

This is literally the worst class at Mizzou.  Professor Thomas is extremely smart but does not understand how to teach economics to non-majors. His class is boring, as he just basically lectures by speaking at you.  His exams are next to impossible, and  l find a way to ask 4 questions in just 1.  Homework is nearly impossible.  He doesn't care

Dr. Thomas's class covered a substantial range of material; however, tests and quizzes were multiple choice and always included opportunities for extra credit. Slide material was up-to-date (usually  to the most recent month) and useful for studying for exams   Dr. Thomas is opinionated but well-reasoned, respectful, and available for extra help.

Dr. Huneycutt was definitely knowledgeable, but the class was poorly designed and by the end of it, we were about 3 weeks behind the syllabus. Reading assignments for the week were huge and we were expected to talk about them in depth in class for points. Not hard to get a good grade in with effort (extra credit!), but frustrating and stressful.

Dr. Huneycutt is clearly very knowledgable in the field but is not equipped to teach. She is nearly impossible to reach outside of class, the syllabus changes drastically with little to no notice, and loads of reading is assigned the night before discussion. Grading takes FOREVER and overall the class is conducted poorly.
Very well educated and always happy to discuss any time period in history. She also loves giving valuable feedback.

In general, the class seemed to be structured horribly. She never seemed to post assignments, so if your grade sucked, you were kind of stuck with it. While the lectures may have been good, it didnt make up for the fact that there was hardly anyway to show what you had learn. Also, she was very hard to reach out to outside of class.

Professor Huneycutt is an entertaining lecturer and you can tell she is passionate about her field. Outside of class, expect to read a lot (especially for the honors section), as well as use the textbook to fill in gaps from lecture. Also, show up to lecture for occasional extra credit. Three papers, short quizzes, and discussions determine grade.

I worked harder in this class than in any class I have taken in two years of college at Mizzou. Her lectures are challenging and assume youve done the assigned reading beforehand. She demands a lot of writing, but gives excellent feedback and is willing to read several drafts. When I finally got an A on my third paper, I knew Id earned it.

Professor doesn't use canvas or put grades online at all. Rarely gives feedback and grades essays really tough. Rarely gives out A's on assignments. Lots of papers and extra readings. Way too much work for a 1000 level class! Would highly recommend choosing a different professor.

She's an engaging lecturer, though since she rarely uses visuals it's sometimes tough to gauge how important some bits are. Quizzes are extra credit, and 75% of your grade comes from the three term papers. The remaining quarter is from the final, which is basically just a rehash of all of her previous quizzes. Go to lecture, read, and you'll pass.

Class is kind of hard, tests have questions that are nothing like the homework or class examples. But the lectures are great, good pacing and she has a good voice. High quality teacher, but the tests have some tricky questions that take deep thought. Big curve at the end of the semester which helped me a lot.

She tried to get students to cheat by baiting them with a "accidental" zoom message to the entire class, stating everything is on chegg, and claimed it was for a professor. Then went after people for leaving Canvas pages during exams. Zero rounding. Words her questions so terrible. completely different than HW and exams.
Very helpful in office hours. Difficult class but she makes it doable with her lectures and detailed homework solutions.
Not my favorite teacher. She is an alright person, but can come across as intimidating.

This class is one of the hardest classes I have taken.  However, Dr. Thombs made this class possible.  She goes over examples in class and is always willing to help.  She gives detailed solutions to each homework assignment as well as the exams when they are returned to the students after being graded.

I took her online Adv'd Behavior Mgmt Course online through MU Direct. I liked the set up because you go at your own pace and she doesn't make you do discussion boards. You read almost every chp in the book. Heavy quizzes. The case study requires a classroom setting to observe and implement a behavior plan so be aware before it's too late.

Dr. Bradley requires attendance, but not to a degree that will affect your grade. Lectures are difficult to follow as the slideshows don't contain much or any text, but exams were all open note. Required readings were often difficult, but here were multiple opportunities for extra credit.

I took this class as four week, and lemme say... She does cram 16 weeks into 4 so heads up! However, having a well maintained schedule you should be fine. You have to have creative writing skills to pass this class. This isn't a research paper, go above and beyond on describing that tree and the sun bathing on it. Class is easy but requires detail.

His first language is Spanish, and he graded us (in elementary Spanish) by comparing our skill level to his. We all were given poor grades on everything and now more than half of his class is dropping. When we confronted him about it, he only avoided questions. friendly guy, but you're just paying money for a class to drop later on. Steer clear.
Tests are extremely hard and barely match the lectures.

Hands down favorite professor at Mizzou. He makes lectures enjoyable while also insuring that all students understand the material. It is important to go every day as there is a lot of hard content covered each class. While still one of the harder classes offered, Grafakos makes 4700 a class that you look forward to going to.

I felt that Dr. Grafakos was very knowledgeable and passionate about the material. The class is difficult, but if you show up to class and try your best he will notice. He made an effort to learn the names of hard working students. Put in an honest effort and you'll be okay.

calc 2 is rough anyways, but prepare to study in this class. hes not super open for office hours/likes to throw curveballs during exams. beware that on multiple choice he often changes the format on the correct answer and wont give partial credit for correct answer in a diff. format. DO NOT SKIP RECITATION. ended w an a but rough road to get there

Loukas Grafakos was an exceptional teacher who explained things very well and was very passionate about math. He was very understanding and caring in all my interactions with him and went out of his way to congratulate people who did well in class. His course was exceptionally difficult, but that's a common experience in Calc 2.

Class is the hardest thing I've ever done in my life.  Professor is knowledgeable about the subject but sometimes doesn't explain enough what he is talking about.  He goes very fast making it impossible to write good notes, and the tests are simply impossible to get a good grade.  Teacher is very nice, but the class is impossible to get an A.

Dr Grafakos has tests that will be quite difficult but nothing utterly unfair. He likes to cover the more difficult problems in class or on one of the prior tests. You can tell he's passionate about Math but sometimes the lectures just didn't cover the material clear to me. Problems from the textbook and practice webassign was super helpful.
The tests are pretty difficult. His accent takes some getting used to. The first 2-3 weeks of class are review and super easy. Don't skip the recitations, they are very helpful.
Great teacher! She is very kind and explains things well.
Prof. Fan is knowledgeable and prepares her classes very well. She also provides many examples and practice with immediate feedback during class. Office hours are also helpful.
Content delivery was not very clear.
Professor Lu is a good teacher. She explains things well and gives lots of practice. I really enjoyed this class and felt like I learned a lot.

Lu is a nice person, but not the best teacher. She just reads off the slides, making lectures drag on. She does give participation points during most lectures. 3 midterms and a final, very difficult tests. Also gave 3 assignments. Assigned a huge group project which was assigned right before Thanksgiving, and due the day after we returned.

Had her for Math 4370, 4371, and 4372. Fantastic teacher and resource for actuarial students at Mizzou. As long as you put in the effort for the quizzes and tests, she will see the work you put in and you end up with a good grade. Attendance not required but recommended.
Very formula heavy class that requires a lot of practice and studying. Exam questions are usually taken from homeworks. Weekly quizzes and homework assignments help to keep up with the material.

Although homework was not mandatory in this class, Professor Bobitan gives plenty of suggested problems.  The material and class are quite difficult, but the quiz and test problems are similar to (or the same as) the suggested problems and class examples.  She is willing to meet with you to help you understand the material well.

Class is pretty easy if you keep up with homework and attend class regularly. He does talk pretty fast and isn't the best at time-management (you might end up needing to consult the textbook over stuff he goes over at the end). Grade consists of tests, which are online and open note, and homework, which is online.
Does not treat you with respect. He knows the content but awful professor.
Go to class, he has random and weekly quizzes. If you actually try on the HW, the quizzes aren't bad at all. He grades pretty harshly, but the tests aren't that hard overall; know the material.
Stay away hes not a good professor. Gpa distribution is a 2.3-2.4 every year.

Rivera is an impossible teacher. He speaks so fast during lecture that you cannot keep up with him. He also grades so harshly on the exams that if you aren't 100% confident in the question, don't waste your time. Its not a for sure thing but its possible that this class will stop me from graduation (I have all A's in my core department classes).

Easily the worst professor I have ever had. Homework is not helpful and is incredibly long. For ENGR 2100 my grade was severely dropped due to missing few days with announced quizzes that had 50% averages anyways. Appears as though he finds joy in punishing class when attendance is low. Materials are not helpful. Take online section if available.

He is the professor that if you show that you want to learn the material, he will give you the benefit of the doubt. expect once a week HW's on mastering (sucked). overall if you show that you care, he will give you the grade that you want/need
Sweet, friendly.

I've always struggled with math but I could somewhat understand what was going on through this course thanks to the professor. She tends to explain things very well, but be prepared that there are more difficult things she didn't cover in the homework and exams. If you go through the homework and study, you'll do fine.

I liked how she dropped 6 attendance grades I thought that was very nice because that was not the case for most classes. What my complaint is, I felt like my math skills didn't improve, homework was extremely long and took a ridiculous amount of time to complete, and test questions felt much harder than what we had worked on or reviewed.

She's super sweet! My only complaints are that the average homework assignment is 70 questions and just repeats the same kinds of problems so that's annoying. Basically a review of high school algebra. The TAs are psycho though.

If you take her class make sure to have a graphing calculator! She says there won't be graphing on the exams then pulls out 4 questions about graphs in the final without any final reviews or anything. She also goes through stupid easy concepts for forever and difficult problems she just skips through. Be prepared to teach yourself!

She was very rude and unhelpful. I would not recommend this teacher to anyone ever. She doesnt seem to care much about her students well beings at all considering how much I know my peers and I tried to reach out to her but all she ever gave back was attitude.

Ms. DeSouza is one of the nicest teachers I've ever had. I have always been notoriously bad at math and she truly helped me learn the basics of Algebra. She is incredibly helpful and never makes you feel stupid for being in intermediate math. Highly recommend taking this class with her if you struggle with math.

I loved Mrs D. She is a very sweet, funny woman and cares about her students. I had her for int. algebra, and despite hating math, she was very patient, answered as many questions as you had, and was very helpful. Math sucks, but she made it a little better. Take her if you can!
Professor Kraxberger is very kind and smart. She'll work with you if you need help.
J1010 is useless. The professor tried her best given the lack of content.
Easiest intro Journalism class there is. Show up to class and do the online assignments and you will pass. All there is to it.

This class is so boring. SO BORING. You have to take it for the J-School so it's a requirement but it's seriously the worst. Don't take notes, just buy the TopHat and you'll be fine. Also it's a pass/fail and, besides the fight to stay awake, is extremely easy.
No Comments

Horrible. DO NOT TAKE CLASSES WITH HER!!!! She will make your life hell for 16 weeks. The class is only worth 100 points and its all group projects. She doesn't answer questions and creates a very negative learning environment for her students. I'm warning you, DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!
I wouldn't take a class with her again. interesting classes and course materials but you're as good teaching yourself the stuff. Group-heavy. very adamant on never giving full points.

Entire class is one group project; had a group that didn't contribute, & after countless emails asking for help one unhelpful email was returned. Ended with a B as a result of poor course design & a teacher that knows her stuff & teaches (interesting) material well but doesn't know how to be a good person. Am not excited to have her again.

New class. Professor was relaxed. During lectures, told what would be on the quizzes. Had guest lecturers who provided quality, real world information. The class focused on applicable public health in current society. Would take class(es) with her again.
She really knows her stuff!!!

Wow!  For a 4 credit hour class she requires a TON of work, 10 hours a week of clinical time  plus 20+ hours a week on completing assignments.  The most frustrating was not knowing until the last minute that we had to make a conference style poster as a final project.  Turned an interesting subject into a nightmare.
Rude, Not Caring If best try to avoid her at all times you will have her as a teacher until you graduate she is very detailed oriented and is not afraid to call you out very nasty woman .

She is the worst teacher Ive ever had. She doesnt know how to grade properly. All of our assignments were graded one day before the grades were so we couldnt fix anything ahead of time. Has way to many expectations

Kim is very knowledgeable and a great instructor! She gives lots of creative freedom and very good feedback. She provides lots of examples for class projects and is very available when you need help. I found the class difficult, mostly because of the time it required. But that is expected when it comes to animation. I definitely learned a lot!

Very knowledgable on the subjects being taught, and had amazing advice or feedback when stuck. Parts of her class, like being required to present every project completed, was horrible, and no one really enjoyed that aspect. I think without that included, everything was great.

I loved that she gave a lot of feedback, but she tended to tear students work down rather than build it up, which was kind of frustrating. Also, her grading system was difficult to get a high A in. But if you're dedicated and really want to go into film - go for it! She's super nice and has a great personality.

I love Prof. Kim! I actually bettered my work because of her and her awesome feedback. You can tell she actually cares about her students success and wants to help. Very nice person and also very understanding. Highly recommend her class.

Professor facilitates lots of discussion in class, so be prepared to give lots of feedback on classmates' projects. She gives feedback, but she grades very tough and inconsistent though and I felt that, at times, I was rolling the dice with how well she would grade me. At times I even felt that she wasn't that knowledgeable about the material.
She hasn't updated her lecture videos since 2020. For a class that uses software that is updated yearly, that is unacceptable.
This class is very hard and you have lots to do. Suprised I got an a
Lyria is fun and very cool. best teacher i had in college

Lyria was amazing!! Her class was very fun, and she gave us the freedom to do just about whatever we wanted as well as the opportunity to be creative. At the same time though; she was very critical and helpful in her instructions. Not only did she help me with my projects for her class, but she also gave me great advice for the future!

Professor Gudenkauf is a great person, but not the best at teaching. She mostly does example problems in class and expects you to do almost all of the practice problems in the textbook to prepare for the tests (and the answer keys are sometimes wrong). Also, the grade is fully dependent on the tests and final, so STUDY. Beware of pop quizzes.

This was the hardest class I have taken. She does not really teach during class and speeds through lecture slides with no time to write anything down, then only does 2–3 examples. This is because she formatted the class to read the textbook before class. Weekly random pop quizzes make attendance mandatory. Exams are very hard. Many people failed.

I don't normally rate profs, but she is better off in industry instead of teaching. Office hours are walk in, unless she has an appointment, but you do not know until you get there. She does not round grades, even .1% and after talking to her, she said that 30 of the 90 people in her class will drop or fail. Take literally any other professor.

The other reviews here are accurate. He's clearly smart but doesn't take social cues. He picks on kids who look like easy targets, calling on them to answer questions in front of the class. I witnessed literal public humiliation! It was cringe and hard to be in the room. This class caused me to re-evaluate my major.

For lectures, Prof Almasri was great at explaining concepts and walking through examples. Likes to call on random people. Goes over time a lot. Scheduled extra review sessions that were usually cancelled

While he is extremely knowledgeable about the course and its contents, Prof. Almasri does an extremely poor job of teaching the contents. He frequently showed up late/barely on time to class and would teach after its end. Exams are very difficult, and he does nothing to foster class participation. I sincerely hope that I never have him again.

Yikes. Prof. Almasri is incredibly unorganized. Shows up to class barely on time (or late) and always goes over time. He forgets when the homework he assigned is due or forgets to assign it altogether (doesn't adjust due date). Students called him out for incorrectly grading a test and he told them he wasn't going to fix it.
Harsh at teaching topics. Definitely a very smart guy, but not meant to teach topics.
My goat Spanish teacher, other than Ivan. He's really funny when you get to know him, and it's easy to get an A as long as you pay attention and do the readings.
Best Spanish teacher at Mizzou. Easy class. He is funny and sweet. Read the things right before class and did great on quizzes.
He seems to be biased against men as a whole in his lectures and covering stories and asking questions that are biased against men. He seems to bash men as a group.

He isn't the most consistent of professors, but I honestly think that's better. He changed based on how the class performs. Everyone keeps making a mistake? He'll start taking points off for it. Nobody does the readings? Quizzes are back! It is easy to do well as long as you so the homework and understand it. This is advanced Spanish.

the class is so boring at times he is disorganized, doesn't follow his own course calendar he grades really easily allows you to make up anything you miss takes attendance every day, is part of your grade doesn't give you more than like a 2 hour notice for quizzes, check canvas regularly

Prof. Badiane is very passionate about the course material but his style is pretty disorganized. He's a pretty easy grader and a really understanding guy. I would recommend taking his writing-intensive section if you need it for your major. It's one of the easier options. Having it on zoom was rough but same goes for any discussion-based class.

Was told this class would be an easy A so I took it, but for some reason he refuses to give anyone in the class 10/10 points for participation despite showing up and speaking at least once every class period. Not sure why he is being so difficult this semester, but I would not take this again his grading criteria is too tough and unspecific.

The class is a little monotonous but there are no surprises and you know what to expect each time! Professor Badiane was really kind and flexible with online class and was one of my more forgiving professors relating to covid circumstances which I know we all really appreciated. Overall, I would definitely recommend him!

Overall this course was a great experience for me. The lecture material was clear and straightforward. We read quite a bit from the textbook for homework assignments but it was a pretty interesting book so it actually wasn't terrible. There was also a group presentation. Prof. Tiwari wants to help her students succeed and is a great resource.

Tiwari was pretty good at explaining concepts and answering questions. HWs were for completion, a few quizzes but they weren't bad and we got to drop at least 1, and exams weren't too bad either. Always posted solutions so you could review. Sometimes let the class get out of hand with off-topic questions

quite literally zero structure to the class, if u miss a class u won't know if there's a test because he tells u literally 1 class ahead to study so u have to come to EVERY class and there is no schedule on syllabus. quizzes on stuff barely covered. pretty condescending at times as well. assigns articles no one can understand and then blames you

Never updates you to any thing about your grade,literally expects you to guess. Gives horrible pop exams that he only gives two days in advance to study for. Expects you to have time to go see him in his office to get any updates. Avoid this class unless you have photographic memory.
Class was always entertaining. Tests and quizzes are ok if you stay on top of the material. He's one of the funniest professors I've had at MU. Going to office hours helped me a lot.
Very enthusiastic about research. Gives random quizzes throughout semester that tests stuff barely gone over.

Honestly, he is the worst professor I have ever had. Nothing we talked about in class was ever tested over. He assigned really dull scientific articles and randomly quizzed us over them and we only used the textbook once. He was disorganized, often told us wrong information about grading and  he would blame the students if discussion sucked.

Mar was a fantastic, engaging professor, and I was excited to come to every class! I learned more in this class than any previous Spanish class. She clearly explained difficult to understand plot points & literary devices. However, she gives no partial credit on multi-select Canvas homework that composes 20% of the final grade. An A was a 94%.

LOTS OF HOMEWORK, BE PREPARED TO READ. Homework 2x a week. She will dock you points if you don't at least participate twice per class day. Heavy on projects. Had three projects due in one week and a final the next week. Goes through material very fast. Take notes and you'll be fine. Very fun and happy while teaching though. Wouldn't take again.

Mar is by far the best Spanish professor I have had at Mizzou. She is always excited to teach class and makes you feel comfortable to learn and participate. Her homework can be difficult at times, but if you participate in class she will generously bump your grade at the end of the semester. She is an amazing person and educator!
Mar is a wonderful teacher, and person in general. She is very enthusiastic about teaching spanish, and will keep you engaged in class. I have only good things to say about her

Mar is by far the best Spanish professor Ive ever had. She is so sweet & engages the class really well. Shes very approachable and understanding, and communicates well with her students. Though the class is difficult, she makes it interesting and doable. I truly cannot recommend this professor enough!!

Im a native spanish speaker, though spanish classes are hard for me because I didnt grow up learning textbook spanish or how to conjugate. When I tell you Ive never been so frustrated with how she grades-her instructions are never clear, hw is weighted heavier than tests. Basically impossible to get an A, let alone a B.

In 8 years of spanish classes, Mar is the best spanish professor I've ever had. She is sweet, funny, and loves to connect with her students. She assigns some tough readings and projects that seem daunting, but she is super accessible outside of the classroom. She even helped me prepare for a job interview. Get ready to work hard but learn a lot!

Very enthusiastic, always has a smile on her face! Not a super easy class but she explains concepts well and makes students feel comfortable asking questions when they don't understand something. As long as you're prepared to do the homework and go to class everyday, I definitely would recommend taking this class with her!

Mara is a great professor. She is passionate about her work and accessible outside of class. Same expectations each week (2 lectures with a quiz, 2 video quizzes, 1 reading quiz). Class was interesting. Graded by a few things so be sure to maximize points.
Mara is a great professor. The class itself is a bit hard but there are the same expectations weekly (2 lectures 3 quizzes). She's accessible outside of class and passionate about her work.

I LOVED professor Aruguete. She is an amazing lecturer and doesn't emphasize big tests or papers. This style allows you to watch her lectures, take notes, and learn. There are quizzes every week, a midterm, and a final. However, her lectures are very enjoyable, and she is accessible by email. I would take classes from her again in the future!
Super easy class and seems like a nice professor! Interesting content and easy to follow along
Amazing professor, so kind and caring. She has a great personality and is so understanding. Her class was so well structured and easy. Highly recommend you take her class,
Literally loved her so much I struggled at the beginning but if you actually do this class and work in it its not difficult and the information stuck so easily

This class was pretty fun. There is a good amount of work (5 assignments) each week. But once you get used to the schedule it's really easy. The lectures were interesting, not very long, and she was very flamboyant.
He knows his stuff, but makes you do to much extra work for his classes.I would not take him again.

Professor Vital is a very kind instructor. He treats students as friends, rather than an authority figure. This class is a move at your own pace structure, with weekly reflections. However, once you fall behind it is hard to catch up as other projects are constantly being started. That being said, he's willing to work with you and is accessible.
She's very interested in student learning.She used unique approaches to teaching that made the class a lot more interesting than the typical lecture setting. Would definitely recommend.

Dr. Mogetta seems very passionate about the field. Each week we read the material and made a discussion post (300 words), and then replied to a peer (150 words). Discussions were fun and engaging. Then, we would take a quiz; it was open note and you can find all the answers in the modules. The final paper was fun, ~1800 words.

this class is not all that it was advertised to be, with a crazy amount of reading and attention to detail needed, the quizzes and discussions are very vague and confusing. even if you can read 30 pages about Pompeii houses and retain it all, you will still struggle to get a good grade due to poor definitions in quizzes

 this class is AMS-2450.

This professor has no care for your personal life. miss a lecture? Sorry, write a 2 page paper to make it up. she thinks the world should revolve around her classes. I am infuriated. She is so picky with grading. Has made me cry on many occasions out of pure rage. Changed all my work to make it her own. I'm fed up. I'll never take her class again.

Mikaela did the teaching, but Marci did all the behind the scenes, when emailing her she was always helpful, and she prioritizes students who haven't gotten as many opportunities in the class so that they can catch up and get more from the course. She seemed to care, but she also had some disrespectful tendencies, and we never actually saw her.

Zero respect for student time. As a prevet student, I spent more time on this 3 credit elective than my 4 credit physics & 3 credit organic chem class combined. The excessive group work outside class was beyond unreasonable. I love horses & was excited to work with sale foals in the next course, but the coarse load isn't worth it so I never did.
No respect for student time. Nice and respected most of the time. Will set off if you do something a little too wrong. Grading for this class was horrible.....just never gets done.

Marci's tests can be difficult and detail oriented, but otherwise she is a passionate and enthusiastic teacher. She gives what I feel is a reasonable amount of homework and can relate to student's lives. She expects students to participate in class and be professional in their conduct. Be prepared to put a little effort into her class.

I was very excited to take her class, as I have a lot of experience working in that field. She's a good teacher who's understanding/easy to talk to and I liked her class a lot. However, her tests were very hard as they are all written (no multiple choice) and she expects your answers to not only be dead-on but be very specific. Fun but stressful.

Marci's expectations of her students are very clear. It is not hard to understand what material is most important and how to do well in the class. I think a lot of the issue lies in the fact that people don't like "hard work" but Marci is a good teacher if you actually go and listen to the lecture.

She is a terrible teacher. She is not understanding or helpful. She has a "power" issue and has to have control. She talks down to her students and treats anyone that doesn't have a passion for horses like crap. She is absolutely terrible. I still received a decent grade in the class but I hated every day that I had to listen to her "teach."

I took this fall of 2023, she was so easy going and overall a great professor! For the exams you got to choose 10 out of the 20 questions to answer, you did not have to answer all the questions unless you wanted to. If you go to lecture and listen you will do just fine!

Dr. Shannon is very kind and caring. She wants everyone to get an A in her class. She offers extra credit and gives review sessions before each test. The tests are easy as long as you understand and review the lectures. The final is optional. This was her first semester teaching this course and she did a very good job!
Super chill teacher but you can tell he is very knowledgable in this subject, highly recommend.

Truly an amazing guy would definitely recommend! PLEASE use hemmingway editor to check for grammatical errors the TA's do not play with grammatical errors for those first few assignments (also papers are usually 1-2 pages max). MGMT 3000W will feels like a filler class but Marco tries to find ways to make content more interesting.

Very easy class, just a boring subject. Marco is a great guy, but I think this class should not be required. Lots of extra credit opportunities, one group project, but the grading for papers is extremely annoying. Even if you get full credit, you're required to revise it which makes no sense.

i dreaded going to his class everyday, lecture wasn't great and attendance was mandatory. tests were easy and only had 3 grades in the class (quiz, midterm, final). study guides are the exact test and tests are open note but also all open ended
Very easy history class. open note tests and quizzes with the exact the exact questions on the review guides as the actual tests. very knowledgeable professor as well. great course.
His lectures are mandatory, exams and quizzes are essay based but he lets you know what to expect.

Do not take this class, so lecture heavy with a lot of information (typically unnecessary info) thrown at you. If you miss 3 classes, 20% of your grade is immediately removed. The only graded assignments are 2 exams, and 2 quizzes.

He talks way too fast and throws a ton of information at you in every lecture and doesn't post the slides after. There's two open note tests based on the lectures, a midterm and a final which are a few short answer questions and an essay question. There's also three quizzes based on assigned readings. I'd take another class if you can.
Best professor I've had yet.

Very lecture heavy, notes move SO FAST, I couldn't type fast enough. Lectures & notes aren't uploaded. Attendance is required and PASSED AROUND through the class. It got to a point where reading the actual constitution was easier than his notes. I filled out an entire bluebook during one test and extra credit is only 10 points for a two page paper.

His class is the worst I've taken in college. He makes you buy around 10 books for the class, only for us to talk about them for a week before moving on. He centers the class material around the topics he wants to write about for his next book rather than what the class says it will in the course description. Do not take.

Okay, I really liked her. She was a less harsh grader than my last Spanish professor and, if you listen closely to the things she says, she is really freaking funny. If you're paying attention, being kind, and participating, then she'll like you. It's that simple.

She is tough, but nothing out of the ordinary. Her instructors were good and class was easy. There is a lot of homework though and she does not accept late work. She is a tough grader and not very lenient. Just get all your homework done on time and SHOW UP. Also she doesn't excuse absences unless you have a sick note or something.

Prof. Murillo can often be a bit strict/blunt, but she does a decent job explaining concepts and cares about her students as long as they show that they care about the class. Keep track of the calendar ahead of time, communicate, participate, and you'll enjoy class. (Note, I took the honors version of the class with a smaller class size)
She does not care about you or your wellbeing.
She's strict but you'll learn

In my entire school career, I have not had a worse professor. We were technically a "hybrid" course which could explain for some of the issues. You are expected to check the calendar every day and if you miss an assignment, tough luck. Do all of the HW and you should pass. Do not take this professor if you want to actually learn the material.
The professor was caring, but sometimes went away from the questions she was asked.
Communication is important with this professor.

Professor Martinez was so sweet and really fun in class. She was clear on what was expected and was really kind when you made mistakes. The class itself isn't the easiest thing ever, but as long as you go to class and participate plus do the homework it should not be too hard.

This professor is terrible. She was constantly underprepared and distracted in class. What activities we did in class were confusing and unhelpful. She is unable to explain concepts in English. Classes often ran long due to her incompetence. Grades come in very late, and the grading is strict. I would not recommend her as a teacher.

Profe Martinez is so sweet and funny! She's my favorite professor so far and makes me actually look forward to going to class. This class is easy for me because I took Spanish in high school. If you study and do the homework, you'll be fine for the tests. Lots of homework, but most of the answers are on quizlet.

She is actually from Germany, but her English is very, very good. She has an accent but it doesn't get in the way. She has a funny way of saying some things like instead of "_____ means" she says "What means _____". She is pretty cool and very understanding. Class is hard because its a language but she's a great one to take it with.
Great professor. Kind and understanding, willing to hear students out and communicate.

Wonderful professor that showed she truly cares about the subject and her students. One of the nicest people I've met. The course was reading heavy and sometimes the work load was overwhelming, but she worked with the class to ease the pressure and push back assignments. She made a real effort to make sure everyone understood the subject.

The reading assignments are not necessary to pass. She blows through her notes so be ready to write a lot. If you study your notes enough the tests should not be to hard. Attendance does not count as a grade but if you want a decent grade you will have to go.

First of all this class is not an easy A despite what my adviser said, at least not with this teacher. Her accent is really thick so sometimes it is hard to understand what she is saying as she pronounces some words differently. Also has high expectations and is cold towards you if you don't meet them. Have to go to class or you'd easily fail.

All information given in lecture. She goes FAST, so prepare to miss some things. The class itself wasn't too difficult, as long as you showed up to take notes. She doesn't usually post note slides online and when she does they are lacking some of the materials said in class. Assigned a ton of readings, but you don't have to read them to pass.

Discussion section leader. Very smart & really sweet. Often late to class, but not a big deal. Gives really good essay feedback; is a tough grader on papers, often assigns multiple things due the same day, but they're usually pretty fun to do if you like Greek mythology. Do your reading and use lots of text references in papers and you'll be fine.

I've taken Italian in the past so it helped that I had background knowledge coming into the class because she mostly only speaks Italian. I like it because it forces you to use context clues. Of course, if you ask what something means she will gladly help. She is young & funny. Love her class & that's good because I have it everyday.
Very genuine teacher that is extremely accessible inside and outside of the class room.  Showing up daily is very big for her, she wants to see that you are interested in getting better each day
Very good. She is pretty laid back and helps you when you need it. Just don't use your phone or computer in class and you'll be fine.
A very helpful professor that makes criteria very clear. Attendance is mostly necessary and is a very nice grader when it comes to late work. 100% would take again also makes the class fun.

Very meh, better than some other professors I've heard. Tests are just review questions, so generally easy. I don't think she would make or break a grade, it'll probably be effort for whatever grade you get.
Nearly impossible to understand. Ended up just having to teach myself the course.

She tries to communicate the material, but it seems like she is really teaching herself rather than others. Grading on quizzes is extremely confusing, sometimes you get credit for showing work and getting close and sometimes you do the process correctly but mess up at the very end and get 0.

I really liked her personality. She seemed somewhat cold at the beginning, but she warmed up as the semester continued. However, she was quite strict and had her rules. Definitely pay attention during lectures and do the homework.

Marina is a smart individual, but she might not be for everyone. She teaches from examples and talks through them. Attendance is sometimes counted; she often forgot in my class. Marina has a thick accent, but you get used to it. There are also quizzes every week; prepare for them! The study guides were very similar to the actual exam.

Marina is nice, but it is too old-fashioned to learn from her. She only does 1-3 math problems on the chalkboard and points to a pre-written notes sheet for the rest. She has an accent and struggles with questions which makes math and word problems difficult to understand. The class was supposed to self-teach the calculus, so I wouldn't retake it.

She can be intimidating, but Professor Makarova really does care about her students. Although attendance isn't mandatory, going to all the lectures really helped me as she repeats the main concepts so its drilled into your head by the end of the lecture. A lot of people on here thought she was a tough grader but I think she grades pretty fairly.

Teacher is so hard to understand. I go to every lecture and find myself lost by the end. She reads through examples rather than teaching them. Does not respond to emails for help and grades really hard.

I took the honors humanities sequence and had prof. Folescu as my discussion instructor. They are very nice and personable but can sometimes be confusing with their analyses. They can be a tough grader so it was hard to get a good grade since pretty much the only assignments we had were a midterm, final, and a paper.

They were really sweet but I found their lectures mostly boring and nonlinear. I took Philosophy of Film with them and they picked good films but their analysis was confusing. There was a reason that barely anyone showed up to class in the last month. No tests just in class papers. I did well on them but feedback I asked for was not too helpful.

This class was really tough. Professor Folescu is super passionate about philosophy, but the course was confusing to keep up with because we got so off track at times. However, there are no tests; only papers. If you go to her office hours, she will give you feedback and help you improve your papers before you submit them.

Professor Folescu is a super personable teacher. I took logic with her and she did a good job making sure people understood the material. With that being said, it was a tough course, and I don't think I would have gotten an A if I didn't go to her office hours. If you show her you are making an effort, she will be more forgiving in final grades.

Dr. Folescu is very passionate about what she does. She does a great job of writing down what she lectures on so we don't miss any of it. There are many times where the class can get boring though after a long lecture and she tends to repeat herself a lot. There are only 3 grades so participating is a key value to your grade in this class.

Dr. Skubic is a really fun and chill professor for an ECE elective. She cares about students trying to learn the material and focuses on the material more than the grades. Understanding to an extent and firm in expectations for the class. Good choice and I enjoyed her a lot.

I don't know how the other professors teach this class, but Animal Phys is SUPPOSED to be hard. Yes, his tests are detailed, but they're always over his lectures (you will have to pay attention in class). The material is interesting and you'll learn a lot - if you try to.

Kirk seems like a great person, but there are better professors you can get for this class. He uses a flipped-classroom style for his lectures, which doesnt work well for a lot of people. You get to use a crib sheet on every exam, but dont let that fool you: his exams are insanely tough & highly detailed. Cumulative final. Labs are fun at least.

He's not understanding and all of his exams are way too in depth. I realize this is college, but some of the things he puts on exams are things he mentions one time, quietly in class. And if for any reason you can't make it to class, his outlines have blanks you MUST be in class to fill in and his Tegrity courses are audio only, no slide reference.

I really like the guy, and it's obvious that if you put in a fair amount of work and ask good questions, he will do his share for you.  But I can admit that he can be very boring and lose his train of thought.
He is rude to students and has not respect for undergrads.

I absolutely loved this class.  It has been my favorite biology class, possibly favorite class in general so far.  Dr. Kirk is a wonderful lecturer and the material learned is very interesting.  His tests are very fair (though they take a lot of studying), lab is easy, and he offers extra credit opportunities.  Great class overall.
No Comments

He made this class much harder than it should be. The lectures are pretty boring, and he blanks out half of the information from the slides so that you spend all of your time trying to fill in the blanks instead of listening to the lecture. If you like torturing animals, then you should like the lab

Dr. K is a nice man, but a little difficult to work with course-wise. His assignments have weird due dates (e.g. post in discussion board by Friday and reply ON Sunday) and is never hesitant to knock off points. I sent an email to him and the TA about it and he still tried justifying it, but ig it's his class. The TAs he picks are also quite sassy.
My fav professor ever was Dr. K! He was super caring and gave great lectures

Heavy workload, with quizzes, group projects, and essays due constantly. Cares less about the quality of the work, and more about the accuracy of APA formatting. Lecture heavy as well, resulting in the class average of his midterm exam being a 68%. Doesn't post lectures on Canvas, so whatever you're able to scribble down in person is all you have.

Took over the summer. Heavy work load. Quizzes every Sunday, two discussion boards, and two 1-2 page papers every week, plus the readings for everything. Most of the topics for the papers were interesting so it was bearable. Definitely do not recommend if you do not like writing papers. The topics that were covered really made up for the workload.

He has weird participation requirements and odd assignment schedules(at least in his online courses) for things like discussion boards. I've taken online courses for several semesters now and he does things pretty differently than most. Other than that the course load was fairly light and the information was interesting.

Took online during the summer. No online lectures. All reading. Book was very interesting to read, easy read too. Ten question quiz every Sunday. Two discussion questions each week. 1-2 page papers double spaced each week.  Easy grader. Put A LITTLE effort and you'll get a high A!!

Overall he's average. Had him for Psych 1000 & a few HP courses.  Barely read the book because he pretty much copies from the text. Attendance wasn't serious. Grades oddly because he picks out random things. If your assignment is worth 20pts you might get 17-19 normally. Doesn't really follow syllabus... peculiar guy. 2.5 out of 5 rating

This class is easy. His power points are directly from the book, and the exams are super easy if study the power points. He tests over the general info. He does use Clickers to take class attendance, but the questions are easy. He's a nice prof. that wants you to succeed and learn the material. I would study for about an hour the day of the exam.

Very passionate about cancer research, but definitely the type of professor who belongs in the lab rather than the classroom. Speaks really quietly, his slides aren't helpful, and relies on a humongous curve to give people the chance to even pass the class. Average on his exams are usually in the 40% range. Nice guy, but could be a better prof.

Dr. Hannink is one of those professors who is difficult, but that you respect for it. He cares about his students and wants everyone to do well; he welcomes questions and is available outside of class most times. As a senior/grad level course, grades are based on participation, tests, and quizzes. Homework is virtually non-existent (good and bad).
My favorite professor at the j-school - he's so so knowledgable about journalism, especially state government reporting if that's something you're interested in!!

Do not take this class if you aren't a Geography major. While Dr. Palmer is a very good guy who cares about what he is teaching, he is a horrible communicator outside of the classroom and he doesn't give clear direction on when assignments are due and how you are supposed to turn them in.

Professor Palmer is one of my favorite teachers. However, he has a strong tendency to ramble. He is very funny, and a lot of the class is devoted to working on the projects. The projects require very little outside of class. If you are not interested in learning GIS, I wouldn't advise taking this, or be prepared to struggle a bit.

Dr. Palmer was such a great teacher and everyone in the class really liked him. There wasn't a ton of assignments but we did use GIS mapping systems a lot. He is always willing to help and explain things to students when they don't understand. He also was fun to talk to and would repeatedly sit with my group and talk about random stuff. 10/10.

He's a great guy but his lectures are kind of unbearable at least for this class. Rambles the entire class time, gives no direction, super GIS heavy when this is NOT a GIS class, meaningless assignments, group projects are messy and no accountability, have to buy the book but we never read it, and the material we do learn is common knowledge

Did like 5 essays and some online discussion posts throughout the class. Recommend if you need to take writing intensive class.. professor is for sure an expert on the topic and he's an awesome guy all around. An easy grader on writing assignments

So nice. I took Native American Geography w him when I was a freshman bc I didn't know what the numbers mean and I was TOTALLY caught off guard with Palmer. The whole class was a study of the theory and value of "place" and he made it so interesting and thought-provoking. Stuff I never would've thought about otherwise. Super laid back, highly rec

Loved loved loved Professor Palmer! His unconventional way of teaching made lectures super interesting, thought provoking, and easy to pay attention to. I learned so much through this class that I know will stick with me for the rest of my life. He is easy going, laid back, and very open minded. Would recommend him 100%!!!

Professor Palmer is easily my favorite professor I've had at Mizzou. He is extremely nice, understanding, and he is not afraid to help in anyway he can. He is easy to talk to, has flexible hours, and will go far out of his way to answer questions that one may ask. I cannot recommend Professor Palmer enough. Great professor, even better person.

Mr. Bremer is one of the best teachers I have ever had in class. Even though this class is all-online, he makes a concerted effort to show up for his students. He is a great communicator, always honest and thorough in his feedback and genuinely cares about his students. I would recommend his class anyone, even those outside of health sciences!
Mark made it really easy to understand what was expected throughout the course and when deadlines were. If ever had a question or something, I would hear back within the same day.

Professor Bremer is AMAZING! He uses real world examples to supplement the lessons, and is always caring and compassionate about classwork. I wish he taught all of the core course work in Health Sciences.
Lectures are incredibly boring and have nothing to do with exam material, half of the time he just talks about his past career work. Didn't learn a thing but easy class with the lab adjunct.

I enjoyed his lectures and that he was an easy going guy. He can talk your ear off, but I can't say anything bad about the guy. He's open with talking about his life so it's nice to hear during his lectures. Class was sometimes a little dull, because the slides seems to be repeated.
Mark is an interesting guy. I enjoyed him all semester until the last few weeks where he made some uncomfortable/sexual jokes that weren't really necessary. Knows what he's talking about.
Mark is a funny dude. He gives lots of his field experience stories in lecture which helps supplement the material. Although lectures sometimes drag on, his lectures are interesting most of the time.

His lectures are interesting but long. Tests are half lecture, half test. He splits the lectures with Frank so it's an interesting class set up. Only two tests and they aren't even the majority of your grade- your lab is. Interesting class.

I never write reviews for teachers on here but I must say that Mark is probably the best teacher that I have had in the journalism school. So great.  He is laid back so you won't feel intimidated in lab because it is hard stuff but the goal is to just take your time and solve as much as you can.  he is very approachable and likes to come up to groups and explain things
Dr. Milanick is extremely knowledgable about physiology and frequently gives extra tid bits about the topic that extend beyond the course. Prepare for analogies
great professor, labs were super easy, explain things really well. loved going to lab.

Amazing professor in general. She is extremely student-centered and it really shows. The only class I have that I really look forward to. You are graded by three papers but she will meet with you and tell you exactly what you need to improve on. Great professor and great person!

Great professor with fun and engaging classes. Doesn't give busy work so it's a nice class to take the pressure off. Would 100% take again!

Talked about the same thing for 6 weeks repetitively. Extremely boring but the quizzes and tests and simple enough if you can actually pay attention.

Dr. Gowdy's lectures are super informative!  She can definitely be intimidating, but she genuinely cares about your success.  She notices when you are putting in effort and helps you best she can. Dr. Gowdy is a no-nonsense kind of teacher. If you put in the effort to learn the material, she will be happy to help. If you don't take it seriously, you're out of luck. There is a lot to learn in this class and the pace is fast, but Dr. Gowdy is a good teacher and will do her best to help you learn, so long as you show that you're trying

One of the rudest professors. This class was a waste of time, and you get absolutely nothing out of it. sometimes she's good and sometimes she's pretty rough

I'm gonna miss her. Thermo 1 was a pain but she made it manageable and I even found myself enjoying it in my bettter moments. I'm sure the new Thermo 1 prof is wonderful, though. Thank you for your work, Dr. Myers.

Dr. Myers was an AMAZING teacher! She is very interested in her students learning and will help them at a moments notice.

Professor Sveum is a great lecturer and goes strictly with the textbook. Go to class and take notes and you will be fine!
Very knowledgeable on topics such as ag. economics and sociology. His lectures are to the point and good to retain info.

Dr Griswold is one of the best professors at MU. Yes, the class is hard, but just study the workbook and review the problems and you will get a good grade.

Avoid Professor Melissa Grissald at all costs. She expects you to already know everything about finance and just reads homework answers without really going over them. Most knowledgeable professor I have ever had. It is clear that Professor Griswold's life experiences have led to her abundance of knowledge in Finance. I've taken two classes with Griswold now, and I don't think she deserves the hate she gets. I think that she is great. Just study the workbook, and you'll get good grades on the exams. She also often tells you what to expect on the exams. It's not hard if you put in a little work.

Dr. Colin's class is very basic and easy to get through. Class attendance is mandatory cause lecture is meant to expose the student to the differing fields of engineering and how they interact connect. pretty annoying prof but the class is easy

She makes every assignment due at 8pm. You are better off switching majors than taking a class with her as professor, unless you want to be told as a grown man you shouldn't be up past 8pm doing schoolwork.

Genuinely makes every assignment due at 8pm. Who does that? She had an assignment due four hours after class ended. Cant make it to an event? Bye bye points you need for this god forsaken class. The lectures are the most boring unproductive things ever made. How this teach hasn't been fired is beyond me.
i would rather take a dump in my own hands and then clap as opposed to having this prof again. Youre better off learning about engineering from a minecraft villager. Studied under Hitler.

Lab reports are very tedious. Have to make up 400+ words for individual and 1000+ words for group reports. All assignments are due at 8pm, even if it falls on a weekend. Class is mandatory to take as an engineer. Every lab report is insanly long for how little you actually do and lear. Multiple labs are purely just asking ai to do things for you. Lots of random assignments due on random days, all due at 8pm even on weekends and no grace period after.

She explains concepts clearly and is a great professor overall. Be sure to read the textbook because the exams are long and cover a lot of material.
