Dr. Herzog has been one of my favorite professors so far! She is very engaging and makes lectures interesting. The class is very well organized and expectations were clear. There were review sessions for the exams, and I did not find the exams to be very challenging. This class requires effort, but you will get a lot out of it!

She is very passionate about the topics, making lectures very engaging. TA's grade assignments so feedback quality varies but Dr H is pretty available to provide extra feedback if needed. There is a "course housekeeping forum" in canvas that Dr H and the TA's use to respond to any general questions about assignments or exams which is very helpful.

Very kind woman who is super passionate about her field. Her class is super organized and she is very clear with her expectations. Attendance is mandatory and your grade will suffer if you miss class. There is a textbook, but you will seldom use it. She says you need to read it, but you will do just fine if you only attend lecture.

Dr. Herzog is passionate and well organized, but a tough grader. Tests and assignments weren't that hard for me (and I barely used the textbook), but others aren't wrong to say they're difficult for a 1000 class. Also, she only provides the recorded lecture for one given absence, even if you have valid reasons for not being present more than once.
Extremely aggressive grader. Never provides feedback. Every single test average is a 76.4%… never gives you the test back. The tests are extremely hard for a class about relationships.

This class caused me so much stress. The instructor grades extremely harshly, and the tests are complicated to the point where it's hard to feel confident about anything. I wouldn't recommend it to any other girls looking for a manageable, low-stress course.

This class is honestly terrible. The instructor grades extremely hard, and the tests are overly complicated for no reason. Scoring well feels almost impossible, and the short workload doesn't match what's supposed to be an “easy” class. Overall, I wouldn't recommend it to anyone, especially freshmen.

Incredible professor and class. If you show up ready to think then you will get an easy A and have your mind expanded. She is very accommodating and knowledgeable. This class is probably the only discussion based lecture that has really worked in my experience.

Melissa Horner is easily the best teacher I've ever had. I have learned SO much in her class, specifically about topics rarely taught about in school. She is so knowledgeable & passionate about settler colonialism. She's a great lecturer, encourages student engagement, and readings are interesting. Take a class with Melissa, you will not regret it!

Melissa's lectures were informative but very lengthy. A lot of the time she would spend class giving a tutorial on how to use Adobe Premier but would get upset when we followed along on our computers because we weren't "paying attention." I feel like her class was better pre-covid. Overall she was just alright, do the work and you'll pass.

Melissa's the absolute best. I was in her first class at Mizzou, I took her 2880 class too, and I'd have taken her 4880 if it was offered at the time. She's so kind and chill and clear and she's not a hard grader. Her class is 2 1/2 hours and it's a joy. Also yeah, you'll totally fall in love with her.

Melissa's such a good professor. She has a lot of passion for the subject, she gives you a lot of time for projects because she knows how busy students can be, and she's so genuinely chill. Highly recommend her and there's an 80% chance you'll develop a crush on her if you take her class.
Melissa is round about amazing. She understand us students got stuff to do outside of class and gives us time to do projects. Sold 10/10.
Had her for Intro to Digital Storytelling. She is super helpful, caring about what she does and students work, and super helpful. Also she's just really funny and an overall cool professor.

The class is somewhat easy, but extremely frustrating. For undergrads the class consists of a semester long group project and midterm (individual project for grad students). Assignment expectations/rubrics/feedback are nonexistent. Good luck understanding him and what he wants from your work!

Mert is the absolute best! Highly recommend his class for circuits 1. He's easy to reach outside of class and genuinely cares about his students. Do the HW, quizzes, and labs. Go to class, pay attention, and you will do great on the exams. The practice exams are very similar. Enjoy!

Dr. Korkali is a chiller. Biweekly open note quizzes and homeworks. TAs that ran the labs were knowledgeable and let you leave early, not a single lab ran the full 2 hours. Exams are a carbon copy of the pratice exams, with questions coming from the textbook. Do HW and textbook problems and you're chilling. Drops lowest of 3 exams.

Had his class after another professor got fired, and he picked up right where we left off. Very nice and willing to help you out, make sure to ask him if you have any questions about the course material!
do homework, do practice exams, do labs, and you will get an A. He is very nice and explains things well.

Professor Fejzula is both caring and well-versed in her subjects. However, her teaching tends to bounce around in place and time, leading to a sort of confused and unrelated week-to-week. Dr. Fejzula is clearly knowledgeable and passionate in her field, and genuinely cares about her students. However, she seems to overemphasize self-care exercises rather than course content, which I found a bit frustrating as I was interested in the course's subject matter. Overall, her class was consistent and easy, but not especially fulfilling.

Professor Fejzula is an incredibly well spoken, knowledgeable, and compassionate professor. She has strict requirements for participation in the course, but is incredibly easy to communicate with and, so long as you keep up with out of class readings and activities, you'll retain most, if not all, of the information and perform well on quizzes.

I'm just not a fan of the class structure. I took this class because I don't know that much about the history of Africa, and I feel as though I have not learned very much. It's not a good representation of the true history of Africa because I feel it jumps around topics too much. She is very smart and kind and knowledgeable about the subject.
Not a fan.

Professor Fejzula is brilliant, that is not to be doubted. She also wants you to learn, as she should. I would not recommend this course. Every class was a dense lecture in which there were NO opportunities for participation. The only grade you get is on the final exam.

He is hands down the worst teacher I have ever had. 10/10 Would Recommend finding another class to take to fill your lab/science requirement. The labs are not too hard and are easy to do alright on. But the test are impossible even if you go to every class he make literally no sense. His tests are in no way similar to what you learn in class.

I showed up to every single lecture and even went into all of his office hours and still failed. The TA's were worthless and I'm ashamed they get paid to be there. Please for the sake of your grade do not ever take this class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. you cannot understand anything at all that he is saying. the only grade you get in this class is from the one final exam you take which is super difficult. he is one of the top worst professors i have had ever at mizzou maybe the worst.
I liked her class
Goat, one of the friendliest professors, never puts unnecessary expectations upon you

Professor Bombard was actually one of the sweetest professors I've had. She's very clear in her directions, and if you simply do her assignments and show up, you will get a good grade. She wants you to succeed and does her best to help you succeed.

Dr. Bombard was a very great person! Some of her assignment styles weren't my favorite, and for an English 1000 class you do need to attend. Dr. Bombard was an incredible creative writing professor. She treated everyone's work with the care it deserved and gave fantastic feedback, all while keeping a central goal of encouraging the artistic growth of each student. Her class was a delight!
super easy prof but sweet! if looking to better your poetry go to her!

I had her for English 1000 and she is the sweetest, as well as a great teacher and an all around kind human being. You can tell shes passionate about what she does, is super helpful, and a pretty easy grader. She does her best to make a fairly dull gen ed class as painless and stress-free as possible. I really enjoyed English with her!

There are a lot of bad reviews about Dr. Urban however he is my favorite professor that I have ever had in my academic career. Super smart and passionate about the material. If you pay attention, take notes, and ask questions you will be fine in this class. He is respectful to his students and very helpful when a lot of professors aren't. 100/10

Professor Urban NEVER graded my work up until the end of the semester, so I had absolutely ZERO idea as to how I was doing in the class. When confronted, he made excuses. So it is the day before grading period is over and over half of our assignments have not been graded. We turned in 5 papers over the semester and only one of them is graded as of now. The final was also unreasonably time consuming. Don't take this if you don't have to.

I did not know my grade in this class until the final day. He assigned lots of essays but never graded them until 4/5 of them were turned in. These were assigned over about a 3 month period. Stay away from this class if you can, it is miserable. nothing gets graded until the last couple days of the semester so you never know what your actual grade is. The exams are unnecessarily difficult and he straight up tells you he doesnt care about your GPA

I had the most intriguing  learning experience from Dr. Palmer. What a guy. He genuinely cares about what he is teaching. He is a working filmmaker, which is cool to witness in real time. Seriously the best professor I've ever had. I've never met a man so passionate about his craft and so understanding towards others. He'll occasionally even bend the rules of his own assignments if what you make was made with heart. He is a model professor and my only regret was not writing this review sooner.
Mike is so chill. He is very understanding and listens to his students. His classes are also very interactive and entertaining.

He is AWESOME! Super laid back and completely wants his students to have as much creative freedom as possible. But other than that I would 100% recommend

Mike is super chill. I legit knew nothing about film/video and it didn't matter as long as I submitted a video that I clearly put effort into. I would recommend him to anyone even if it's not their major.

I LOVED DST1880 w/ Mike. His lectures are funny, as is he. I enjoyed viewing his work for inspiration in class. Fun guy to talk film/TV with too. Love Mike!

I recommend taking someone else if you're new to film production. There isn't very much guidance or input from the teacher. The 1st project has been turned in for nearly 2 months and it still hasn't been graded, making retakes impossible. Because of the amount of classes cancelled the final project has to be done over Thanksgiving break.

He's an amazing professor. His class is very organized and he explains assignments very clearly. He cares about students progress and gives some extra credit. Really cares about his students and their progress. Very responsive to emails and office hours. Would take his course again.
Monson tends to make everything ore complicated than it really is.
this guy is horrible, would advise not taking his classes, biggest jerk in the world
Funny dry since of humor.

Stambaugh is a great professor. Exams were a little unclear, but fairly easy with minimal studying. Hard to get a bad grade. Very clear on expectations for all homework assignments, and provides a lot of review for exams.

Dr. Stambaugh is a great professor who is very considerate and wants students to succeed. I actually learned a lot from this class and actively participated because he made lectures and assignments interesting. You need to study for the exams, as some questions are super specific, but overall a great course. Not a lot of homework.

No lectures, just reading from the textbook followed by reading online commentary. Feedback consisted of what you got wrong with a note to reread the commentary.  That's it. Doesnt answer any of your questions, expects someone else to do all of his work. Assignments are outdated, the whole course actually is outdated. Couldn't even find the right textbook edition and was accused of cheating

For an intro class, I thought this was tough. I'm an A student. I bombed the midterm (D-!) because the questions are super tricky and hard. He did curve my B- to B.

I took this course as an independent study course and it was very interesting. I enjoyed the content and the class overall as it was very independent. I never actually met the professor but he graded fair and created a great course.

First of all, I'm an A student. The fact that I got a C+ in this class makes me furious. The tests are IMPOSSIBLE! I studied for a week for the final and still didn't pass it. Horrible Teacher, doesnt know what he is talking about. Thought I was going to fail until the curve saved me.  His tests are impossible and he isn't fair.  Avoid him at all costs

Mr. Olson was the awesome, not only did he show his determination to the field of History. mr. olson is a freaking legend! he's passionate about the subject of history and makes it real interesting and fun. he's always going out of his way to make himself available outside of class and he really tries to help you understand the material. mr. olson makes history feel like a story instead of just dry facts. i would take any class with him

Prof Sunde's priority is clearly research or something else- teaching gets little attention. 100% of course material is from the textbook or research articles. Professor Wales is emblematic of a greater issue I see with every government teacher I've ever interacted with. They study bureaucracy but are in no ways a part of it so they set up imaginary gears to crush you. If you take his class be prepared to be given an F on a nonsense fluffy assignment with no explanation. Great class if you hate yourself.

Mr. Wales is now at Clemson and I took one of his first courses here. He likes to read directly off the slides and connects them to real-world issues but his teaching style is not great. There's not much work in the class and the exams are 20% apiece.

Wales is a decent lecturer, kind of monotonous, but the biggest problem I have with him is a lack of flexibility. Don't expect him to give flexibility with due dates for personal emergencies since he "already has a late policy" (10% off per day). Also doesn't always post lectures on time. Easy class but not my favorite instructor.

Professor Wales is a good professor. You can tell that he genuinely is interested in international relations, and that he enjoys teaching and talking about it. He can be a bit unenthusiastic at times, but nothing major. Overall, I enjoyed the class and felt like I learned a lot.

Incredibly passionate and deeply knowledgeable about the subject, bringing enthusiasm to every lesson. Their energy and dedication make the learning experience engaging and enjoyable—I wholeheartedly recommend them!

Dr. Byrne is amazing professor! He lectures for every minute he has during class periods but every detail is useful. The class is structured very well with labs following the lectures very well. Throughout lecture he will tell you everything that is going to be on exams. GO TO CLASS AND YOU WILL PASS THIS CLASS EASILY WHILE ENJOYING IT!!

For a writing intensive class, I did not find J1300W too stressful. He is decently fast when it comes to grading and gives helpful feedback. There were several times when he regraded assignments to be a completion grade because we had not received feedback for that type of assignment yet. Would pick him as my prof again! He is very chill.
Throughly enjoyed his class, made it very engaging and was one of my favorite classes this semester. He was very chill and laid back...very easy grader.
Great class. You do a lot of your writing outside of class so there is homework, but he typically gives you in class time. He is a great professor and will help you if you need it, just ask.
Great professor especially if your new to Mizzou and the J-School. Class was chill as long as you do your work.

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! I am not an art history major (I am an entomology student) but took this class out of necessity for credits. Absolutely amazing lectures - every class is like a Ted Talk. Michael Yonan is an incredible professor. His lectures are so interesting. Take good notes, study for tests, and go to his office hours and get to know him. If you go ask him for feedback on your papers, he will take the time and thoroughly go over what you did wrong, what you should emphasize, etc. He is awesome!!

I really enjoyed Dr. Yonan's class! I'm not an art history major/minor so I had some catching up to do but the class itself was enjoyable. It is writing intensive but as long as you follow the rubric and hit up the writing center you should definitely pass. No tests, just two papers and two in-class writing assignments.

Definitely plays favorites for art history students, and while participation in discussion is part of your grade he typically only calls on art history majors. If you're a fine arts major or art education major, don't take his class.

Don't be fooled by his syllabus. He only states attendance yet at the end of the year he knocked down my grade for not talking in class (in a 50+ person lecture!) He is a really great teacher.  He is always helpful and really presents a new way to study art history.  His classes aren't about memorization, like most art history courses, but rather about discussion.  This has been the first and only class I've ever had where discussion has actually helped me learn.
Loved This Class. Super Informative And Super Interesting. Dr. Yonan Has Well Organized Lectures And Maintains Interest In Class.

just started teached here from slu - really good teacher. simple class assignments, tests are exactly what he says they will be. very open to you coming by his office-- make an appointment first though!!

Love Goldie with everything in me. He is a great guy and an even better professor. Sure, his lectures aren't the most entertaining thing, but studying concrete is not the most exciting.

Made drafting very enjoyable, great teacher

Save your mental health and GPA and take Orgo 1 with a different professor during the summer. Dr. Harmata seems like an interesting guy, but god, his teaching style is awful. I dropped the course a month in (and I am generally studious) because I could not understand anything he taught. Chief Budds LIVES for his students and for their education. Get on his level and you will be transformed into a beautiful academic butterfly. Dr. Budds is a very interesting man. He has good jokes and is very knowledgeable. Lectures are long but interesting and tests are pretty easy as long as you STUDY THE MUSIC.

He made class so interesting. He's so funnny! The music we studied was so cool. I loved this class! When I hear the freshmen talking and playing music for this class, it makes me miss this class so much!
So frustrated during this whole class. His tests either made or broke you. There is basically no recovering if you get a bad grade on one test.

I took her Jane Austen class and loved it! She is now one of my favorite professors, and has me, a non-English major, searching for classes she teaches to take. A lot of reading but that was expected. Weekly writing quizzes where you write about a topic previously given to you. Allows edited versions of papers to be turned in for a higher grade.

She is so caring and genuinely wants to connect with every single one of her students. I was looking for an easy honors class and while attending class is mandatory and there is quite a lot of reading I recommend. Very good lecturer with a lot of passion and experience. A little old school but always rewarded real interest and effort! I had a lot of fun, really enjoyable class.
Fantastic lecturer and very personable. There is a LOT of reading but that's to be expected with a course titled "Reading Literature" lol.

Very easy to pass if you could finish readings and simply pay attention but lectures were often filled with unnecessary political bias which also hindered the selected readings of the course. Dr. West was super fun. As a non-english major I was just looking for a relaxing class and I picked this one because I liked to read. I learned a lot and enjoyed most of the stories she has us read. We also had the opportunity to watch movies for some writing prompts, which was fun. Would take it again.

Was an okay class. if you really needed to, you could put assignments off until its due but definitely not advised. Does not communicate grading criteria well. Does not give any reasonable feedback before or after the assignment is submitted. Overall difficult to get along with. Student success is not a priority at all for this man.

Took his class online and it was super easy, maybe spent 1 hour a week on readings and taking the quiz. Only like 5 or 6 discussion boards all semester and don't have to read the book for quizzes bc its all on quizlet. Big part of your grade is a group project and my group had a ton of problems, and he was really understanding.

He was very bad at communicating due dates and expected criteria. Your main grades are group projects throughout the semester. When I reached out for help, he did not give me any helpful feedback and I was quite disappointed.

Attendance is not mandatory but lectures can be intricate so it's still advisable to attend. She publishes all materials on Canvas so everything is accessible and organized. A lot of reminders about assignments are given in class so not attending could mean missing an assignment unless you check Pearson frequently.

Dr. Downer is one of those people that really REALLY wants everyone to succeed and wants everyone to have the same passion about science that she does. That makes the disorganization and 30 minute off topic rants easier to take. The textbook isn't necessary but definitely attend class, she will give the peeps in class a leg up on tests and quizzes.

As long as you participate in class, schedule office hours (keep trying to email even if she doesn't respond), do the homework, and study for the tests you will be fine! She can be disorganized at times but she also cares very much about biology and students success.

If you want a professor who won't even follow their own syllabus, this is perfect for you. It is also great when she makes a big deal about cheating and punishes everyone and says no one gets a curve, but then admits on the last lecture that it was only a handful of students involved but yet we all got disciplined. She is just all over the place.

So unorganized and forgets to tell you about assignments she posted. Tests are fairly easy if you actually study, but she formats some of the tests terribly. She attempted to punish the class for a few individuals cheating and then came up with the worst possible solution for future tests. Finally, she will not respond to your emails. ever.

Dr Downer's organization of the class is not perfect BUT CLEAR.  I guess you cant please everyone. She cares about student sucess and takes cheating seriously. There were some bad actors in this class and yes there were consequences to prevent a repeat. But security measures though a PAIN were never harmful. I would HIGLY recommend.

Professor Dwoner is very unorganized, even for a general biology class for non-majors. She really does whatever she wants. She changed the exam format the day of the exam and was upset we didn't finish after she took up thirty minutes of class to talk about how the final would be "the hardest she has ever made for students."  Avoid this class!!!!!
Great class. Loved the topics. Lectures are a bit long but just go to class and be engaged. Ask questions and take good notes. You will be FINE.

Extremely knowledgeable professor who is very polite. She will literally spend time with students outside of class, and kindly imparts knowledge. Clearly loves what she does and is passionate. Take her.

As long as you watch the lectures, the tests are a piece of cake. There's daily reading, but I didn't personally find it necessary. There are weekly quizzes but they aren't too bad either. Teacher is very sweet and even sent out emails to let you know you're doing a good job.

Being a big fan of mythology and the ancient world to begin with, this class was really enjoyable and Professor Binek's lectures were fun and easy to follow. If you attend lecture, take notes, and do the assigned readings you will succeed in this class and have fun while doing so.

I never read but I went to every single class. She is very passionate but quick to talk so you have to be fully focused or might as well not even go to class. Getting an A is very possible but get ready to work and study. I thought it was gonna be a blowoff and its not . Weekly quizzes based off readings :/ tests are so hard if you're not prepared.
Binek was great! I loved learning about the content and stories, and she did a great job explaining the stories. She was positive and upbeat. The way she taught made me want to come to class.
very knowledge; kind and always willing to help or discuss; great use of TAs; lectures were well structured and highly effective; course work wasn't boring; her slides were phenomenal

Prof. Binek presented everything extremely clearly, showed what was important & her lectures were entertaining with plenty of images & bit of humor. There is quite a bit of homework, and the tests can be difficult. Would recommend studying a lot. Bushman is helpful at answering questions.

Lectures aren't posted online and there are quizzes in class, so attendance is basically mandatory, but it doesn't hurt your grade. The only thing is he goes over things relatively quick, and it can get confusing. There is weekly homework and as long as you keep up with it, it's an easy B

This review is for Math 1160 Precalculus. Mr. Bushman is great. His lectures were always detailed and would answer any question. He never assigned homework over the weekends and breaks. This is for Precalculus class. Bushman is a tough grader on exams. Attendance is not necessary mandatory as he does not do Iclickers. He does encourage people to go to his office hours which do help for this class. Hw is not hard and you get a week to do it.
Super nice guy with great math lectures. This is a review for a PreCalc Class, it is not available on rate my professor.

He was very difficult to work with! His emails were kinda rude. Doesnt care about your situation if you miss and assignment or something its on you and dont ask him for leeway because theres no such thing in his books!

This was maybe the worst class I've ever taken at Mizzou. I spent more time reading for this class and I did on my Calculus and Stats classes combined. Hofer is an interesting guy, I took this class online and the entire semester he only posted one actual lecture. The rest was just reading (LOTS) and quizes every week. Late pushing out the required work for the week multiple times including the week directly prior to finals. Awful class and awful experience. He assigns a ton of reading. Literally I am spending more time on this class than I am on anatomy or calculus. Dr. Hofer is easily one of my favorite professors. He's witty, engaging, and fosters non-contrived discussion of and interest in the topic material. If you like the old-school professor vibe, he's got both the tweed jacket and controversial, but well-argued, viewpoints. Also the readings and essays for his classes are actually interesting!
Love him! Super candid, but if you put in the work you will learn a lot.

Dr. Hofer is super fun to take, if you're ready for his no-holds-barred communication style. He tells you what he thinks regardless of how you feel about it, but is always willing to listen to you disagree with him if you can make a good argument. Works to be fair in his grading, but grades on only 2 tests with extra credit opportunities. Fave. :-)
Really chill and most classes get out 20-30 minutes early for J1300, at least for my class. Really nice and gives super good feedback, grading kinda harsh and to the point he doesn't mess around

Engaging lecturer & generally pleasant. I am definitely a better writer now than I was before I took his class. He is happy to review your work before you submit it, and he gives great pointers. If you ask for help, your grade will improve.
It's easy to get a good grade just by going to class and turning in the assignments. You have to be on top of the projects though, he won't give you a million reminders.
Boring lectures and unclear assignments at points.

Very pump emo guy which is fine but I had no clue. He's cool but scary. He is hard to talk to and the material is hard for some to understand so it's hard to get a good grade in these conditions. The material was more like philosophy to me and was very anime and heavy metal, so if you like that, you'll love this class, just not for everyone.

I took this online course Summer 2022. There are only a handful of Canvas quizzes at the end of each week that you need to read the material. He is intelligent and knows what he is talking about but is extremely unprofessional and treats his students like trash. If there is one class I recommend you NOT to take it is this one or any one he teaches. You will regret it, I promise.
I love Professor Katz and wish I could take more classes before I graduate. I really enjoyed the class content.

Mr. Katz was hard to follow, and it was difficult to see the greater significance of the work we did, both in and out of class. The material was always explicit and often bordered on offensive. I did not realize that much of the material would make me feel uncomfortable. There were rarely trigger warnings for lectures, readings, or videos.

I found the course content to be all over the place, and Prof. Katz was sort of all over the place too. He gave pretty good lectures, but would often go off on side tangents or show examples that seemed to be included more for shock value than for educational purposes. The quizzes were multiple choice so that was nice, but they were still hard.

cool guy. has a talent for diluting the content of the book into easily digestible lectures with lots of interesting video examples. wish I had taken lecture notes because despite reading the textbook cover to cover I still barely scraped a B. that's on me, this class was pretty easy. only complaint is that he's a little hard to talk to at times.

He gives you a week after returning painting assignments to make adjustments based on his feedback for a 2nd try at a better grade. Genuinely wants to see progress. The last 3 assignments we got to decide what to paint as a class. He drops letter grades after 3 absences. He grades easy ("meeting basic criteria" and looking like you tried gets a B)

Nathan is one of the best fine arts professors I've ever had. He is extremely artsy, but he can put a lot of weird, artsy things into layman's terms. He seems to focus on conceptualitythemes in fine arts. I wouldn't take his classes if you aren't really into that kind of thing, but if you are, he is definitely the best choice.

Nathan is a seriously awesome professor, he is super nice and helpful. He doesn't like when people skip class or lectures, but I don't understand why anyone would want to skip his classes; so cool.

Nate is a great drawing professor! He's very nice and helpful. He encourages class discussion, and speaks philosophically; but because of that, he can be unclear; he's vague and ambiguous. Nate is a great professor, and for an intro course, he does a great job of making geology interesting for everyone, even if they had no prior interest in the subject. You really don't need to worry much about your grades, as long as you try your hardest in the labs.

Very average class. Lab section can be difficult/tedious, but exams are online so you can definitely pass if you need a science credit

Actual lecture was really good and this guy tried to keep lecture fun and engaging, very funny. Lab was graded very tough by the TA and felt super long. iclicker attendance mandatory. All quizzes and exams are online which is nice.

He has great lectures and very nice. However, quizzes/tests are waaay harder than lecture material. I truly loved Dr. Hopkins. He's very engaging in his lectures and makes lots of jokes. He really cares about students if they put any effort into the class. This dude is pretty intersesting, and getting into the class I didn't know what to expect. But if you enjoy the course material he is very infromative and for sure knows what he is talking about. Good Guy, Good Class, Intersting Topics.

This professor will help you succeed in Calculus 1 and 2 extremely well. I had him for both 1225 and 1226 freshman year and he really helped me understand the material well. Consider yourself lucky if you have Dr. Nav as your calc II professor. He is very kind and puts in a ton of work to make sure you understand the material. I had Dr. Nav for Calculus II. He is by far the best professor I have had at Virginia Tech. He makes Calc II far more manageable and you can tell how much he cares about his students. If you got Dr Nav you're actually blessed. Best professor I've had in college. Does everything in his power for you to succeed in the class. Really good professor, made the content of 1226 understandable even though I ended up missing a lot of the lectures towards the end. Provided tons of helpful resources for exams and gave a decent amount of extra credit. Also incredibly helpful in office hours.

BY FAR THE BEST MATH PROFESOR IVE EVER HAD.
If you are planning on taking Calc 2/MTH1226 at VT, this is who you want. Lectures are useful but not required, they are repetitive and you can just read them online. If you want a passing grade, deadass just go his office hours, its extremely important you do. He WILL GO THROUGH EVERYTHING WITH YOU!

Amazing teacher, took his 1226 class at Virginia Tech and he was extremely helpful and respectful. Always available during office hours and there is extra credit every week. The math department at vt is usually miserable, but his teaching was great.

I loved Professor Rahman- the topics and discussions in bioethics were super interesting.

Great professor!! Made philosophy interesting- I had no interest in it before, and now considering minoring in it. As long as you do the readings and attend classes you should get an A. He is very understanding- lots of extra credit and other points toward the end of the course.

It's just that he is foreign so it is hard to understand what he is saying. Don't take the class because you have to speak out in class every week for participation points. good guy

Mr. Benner is extremely kind, helpful, and supportive to all of his students. Even though students need to learn how to use different kinds of software alone, he is very flexible to work with; if you need extensions or help with projects, Mr. Benner is always there, and he tries his best not to make students feel bad for being behind or messing up.

Professor Benner is a genuinely good teacher and an understanding + kind person. Lets you turn in projects a little late if an interview fell through. Lots of group work + interviewing required (it's journalism.). Let us out of class early often. Lectures might be a little boring, but just do whatever and then answer when he asks questions.

My only genuine complaint is how often I walked all the way to class, for it to end 10 minutes later, classes could have been an email. You will have a new project every week, but Nic was amazing, and if he weren't my professor, I would not show up to this class, but I did every week. He's very understanding of late work and was an easy grader.
Great professor. If you are interested in film or photography, specifically, he would be a very good person to know. Thoroughly enjoyed the class and learned a lot!
Nick was a nice teacher. He was always available if you needed help. He grades fairly and gave good feedback.

Just had Nic this semester for J1200. He's talented & a great explainer. Went into the class with 0 knowledge about any of the software, but he helped all of us. He made the class fun and interesting, and he's overall just a really nice guy. Once freaked out because I turned in an assignment 5 minutes late- emailed him and got full credit.

The exams were a little difficult, but there were plenty of extra credit opportunities on exams and projects. The semester project also seems intimidating, but was super easy and not very time consuming. BEWARE of mandatory cumulative final exam

One of my favorite professors I had at Mizzou. Knows how to teach the material while being entertaining(a lot of professors can't do both at once). Taking notes and studying for exams is so easy the way he teaches! As a senior, this was just a fill in class but I wish I would have been able to enjoy Dr. Blay for more classes while I was at Mizzou!

Professor Blay is incredibly laid back in class and delivers really interesting lectures. His exams are hard but fair, and the assignments are long, but you have a while to complete them. His pop quizzes are easy if you pay attention, so try and do so! The semester project is fun and isn't too difficult! Also, super funny! BE RESPECTFUL!

Dr. Blay has been one of my favorite teachers so far at Mizzou. His lectures are interesting, and he grades fairly. You will need to go to class and study for tests, but if you put in the effort, you can definitely get a good grade. Would highly recommend for Vertebrate Biology!
Great professor, cares about students and always willing to help. Has pop quizzes in class to take attendance. Not a lot of homework but test are HARD.

Great professor who cares about his students. He wants us all to understand, which is why he gives pop quizzes (controversial but they are not hard if you pay attention). Tests come directly from slides. Accessible outside of class and hilarious. You have to go to class because he doesn't record his lectures and quizzes are at the beginning.

His lecture slides are the worst. They never line up with his outlines. I have never had a class with him where he actually teaches the things on his slides. Basically none of the content he teaches is relevant to his exams.

Great professor who pays attention to where students are at in order to best explain the material. Easy going and his lectures aren't boring. Multiple choice can be tricky, but he gives back points for questions that are frequently missed. Doesn't record lectures and has pop quizzes, but they are like 3 points, so missing 1 or 2 is not a big deal.

Professor Potter was easily the best professor I've had at Mizzou. I took his Comics and Cartooning, and despite being a journalism major, I had so much fun with this class. I received in-depth feedback that helped me refine my art. Potter is one of the most caring and intelligent professors at Mizzou and I highly recommend any one of his classes!
Excellent faculty member. Should be the go to for DST major students.

Probably the best professor I've had. Genuinely cares about his students, and was VERY understanding if you had to miss a class for a good reason. Rather than tough grading and strict rubrics, he believes in giving students detailed feedback to encourage real learning and self-improvement. Fosters creativity, discussion, and understanding.

He is one of the only teachers I have had that I believe truly cares about me and my learning. I never got below a 100% on an assignment in his class, he cares that you learn and actually try on assignments more than how well you match a rubric. He is an amazing professor and I would recommend this course to anyone I know.

Potter is energetic, motivated, and responsive. He genuinely is passionate about what he teaches and makes an effort to adapt the class to his students needs. This course might be difficult if you don't already have a basic understanding of digital programming and media editing. Homework is reading heavy in the beginning and shifts to media later.

Potter's the bomb. Take all of his classes. They're all so cool and you'll become a better writer. And a better artist! You gotta read, watch, and play a lot of digital content but it's all pretty compelling. He's god-tier in the DST department and he's hilarious. and super cute. and he really likes k-pop.

Nick is the best professor I have ever had. He's super down to earth and chill. He understands that life happens and school is sometimes second priority, while still holding people accountable. Not to mention, the "textbooks" we needed were video games. Easily my favorite class ever.

You're going to work for your grade in Dr. Potter's class, but you're also going to learn SO much. I took his course as a random elective because it sounded interesting. I didn't expect much. I came out of the class with more academic growth than I've experienced in any other course at Mizzou. He's a wonderful professor. Definitely take the class.
She rules. Shes young and fun. I took her for learning strategies this semester and the class helped out a lot and was interesting and fun!
Bartow is the best. She will teach you anything you want to learn and work with you until you know it. She puts a lot of time and effort into the class. If you are able to apply for UAP 100% do it.

Professor Bartow is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. She makes it very clear that she cares about her students well being and wants them to be successful in her class. She goes above and beyond.

Have you considered that you do not deserve a professor as good as Monnier? Have you considered that you, unworthy that you are, might combust in the presence of a Divine of the Humanities? Never criticize Monnier in my presence. She, along the rest of the Russian faculty, is the lone bright spot in the otherwise Stygian night of the humanities at Mizzou. Give her more money.

Tough grader. At the same time no clear grading criteria. Most of the time I didn't even understand why I received such a grade. A lot of materials to read and 0 explanation in class. High expectations and no help. Got C (average) for participation even though I talked in each class. Makes me wonder what others who never said a word got.

Dr. Monnier is awesome!! She really cares about her students. She's actually a Russian Prof so she just teaches this class on the side, but she's obviously really interested in the material. The class does require a lot of reading, but in general, I think she tries to make the books we read really accessible. Aweomse gal!!
Dr. M is amazing!

Dr. M is the best teacher to have when you want someone to nerd out with over the best works in literature, art, and music. She truly cares about her students and isn't afraid to tell you when you're obviously slacking in her class.   If you're lucky, you'll get to see her pug, Buddy!

Best teacher I've ever had, hands down, in high school or college. Give your best effort, and she will give it back and then some. Always willing to help, whether through email, office hours, or in class questions. Having Dr. Monnier as a professor is a privilege by seeing how much a professor can truly love their subject, as well as their students

worst class to sit through. not sure how she got so many reviews. lectures are awful and boring, great for catching up on work for other classes though. she makes you read like 20 pages then gives you a 5 question true/false quiz each week... why. doesn't keep grades up to date. we are 6 days away from my final and grades from january aren't in.

I took her writing intensive 3430 class my freshman year and got a rare A+. She's funny, friendly, and really knows her stuff. The WI class meant lots of papers and I was actually excited about them - we were given room to be creative and pursue our own interests. I learned a lot, as this class is very pertinent to my future career.
Visit her in office hours. Very informative and wants to help.

not too hard of a class but i found it impossible to get anything better than a B on her exams. she offers extra credit which is a plus and she tries to make lectures interesting so it's not terrible going to class

Dr. Campione Barr is an extremly nice woman! She is willing to help if you are willing to learn! Anytime I ever had a question she was quick to respond to me with detailed answers. The other two bitter students mustve recieved bad grades due to their lack of effort! She gives you extra credit - drops a test and two quizzes! LOVE HER!

I have no idea why the last 2 people would comment that.  Dr. Campione-Barr is one of my favorite professors.  She is always there if you need help, and extends her office hours around exams.  If you study the powerpoints and read the chapters.. you will do well on the exams. I highly recommend her for any psychology course!

Confusing test/quiz questions. When I emailed her asking for clarification on a quiz question, I got no response. Makes distracting grammatical errors on slides and reads straight from the slides. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. She is so confusing, I feel like she just yelled at the class. She goes super fast and reads straight off the slide, which are poorly written. Her tests are fairly easy and she does show interesting videos but she is confusing. THe class is boring

A pretty okay teacher. Mostly just reads from the notes, but tries to make it interesting. You can tell she cares about the subject. She is very willing to help if you go in after class or make an appointment!
She rules. Shes young and fun. I took her for learning strategies this semester and the class helped out a lot and was interesting and fun!
She rules. Shes young and fun. I took her for learning strategies this semester and the class helped out a lot and was interesting and fun!

This class is fun, and she brings in items from the MHCTC! No tests but there is a quiz per decade that you complete outside of class on paper, they're mostly easy. Lectures are entertaining and vibrant. she is so silly and passionate about the subject and you can tell she has fun sharing about it. Quizzes are so easy and you don't actually have to attend class to get the questions right, just be sure to put a lot of detail or you will get points off (this is bc the class is technically writing intensive).

Overall terrible professor. She was very unorganized and hard to work with. Her class was very lecture and quiz heavy. She seemed to be in lala land the entirety of the semester and failed to communicate with her students.
Lectures were good, quiz questions were sometimes a bit hard to understand. Good feedback on papers

Grading was pretty trash, no matter how hard you try her or her TA WILL take off points. Lectures were a snooze fest but you can skip through most of it to find what you you need. Not very hard and you get credit in multiple areas, but otherwise the class is pretty dog

She's pretty decent at what she does. It's not a difficult class in the first place, but if you look at the rubrics for the portfolios you turn in, you will be golden. Really easy A if you just put in the work.

She was a mess all semester. She was really nice, and the class in general wasn't that difficult. Only a few grades, two portfolios (one at midterm and one at end of semester), and a peer review for each of those portfolios. Overall, she's pretty good, and just do what you are supposed to, and you will walk out with an EASY A.

I really did not like her class. There were four papers, that actually took some time to write. she is the kindest and goofiest teachers I've ever had. I'm trying to take another english class she's teaching next semester just so I can have her again thats how cool she was. She understands that we are all busy and is super relaxed with due dates. If you show up everyday and do all the work you'll definitely get an A!! a true angel!!

This was one of the easiest English classes I have taken. Just go to class and you will be fine. I didnt feel like I learned a lot of new material, but mrs songstad helps you out with areas that you struggle with. I only wrote 2 papers in this class and they were easy.
First class i had at Mizzou and she did a great job at getting her students acclimated to the college class structure. Doesn't allow phone use.

Funniest professor I have had so far! Ms. Songstad made morning classes something to actually look forward to.  Very engaging when going over your work.  One of the few professors who cares how you are doing in and out of class.  Ms. S teaches in a way that you remember it even a semester later. 10/10... or maybe even 11/10
She is so easy to work with. She answers questions and emails quickly. Really make sure you are understanding what you are learning and makes the class interactive.

2120! I loved Nicolette; she is very kind and understanding. This class taught me a lot of things that were actually useful in life, and I got a lot out of it. It sucks that this class was so late in the day, and I did not go a lot of the time, but I still ended with a good grade.

Nicolette Leiby was my least favorite professor. Hands down the worst teacher I have ever had. If you have her class, drop it before its too late. This teacher openly told us at the beginning of the school year that she was unorganized and has lost papers before (she is). Nigelle is a very very very nice person, but is no where near a good teacher. she gives terrible feedback and doesn't communicate well with her students about when assignments are due. do not take this class. the worst.

Ms. Cochran is a sweetheart and is happy to help you when she can. However, she is a tough grader and isn't the best at explaining content. The teacher was never clearly explained assignments. Canvas was like a maze trying to figure out where to turn stuff in or where to find what was even suppose to be done. This teacher makes me dread going to class and will dock points for being absent.
I've always had amazing English teachers up until this point. This class has not taught me one thing so far.

Never take her class, she put in grades very late like not until march, and is extremely disorganized. I have a harder time in school but I still try my best and she has not been supportive what so ever. She mixed me up with other students that weren't attending class and gave me a bad grade because she didn't know who I was. Easy class made hard by professor. Was late on many assignments, but did extend the deadlines. ALOT of reading, most required to do well on quizzes. Exams - DO THE PRACTICE QUESTIONS - she grades tough but when class average was low, she gave opportunities to fix mistakes for more credit. Try to find different class, but if no choice it is passable

I have her online course and she is very sweet. However, her online lectures and readings that were due for the week would be posted late frequently, but did extend the due date sometime. NEVER take her class. She was disrespectful to feedback and questions, lacked communicated and was incredibly disorganized, and a very harsh grader. The course load was ridiculously difficult for a 2000s level course and she was not kind to questions about grading. Lectures are heavy, required and unorganized. Tanked my gpa

The worst ever. This professor constantly showed up late but expected perfect attendance whenever she was on time. Posted quizzes over the weekend and then made them due by 9am Monday morning. DO NOT TAKE

Whatever you do, avoid Syam's class. He is a nice guy, but he is a VERY difficult professor. He expects students to consistently score as high as the MBA level, and does not provide the adequate materials to succeed in his course. His test scores are Ds every time, but he will tell you otherwise.

Always say he is available for questions but is never available and has no set time for office hours. NEVER ANSWERS EMAILS. Class average on exams is around a D. Doesn't accept doctors notes or try to go over missed materials even when I tried to reach out. 
Assigns case studies and doesn't give us clear instructions or cares if we get it right.

Syam is not a good professor. He is unclear on instructions and when he says he will be available for questions he is not. If you have another option, DO NOT take Marketing 4000 with him. His class averages for exams are terrible.

I really enjoyed Professor Syam, he always encouraged us to come to office hours for help and he checked in with groups every week to make sure we were understanding of the material. Always caring as well. There is a grade section for attendance, and he will take it randomly so try and make it to class if you can.

Harsh grader, gives Harvard case studies and expects us to know how to do them. Doesn't care if the whole class does poorly on case studies, not willing to make changes. Says that attendance isn't required for the class but then says it is. You work on case studies with a group and my group didn't know what was going on and finished with a C.

not sure why there's no entry for prof Syam on this website, because he is an amazing professor. if you strayed away from marketing because Joel Poor was so garbage, Syam will bring you right back. not an intensive class and genuinely fun to attend.

She is the sweetest professor! She gives great feedback on the semester essay! Fairly easy class, post and reply to a discussion board prompt 1x/week and there is 1 essay that you write throughout the semester. Super interesting class that REALLY expanded my views.

Dr. Sanchez is so sweet and is very interested in learning about her students! I really loved taking her social work 2000 class. Course work was not difficult at all; maybe a bit of reading, but not terrible. Would definitely take again if I could!

By far one of the best professors I've had here. If you follow the outlines for writing essays, you'll do fine. He even goes over your essay with you before it's due. Attendance is mandatory but it's not the end of the world if you miss a class or two. Very chill and funny guy I definitely recommend choosing him to be your english professor.

this dude's an absolute legend. super casual and open with his students, made the classroom way less intimidating. also offered great feedback on papers and was very lenient with grading. all in all, really solid introductory english course that also introduces you to MU resources for writing future papers. 10/10 would take again

Professor Siela is my favorite professor Ive have had in college so far. The class was pretty easy and was essay based. He wants everyone to get an A and he will help you get it. He gave great feedback on how to improve your paper before you would turn it in. He is halarious and empathizes with his students and is just all around a great person.

Professor Siela has an easy class, for sure. I did not get much out of it, though. He was nice, he likes to tell stories, and he does not grade terribly hard. Have something decent to turn in, and you will get a good grade. This class did not challenge me, but it did not hurt my GPA either.

I think we wrote 4 papers the entire semester and the entire class was out of 100 points. Prof Siela is literally so cool and I couldnt have asked for a better professor. He is such an interesting guy and is so laid back! Has conference weeks and tells you what you need to do to get an A on the paper. Take his class

I was nervous going into this class because I am not the best at writing. Professor Siela has helped me so much to improve on my writing and english based skills. He is so fun and is super understanding and really just wants for us to succeed. Some readings, a few essays that he gives tons of help and feedback on, and about 15 in class assignments.
Professor Siela is super layed back.

Prof Siela was easily the best professor I had my freshman year. He was super accessible outside of class and was sure to answer any questions I had and would be understanding for any problems I had. He is caring for students and wants to make sure you have all you need to put forward your best work. He's also just hilarious.

He doesn't use Canvas. You don't have a clear idea of what your grade is until the end of the semester. This course was a requirement for me but I wish I did not have to take it. It is completely online and the set up of the class seems disorganized. There are many readings and the tests are not easy- make sure you remember every little thing you read. Pretty heavy grader too so make sure what you do is perfect.

If one is a full time student and works 40 hrs, his class is near hard to participate in. It is a fully online class, and the set up is frustrating, as is the process for turning in materials. Syllabus is on Canvas, bigger papers are published in assignments not modules, all work turned in via email, except for discussion posts. So much reading.

I had Noah for my capstone class and he was one of the nicest and most approachable professors I've had at Mizzou. He's knowledgable about the subject matter, and if you do the readings and come to class you'll be fine.

This class was very challenging; lots and LOTS of reading and papers, but it was a writing intensive course. He's kind of intimidating, which makes participation hard. Professor Heringman assigns an intense amount of work. He could probably tone it down. However, he's is passionate about his subject and really wants his students to succeed. He fully expects participation in class and will embarrass you if he knows you haven't read. The works he assigns are interesting and relevant. An intelligent, kind professor.

Assigned 200+ pages of reading almost every day.  He wasn't clear and mumbled.  His syllabus was confusing.   His grading was all over the place and his comments weren't helpful.  He wouldn't even really teach class and had other students lecture instead.  I won't be taking another class with him again.

Very knowledgeable and personable professor. Very challenging, but enjoyable if you can just press on and work your butt off.  Read every word of his syllabus!

Myers was very unwilling to work with my accommodations through the university because he felt it would get in the way of my participation. The grading is very strict and attendance is mandatory. Would not take again.

Noah is a Pompas Jack. Does not take feedback well and talks down to you. The class started with 21 there was only 8 of us at the end. All making C at the end of the class. Noah is very kind, but for such a young professor I wish he would be chiller. Sometimes he acts like an uptight strict old man and does not give much slack. But he teaches very well. He is very funny and teaches his class all in Spanish but makes you understand what he means with movements and he is hard but if you want a challenge he is great.

Hes a nice guy, but it feels like he should be teaching an upper level course by how harshly he grades. If youve never taken spanish before, do not take this course. Professor Myers will really challenge you with this class. Study well in advance, don't do your essays last minute, and you will do great. Go to class everyday and participate!

Really considerate grader. I could have gotten a lot worse scores than I did on essays and exams but instead he just made comments on my mistakes and didnt take off all the points. He cares about the students.

Class is intimidating at first but it gets more comfortable. He is very friendly and accessible for help. He opens every class with Spanish music videos and learning about the different countries is cool. Group conversations every day in 2160.

He showed up late everyday, gave us a surprise exam with zero warning, introduced a 300 point project (worth 40% of our grade) on the second to last class of the semester, and didn't grade anything. The worst, most unreliable professor I've ever had. There were so many things that went wrong throughout the semester, but I can't fit it all into this review. Don't take this class if it's not required. She grades harshly good luck!

Don't even bother study for the tests! They have nothing to do with the lecture or the study guide she gives out. Professor is also just rude. Also be prepared to never have a class cancelled/ attendance points with zero exceptions

Nora gives a rubric for writing assignments then takes off points just because she feels like it.

Oksana is a great professor! She is so real! Her class feels like I'm actually learning. It can get difficutl at times, but she gives you everything you need to be successful. Do not believe the negative reviews (they are just sour students that got caught for using chatgpt on their exams)

As an online student, I wasn't aware of who was in the class or what outside materials others were using. I would recommend choosing a different course or professor unless you're prepared to defend every step of your work... word for word.

Bring your tin foil hats to class! She has no concept of real world economic/finance problems and it makes sense why she is stuck in academia. Very funny and personable! A study group makes this class very doable.
Bad person!!!!
She treats grad students like 5th grader. No respect or trust whatsoever. Tries to ruin students' lives.

Run away!

Professor Ola was a nice and understanding teacher. It takes a bit of work and proper understanding of the content, however as long as you show up and make an effort you will have the ability to do well. just make sure to do the readings and participate.

Professor Osman has such incredible, in-depth knowledge of black studies. She also brings in gender perspectives on peace which really opened my mind. Prof. Osman was fantastic! She was so caring and helped me learn how to think more critically. She gives solid feedback. Be prepared to work hard and think critically during her class. I would recommend her course. Also her marking is very fair.

Lectures the entire class and goes through slides really quickly. Don't bother trying to take notes because you won't keep up and everything is posted online after class. Pam is AWESOME!!!!!!!!  That is all.
The best teacher I have ever had.

I didn't do well in this class, but that's on me. Spanish is just hard for me, but she always but in a lot of effort and time for her students. She seems to care about how well you are doing in this class and flexible if you are open with her.

Prof Dey comes across very strict and was difficult to understand at first. She really does care about her students though and wants them to succeed. This class wasn't too bad....go to class or you'll end up with a C. She's a really nice lady but her TA's were not too nice.
Easy to earn an A, sometimes went on tangents about things I could care less about, but it was still on the tests.

Professor Friedrichsen is great and extremely friendly.  You can tell she really cares about her students. Very difficult class and the tests are insanely hard with no where near enough time to complete them.

Professor Pinhero is an amazing professor! His lectures are really interesting and he is a super nice guy. His homework is extremely tough though. Great class

purely test based grading. Fail your test=fail the class. Though they are curved but you dont know youre true grade till the end of semester past the W period so that causes a lot of stress. poor explanation on the classes. harsh grader. not equal

Exams are extremely hard, in addition to the fact that grading is tough too. Old-style teaching in which it makes studying generally and solving problems in the homework harder than it looks like. I would never take the class again

Dr. Chan is such an incredible professor. I took MEB with him in China, and not only did I learn so much from him, but I believe I have made a life long mentor and friend out of him. horrible professor made me change my whole major. fed up with teaching so taking it out on students.

Awesome professor! He keeps the classes interesting! Just attend classes, and do the homework.

Very nice guy. And you can tell he's very brilliant. It does get quite dry during lectures but, as it's Statistics, that's the nature of the beast. GREAT TEACHER AND REALLY NICE. VERY EASY TO GET AN A. TEST ARE NOT HARD JUST MAKE SURE YOU KNOW WHAT IS GOING ON. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
Speckman is a beast professor. Avoid at all cost !

I really enjoyed the class although he did not come up with a lot of stuff outside of the textbook. Went once to office hours and he was super nice. Easy A Class you won't lose much points if you were being careful.
Really nice guy, not much to him to be honest. He knew the material well regardless that he taught from the book. The book was actually a perfect teaching outline.

Excellent teacher. Always cared about his students and was always willing to bend his lesson plan to what interested us. Tests were reasonable and he prepared us well, not just for tests but for everything beyond as well. EXCELLENT TEACHER! (Redundancy permitted)

I'm not too good at math tbh, but this class was alright. Paul sometimes explains things in confusing ways, and there's often been times where I just go to YouTube to find clearer explanations. Lectures are long, but easy to stay engaged. Dr. McSteen is very knowledgable, but explains things well. Exams can be tough even if you study and think you understand the material.

Super fast-paced. If you skip class, you will probably have no idea what is going on in the next lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory, but iClicker is bonus points, and so is discussion. Passionate teacher, very knowledgable about genetics, moves fast and weekly quizzes (good study tools).
Great professor! Tests and quizzes are difficult, but are open note, so are very fair. You must attend lecture for extra credit points & can get more extra credit from other various assignments.

Dr. Zhu is a very nice lady who clearly puts in effort, but her lectures are difficult to learn from. Very chill professor, very fair grader. There are a ton of "busy work" assignments, but if you put in even a little bit of effort, you'll get full credit. She's also flexible about due dates and tries her best to help you succeed in the class (required conferences for essays, peer review).
That entire class felt like a fever dream. The work was easy though. Wow. Just wow.
very nice but and lots of participation points but the essays were graded harshly

she gives you the illusion of choice then makes you spend half of every class trying to guess what she wants. anyone who has taken an AP lang type class will be bored out of their minds in this one. she doesn't grade quality of writing which would be great in any class except this one (a required intermediate comp class for future english teachers)
Best class I have ever taken. Free money. Don't listen to anyone else.
Very understanding with college students and their lives outside of school. Very flexible with making adjustments to the schedule to best fit everyone's needs.

Her feedback  bizarre & layout of the website  no help. Prompts say "Write an essay of 23 pages in response to each question." So I did but she expects 2-3 pages PER QUESTION, not 2-3 pages total. He is such a nice and passionate professor! Make sure you go to lectures because they are a big part of grade, but if you go to class it is such an interesting class and an easy A!

Honestly one of the best prof i've had at Mizzou. He's very educated and enthusiastic about his lectures, and really cares about his students. I was sick for about a week and messed up one of my reading quizzes and he was very open to fixing it. a pretty cool class, interacts with class sometimes during lectures

Dr. Zambito is a fantastic professor. The  lectures are informative and engaging. You can tell that he is a very cool and knowledgeable about his craft and has dedicated plenty of time to perfecting it. I am so glad that he is at the University and I hope that he stays forever.

Lectures aren't mandatory but very engaging. The content is fun and really interesting. Quickly turned into one of my favorite classes. Online tests and weekly quizzes are based on lectures and part of the readings but are very fair.

Very fun to listen to! Engages students in lectures in a fun way (but not required to participate). Grade is based on weekly quizzes and exams every three weeks, all of which are online and open note/open book.

Class was easy, but be warned if you're taking the online version of this class. The class switches between two professors as the course goes on, and only one knows how to properly set up zoom. Enjoyed Dr. Zambito. He was energetic and made this class enjoyable. Quizzes are almost entirely from the lectures, but reading quizzes are a bit tedious. Overall, I would certainly recommend Dr. Zambito for anyone who wants a chill elective/humanities credit.

Biochem is a difficult course which is why professors receive such poor ratings after people take this class. However, I think that is class is doable if you put in the work. DON'T TAKE HIM. idk where these good reviews are coming from, but he is HORRIBLE. I'm a straight A student and I can barely keep a C in his class. Class exam averages  50s. Dr. Tipton is one of the best professors I have ever had at Mizzou! The class is tough but make sure to read the book and memorize the mechanisms to do well on quizzes/exams. Dr. Casazza is an amazing professor.  He is definitely intimidating at first. He helps out tremendously if you need it. His lectures are super easy to follow and they are extrememly well organized. At first he seems mean and angry, but he is actually an ok guy. He is pretty easy to follow and tells you exactly what will be on the tests, for the most part. He responds to emails quickly as well. Good class.
