Overall, I enjoyed Grant as a professor, and I hope students go to her classes with an open mind.

Professor Grant's class was awesome. Sometimes Grant taught, but there were plenty of guest lectures. Class is structured by a weekly theme and exams are not cumulative. Fairly easy class if you go to class and look over the weekly readings and videos. This class was one of my favorites in the J-School.
The class was very interesting and it definitely challenge you to think. My only problem with her is how her examination questions, especially in the essay part, does not connect together.

Bailey is very interesting as a professor and the content is extremely important but I felt like the class set up was difficult and the grading was unreasonable.  Role play is painful but the way it is graded where you had to say certain words and perform perfectly created a situation where it was a performance and not authentic.  Expects a lot.

She is amazing. But, that doesn't mean it's a super easy class. Do the reading and prepare to be challenged with essays and exams, she does expect what you write to be good. At times essay grading is a little confusing, but nothing to be super concerned about and conferencing helps.

Dr. Harper is my favorite professor during my time at mizzou so far. She, alongside Dr. Rymph, made book club exciting, adventurous, and fun. It is a lot of reading but the memoirs were very interesting and easy to read. And it's only around 6 students. She was always kind to me and gave me support.

Dr. Harper is one of the best professors I've ever had. She's incredibly caring inside and outside of class, and she's someone that it's easy to be comfortable around. She can be a hard grader when it comes to papers, but I think she just expects a lot. You don't need excellent papers to do well, though, as you have other easy grades!

While attendance is not mandatory it enriches the class ten fold. The class is always involved with reading, however as long as you are a fan of mythology (or Percy Jackson) you will find enjoyment throughout the entire thing. With mostly forgiving grading the class is more focused on discussion and development of characters rather than memory.

This is a class to be a writing tutor, so you have to want it. Dr. Harper is very constructive and helpful, but tough, which makes you an excellent writer. It is a HUGE time commitment between tutoring practice and writing assignments. However, Dr. Harper is everything - super knowledgeable and keeps it fun.

Dr. Harper is a fun person and passionate about the honors humanities sequence. However, she grades essays very hard, and several of her prompts are very vague. I would recommend conferencing with her on the papers before the deadline. And stay ahead on the reading! I know its a lot!

I have never loved a professor more. She made everything we read fun and relatable while also making us understand it on a far deeper level than before. Amazing all around, definitely the best in the entire humanities sequence
Love her in a purely admirational-aspire-to-be-her-someday sense.
Literally the sweetest prof at the law school. He genuinely wants all of his students to succeed.
Great class! Assignments and grading were clear. Rahmet was kind, helpful, and easy to reach. Course content was interesting and connected well to real life.

Rahmet clearly communicates expectations and everything is laid out well. If you stay on top of the work you'll learn a lot. She genuinely cares about her students and she was always willing to help when I reached out.

Without question the worst professor I've had at Mizzou. Lectures are as captivating as watching paint dry. Tests are written to trick you. Between the two quizzes, the discussion posts, and the "engagement activities" you have to do each week, you'll spend 80% of your time in this course doing busy work. Couldn't possibly recommend her any less

While this class is very interesting, the grading sucks! There are very few items to be graded on, and the tests dictate your grade, so it is difficult to come back from a poor test score. While Rahment herself is very kind, this class structure was very strict for a 2000-level course. I personally would not take from her again.

It was a really good and straightforward class. Writing and reading heavy but there're interesting/entertaining commentaries on each topic that help you grasp the material better. would definitely take her class again.
There's a lot of writing involved in this class but the assignments are all explained well with clear grading criteria.

This professor is not understanding at all. I received a A+ on all assignments in the class. I accidentally submitted the wrong assignment and did not know until she graded it, so I received a 0 and could not submit the correct version. There are no lectures. You have to get 3 expensive textbooks and teach yourself.

Never taking this professor again. She will accuse anyone of plagiarism if their Turnitin score is above 1% and gives students a 0 if a source isn't cited in her own way. She also makes you buy 3 very expensive textbooks and doesn't post video lectures. Sorry, but I'm not paying tuition to teach myself through textbooks.

He's a great professor, and his lectures are genuinely interesting. However, do not take any of his courses if you'd freak out when your GPA inevitably drops because you get an A-. Because you will get an A-. He also gives no feedback on anything you submit, so you'll never know why you keep getting a 9/10 instead of 10/10.
My absolute goat, taken his classes like 4 times and signed up for another next semester.

This class was more writing than I had anticipated. I wouldn't say too much work, but more than I expected for an elective. The grading felt random and strict. He never gives 100% and doesn't give any feedback. Ramsay is a good professor who cares about his students and class discussions were fun but I had to work for an A- which will drop my GPA.

1. I have taken him for 2 semesters and have never received a 10/10 on an assignment, not a super hard grader but will almost never give a perfect score
2. Often cancelled class, or during class we did something chill like watch X files or have discussions, never work in class
3. Great movie choices, smart, funny, great teacher. I would recommend.

He rocks!! My class was fully online and he was still great about reaching out and making it as enjoyable as possible. I definitely recommend taking him in-person if you can though, just because he's cool. The class was also pretty simple, with the only assignments being weekly discussions, weekly film summaries, and two papers.

Even if you aren't into film, you will enjoy his class. Ramsay cares about his students and chooses movies that he thinks they will like. The honors course is not much harder than the regular one. The classes are for discussions, not doing work. All assigned work is to be completed outside of class. I plan to take more of Ramsay's classes.

Professor Wise is definitely the best professor I've had here. He made every class super enjoyable and it was actually a very fun environment. He's very passionate and knowledgeable about the movies we talk about. The homework, papers, and exams aren't difficult, either. Would definitely recommend to anyone looking for an easy/enjoyable course.

Ramsay Wise is awesome. I took his honors film course and had a lot of fun with it. We had to do some questions and a small writing prompt (250 words) due every week so the work was extremely manageable. He's a bit of a goofy guy, but it's because he enjoys teaching this course so much and he just has fun with it. HIGHLY recommend!
I took the Chancellor's Leadership Class with Professor Smith. He's kind, knowledgeable, and knows a ton about journalism. He gives very thoughtful feedback and takes a personal interest in you.
He's a real gem. He cares about his students and is really passionate about leadership. He was very approachable and was very understanding about any situations.

Randy Smith is one of the nicest teachers on campus, but he's also one of the toughest. Outside of class, he's very very helpful should you ask for it, but you are punished severely for your mistakes in this class (J2100), so make sure to ask for help early.

He is a sweet and very accomplished guy, but so so so horrible at outlining expectations. You could ask him the same question at a different time of day and he would give you two different answers. Additionally, he is kind of boring. Never updates his canvas page so the criteria listed online is super inconsistent with what he says in class.
Boring lectures. Lots of guest speakers. Always promotes his startup website. I won't recommend his courses if you are taking as electives.

Poorly organized and inconsistent in instructions and grading. Recycles tired material from other courses. Does not follow syllabus. Employees 1960s business models for 21st Century journalism startups. Stay away unless you have a time machine.

I took Creative and Innovative Journalism and did not care for the course at all. We had guest speakers nearly every week that were terribly boring. The weekly quizzes and BB posts were fine to deal with, but the whole semester lead up to group projects that were TERRIBLE. He was so ambiguous and expected way to much in such a short amount of time.

really great teacher and easy to take class from. all the notes were online, and the tests are very similar to the practice tests which he goes over in class. sometimes the problems from the review are in the exams(and he tells you). he makes his expectations really clear and is aware that the topics are often difficult for students. just study

The lectures go pretty fast but he posts all of the notes on Canvas making it fair. Gives out a practice test before every exam with questions very similar to those that will appear on the actual test. Overall good professor who explains topics well and ensures you're prepared for every exam.

Raquel Alexandra de Moura Lohner Arouca.name: Raquel Alexandra de Moura Lohner Arouca

comments.text: She's passionate and brings valuable firsthand experience in humanitarian aid. Lectures stay engaging, even when content leans dry. Encourages class discussion and welcomes diverse perspectives. Only complaints: essay rubrics were missing, so expectations were far from clear and canvas page was confusing to navigate and lacked a "grades" tab.

This class was very boring and the professor seemed somewhat unqualified and unprepared. She was pretty unprofessional and I would say it was one of the worst classes I've taken so far here. Not really sure how this course was greenlit. I wouldn't recommend it.

Professor Abousalem is amazing. Since she works in humanitarian aid she has lots of experience in the field that relates directly to the class. You can tell she is passionate about her work and getting to know her students. Show up to class, take good notes, ask questions, and no matter your major it will likely be one of your favorite classes.

Dr. Ronci is perhaps one of the best professors I have ever had. All he asks of you is to come to class, contribute to the discussion, and write what he tells you to. He has about 30 years of teaching experience, and it definitely shows. Yes, he is very intimidating at first, but treat him with respect and he will do the same for you!

Ronci was so informative and fun to listen to. He's certainly opinionated, and you likely won't agree with absolutely everything he has to say, but he knows what he believes and why he believes it. DO NOT SKIP CLASS. He has a very low tolerance for students who don't show up to lectures. Take the time to meet with him one-on-one when writing papers
Good teacher and good dude. opinionated but at least he backs it up instead of having arbitrary and petty biases. Take him with an open mind and you will learn lots.

Raymond Ronci was hands down, one of the worst professors I have ever encountered at the University of Missouri. Not only is he completely unclear about grading, but treats every class as an opportunity for a political manifesto. Do not take this course, tread with complete and utter caution.

Ray is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He's hilarious and totally ignores political correctness so avoid him if you're not into that sort of thing. Also; avoid getting on his bad side. Show up to class regularly and ON TIME and you'll be fine. Pay attention to what he says, and put it in your papers. Easy way to get good grades.
Very interesting and intelligent teacher, he's a tough grader so be able to take criticism. Love his classes, especially critical theory

Very demining, believes any generation other than his is terrible and if you don't share his opinions, you will fail. I can tell he is full of knowledge but fails at teaching it correctly. He is also very unclear on what he wants from assignments until after you turn it on and receive your grade. Class isn't mandatory but he definitely knows.

Awesome professor, you do have to work for an A in this class but he is more than willing to help if you just ask. Some people are intimidated by him--but once you get past that you'll learn a lot from him. He's truly passionate and dedicated to what he teachesthe class and expects the students to be as well. SPEAK UP in his class.

I love Marks so much!! If you ever have to take a classics or latin class TAKE HIS. He really understands when students are struggling and will always try to help curve exams and quizzes so the class can do decent. Definitely a lot of memorization for the weekly quizzes and occasional exams, but he is super clear with what you will need to know.
I looooovveeeeeeeeee Ray Ray Marks. So funny and kind. Good at balancing letting you off easy while still teaching you what you need to know. Super chill guy.

Not a hard class, but definitely time consuming (homework each night was translating about 30 lines of Latin to discuss the next class). Dr. Marks was super helpful and very knowledgeable on his subject.

Professor Marks is my professor for Latin1100H and I have really enjoyed his class. He is such a nice guy and very well-versed in the subject. The language is hard, but the activities we do in class help me to understand it better. I would highly recommend Professor Marks as a professor and am sad I won't have him for Latin1200H next semester.

She is one of the nicest people ever. She really cares about you learning something helpful from her class to use in your life. I did this class as a humanities credit and she took time to make sure I felt part of the group even though I am not in theater.
She really made the class feel like a community and she genuinely cared about you and your grade. She also actually stays in touch if you need her for anything after you're done with her class.
Need to see plays for credit and talk in front of people a lot. Overall easy class. Professor V is really kind   and has good energy

i loved dr. brings! she is super accommodating and understanding to all students. she's also incredibly kind and the lectures and projects are very easy to understand. i highly recommend her to anyone taking english 1000!

She is the sweetest soul ever! You get to miss four times and still get an A anything higher than 4 and your head is affected. Free submission no penalty for late work for a whole 24 hours! She is so great and gives great advice in conferences. I highly recommend she is so great.

I just don't like English courses, so I didn't do great. However, Dr.Brings was super nice and had clear instructions with a great late work policy! If you want a laid back but informative English class, she's the one to take!

She does an amazing job engaging her students, and she's the kindest and most caring professor I've ever had. Extremely well qualified, although she has a slight bias toward one way of linguistic analysis. Still respects all viewpoints though, and very good at teaching people not experienced in the field. 10/10, would take again.

Actual class was LINGST/ENG 4420 - Historical Linguistics. Easiest grader ever. Not concerned with giving bad grades but with actually ensuring you understand material. Zero homework this year and onward as AI accessibility has messed with her ability to fairly grade assignments, so that's a plus.

She is great! She goes super fast through the slides but if you listen and participate she will reward you in your grades. She gives lots of practice and examples. One of my favorites for sure. Gives more than enough material for quizzes and tests. She says they are pop quizzes but she tells you when they will be and what is on them lol. Love her.

The class was interesting but it felt like she was throwing in random group projects for fun. The grading was very vague and she kept asking for "more" information, yet didn't make that clear during the actual assignment, such as the midterm exam. Fun professor though! I just wish there was more structure.

not a fan of her or her class at all. she goes super super fast through all of her powerpoint’s and doesn’t allow enough time for people to stop her to ask questions. very sassy and passive aggressive when answering questions. one of the hardest classes i’ve ever taken. would not recommend. if you can take another class, take it
Fantastic person. Very intelligent, caring, and helpful. Perfectly balanced workload. Made me love realize I love linguistics.

Rebecca Grollemund is so nice, friendly, and clearly has a lot of enthusiasm and passion for Human Language. There are only quizzes and she gives students more than enough material to study for them. She loves to give extra credit to those who participate! She also is more than happy to help you when you aren't understanding something. Love her!

i loved dr. brings! she is super accommodating and understanding to all students. she's also incredibly kind and the lectures and projects are very easy to understand. i highly recommend her to anyone taking english 1000!

Loved this class. Lots of reading. Weekly discussion & quiz. Two short reflection papers and two tests. One group project at the end. Lots of reading/video lectures from different sources. Always available to help & participates in all discussions. Open to changing things & gives opportunities for extensions. Lots of info!
So kind and clearly loves what she does. Wants to get to know you on a personal scale and actually cares about you and your experience in her class.

Meisenbach was one of the most scatterbrained professors I have ever had. The lecture material is inconsistent and the syllabus is just a rough outline of what you will be doing that semester. Grading really comes down to how tough your TA is on the few assignments you are given. Wrote ONE essay in the course, that makes up the bulk of your grade.

Very very helpful professor! Extremely communicative and responds to emails very quickly, which is appreciative from procrastinators like myself! BE SURE TO GO TO LAB!! There is always something due and attendance is a lot more strict in lab.

Dr. Meisenbach is my favorite professor that I have had at Mizzou.  She really cares about her students and their success.  I took her Organizational Communication course and was inspired to change my emphasis area.  She is passionate about what she teaches and does a great job applying her lectures and course material to the real world. I love her
She was very funny, interesting and you can tell she knows her stuff. Clicker points used so attendance is mandatory if you want your points. Book used frequently, twp papers

In Comm 3100, there is no textbook required, because she puts the readings online. You only have to buy a clicker. Dr. Meisenbach makes class interesting, humorous, and discussions are fun. Writing Intensive, but only a few papers due.

Incredibly disorganized, discombobulated, and just so hard to follow. Had to teach myself the entire class, learned absolutely nothing, and I am barely passing. The entire class seems to feel the same way, as we communicated through our group me that she never responded to. Impossible to reach, constantly cancels class, and pushes back everything.
Homework due dates are unorganized and inconsistent. Tests are very difficult even with a double sided cheat sheet.

To put it nicely, Rebecca Whitworth is just not a good professor. In class we rush through the notes and hardly take in any of them, and the homework schedule is very confusing and inconsistent. Unless you enjoy having to teach yourself outside of class in order to pass, I would recommend finding a different professor.

While the class is labeled as in-person, by week 10 there have been a total of 4 lectures not online. She uploads the weekly work on canvas, seemingly whenever she remembers that she's responsible for a class. She couldn't care less about teaching, very lazy prof.

Everything in her lectures is pointless and way over our heads for a beginning econ class for journalism majors. Always came to class stressed and discombobulated and it started off the class with a lot of stress. Cancels class a lot and doesnt upload the make-up videos until very late. Although, you will 100% pass and the class is easy.

This class was interesting when Marty (journalism professor) lectured. I know she is young, but it was really stressful when she would arrive on the Zoom stressed out, scatter-brained, and flustered. The only good was the Friday homework class where she gave all the answers. The TA's will get you through. Take this rather than the other option @ MU

This class is so easy to pass. I took it online so it was easy to use my notes and quizlets, but she encourages that! On Fridays she has reviews for the homework, where she literally just tells you the answers to the homework. Other than that I barely showed up to class. The journalism assignments were the only thing frustrating in this class.

I learned very little in her lectures. She explains very simple things in the most confusing way possible. Had to teach myself from the textbook and attend tutoring. Many extra hours wasted because I wasn't able to learn in class. Her tests were badly written and had grammatical errors that made some questions unintelligible.

I took her Environmental Justice class, and I'd recommend that class to everyone. She's great at encouraging conversation, challenging us with new perspectives, and being sensitive around tough topics. Plus, she's a wonderful human being whose compassion for her students and the people affected by injustice is tangible in every lesson she teaches.
Her class was extremely easy, and she clearly cares about her classes content and hearing everyone's thoughts and opinions.

I had her last semester for Recent Theories in Sociology and got a lot out of that class. She's super organized, and uses presentations to guide what you need to remember, but you gotta read and listen to her lectures for key info. What I loved was her willingness to engage in conversation, and overall compassion towards sensitive topics.

I'm surprised that so many people didn't like having Dr. Scott! I thought she was funny and engaging, which made her lectures enjoyable. The readings are boring, but she brings them to life during lecture. As long as you listen in class, the tests aren't hard. I hardly read the textbook because the readings were long, and I still ended with an A.

I really enjoyed how casual and conversational Soc31000 was. You definitely have to take notes to get all the information down, but it's almost impossible not to get a good grade in this class. Unlimited attempts on quizzes, open book tests and a take home final.
Definitively veers towards the Feminist Tradition in theoretical view. Does not like criticism, challenges towards class content, and, well, not a very good instructor.

She's very educated on the material, however if the content doesn't interest you it'll be hard to pay attention in class. There's no powerpoint to highlight the important points so you have to pay close attention to the lectures. Study guides are 10 or so essay prompts and the exams questions are pulled from those prompts so there's no surprises.

I tried to be optimistic and find the good but the course is just boring.

Very knowledgeable but not helpful. Grades strictly and according to personal beliefs. A lot of the information in the class is useful and applicable. Not great at providing constructive feedback or working to support knowledge base.

I took her online Intro/Methods of Early Intervention Class. She requires discussion board posts each week with lots of reading. There are 4 quizzes on MO modules for EI, pretty easy. There are also two papers, 8-10 pgs and 12-16 pgs you have to write. Not horrible but can't fly through at your own pace either. She is knowledgeable and helpful.

this class is geniunely the worse class and professor I have ever had. Only talks, and barely puts any notes, and no homework. Reduced the extra credit to TWO percent! Just talks the whole time, way too quickly personally, and expects you to essentially teach yourself. Do not take her if you can avoid her.
Dr. North is a tough grader for exams and your grade is almost completely reliant on the 3 exams. She does give lots of opportunities for extra credit. Her lectures are not the most coherent.

This course is very difficult unless you put in the work. Dr. North comes across as rude and expects a lot. Exams are almost completely written answer and im not sure that anyone receives a 100%. After saying all that, I loved this class and I loved Dr. North. She is very sure of herself and her work. I learned a lot and enjoyed the material.

If you're reading these other reviews and freaking out, relax the world will keep turning. She's not that bad, not an incredibly difficult grader, lots of extra credit opportunities (7%), tests are written but straightforward and directly from the lectures. Attendance and participation are not required. She gives partial credit on everything.

No lab so don't hope for any extra point opportunities or hands on experience. The only bonus opportunity was to get a workshop certificate by sitting in for two workshops which if you do all that, you only get 5 extra credit points, wow! She won't let you attend on zoom unless you're sick. Incredibly tough grader as well.

Wow. Avoid at all costs. She is horrible at creating any kind of positive learning environment. Worst experience I have had at Mizzou. Makes me totally disinterested in staying in the water resources field, or SNR for that matter. Find another route, this one needs detoured.

Rebecca is very nice and accommodating. Classes can be boring, but it's not entirely her fault.

I had a great time in Dr. deGraffenreid's class. While the class was lecture heavy, she kept it very interesting and applied it to our lives, and was very open to any questions we might have. Rebecca is a good person who tries to make her class fun. But, her lectures are just so hard to sit through. She overloads her lecture slides with too much information making it hard to keep up with notes and also pay attention enough to understand what she is explaining. Dr. Cocroft is such a cool professor. He is so humble about his accomplishments in research, but is quite impressive if you look into it! His class was relatively easy and his lectures were amazing! I would definitely recommend working with him if you get the chance.

In all my 4 years at Mizzou, I have come across many great professors, though not one competes with Dr. Cocroft. He is truly an inspiration and genuinely cares about his student's success and even went through the effort of learning every single person's name in the whole lecture hall. Very knowledgeable professor and is truly kind in his teaching.

Dr. Cocroft is an amazing professor, and by far my favorite professor at Mizzou. He is very understanding and knowledgeable. He provides good feedback and time to complete assignments if you miss a class. 
He encouraged me to come to class when I was having rough days and never once dismissed me. 
His dog, Peaches, is so sweet and loves belly rubs.

Dr. Cocroft is a soft spoken professor, but he really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He is always invested in what students are taking away from his lectures/assignments so dont be afraid to bring him suggestions about the class!

Dr. Cocroft is the nicest professor I have ever had. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. His lectures are pretty interesting, and he caters in-class examples to the interests of the class. He does in-class assignments so attendance is mandatory (you can miss class twice). Take one of his classes if you have the chance!

Reggie is honestly the goat. This is a very tough class, and since he has been teaching for so long, he understands this very fact. There are 3 exams, all 2 hours, and very difficult. The homework requires a lot of thinking and time each week. In this class, you will find many people starting to discover if this major is what they really want.

Reg is a great professor.  You can tell he loves what he does because of how well he teaches the subject.  Mass and Energy Balance can either be a fun class or a hard class based on what professor you have.  As long as you show up to every single class and pay attention to what Reggie says, then he will make this class fun and worth your time.

Diffidently some tough love, but only because he wants you to grow and build skills that are useful outside this class. If you're having any sort of trouble school, personal, otherwise he wants to help. Just be willing to go see him talk. Work hard, make sure you understand material, practice and you'll be fine.

There's five exams and they are weighted 80% of grade. 4-5 questions on each exam and they are hard. No shortcuts in this class even on homework bc its all about understanding material and processes. I had to retake it twice and dropped it both times. Nice and understandin guy. He says use your intution but it's a beginer class? Too much pressure

Takes pride in a low grade.  Almost treats the class like it's his entertainment and doesn't seem to remember that his student's education is more important than trying to entertain yourself. Loves to be open ended with his explanations rather than go in depth about a topic because that's more mysterious. very corny so beware. adds layer of stress
Super sexist. If you're a girl in his class good luck. All these other ratings are probably written by men. He gives all the boys in his classes his phone number.

He's a bit intimidating at first, but he's honestly a really good professor. When going over problems, he breaks them down in a way that makes them very easy to understand. The tests are quite difficult and can make or break your grade, so make sure to study hard and prepare well for them. Try not to miss lectures either.

Reg is a great teacher and a caring individual. He wants his students to do well, but he wants them to put in the work to earn it. I've learned a lot in his class, but I've also cried a lot over this class. It's very tough, but he is there to answer any questions whenever you need. Be prepared to be pushed to your limit!

He grades very strictly, with most exam points from short answers. Missing a lecture or pop quiz costs significant points. Lectures are 40–60 slides read word for word, making the class about memorization, not problem solving. It focuses on herbicide families and barely covers modern, more environmentally friendly techniques. Also study EVERY fact
Tests often include very random facts from the slides that you would never have memorized. Writing intensive section is poorly structured
Dr. Smeda is a fine professor, but a little old school. It seems like he wants to make his class as difficult as possible and overwhelm you with information.

He is a nice guy but I had him for Plant sciences 2370 and he co-taught with his wife.They organized several field trips off campus for us but did not arrange any transportation while requiring attendance which was annoying as a student without a car. He would only teach at lab and most times would not go to lecture, only his wife would attend.
AMAZING professor. Smeda has amazing stories that apply to the materials he teaches
Smeda is a good professor and clearly explains topics in class. Take good notes though, because he won't post the slides and the exams are all short answer. Lab is usually not too difficult.

This class isn't particularily difficult or helpful. It seemed strange to have a pretty detailed written exam for a class that's otherwise just about practicing graphic design. It's a true intro to design -- if you have previous experience, you won't learn much.
Resume project was useful because I just used my newly designed resume to help get a job!
Truly cares for her students

Seems kind but is a harsh grader and not flexible to more attempts. The extra credit assignment is fun but not nearly enough to make a change. I tried, studied and submitted all assignments on time.Don't recommend.

easy class, I would recommend it as a j-specialty for anyone, even if you don't like design. She gives clear expectations for the assignments and her grading was surprisingly objective for a design class. Attendance isn't required but you should attend class to get the notes for her tests, most of the questions come directly from the slides.

Renee is a sweetheart. She's a very nice professor. The assignments aren't hard, but you're graded on how your classmates do. You can have a strong design, but if one of your classmates had a more creative (or unique) design, your grade would be lowered. She takes forever to grade work, but she's still very nice and encouraging.

Zero participation on the DB and rarely makes announcements Uses a general grading rubric and provides no useful feedback; content of the course has so much potential for teaching but there is none by this professor other than the use of another professors tegrity lectures and notes (which are awesome); material is outdated; APA knowledge a must

He is so AWESOME. Coolest professor so far. I really learnt a lot from this class. It's a really helpful class, not academically but in REAL LIFE. exams are a little bit hard, but if you pay attention in class(which is really easy to do because his lectures are always entertaining), read the book, then you'll be fine.

Only go if you're going to go to every single class. I missed 5 classes and it affected by grade by about two percentage points even though I'd gotten an A on all exams. I found the exams pretty difficult because questions were so specific.  Read the book and go to class everyday.  Feistman is cool but not always helpful.

Attendance is mandatory with clickers. To me the lectures were boring and the same thing every week. Feistman is cool but the tests are hard because they are over different beliefs and can be kind of confusing. One good thing about the class is that he drops one of the exams. My advice do good on all of them and drop the final. Read the book
Attendance is mandatory.... the only downfall of this class. Other than that pretty easy. As long as you read the book and remember online assignments you should be good to go.
The class is super easy- pretty much no homework. He also drops 1 test and the final is optional

The class overall is a bit ridiculous. Didn't learn a thing and attendance is mandatory because he uses clickers. The point values he places on assignments don't make sense. He asks for you to write in a "Journal" then grades them like academic journals.
Great !

I had Prof Callahan for a history class about religion in the United States a couple of years ago. It was my favorite class at Mizzou and not like any of my other history classes. I expected a class about the history of religion to be boring because I'm not religious but it wasn't. Lots of cool stuff and different ways of thinking about religion.
I loved this class. Professor Callahan makes you work, but you'll learn a lot.
Easy class that really helps open your eyes to the changing world around you. Callahan shows you how to see religion in so much of our pop culture . Fun class

Good professor, very open minded and accommodating to students. Likes projects, so be prepared for a little group work. He is good to work with, though. I didn't read the book until the final, and that was the only time I actually used it--- we had no tests! Only a final. Attendance is mandatory.
Totally not the class I expected, in a good way. Callahan was great! Enthusiastic, smart, and helpful.
The professor was very informed and could explain the class concepts using examples that everyone could understand. I appreciated the unbiased info we heard in lectures. A very fair professor.

Professor Callahan gives clear lectures and covers as many points of view as possible when talking about class material. He grades fairly, and gives useful feedback during office hours. While taking one of his classes I noticed he was very passionate about his work and excited to see students discuss and learn from each topic.

Religion and popular culture was one of my favorite courses. I learned a whole new vocabulary that isn't just about religion. This isn't a course about world religions. It's really about thinking about where our ideas about religion, society, gender, race, class, and being human come from in popular culture. Easily the best prof I've had at Mizzou.

He does not care about his students and often made me cry in class. He is very particular with pronunciation and will make you repeat a word 15 times until you get it right. Very hard grader on tests. I felt very belittled in the class, and he would often talk down to me. I have never felt so much anxiety in a class before taking his class.

I'd give her more than 5 stars if I could. Dr. Rikki is amazing. She is very knowledgeable in this subject and genuinely cares about her students, and it really shines through. She gives very detailed feedback on all assignments so you know exactly why you got the grade you did. So kind + is always willing to listen to her students. Take this prof!

This professor was good, but she never answers her emails. It's really bad. You will need her help with an assignment in her class and she wont answer for a week and then your speech gets a low grade because she doesn't email you back. No final. A TON of discussion posts and attendance is required. Sometimes the busy work is outrageous.

IF YOU HAVE THE CHANCE TO TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROF, DO IT! Dr. Roscoe is an amazing teacher, she cares about each student, is willing to help them succeed no matter what academic standing they are in. She helps you get the grade you deserve, you still have to put in the work, but she will guide you to the finish line! Best Prof ever!!

Rikki Roscoe is a very nice teacher who obviously cares for her students. She is very good at giving feedback and you'll do well as long as you turn things in. This class is very organized and structured by nature (it is pretty consistent across Mizzou) and there will be a lot of busywork, but overall you will enjoy showing up to class with her.

Dr. C gets a bad rep, however, her class is easy to pass. She has numerous homework assignments, in-class worksheets, attendance papers, and quarterly projects that everyone gets 100% on because she doesn't actually read them. The exams are the hard part; they don't quite correlate to what is on the lectures and study guides, but overall super easy

Dr. C gets such a bad rap, but she is truly a great professor. Her class is hard, yes, but welcome to being a biochem major... If you are organized this class really doesn't require more than 3-4 hours outside of class each week. The skills learned in this class are necessary for any research/lab work. Dr. C wants to see her students succeed.

Dr. C is an amazing professor that really cares and tries to relate the material to the real world. The midterm and final were somewhat hard, but she gives out enough extra credit so it doesn't matter. She gives out a lot of practice and teacher material that is relevant and important in the real world.

This was a great introduction into the world of biochem labs. Lots of extra credit at the beginning which helps a lot if properly taken advantage of. Dr. C speeds through her lecture slides; however, most of the material isn't on the final, and she posts slides online. Go to PLAs with lab questions since her office hours are "by appointment only".

She has the expectation that freshman will be able to perform an experiment at the level of a tenured professor on the first try. Just was very negative and would constantly talk down to us. Gives extra credit at the beginning to justify being such a picky grader.

Dr. C is a somewhat ok teacher. However, her labs are never straightforward, and you will constantly be asking the PLAs questions due to everything being extremely unclear. The amount of work is ridiculous. If you are an organized person, prepare to be angry. Her entire course is unorganized and makes you want to crawl into a hole.

SO MUCH HOMEWORK!!! her homework will take you hours and the PLAs will grade toughly! Her tests are ridiculously short for the amount of work she expects you to do and then blames it on your time management. She a great lady but I would not take one of her classes again.

This class is an easy A, but I feel like I learned nothing. Dr. Chaudhary is not available outside class or by email. The PLAs make or break the class. The lectures are confusing. The assignments take forever but teach you nothing. Having taken the biochem class that comes after Dr. C's, I can say that this class does not prepare you for it.
nice person, easy grader, great lecture

Robert is the rare breed of graduate instructor you'll get: one who is funny and teaches well! When I took his class in the fall semester, I always looked forward to lecture -- he made it interesting by bringing up cool facts and wasn't afraid to use extra credit to motivate us. That being said, the course was easy because of his generosity.
Really love him

This post prod class was probably the most useful film class I've taken so far. Anyone can teach you how to technically edit, but he will go above and beyond to ensure a deep understanding of the thought process behind every cut you make and ensure you are set for any video production in the future, whether or not you want to be an editor.

Exceptional teacher. He will give you opportunities in class that you will not get anywhere else- seriously. He is a working filmmaker with films on Netflix and an array of Oscar/award-winning filmmaker legends. If you are even slightly interested in documentary or film, take his classes. This class made me switch to the documentary track!

Very manipulative, demanding, and heavily picks favorites. Makes students compete against each other for trips to film festivals. Didn't really teach me anything outside of the basic definition of documentary. He thinks his class is the only one that matters. Talks about students behind their backs, to other students. Extremely unprofessional.

The professor really emphasizes to read the book for the exams and to come to class. The lectures don't help because he rants about a bunch of stuff that will definitely go over your head. He asks the class a question and waits 30 seconds to a minute for a response when the question isn't even something he has fully taught the class yet.Theres more

Not a fan of this class. Lectures were a lil boring, we were assigned LOTS of homework, everything was graded very harshly, report revision comments felt rather unprofessional and sometimes overly rude, and made it a point to give no frame of reference for what was to be on tests. "If you went to class you'll be fine" was not necessarily true lol

I got an A in the class, but don't take that as a sign that the course was easy, as I scored very near the top score on every major assignment, usually around 20% above the exam/ essay average. The professor is arrogant and snarky when you ask him questions and hides any information about upcoming exams. Generally rude and harsh. TAKE ANYONE ELSE!

Started off enjoying this class. Halfway through the semester, I dread this class. First exam was basically a toss up, had no idea what to prepare for, got lucky and passed with a C. An insane amount of assignments. Extremely tough grader. His email responses are rude and unprofessional. Unsure if I'll pass the class now. I'm extremely frustrated.

Dr. Winholtz is a wonderful 2200W materials professor who is very passionate and detailed in his lectures of material. While the class may be a bit more difficult than some, you will know the material in depth by the end of the course. Recommend for anyone interested in materials path of MAE.
He grades tough, there is a ton of homework during class and outside of class
Great teacher highly recommend!

Great guy, you'll need to delve into the class to do well, but if you continuously ask how to better your reports and presentations he will give you good tips. Funny, and makes fun of stupid questions just an overall good teacher who knows what he is doing. One downside is the textbook is absolute garbage.

I really like Rob's fieldwork stories and learning from his experiences in Brazil. We watched many movies which I enjoyed.  Final project was tough but I ended up very satisfied with what I was able to put together.
Probably one of the best professors Mizzou Anthropology has to offer!
Probalby one of the best courses I have taken at Mizzou. Lots of freedom to pursue your own project and follow your own interests. Rob is approachable and helpful.

Walker is nice and passionate, but does not teach very effectively. HW was only ever about coding in python, which was never taught to us in depth, and the final exam covered material that was only ever made available during in person lectures (not recorded) and a 700+ page novel. Cool guy, but don't take unless you already know how to code.

Dr. Schnabel is an amzing professor, you will suceed in this class as long as you try. Exams are hard yes, but you can get good grades. Read the book, he takes some exam questions from the book.Go to class he will tell you whats on the exam. Finally do your packback becuase there is extra credit.

Do not take. Worst professor I have ever had. He will tell you "don't wait to ask questions" but talk to you like you're stupid if you ask questions. If you feel he graded a question wrong on an exam (doesn't give a key) he will regrade your entire exam and "mark things wrong if he realizes he should've marked them wrong in the first place."

Worst professor ever (as a teacher and as a person). Incredibly rude when asked for help on anything and doesn't show the correct process on how to solve problems. Studying helps some since you don't go over almost any of the actual information you need to know in class. If you don't know exactly what he wants to hear, you wont do well on exams.

A majority of points come from the four exams and the homework papers to along with them. Extra credit from packback will boost your grade a ton. He is very sarcastic with feedback so talk to the TA if you need help. Don't expect him to actually put in the extra credit for attendance, he lies about it. If you study you'll do decent in the class.

He has a dry sense of humor and will do test reviews the day or two before the test. He offers discussion board which adds up to easy points. But that is where the good ends. He will talk down to you and be condescending every step of the way. Whatever you're doing, it's not enough. Life outside class does not matter. Only his class matters.

This class is genuinely the hardest class I've had to take in Animal Sciences at Mizzou. The tests ask about VERY specific scenarios that are glazed over in class, making them hard to study for. Schnabel has very unrealistic expectations of his students and is not helpful or kind when asked questions. Students are expected to learn at his level.

One of the hardest classes I have ever taken. 400/600 points are tests. The final replaces your lowest test score but if you do worse it still replaces it. He is not very approachable and when you ask him a question he just responds with another question. Study any red material on the slides as they will show up on tests.

Rudest experience I've had with a professor when asking for help. I did everything he told us to do to be successful in this class and when my grade did not show that I got in contact with him to look for help and other resources he replied quite unprofessionally and in summery told me I was not putting in the effort I told him I was. I got no help
He gives good lectures on the content but they are so boring. He grades tests incredibly easy though.
I took Honors Philosophy: Ethics of Right and Wrong. Very entertaining and easy. Professor was very accomodating.
why come visiting emory, go back to your univeristy to teach, dont ruin our Phil departmnet

You are only graded on 2 papers and 4 exams that max out at 15 points each. If you are one of the lucky ones who scores over a 10/15 on anything be happy. He grades way to harsh and has very poor communication skills. You never know exactly what is happening and where and when things are due.

If you take this class you will only have 7 total assignments for your final grade, of those assignments, 4 of them are exams with a maximum of 2 questions. In your lab (where you should receive help) the TA will ask 3 questions and then sit there in silence. It seems like they don't even have a plan for this class like they're just winging it.

If you use the Canvas 'to-do' list as a reminder to complete assignments like me, make sure to write down all the dead-lines from the syllabus. All of the assignments and grades are listed on Canvas besides for one of the reports. I lost 15% of my grade due to this inconsistency. Don't bother asking for redemption, he will just ignore your emails.

I think he's a pretty funny guy. But he unfortunately takes his entry-level class too seriously and isn't great at communication. There are about 8 grades in total for the entire class, so if you miss out on one (as I did), consider yourself done for. At the time of writing we're over halfway through the semester, and he hasn't graded any. Dropped.

He was really unorganized, the TAs in discussions had to help everyone figure out what was going on and sometimes they didn't even understand. Just read off slides that were later posed and I'm pretty sure he didn't even look at any assignment that were turned in.

I wasn't looking forward to J1100 since it's a basic journalism course but Professor Jones made his lectures incredibly engaging. He provided relevant real-world examples for abstract ideas. When classes transitioned online due to COVID-19, he handled the best of all my professors. The final group project was also very creative and fun.

Professor Jones is the kind of person you WANT to listen to, which is essential when teaching a lecture hall full of freshman. He has the kind of charisma that keeps students coming to class because they know they'll have great discussions and understand the concepts by the end of class. This class isn't difficult if you go to class. : )

Emulated exactly what you should want out of University lectures. Great structure, thought-provoking discussion, humor, and the implementation of valuable guest speakers with diverse backgrounds and skillsets. This class isn't hard if you love the subject and if being taught by someone who loves the subject inspires you. (you go to go to class)

Robert Jones's class was the best! I was slightly dreading taking a "journalism and democracy" class, but I was pleasantly surprised. Jones had a very personable demeanor that made students comfortable engaging in class discussions, he used relevant examples that made content easy to digest, and he truly cared about our learning, even remotely.
Prof. Jones did a really good job at teaching this class. I thought this class was going to be boring but I ended up looking forward to it. The lectures were super engaging and I learned a lot.

Mr. Jones is probably one of the best lecturers I've ever had. I hardly ever cared about the material, but he's just so good that I'd stay engaged the whole time. Exams seem easy, but you really do need to at least review, so taking notes is kinda essential because we go through a lot of information.

Professor Jones has been one of my favorite instructors during my time at the University of Missouri. I looked forward to his class each week as he was engaging, informative and relatable. Professor Jones handled the transition to online classes very well this past semester. I would highly recommend this professor to others.

Prof Jones was probably one of my top professors in my freshman year of college. He clearly outlined the expectations of the class from the beginning, so I knew exactly what to expect. He added a color coding system to his lectures (green for definitely write this down, yellow for writing down the main idea, and red for just pay attention.)

Professor Smale is charismatic and kind. In Colonial Latin America you would never expect to have so much fun. His eccentric teaching style is all tangents and fun facts; its super engaging. His assessment style matches this perfectly as he only asks you to write what you know. I recommend this class to everyone especially aspiring educators.

I took Social Revolutions in Latin America, and it became one of those classes I was genuinely excited to attend because the lectures were so fascinating! Professor Smale brought this vital history to life with the stories he told, the readings he assigned, and the questions he encouraged. If you pay attention and do the readings, you'll be fine!
A gem of a man, but loves his tangents and goes over time more often than not.

This class is a great history elective that has interesting topics while being fairly easy. The only things really graded is attendance, short reading quizzes, and short comments. The lectures are definitely all over the place, but he is a super funny guy. Only complaint is that if you took his colonial class, its super repetitive for first 5 weeks

Definitely one of my favorite professors this semester! He shows his passion for history through his lectures and it really makes you want to learn. His PowerPoints are mainly just pictures emphasizing what he will talk about, however, he is not hard to follow.

Dr. Smale is so awesome. He gives energetic lectures that are seemingly scattered-brained, but absolutely educational. All you have to do is provide strong short comments every week and take easy quizzes... if you read/ skim the texts. I did not read everything but definitely read my fair share. Take Smale!!!

Professor Smale is a very interesting and funny person. His lectures, all though required, are interesting to listen to. Beware, he does not have bullet points for you to copy and he definitely is all over the place, but he means well. The class is super easy, normally a reading quiz that you do online and a short comment. Plus, he gives feedback

He is very nice and caring when it comes to his student and is always wiling to meet to discuss grades, assignments, etc. However, he does get distracted very easily and sometimes takes up the whole class time discussing something that is not on the syllabus. Be prepared to be all over the place, however it will be rewarded with a good grade.

His reviews are very similar to the exams. He has a policy that you can replace your exam scores with whatever you get on the final, so most people recover their grades on the final. All homeworks are participation, but he does go over them in class so you can check yourself on whether you got the right answer. I highly recommend his classes.

Quizzes on material he hasn't even taught,I know hes trying to force students to do the reading but this is very detrimental to students who learn from being verbally/visually taught,The exams were 10x harder than anything ever seen in the class,You'll never know your performance in the class until after finals,Also makes annoying mouth noises 24/7

O'Connell is a tough, but motivating professor. The fast pace lectures, difficult content and structure of this course is overwhelming to say the least. This class is the ultimate grind for understanding, and you will be in the same race with the rest of your classmates for the final exam at the end of the semester worth 70% of your grade.

Professor O'connell is a great teacher. The course content is naturally difficult so no matter what this class takes a lot of work. He does a good job of breaking down the textbook and making it clear. In order to make the classes more effective you do have reading assignments/problems to do before lecture, but they never took more than an hour.

He knows his stuff, but you can tell he used to be in the military. He didn't have set office hours, which made it somewhat inconvenient to meet with him. His notes were pretty hard to follow because he jumped around the board a lot. His grading scale was very generous though.
Has a different approach to teaching which is really helpful for this class in particular. Really cares about his students and their learning. He's a little blunt, but he knows his stuff.

Awesome teacher, actually cared about students and if they learned. Has a different hands on approach to learning which is great. Speaks english which is rare for engineering, and is just an all around fair teacher.
If there is confusion it can be resolved with communication. Engaging in the lectures is key

I have taken four classes with Dr. Walsh and look forward to more. He is not traditional in the way he approaches classes which takes some getting used to. Political and stuck on lecturing information useless to topic.

Very boring and does not post grades throughout the semester you dont know your grade until the end. Teaching zoom classes but doesnt know how to work zoom.
Great professor that I have always looked forward to his classes. He doesn't try to trick you on tests and is fairly lenient on submitables as long as you put in the time.

I took Walsh for ARCHST 2100 as a humanities to get done, and I ended up liking the class and the professor so much I got a new minor. He genuinely seems like he cares about the material and his students, gave out very little homework, and was an easy grader. Super doable class.
