Was sick a lot and canceled probably half of the classes or had her TAs teach for her.  All tests are really easy and literally from things right from lecture.

The most boring class I have ever taken. Mandatory attendance makes you sit through her hours of rambling and hardly making sense. Taught myself more than she did. Some topics are interesting, but she's not extremely educated in the matters. Easy class overall, just hard to sit through.

this was THE most boring class i have ever taken, if you have ever studied any psychology, prepared to hear it all again. you have to attend because attendance counts. class drags on for ages it seems. she seems nice but definitely has favorites.
Everything learned in class could be learned from the book.  Make sure you go to class though or lose points.
Robbie is a great prof.  I would recommend any of her classes.
Robbie is a very nice teacher!  Make sure you go to class because attendance is counted in this class.  Her tests are easy, but there are many application questions.  I highly recommend her class!
She is a great teacher but GO TO CLASS att. counts!  this class is a lot like psyc. and gives you a feel of what the education field will be like.

This class was so fun! My first film class at Mizzou, and was very enlightening to types of films I otherwise would not have known. Transnational/migrant films are more important than ever. If you're a film non-major and want a film class, this is the one!

She is awesome! I'm surprised to see negative ratings about her. From my experience, she's super understanding and brings great energy to class. The coursework is challenging, but she's a great instructor and will re-explain until you understand. I wish I could take another class from her.

I don't think there was a single assignment in this course that wasn't docked. Professor grades harshly and unfairly and will think of any excuse to knock your grade. The reading material is impossible to find or watch videos on.

She grades very partial and not fair. Do not expect to get full credit on any assignment.. EVER. Always has a comment to make about something you did not answer correctly, but the class is difficult to understand.

She's a really nice professor, the lectures can drag on a lot though. The class is based on reading books, a few online assignments, a presentation (group), attendance, and papers. She can grade kind of particularly but it's really hard to get below a B with everything.
Had her for Woman and Gender Studies, she was a great teacher. She was helpful and had a very open mind when listening to students. She would also review over all important material before the tests.
Great class!
Quizzes are open book. Essays are very important to do well on.  Reading the assignments isn't necessary but is recommended if you want to do good on the midterm and final.
Professor Harris was delightful to have this semester. She was sweet, funny, and held the classes attention. I am glad I had her, she is a joy to be around.

Dr. Harris is one of the sweetest professors at Mizzou. I look forward to having her again when I am taking all nursing courses. She is caring, funny, genuine, and so positive it's nearly impossible to have a bad time in her class. She was real, honest, and informative when it came talking about to the field of nursing and our futures as nurses.

Do not take this online with Dr. Hurst. It is terrible. There is something due M-F. She grades extremely tough! The little quizzes you have to take make no sense. You have to teach yourself everything. There is tons of reading as well. I have taken several upper level science classes that are WAY easier than this!

Very caring and flexible professor. The class requires a bit of reading and writing daily assignments but it's easy to get into and is often more enjoyable than a typical lecture and quiz format. Don't worry about the course load, as long as you show thought in your writing, she will give points and quality feedback!

Dr. Hurst is your stereotypical entry level course instructor. She expects you to be as passionate as she is regarding the general principles of environmental biology. She also expects you to dedicate every ounce of your time and effort to her class. It is not an exaggeration to say that there was an assignment due every single day. Very Tedious.

She's a fantastic professor and the course structure is very engaging! You simply go through some resources (videos, articles, etc) before writing discussion posts or reflections every day. It takes barely any time and as long as you get interested in the subject, you'll do fine! She's also super sweet and personable in her comments back!

No exams or textbook which sounds easy at first but the Professor has a very ambiguous grading criteria which seems to change as their mind does. Will always find something wrong with your discussion posts and responses and could not care less if you learn anything.

Dr. Hurst is amazing. She has to be one of the most caring professors I have ever had. Her lessons are well thought out and assignments are all very well detailed on expectations. There is something due each day M-F, but she posts early and you can work ahead. If you work hard and show your knowledge, she'll excuse you from some of the work.

Dr. Hurst is the most amazing teacher I have ever had. I could talk about her all day long. I have learned SO much from her class. I have never seen her face but she almost feels like a second mother. She is extremely caring and generous. Her class is designed for you to learn and excel. Don't be afraid by the amount of work, it is very doable

I ended the course with over 100%. No exams, no zoom meetings, and no text book. There are small assignments due daily M-F, but they are put up at the same time so you can do them all in one day. Extra credit is given on most of the assignments if Hurst likes your work. It's an easy A, but you learn a lot and Hurst is an amazing and flexible person

Her instructions are extremely long for assignments, but somehow still unclear. She is picky about a lot of things, so read the fine print. She loves to do group assignments for essays, which is difficult since it is an online class. The exams are atrociously difficult, with only 75 minutes for over 90 questions. I do NOT recommend this class.

This class is atrocious. I have never in my life had a 3-hour lecture video until this class. The amount of group work is infuriating. Exams are insanely difficult with random details. It is way too much work. Instructions on assignments are 3 pages long, with extremely detailed things done in highly specific ways. timely with email

Difficult tests and quizzes. felt like she made questions harder on purpose to bring down the average. You can do a lot of work for this class, just to have your grade lowered because she gives hard exams. She is also unclear about many assignments.
She makes tests and quizzes very difficult. She is kind and very knowledgeable, but it will take a lot of work to get a good grade. Not much room for error if you want to get an A.

Dr. Bowman has high expectations for her students. However, if you communicate with her, she is very caring and understanding. Some of her quizzes are excessive and her final is a group project despite being an online course. She does require a ton of reading and lecture, however she grades quite fairly. I enjoyed her class more than I expected
Extremely long lectures, hard assignments, hard grader.

Long lectures and tough quizzes and tests. Very hard to get an A. There are no free points or extra credit; you just need to do well on the tests and assignments every week. Very hard to get an A on the weekly quizzes. Very knowledgeable, but take a different professor if you want to get a good grade.

This class typically had a quiz and about three lectures a week that were long and boring. The exams were difficult and no one ever got a 100. She doesn't curve grades and the month that she covers insurance is homework heavy. There is a group project toward the end of the semester plus a final exam. The content can be difficult to understand.

I have liked Professor Rotman. This class isn't difficult but the content can be kind of dry. She encourages participation in class, and didn't cold call in this class compared to the previous course I took with her. If you study the content and go to class you'll do fine. She requires attendance to a book club, requires reading a book.

This should be a 3000 level. You might struggle w/ the material unless you're Pre-Law. Very law-heavy and assigns a lot of readings, but you can get by w/o doing them. Tests are written responses only. Assigns pop quizzes but they're easy and a small portion of your grade. Good precursor class if you have to take Env Sci 4400w (same prof).

Professor Rotman is an awesome person but don't be fooled that this is a 2000 level class. It would probably be easier for those with a law background, but coming from the environmental side, some of the law stuff is more difficult to grasp. The tests aren't easy but she takes that into account while grading.

Dr. Geisert is hilarious to listen to. His labs are amazing and very fun, but his lectures can be a bit scattered with slides not matching to the handout. He is one of the best to talk to if you are struggling with the material, he is always willing to help. He is retiring so he isn't around much, but snag him if you can.

Dr. Geisert is literally my favorite professor ever. If you are a student who cares and does well, he will let you know. His exams are fairly easy considering you can predict a majority of the questions he asks based on how much time in class he spent on each section. It is easy to get a good grade if you just tried.

Dr. Geisert is one of the best professors I've had at Mizzou. He really seems to care about how you do in the class and he goes over and above in terms of review sessions and making the class as fun as possible!

Took the Chancellor's Leadership Class with him. Great guy and totally willing to write you a rec. Def a class you need to participate in to get points, but he's really nice is you have a good reason for an absence. My alarm didn't go off and I missed 2/3 of class and he was super understanding!
Ron is lovely. He's a real journalist and gives amazing feedback. He cares so much about his students and will support you in any way he can.
He goes on a lot of tangents about his experience in the field, but is very interesting to hear from. The class dynamic is very relaxed.

The class is interesting, but engaging most of the time. He usually ignores what the class period is planned to be about and what the assignment is in Canvas and talks about whatever he wants for at least the first 30 minutes, which is a little odd but fun. Prof. Stodghill is a very nice man and cares about making students good at what they do.
Awful...Terrible...Beware....NO

Wasn't responsive to emails. There are assignments from August not graded and it is the last week of the semester (December). When assignments were graded months later feedback was given that was no longer helpful but I was unable to get any points back because it had already been so long.

I would shy away from any class that this man teaches. The entire semester, he was ill prepared for class. He only gave 1 grade the entire semester until the final. Then he gave random grades at the end of the semester. He did not notify students of the grades they received on their final. He did not notify students that final grades had posted.

This by far is one of the easiest four-week summer courses offered at Mizzou. It is my recommendation to have at least a year's experience in the common Adobe products however for it to be an easy course. Graded primarily on effort and not picky on your style of design. Don't miss out on an easy GPA booster and enjoyable class.

Loved this class. I already knew some Spanish so it was a breeze but even if you know nothing, you learn from the ground up. Very easy to make up missed attendance. I think if you take the honors section you actually get Rosa as your prof and not a TA

This class is very heavy in class participation. You will have to answer a lot of questions in front of the class but Professor Morales doesn't make you feel bad if you don't know the right answer. Her lectures were engaging and went by really fast most of the time. She does give her instructions in spanish sometimes which can be confusing.

I have taken low-level Spanish before, so take this review with a grain of salt. Professor Morales cares about her students. If you participate and show genuine interest in learning the language, then your experience will be even better. Sometimes the locations of assignments in Canvas can be unclear, but if you ask she is more than happy to help.

It is much easier to learn Spanish if its taught by a native speaker, which is true with Prof. Morales but sometimes she speaks only in Spanish during lectures which is hard to understand. You WILL answer questions in front of the class and work with your table/partner.

As an instructor, Rosa was lively and always came ready to teach; however, I had a very personal emergency that required me to go home and miss a week of class. While I did not expect any sort of special accommodations, I did expect some degree of understanding. She completely lacked sympathy in the matter and was not understanding whatsoever.

Rosa is a lovely woman! She really cares for each of her students and is happy to help if you are struggling. The homework was a drag but it's all related to what you learn in class. Didn't like the 7 HW assignments sometimes assigned but she's funny and loves to encourage her students to practice!

Professor Morales is very kind and a good teacher. The class moves fast and has plenty of homework, plus a test every couple of weeks. But she prepares you well for tests and lessons are very clear. The textbook is EXPENSIVE but it's not the professor's fault.
Wonderful woman and great teacher. A little hard to catch up if you've never taken spanish but she is always willing to help. As long as you attend and try your best you'll do great

She does not care about her students. The class was easy to pass but she was an awful professor. She asked for feedback and then told the class she did not care what we said and did whatever she wanted. Take this class online she is horrible

She will call your disability fake. I mean of course why would a disability be real?? She gives you assignments in class which you will get done with before class is over, but will yell at you in front of the whole class for leaving when all work is done. She does not respect you as a student, a person, or really a human being for that matter.

I had to meet with Rose during my semester with her. During our meeting she told me my learning disability wasn't real and I was trying to take the easy way out. How can you teach this course and say this to someone with an IEP on record with Mizzou.

Very fake. Comes off as if she cares about the class and you as a future teacher, she doesn't. She's there to get a pay check. Made weekly reading logs and said they were optional, then made only me do them weekly for a grade (had an A all semester, so she was targeting) doesn't go by accommodations and when she's aware of them belittles you. Avoid
TAKE ONLINE. longest semester ever. Overall, rude. Doesn't listen to feedback even when she ask for it. So glad to be done with the class.
AVOID Rose at all cost. She's extremely passive aggressive, gives terrible feedback. Tells you to do one thing and ends up giving you even more work to do. TAKE ONLINE.
Take this class online. save yourself. never been more bored in my entire life

The class itself is really boring. I would take this online, it is a waste of time in person. Feedback is taken, but not acted upon. Textbook is not needed to purchase. Super easy A, but not worth it to take it in person.

I did not love Dr. Zia's teaching style due to the lack of clear example problems that often left me struggling on my homework for hours because I did not understand the problem. However, she is very generous with extra credit and participation grades and seems like she wants you to succeed. Overall wouldn't take her again but a nice person.
Judgmental and mean spirited. Violated ferpa. Asked students to come to office hours for no apparent reason.
I genuinely could not believe how every question I'd ask her she would take personally like I offended her honor. I'm appalled by her ego

What can be said about Ross that hasn't been said about Neuschwanstein Castle (which I spelled correctly on the first try, thanks to his teachings)? He stands above others as a monument to the German experience, full of wonder and only slightly self-obsessed. His love of beer is second only to his love of teaching.

Herr Ross is simply just one fine specimen of a human, as well as a great teacher. He not only gets a class of uninterested students (mostly freshman) to be interested in German, but he does it while being one of the most attractive instructors I have ever had. Do your eyes a favor and enroll in this grad students course before he's gone.

Prof. Carlo is my favorite professor. I took positive psychology/applied pos. psych. and her projects help make my life better rather than tougher. She practices what she preaches and is very accessible for help, problems, etc. The class is online, but I feel that she is just as clear and able to communicate as if in person. Highly recommend.

Class: Positive Psychology. First online graduate class I took and it was awesome. Really interesting content and she is great with feedback. Class and syllabus were very clear and the course page on blackboard was laid out great and very easy to navigate and understand. She was awesome and I hope to have another online class with her again.

Really super easy class.  If you take notes and skim over them and vocab from the book you'll most likely get a good grade.  Class isn't mandatory but some things only discussed in the  power points make the test.  I recommend her to get this credit out of the way.  Not bad at all and super sweet person.

Completely unorganized, I feel like I learned more in my intro to Clinical Psych class than I did my Clinical Psych CAPSTONE, which is completely ridiculous. Seemed totally unprepared to teach the class
I took her for my capstone. She did have super easy tests but her paper guidelines were difficult to follow, but luckily she was gentle on her grading

She appeared to never know exactly what she was talking about. Somewhat hard to understand, but a super easy test writer. She often gave out study guides - and I was in an "honors" course. Take her over a regular Psych 1000 class - she is super easy!

SO unknowledgeable. Was corrected number times in her power points and very often unorganized. I honestly can't trust anything I learned in that class because I felt she did not know what she was talking about. Super easy, though
He truly helps people learn and makes people good at writing

Professional journalist who expects first-year students to meet his too-high standards. Lots of homework and small assignments until the end of the semester, when he piles on 3 large assignments in just a couple of weeks. Feedback is unhelpful and irritating, grading is harsh, and unable to reach outside of class. He's the reason I quit journalism.

Teaching and grading was reflective of how editors expect their journalists to write in an actual newsroom. Always gave clear and detailed feedback and was very open to meeting to discuss grades and look over drafts. Lots of homework, but not too difficult, and large projects were broken up over many weeks with multiple editing check-ins.
chill guy easy class

Prof. Hernandez taught 1/3 of my online POL_SC1100 class. His lectures are decent, but often very long. The class is overall easy and boring due to the online lectures and ultimately useless discussion section. Weekly online quizzes that I recommend you do while watching the lecture. 4 online exams and an online final, all multiple choice.

He is kinda confusing and his tests are hard. He is a good teacher if you pay attention but people sit on their laptops. I think he thought we had all taken Calc 2 (didn't matter- cheated on everything). he's really nice personally & really funny. I just can't take this slander, the class is just set up badly! Please he's cool & cares!

Very smart, guy. Bed teacher. You'd have more fun dingdong ditching his house, than taking this class... so do yourself the favor and don't take it. Take a higher level econ class with Tabitha or someone else, this class isn't worth it.

Awful, awful, awful.  If I could've given 0s I would've.  Save yourself and do not take a course with this man.  He is very knowledgeable in economics, but couldn't teach if his entire life depended upon it.  I would rather slide down a razorblade into a pool of alcohol than take another one of Rudy's classes.

It was a rough course for me because out of the first 3 classes, he cancelled 2 and showed up 10 minutes late to the other. By the time 3 classes had gone by, it was too late to change courses. I did not like him as a speaker and felt his Powerpoint lectures were too long and uninteresting to understand. He was as unorganized as one could be.

GRAD STDUENTS: Not as bad as her undergrad. Her feedback sometimes reads like a dissertation. You'll still write & read a ton. Meet deadlines & be detailed. She says she wants short, precise work, but really, she wants everything covered or you'll lose points. Reach out if you need to. Her assignment instructions can be confusing so reread often.

This is the worst professor to ever step foot in a classroom. She was removed from the Capstone professors as she finds pleasure in failing students. She lives a sad life and feels the need to project her pain onto her class.

This professor genuinely thinks she is the smartest person in the world. Her teaching method is horrible and I have learned absolutely nothing. I highly recommend taking any professor but her. She should not be a teacher anywhere
Buy the book and save money, be smart. The class consists of PowerPoints summarizing the book.
It's okay
The coursework is completely grade based and the online material is full of errors.
Tough class, labs were ok but the quizzes were very difficult.
he is literally so sweet and genuinley cares about what he teaches. he always makes sure to ask if anyone has questions and wants us to suceed on the work. just show up and it makes the class easier!

A very respectable and knowledgeable professor. The lectures are easy to listen to and as long as you pay attention and take good notes it's a fairly easy class. He is clearly passionate about the content. I would love to take another class from him.
He is a really nice man and his class is pretty easy if you show up and pay attention. He is also available to give you the lecture in his office hours if you miss class for any reason.
He's very passionate about HDFS

It was easy to get a high grade with an extensive curve applied to each exam, extra credit opportunities for each lecture attended, and extra credit for giving a five minute presentation to the class, but I didn't learn anything. The lectures were messy and frustrating. She didn't give any indication that she knew the content she was presenting.

Tests are all multiple choice which may sound easy but they are not, every single answer sounds right. Quizzes in recitation (not open note). Calls on u randomly in lecture. Forced to do 1 group presentation, attendance is mandatory through iclicker.

Go to class to get extra credit; it is worth it. Dr. Angelovici was kind, but it wasn't easy to communicate with her. Tests could be difficult but manageable. The lectures were hard to follow, so re-visit the slides after class. If you study and go to class, you should perform well. I am not quite sure how much I actually learned, however.

She's kind and tries her best, but an awful professor. Speeds through lectures and refuses to post lecture slides. I genuinely don't think she knows a word that comes out of her mouth. There are extra credit opportunities and tests are easy but if you are looking to actually learn cell biology, DON'T TAKE.

She made it impossible to take any kind of notes in class, written or typed, and went way too fast. like not the amount of content was fine but you could not learn anything in class because there was no time to take the notes needed. Also made every person in class do an in-class presentation over the semester.

Most lecture slides came straight from the textbook, and often the test material did come from the slides. Some lectures were fast, though, that is the nature of upper-level biology courses. The class will not be difficult if you put in a reasonable amount of work, I did not do any crazy studying and was successful.

Probably the worst professor I've had. Lectures are rushed and don't make a lot of sense. Exams had lots of typos and sometimes there were questions on random things we didn't cover. Extremely disorganized. Assigned us 3 units to do on our own. Got a good grade because she adds lots of extra credit in the end, but I don't feel like I learned much.

This was probably one of the worst teachers I have ever had in my academic career. I would not at all recommend taking her class. She is horribly disorganized and really has no idea what she is talking about. Her slides are copied from the textbook and some of them just have word vomit all over them and she spends like two seconds on the slide.

Professor always cancelled class for various reasons and never showed up to lecture. Not responsive to emails. Exams are quite difficult but often curved 20%. Did not grade assignments until the end of the semester. Take another professor.

Definitely one of my favorite Professors I've had in college. I would definitely take more classes with Dr. Chacon. The material is hard but he teaches it well. He does go a bit fast in class. I think recording in-class lectures could help students look back. I get not wanting to post those sessions because students will skip class.
Professor Chacon is great. He is organized and regularly communicates with students through email and announcements. The exams are a little difficult, but he provides extra credit as well.

Professor is straight forward. Grading is straight forward. Easy class overall. Attend class for free test questions (typically gives you info that you specifically need to know and market updates). Extra Credit is a game changer. Tests are multiple choice. Calculations are simple. Only draw is his class is at 8am. Go to class, get easy A.
Great teacher... Made a lot of good analogies and broke things down in a way that was easy to understand... and cute :)
Great professor, learned a lot in his class, really seems to care about the students

I honestly can't say enough good things about Dr. Thomas. His class was inspirational and challenged me to think about journalism in new ways, but the biggest impression he left was due to his kindness and easygoing teaching style that made class fun to come to. One of my best class experiences at Mizzou.

Professor Thomas is great and has a cool accent. His lectures are interesting and he involves the class in the discussion so it's never just him reading off a PowerPoint while students take notes. His class is fairly simple to get an A in, there's always the same homework every week and nothing special is thrown at you. Lots of extra credit.

Thomas gives good lectures that are easy to follow. Every week there are three assignments due but they are easy, especially if you go to class. Your lowest exam and assignments are dropped. He wants students to learn and also succeed in the class.

This is a large lecture hall but he makes it a great class. Plus, his Welsh accent makes it easier to listen to lectures. There aren't a lot of assignments (short quiz, discussion board, and simple learning audit each week, which in total takes about an hour). The textbook is required but TBH you can get by without it, I never used it. 10/10!
There are lots of great professors in the j-school but Ryan deserves credit for being the nicest. He is funny, positive and laid back, and just comes across as a really good dude.

He is a really good lecturer. The smallest parts of info will show up on tests, take good notes. If you do, then the tests are okay. Make sure to take your time because they make up all of your grade. He drops the lowest score (out of 4 tests) which is nice, but don't rely on it. Get ready to spend time on the videos. You have to be self motivated!

He is a really good lecturer. The smallest parts of info will show up on tests, take good notes. If you do, then the tests are okay. Make sure to take your time because they make up all of your grade. He drops the lowest score (out of 4 tests) which is nice, but don't rely on it. Get ready to spend time on the videos. You must be self motivated!

Thomas is a great teacher. This class has a lot of content so if you want to pass you really need to get down just about everything he says. You really have to work for it in his class so pay good attention, he's a really smart guy and easy to work with but you have to be able to keep up with him to do well in his class.

I usually do well classes, and I did, but i STRUGGLED.  I'm in 2 4000 level chemistry classes, and this class alone took more work for the A-.  Most unfair grader I've seen- he  doesn't try o give you credit, he tries to take points off.  The rough draft paper highest grade was an 85%, even though he said the whole point is to improve.  Avoid him

I'm usually a straight A student and struggled insanely in this course. He was very biased in feedback and graded hard to the point it was nearly unattainable to earn an A. Every student that I have spoken to that has taken this course agrees with these statements. If you can avoid it, please do not take this course with him.

Ryan's a fun guy, but the class is graded on too few criteria for a philosophy class. If you mess one test up (easy to do) then your A is screwed and you won't get it back. The wording of multiple choice test questions is not clear-cut and leaves a lot of decision making on the table about which answer to choose even if you know the content.
The topics we discuss in class are really interesting and I liked the discussion aspect. You definitely have to go to class to get a good grade. He is annoying but he cares about his students.

Ryan is very passionate about what he teaches, takes student feedback, and is accessible for help. Even though this class is only graded on exams, participation, and quizzes, if you read, take notes, and go to class, it is not too difficult. He also offers extra credit. Not an easy A, but if you put the work in, it is easily attainable.
Attendance is mandatory, he does not post the notes, and you have to read philosophy papers.

Professor Kulesa is full of personality and passionate about what he teaches. I never once dreaded going to this class because it was always positive. We have open discussions about different topics and it allows us to be open minded. Grading is clear and he provides great feedback. He is understanding and allows makeups.

Great class. Ryan is an amazing lecturer, and always made going to class a great time. He connects with his students very well, and allows for a great time for discussion in class. The class can be hard, and it's not easy to just slack off. If you want to take this class be prepared read outside of class the articles, and pay attention in class!

Loved Ryan as a professor. He is very personable and always willing to help. However, like any Journalism class be prepared to work. There are a lot of critiques and projects within the class. Ryan did a great job of making it easier to get through and did well with explaining assignments and answering questions.

Amazing professor who embodies what it means to teach. He is educated, passionate, and all around a nice guy and it was a pleasure attending his lectures. If you have him for any class, consider yourself lucky.

Sabreena lectures very poorly and never posts class example solutions on Canvas, leaving you helpless on the very difficult homework. When asking TAs for assistance, they are often very disrespectful or will literally ignore your questions. Dr. Anowar can even seem rude at times after students ask questions about her horrible lectures

Professor Anowar does very well during lectures at fully explaining the material and answering questions very thoroughly and effectively. She did an excellent job at responding to my emails in a timely manner with a complete response to my query. Homework and exams are extremely difficult compared to the practice materials. Labs are very extensive.

Worst teacher I ever had. Ignored emails and rarely showed up to office hours. Had little sympathy for COVID-19 absences in lab and offered little recourse. Metric ton of lab work to do, tough exams, and homework that didn't make much sense. Professor sometimes got confused during lectures and literally couldn't explain it.

Took an excessive amount of time to grade assignments, even though there were very few. Any emails that I or my fellow students sent were ignored for several days, some even received no response. Professor and TAs were sometimes very rude when I asked for help. Were unwilling to help accommodate labs and assignments due to COVID-19.

Her style is different in a good way. I like the creative projects, even tho I cant draw. She does reminders on canvas but not in class, so you have to check canvas as sometimes they are due before class and midnight. She gives effort to make class fun, but sometimes your group has a bad attitude, which sucks. She is super nice/understanding.

The highlight of my day is going to class with Dr. Sabrina. You should read the announcements that she posts because sometimes she won't mention an assignment in class but it will be posted in the announcement and module.
Great at using Canvas!

One of my favorite professors! I hate science and kept putting off taking my science req until my junior year. If you hate science then take her planet earth class. I actually enjoyed the class. There are some rando assignments that require you to draw which I didn't love and more work than I thought, but I didn't feel it was a lot of busy work.

She is such a nice person, just really bad at using Canvas. Really read everything she posts with the date and time it's due, sometimes things are due in the middle of the day for no reason. The tests aren't bad and the field trips are fun, just be ready to send emails when things online don't work correctly.

Amazing professor. Very discussion based class, and she had us meet in a different place on/off campus every week so that was really nice. Very chill grader -- frequently gives late credit and extensions for assignments. Also is very open to feedback and takes course evals seriously. No complaints overall - if you can get her, then do it!

Just finished planet earth! Downside: you will leave class wishing all your other professors were like this, and they are not. 10/10 would recommend. Take her class. Your GPA, mental health, and serotonin will thank you. I also hate science but somehow loved this class.

Amazing professor, best I've had at Mizzou so far. Very helpful, and teaches well, she doesn't just read straight from the ppt. like some teachers, she actually talks through what she's teaching. The grading is very fair, 9/10 just do the work and you'll get an A. exams are pretty straight forward as well. I loved taking her class!

Went to her multiple times about how I could do better on her tests. All she will say is get better sleep. She will not listen to any feedback and she will not have anything graded until the week of finals.
Amazing!

Dr.Bush is great! She's very nice and understanding. But if youre someone that doesn't want to show up to class/participate you may not like her class. And I would consider myself one to not like showing up and being engaged, but I learned from her more than any other professor at Mizzou. I took 3 different courses with her, all were my favorites!

Uses a flipped classroom model with completion-based homework and mandatory "active-learning" sessions twice a week. This class takes a lot of your time, but Dr. Bush does respect students and will work with you. Hard to adjust to the different course structure, it's not for everyone (including me. You have to try to fail this class.

i love love love her - I've had her for 2 biology courses and she teaches super well along with making sure you understand the material. She also gives easy points - such as attendance points, group work, and small assignments in order to help your grade if tests go bad.
Poor course structure

I was nervous going into this class because science wasn't my thing in high school but Dr. Bush was great. Make sure you go to class and take advantage of stage 2 of the tests and you'll be fine. Just don't turn in your scantron late!

We had assigned seats in a lecture hall. Horrible with getting grades in on a timely manner even when asked in person or emailed. Tests every wednesday worth 35% of your grade and questions were never clear and you often left the class more confused than when you walked in. Consistent snarky comments and acted as though she was better than you.

Attendance is 10 points every class. As well as a test every wednesday. Weekly homework assignments and every once in a while a more time consuming homework project (4 total). She was nice and I did not have to try super hard just show up and you will be fine!

I absolutely loved her class.  Her lectures are always clear and interesting. She cares a lot about her students and was willing to meet with me outside of office hours for help. There's a short test every week, which worried me at first, but it was actually helpful for keeping me on top of everything.  Just make sure you go to class.

I actually hate the way this was taught. 90% of her material she teaches she does not give reasoning on why she is doing it, it's “just because you can”. The lectures aren't like the exam. The amount of quizzes is absurd. I have never had this hard of a time in one of her classes. So good luck!

THIS REVIEW IS FOR REINFORCED CONCRETE. Example problems are often incorrect and are very difficult to follow. Nothing is explained intuitively and you're expected to know everything based on slides with very minimal information. Slides just provide equations and don't provide explanations on when to use them. Final project took 30+ hours.

I've enjoyed my time in materials. Dr. Orton is a great lecturer with very clear expectations. Grading is very fair and she is always open to explain her reasoning for taking off points where needed. I would highly recommend this class. There is a lot of material, but if you pay attention during class it should be an easy B if not better.

Dr. Orton was very knowledgable about the topics she was teaching and set up the class and the labs very organized. Although the class was difficult, she would do her best to provide chances to make up missed points.

Worst class I have ever taken. Every lecture is either a powerpoint or a guest speaker. She expects you to know material that she did not teach and expects homework to be submitted in specific formats but does not tell you until she counts points off while grading. Outside of class she will ignore you or be rude and cold. Do not take her classes.

Dr. Orton acts like she cares but in reality it seems like she doesn't. If you see her outside of class she acts like she doesn't know you. She is condescending towards student in class and will guilt you into asking questions. For a one credit hour class, she gives a lot of busy work and requires attendance, I would not recommend taking her class.

This was a new class, but I got a lot out of it for not being a degree requirement. There was a lot of work that was usually busywork, but the lectures were interesting because of guest speakers and simple design problems. She would always give feedback and communicate exactly what was expected. She was also quick to respond to questions.

CV 3600 was by far my favorite class taken at MIZ. Dr. Orton does a good job teaching and is one of the better professors I've had. It's the kind of class that if you work hard, you will be rewarded. Labs are every week (which is a grind) but really interesting compared to some of the other mundane labs at Mizzou. It's Excel heavy in lab analysis

Sarah Jacquet is a wonderful professor and a downright cool person. I am not a geology major whatsoever and she made learning so much fun. There is an iClicker quiz after each lecture so make sure you are paying attention, although it is hard not to because it is clear how passionate she is! I would 100% take a class from her again! 10/10

Professor Jacquet is an awesome professor, and this is coming from someone who hates geology. I am not a geology major, and took her class to get my final science credits to graduate. Class seemed very daunting at first but Dr. Parsons breaks everything down in a way that feels like taking middle school algebra. Useful class to take before the more rigorous econometrics coursework as it lays a solid foundation for the more in-depth stuff you'll do next.

i took intro to applied economic practice with her (econ 3271) and her syllabus and grading style was AMAZING. she respects her students time and treats us like adults.

Attendance = 10%
Homework (One Drop) = 48%
Case Study One = 8%
Case Study Two = 10%
Case Study Three = 10%
Case Study Four = 10%
Case Study Presentation = 4%
Late Work = 20% Off

Professor Parsons was really easygoing and helpful. The lectures were very clear and all the homework assignments were the same as the notes we took in class. The case studies she does seemed hard at first, but once broken down, were super easy. She also offers good feedback and is a super nice grader.

Covers using Stata and econometrics in a very gentle and easy to digest way. Homework and projects are most of the grade and the expectations are clear. Great class to take before taking upper level econometrics

Sashi is not a bad professor. He is a nice guy, and is helpful during office hours. Honestly, I got A's on all of his tests, because he is very clear on what kind of problems are going to be on the exams. All of the people on here who said his class was hard were probably engineers who don't understand that you have to study for physics classes.

One of the worst teachers ever can't believe he is still allowed to teach. Can't understand him at all, he can't even do consumer math. Worst class ever taken at mizzou thanks to him. Head of physics department Peter Pfiefer doesn't care about the physics department hence why this guy gets to teach still

For all of you who have a problem with his accent; grow up. Most of you were talking during that class anyway. It took listening and hard work.The class was great, and grading fair. Teacher super helpful, and very accomodating.

If you have Sashi for any physics class, get out if you can.  He is extremely difficult to understand, and complains if a test average is over a 65. I actually liked physics before this class, but unless you are an electrical engineering major, you will not fully understand the 2 1/2 months spent on electricity in this class.  Good luck.

After taking Sashi Satpathy, I can honestly say that I wasted my time in this course. Honestly, this is all i remember..."You will be doomed to death because somebody will eat you up, OK?!" And that's probably quoted more clearly than actually said. Please stay away from Sashi if you are interested in Physics and want to actually learn something...

If I found out today that I had Sashi Satpathy again next semester, I would have a psychological breakdown. His english is atrocious, and his ideology on test grades is ridiculous. Do anything you can to avoid taking University Physics 2. I got next to nothing out of this class, and the course material is now completely unappealing to me.
No Comments

She is a very caring professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed. She puts real effort into her lectures, but her teaching style doesn't always make the material easy to understand. The workload is light with only 3–4 easy homework assignments, and the midterm and final are manageable since they are similar past exams.

Worst lectures of all time. Luckily, practice exams match exams nearly perfectly so it's easy to get a good grade in the class. The two or three homework assignments she gives are easy and a decent grade booster. Labs are easy. Not good at teaching whatsoever but clearly cares a lot and class was easy to do well in, so I can't give lower than a 3.

Dr. Sazia Eliza is a very knowledgeable and caring professor, but her teaching method isn't effective enough to convey the material. You will have to do more reading and figuring stuff out on your own in order to get a good grade. Grades on very few topics discussed in class.

I admit that she is very smart and a nice lady, but she has absolutely no idea how to teach a class. Lectures are very concept heavy with little chance to apply what you learn with examples, so nothing really sticks. Class organization does not reflect a college level class. She is consistently late and unprepared, and cancels classes very often.

She's a sweet lady but is extremely disorganized.  She cancels a class almost every week (we meet MWF) or sometimes turns it into a Zoom lecture. She would talk about concepts the whole lecture but not give us an opportunity to apply them, so by the time we got homework we had no idea what to do. Everyone in my class was confused and frustrated

She's nice and appreciates feedback. Class was only 50 minutes long, so exams are going to be 3 questions basically every time. At this level of engineering, most circuit problems take 25 - 45 minutes each, so yeah... if u mess up once during an exam you will be hit hard.  She also is quite a tough grader which makes it even worse.

She was constantly late to class, usually around 7 minutes or so. Her lectures felt very unorganized, and if you asked a question that she did not have written on her lecture notes she would have no idea how to answer it. She changed our final exam question several times during.
TLDR: Class organization and professor preparedness sucks. Good luck.

Easily the worst professor that I have ever had. Nothing is ever graded so it is impossible to know where you stand in the class. Exams are unnecessary difficult and unorganized, usually consisting of 1 or 2 questions. One time, she even changed the one and only exam question 30 minutes into an exam 4 separate times. Usually, about 10 minutes late.

Scott Cairns, hands down, has been my favorite professor at Mizzou so far. He didn't give any tests in my class but we did do a lot of interesting reading and writing. His feedback is golden and he tells great stories. Participate and think critically in his class and you'll get an A, for sure.

I was told that I would be enrolled in a class with Darwin's "The Origin of Species" as required reading, however I was instead enrolled in Dr. Cairns's class with "Genesis" as required reading. Despite that, Dr. Cairns is by far the best professor that I have had in my six years at Mizzou. I got the grade that I deserved.

Tell him a joke and he'll love you. Easy class and he's interesting, even if he does repeat himself a lot. Grade is heavy on participation but the class is small so it wasn't too bad. Would take again.

Professor Cairns is a charming man. He is passionate about poetry and shows that continuously throughout his class. If you come to class, do your assignments, and participate every once in awhile, you will do well. He genuinely wants you to do well and is always willing to work with you to improve your grade.
Favorite prof ever.  This guy is serious business.

Dr. Cairns is a very funny guy. His class is enjoyable and not difficult. I liked listening to him talk about generally nothing (and doing some name dropping), but when he got down to talking about poetry he had some interesting views. I wasn't always in agreement but they were good to think about. He changed the way I write to a great degree.
course wasn't difficult; minimal work; and he made class interesting and used his time well
Good: Great: Grand.  How's that for poetry.  Not as much prose as I would have liked, but an excellent, inspired teacher.

Dr. Anderson is a passionate and intelligent scholar, but he is a dry lecturer. The discussion is the only engaging part of the class. Always remember to be respectful to our educators, regardless of your feelings about them!

I took History of American Religion with him and the class was very interesting. I learned a lot and even though his lectures are long, he is very engaging and if you read the books and study you can easily get an A in this class. He is also a very nice guy and always has good energy.

He talks really fast in the lectures, but the quizzes are not too hard in the class. If you keep up with the notes and the reading you will do good, but you will spend so many hours of your week reading and studying. Out of all my classes I spend the most amount of time on this one and I am a STEM major...

So basically lectures are optional, but discussion is mandatory. You are given a weekly quiz over the lecture material and over the material that you were supposed to read for the week. If you are in the honors section, you have to do a weekly newspaper project (which is super easy). If you go to lecture and do the reading then you should be fine.

Dr. Peck is actually the best! He is so incredibly kind and supportive of his students, and even though he is incredibly smart he does a good job of teaching undergrads. Very lecture heavy and has pop quizzes, but the material is not too tough if you keep up. Wish I could take him for every biochem class!

Dr. Peck is one of the kindest professors you will meet. There are weekly pop quizzes, but they are incredibly easy. There are ~15 homework assignments for the whole semester and three exams. The exams are easy; however, he does grade them tough. He cares about his students inside and outside of class and is extremely understanding/accommodating!

I took Dr.Peck for 2480 and beware of pop quizzes!!!! He will hint at when they are but you have little idea when they will be. Because of this he expects you to be in class every day. The class is so lecture heavy. All written exams. He does care about his students and is really approachable outside of the lecture.

Scott was my absolute favorite editor at the Missourian. He was really easy to work with and had reasonable expectations given that this class was a first time reporting class for many students in it. He was very fair and if you put in the work, he could tell. Honestly, probably my favorite teacher I have had in the Journalism School so far.

Scott is the best. His lectures are valuable, he will not waste your time. He will absolutely make you a better writer, but you have to be willing to work for it and take risks. His dad jokes make him a real gem. He struggles with Canvas, but is understanding and will re-work assignments to ensure fairness. Take Scott! You won't regret the decision

Scott is the best J2100 Lab Steacher!!! He is so knowledgable and he wants you to succeed. He will stray from the syllabus a bit, making the schedule work the best for the class. He is so flexible and reliable - will reply to emails within minutes. He never speaks in a condescending way and doesn't assign crazy amounts of work!

If you have the chance to take a class with Scotty Swaff, DOOO IT! He's the actual best – he is really lenient and really helpful, you actually feel like you are learning and he makes class interesting. Also I'm pretty sure he knows every single person in Columbia, which is really helpful in terms of finding people to interview.

He's a tough grader but that's because he knows what he's talking about. He has tons of real-world experience and really wants you to succeed. By far the best j-school professor I've interacted with so far.

Scott is the best journalism professor you could ask for at the J2100 level. He's got a world of experience, though that means he has extremely high standards for your work. This class will be extremely tough, but if you love journalism and writing, you'll enjoy every minute of it.
He is the best editor at the Missourian. If you want to remain sane and have the ONLY nice editor get him! Just do your best reporting and he'll give you a good grade.

Amazing editor. Extremely helpful and nice. Best editor at the Missourian-- most sane too. Work hard enough for him and he will write recommendations for you and be very helpful to you for the rest of your time at the J-school!

Probably one of the rudest professors I've had. Seems to have a pretty short temper and consistently degrades students for asking improper or stupid questions. He definitely understands the content well and his lectures can be quite helpful, but expects more from his students than what he provides.

Kovaleski's teaching style is that of your typical cocky high school teacher. He gives 3 homework assignments per week which is absurdly unhelpful and unrealistic. Is it just that the content hard? Partially. What doesn't help is him bragging about how difficult his exams are. Save your sanity take this class from another professor...

Hard professor with a cocky attitude. If you don't know the know the subject and are taking it new, you'll most likely fail. Expects way more from you than what he teaches

Excellent teaching style. He makes you work for what you should, and gives you what you need. The class (Electromagnetic Fields) is difficult, but that's because the material is difficult. He doesn't water it down to make it manageable, but he will work with you until you understand it. You will learn a lot if you listen and do the work.

Hand down one of the best teaching styles out there. He gives you plenty of examples to work from and he is great at keeping your attention during lectures. I wish other teachers would take notes on his teaching style. Thank you for a fun class Scott!
Tough class, but it's because the material is difficult. He is a good teacher and explains the concepts very well
Mr. Branton was dope. I had him for both COM 1200 and 3460. He clearly cares about his students, gave us time in class to work on projects and was flexible with deadlines. Highly recommend.

If you take this class, you can expect the most bizarrely inconsistent due dates in college. One week, you will have something due Saturday. The following week, you will have something due Wednesday. The best part is, for all his major assignments and projects, the guidelines are as vague as humanly
possible. Expect late replies to emails, as well.

One giant group project with unclear guidelines. He doesnt grade anything in a timely way- your grade will be a complete surprise after finals week. No communication he misses classes and assignments and is difficult to reach

The course material was great however, Scott's teaching style was not. Dr. LaCombe is the best professor that I have personally, ever taken! Love his style of lecture and general teaching style.

Great professor, would take again. Expectations were outlined clearly and we were reminded consistently of upcoming deadlines. Additionally lectures were clear and provided everything needed for the exams.

Professor LaCombe did an incredible job considering this was his first semester teaching at Mizzou. His lectures were interesting and always what was exactly on the tests. However, he didn't put much in the gradebook.

He talks really fast in the lectures, but the quizzes are not too hard in the class. I thought the content in 2160 was kinda boring, but not rlly his fault. Dr. Scott is a great prof, very accessible outside of class. Participation def matters. You really just go over HW in class, have a couple essays, and like 2 group projects.
Taylor is fantastic! Dude is super caring, organized and clear. There is a reason that he's the coordinator over some of the other professors. You genuinely could not ask for more!

Very very kind professor-I would absolutely recommend him for any French class. Prof Taylor fostered excellent and insightful discussion while teaching course content. Doesn't really get better than him.

really couldnt ask for a better french teacher. really expressive which helps with comprehension, and he understands that all students are at a different level. gives feedback on ALL writing assignments which is hard work with a lot of students. easy grader, awesome teacher, and super funny. cares about his students and makes class fun.

What a fun and enlightening class! Se Yong was great at picking topics that genuinely changed my perspective on issues and fostering discussion during class. This was the first philosophy course I took at Mizzou, so the essays really helped me refine my writing for future classes. Take this course, whether you're majoring in philosophy or not!

He is very fun, absolutely excellent at fostering conversation and debate while still remaining neutral. While the readings can be difficult at times, they are great at making you think critically about the issues covered.

Se Yong is the salt of the earth, one of the kindest people I've ever met for sure. He's a very good thinker and leads great, thought provoking conversations. The grading rubric on the exams is a bit ambiguous, but as long as you keep up with the readings and the in-class discussions you should do just fine. Definitely take his class if you can

I took Professor Bae's class on Contemporary Moral Issues and I truly enjoyed his teaching style. The class is led mainly by student led discussion with Bae jumping in occasionally to offer counter arguments or pose the student to think deeper about their beliefs. The class is paper heavy. Expects a lot for a freshman class. Doesnt really teach, more just criticizes. You need to teach yourself in this class. Talks down to you a lot if you reach out. Very poor communicator.

There were no quizzes or exams. Just writing papers. I dont know how it wasnt an English intensive course. The professor was very nice and open to all questions. Be sure to give a good effort while writing the papers!

Professor Gurd is very passionate about his field, and that is clear in his lectures. He seems to bounce well off of student participation in his lectures and he likes people to be engaged. Not your man. He seems fun in class and you can talk to him outside of class, but he doesn't comprehend that this class is pointless. If you misspell a greek/roman name? Incorrect answer. Can you hardly see the painting you have to recognize a character in? Incorrect answer. The tests aren't based on understanding, they are based on small details.

Lectures were very bland and not very interesting (Unless you love pre-civil war history).  The exams included 4 short essay responses and 1 long essay response.  Not the hardest exams if you study the key terms, but in a 50 minute class period, I often felt extremely rushed/stressed. I never got the best chance to really display my knowledge.

Franzel somehow made medieval German literature manageable and engaging. There were a few hiccups with his class management, but I do not regret taking the course in the slightest. He also makes a mean spicy eggplant dish. I'm still waiting on the recipe though. Overall, a great professor!

He was a terrible teacher and didn't know what he was talking about in class. People would ask him questions and he would have no idea about a simple question. He would just read off of a script each lecture and the PowerPoint he would put up wouldn't even match the material you were learning. Overall its the worst class and professor ever.

Franzel is a great professor and I've enjoyed both classes I've had with him. He's helped me a lot when I couldn't get classes to fit in my schedule and even let me in on some grad student classes to make things work. His medieval German lit class was one of my favorite and something I hope MU will offer to undergrads. The material is a great read.

A great facilitator of discussion. Had him for both a large lecture and a small seminar. He does his best when there are fewer student. A very nice person, patient, and knows what he is talking about.

Dr. Franzel is a wonderful teacher, and this class was a real pleasure. There is a lot of reading, but if you do what you're assigned and come to class prepared, you shouldn't have any problems. Professor Franzel is a personable guy with a broad worldview. He leads an open discussion for the class, but sees himself as a facilitator more than the leader. He is a nice, likable guy that isn't intimidating. As for his teaching, he really valued critical thinking and looking at the big picture as opposed to the specificities of texts.

Prof. Franzel was a great conversationalist and really valued our feedback and participation. There was a relaxed atmosphere during our discussions and his overall personality was charming. The only downside was being sort of in the dark on our grade throughout the semester...
How is he a professor?! He came into class with the materials from weeks earlier because he couldn't keep track! I don't need to expand. He's honestly just bad.

Assigns a LOT of readings per week, if it wasn't for ChatGPT to summarize all of them.. idk what I'd do. 3 papers that weren't terrible, although had to write first draft in person on paper.. When you write out all the questions you need to know the answers to for an exam, before you've answered any of them, it's a 12pt, single spaced, 5 page document. They were online this semester so it worked out fine, but he's considering putting them back in person and has mentioned that several times.

Tests are 90% of your grade, with quizzes being 10% the quizzes are easy as long as you take notes and do the readings. I would recommend printing out the notes before going to lecture, that way you just need to write down what he says. 
Rough class, not what I was expecting, but not awful.

Great teacher while the class is lecture heavy there's no other way to teach it and he does a good job of making sure to engage students. There are pop quizzes but they're never really a surprise he always gave the warning to make sure that you do the reading when he assigns them. Overall a good class and professor.

I really loved this class. Lectures were engaging and coming to class was very important (especially because of pop quizzes). Not a lot of points, but the actual exams (3 total) were all online and open note. Also provides detailed plans concerning exactly what is covered in each lecture, which is available to students at the beginning of semester.

There is a lot of information you have to know. Not a lot of points so make sure you show up to class and take the pop quizzes. He does curve test but it is a linear curve. There is a lot of information on slides and he kinda goes fast so I suggest typing out the slides before class and just fill in the blanks in class or print off the slides
Hard content, graded off of quizzes and tests. Not very accessible outside of class. LOTS of pop quizzes.

Mr. Douglas was very funny and made sure the class was understanding the material. We had short quizzes every week, but we were allowed to work with other students. Attendance was not required but in order to understand the material, you better go to class. Sometimes we got extra credit point for attending lectures.

I really enjoyed this class. I didn't want to go straight into Calc 1 for my first semester so I took MATH 1160 for precalc review and I'm glad I did. 

Lectures were 3 times a week, discussions were 2 times a week. We had a short quiz (5 questions max) almost every week. Homeworks were from the online book. No surprises on the exams!

Sean let us call him by his first name which I love. Hes pretty young and treats all the students like friends as much as anything. He explains things well for students skilled in math and those who struggle. The course is based on online homework, and in person quizzes and tests. If youre good at math its low effort and easy.

Absolutely love Dr.Greer, he was always engaging and made lab fun. He didn't force us to stay the whole time. as soon as we finished our lab exercise and minute clinic, we were free to leave. we mostly left at 6-6:15pm for a 5-7 class. GO TO OFFICE HOURS he'll give you points back if you can explain and give the correct answer. A great guy!

I had Dr. Greer for anatomy lab. Lots of points available, pre and post lab quizzes and then 3 exams. Exams can be tough so make sure you study and study a lot. The exams are mostly identifying things on models or pictures. Go to lab or else you'll be confused, it's just helpful when putting the terms into perspective. Don't be scared, it's doable.
Sending love from Lugoslavia! 10/10 Professor.
Interesting topics but the grading scale doesn't make sense. Very independent course.
Professor Griffith will attack you for your cereal choices, but all in good fun. Gave excellent feedback and asked stimulation questions. Loved it, 10/10.

Prof Griffith is a great professor. Very interesting and engaging lectures that leave you thinking. Even though I didn't even read the readings I was able to submit my submissions and get 100% on all of them. Somewhat tough grader for papers but not tooooo bad. Great class, I learned a lot. Thank you Professor Griffith!

Prof Griffith was by far the best professor I've ever had. I took it first semester & was worried about having to attend every class 3 times a week, but not only was the class material interesting, but he is the funniest man alive. Content-wise, you do have to read the book & take notes, write essays, & participate in class. But definitely take it.

Selwyn is a really cool prof. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. His class is always interesting and I enjoy going. He is very funny and helps you actually understand the course material. I rated him 4/5 because his quizzes are kind of hard. I would recommend his class to anyone!

Sen Xu is a down-to-earth professor. The homework is only worth extra credit points for the exams. The exams are worth 50% of your grade, with the rest being canvas quizzes (verbatim exam questions), attendance, and discussion attendance. The lectures can be boring, and anyone complaining didn't take advantage of the opportunities he gave.

Yes, the class is difficult, but the homework is not mandatory & counts as 5 exam bonus points per exam. Exams are worth 50% of your grade, with the rest being online quizzes(literally test questions), discussion attendance, and lecture attendance. There is so much extra credit, & anyone complaining did not take advantage of ANYTHING offered.

Xu is better than David from what I hear but I simply cannot pay attention in his boring, rambling lectures. Exams are not bad but no dropped exam and no dropped attendance makes it tough for a lot of people. Make sure you make your own grade calculator because canvas will not display the correct grade. Overall it was meh.

Class isn't bad, besides the fact that you never know what your actual grade is. Chapter homework is put into the gradebook even though they only count as bonus points for the exam, which inflates your grade in Canvas. He also doesn't give any drops for attendance.

Dr. Xu clearly does not take his class very seriously. He spent the first day of class talking about prostitutes in the red light district. He grades completely inconsistently and makes you turn in everything handwritten, even though he frequently loses track of your assignments. He provides no feedback on your assignments. You will get screwed.

I had Sen for genetics and it was almost the same as evolution, except no exams. Evolution is very reading heavy, with 9-15 page papers you needed to read every week for discussions on thursdays. Quizzes are not difficult, and there are no exams. Overall an easier course out of the evolution classes, and I would take this again.

She doesn't teach anything, she just rambles on over off topic things and then expects everyone to know what is happening. There are so many pop quizzes over things that she either hasn't taught or barely taught. Class averages for exams were in the 60s. Does not answer any questions students ask in class and said she was done answering questions.

Attendance is "mandatory" but doesn't get taken daily, just at random times. Dr.Cho is very nice though, and while I enjoy her classes, I don't feel like I learn very much from the lectures. Most of the learning through this class feels like it comes from the lab component, in which you rotate through different areas of a hotel once a week.

Kopeikin is okay, the class is not. The second half of the class is quite difficult. The HW and quizzes are pretty difficult, and unnecessarily long, and very confusing. Lectures barely covered the material. The only good thing is that there is lots of opportunity for extra credit. I would strongly recommend not taking this class.
Good Professor, the quizzes can be difficult. Overall great class and the textbook and homework are online.

Sergei is very rigorous with all the math in his lectures, as a physicist should be, which can be interpreted as either a good or bad thing. Personally, I think it made me learn more than normal classes. I know a lot of people are scared of his classes due to this rigor but it is offset by charming and hilarious stories and tangents. I recommend.
Homework takes big percentage of your score.

Excellent prof! Clearly cares about students - he wants them to learn as much as possible and do well. Happy to answer questions and chat about most anything. Grades every line of homework as if he is reviewing it for publication (very helpful). Class content was hard as nails, but that's QM. Overall, wonderful experience.

He is very enthusiastic about what he teaches, which makes for an excellent class. His lectures are very in depth and helpful, but he also has hundreds of great random stories which makes his class even more fun. The more effort you put into your homework the more effort he will put into giving you very helpful specific feedback on the assignment.

Sergei is an impressive scientist. His Russian background makes for some hilarious in-class stories. However, beware of the class:He teaches a Mathematical Methods class which is extremely difficult and covers nearly everything in math. Contrast with his Quantum class, which asks just for summaries of important topics in exams despite tricky hmwrk.

He is very passionate about his studies and what he shares in class! He rambles a lot, but he always catches up to where he needs to be. Loved his class this semester and thought it was easy! Very light work, weekly quizzes and 2 essays, and 2 exams.
Super passionate (rambling at times, but interesting nonetheless), weekly quizzes, and lots of note-taking, would absolutely take another course of his.

My class was actually AMS2100, wasn't listed. His lectures are great, he's clearly very passionate and knowledgeable about the material and it shows. Overall he makes himself fairly open. Provides recordings of each lecture in full detail. The only complaint is that it takes a long time for him to respond to emails

Waits until the last min to grade essays, and then grades them harshly. The finals are super easy, but it's only two essays and two finals, so your grade rests heavily on his lazy essay grading.
Not too hard of class. Sometimes the lectures would go over 50 minutes which got annoying at times. The essays are graded kind of tough. If you do the readings and lecture you should be fine.

This class was difficult for me due to the whole Latin thing, but the professor was very accessible and eager to help. You will use the textbook everyday, and there will be homework every single day. Most of the grade will come from quizzes that happen every two days or so, and you have to do well on tests. There is a small amount of extra credit.
Go to class, his tests are based off what he talks about in class not what is on the powerpoint
10/10 professor. Nicest professor ive ever had.
Great professor. She gives clear guidelines on all assignments.

An incredibly kind professor. Even when I would mess up in 1 of the 3 oral exams (the exams were very easy and only lasted 10 minutes), she would help guide me and give me a good grade. It is super easy as long as you learn the basics on the "quizzes," you'll do well in the class overall.

Dr. Lee was an amazing professor. Her lectures were short but comprehensive. This was nice because I was able to spend more time coding then taking notes. The quizzes were extremely helpful for assessing how I was doing, and had infinite attempts (this is essential for learning to code). The oral exams were 15 mins long, and conducted well.

Dr. Lee teaches a the senior statistics capstone and she did a great job. This class is writing intensive, but honestly, if yo do the work it's graded easily. Attendance is worth 20% of your grade, so it is important to show up to class. There is also a semester long group project, but it isn't anything too extensive, and nothing to stress over.
Not clear at explaining most things. almost easier to work through lectures on your own. Quiz for every lecture and homework once per week. Hard to actually learn because there's so much to do.
She is really sweet and helpful!

She is very difficult to understand. She is a nice enough lady, but does not really know how to teach. This class should have (and could have) been easy, but she had only one way of explaining things, and that one way usually made little sense.

Unlike most people, I didn't mind Shane that much. His lectures were pretty boring and I played games all throughout class, but I finished with like a 96. The quizzes aren't hard if you skim the readings and have them with you. The exams aren't bad and Shane literally provides a Google Doc for the class to create a group study guide.

The course load for J1100 is already confusing as it is, but with this professor you won't know even what you're supposed to be learning. Reading the books won't save you at all. This professor ignored when everyone was failing and panicking. The quizzes are timed and extremely difficult as the books barely mention what is on the quiz.

The content in this class is already difficult in itself, but when you mix this instructor with the course, it's hard to earn a good grade. I read and studied a lot for this class and still only got an A- because the quizzes and tests are extremely unreasonable. Weekly quizzes that are nearly impossible to get good scores on. Be prepared to read for hours a week. He goes VERY FAST during lectures.

- was impossible to reach throughout the semester

- there is so much out of class work

I really like shannon as a person but the rubrics need to be changed. also, this will be different for everyone but my TA graded sooo harsh and sometimes it felt like there was no way to correctly do the assignment. we were always given very vague instructions and little directions in class, so we were left to do assignments completely on our own.
Condescending and is not open to feedback whatever she says goes. By any means avoid Shannon.

Shannon really cares about her students, lectures are engaging and well planned. Had us often collaborating with others during class, students get a voice on class content. I'm a senior at Mizzou, this class was the worst experience of my college career. Srinivas is easily my favorite teacher. His content is engaging and he has a way of teaching that makes me actually want to learn and pay attention during class in general. It was one of the best courses I took at Mizzou. I feel well prepared for the job market in analytics.

Eng Quality Control was a university level class that prepares you for your IE career. Prof. Srinivas has an amazing way to deliver his lectures. Be ready for a Python analytics group project!

Systems Simulation was an interesting class that helped teach the Simio program. However, lectures were focused on data and stats, so Simio was only learned in lab. Group project is tough, need a large amount of data for it. No rubric for final report or presentation. Class structure is great. Sharan can be tough at times though so work hard.

A very fair and organized class. If I remember correctly, there are 4 exams, but only your highest 3 count towards your grade. I completely bombed my first exam (D). TAs are readily available outside of lecture and are more than willing to help your understanding. Ended up with an A+. Just take the material seriously, and you'll be fine.

Sharon Ryan was a fantastic economics professor who worked super hard to ensure you actually learned the economics material. Tough but fair. Great teacher. Truly enjoyed the class, her lectures and the challenge of the course. I also majored in economics.
Really helped me understand economics. Best professor yet!
SO, amazing I have no words.
N/A

if you are enrolled in her class DROP IT NOW!!!!! she is the worst teacher i've ever had and I dreaded going to her class everyday. the devil in disguise no joke... save yourself now and drop

Pretty much you only have to do a certain number of homework assignments for a grade. I recommend you do them early, theyre easy. If you turn in extra ones shell grade them and give feedback which is good for tests. The tests are the homework assignments with different numbers.

Frau Gabi (Shelby LaFollette) genuinely cares about the content she is teaching, but more importantly, she has the utmost respect and devotion to the students that enter her classroom. this class was way too difficult for a gen ed requirement. One of my favorite professors so far at Mizzou. The class is not too hard but also pushes you to really learn the content. She has a great attitude and is very likable.

Sherry is easily the best professor I have had at Mizzou so far. Shi - Jie is undoubtedly the best lecturer I have ever had. Thermodynamics is not a trivial subject, however there was never a point where I was not following what he was doing on the board. I have had this professor for Introduction to Quantum Mechanics and Thermodynamics. I have had this professor for thermodynamics as well (4120) and he acts same in both. Best professor I've ever had.
