Consistent grader with good feedback.

Lectures are well-paced. Sometimes tests on things that he said in class that aren't in the textbook, but you could probably reason to them if you have time. Exams aren't toughly graded, but they will take all the time you have in class - make sure you know content! Homework isn't long but is /difficult/. Professor is very available outside class.
Exam questions were all related to the material discussed. Still difficult, but more than willing to help and go the extra distance if you put in the effort.

Shi Jie is great. I took Thermodynamics last semester and after taking one look at the book, thought I was going to fail. I ended up with an A. If you pay attention and study hard, then you will pass. He was always willing to clarify, and had some quite elegant explanations for some concepts.

He is the most coherent teacher in the physics department.  His classes my run a little long on occasion, but its worth not feeling completely lost at the end of class. Best physics teach I have ever had.

Professor Sharma is a stickler for rigor, so it was a bit intimidating to ask questions, but he always wanted to make sure that each concept was explained precisely. He provided a great deal of help in preparing for each exam and included practice problems. Definitely a great professor for math majors.

Teaching style is very slideshow heavy and basically copy and pastes notes from the book. Must do your own studying when you are outside of class. Attendance was necessary for his Calculus 2 class so do show up. Tests make up an insane portion of your grade so make sure to stay on top of your homework as it will make up a large portion of your test

It's calc 2, its gonna be rough. The exams were based of the hw, in class problems, and book review. Put in a lot of work and you'll pass. His "motivation" and "intuition" made no sense to me and was time wasted that could be used to do practice problems. Exams make up a majority of youre grade so you can only really mess up terribly on one exam.

Dr. Shukla understood the limitations of a 1 hour per week drug discovery and design discussion course for underclassmen. However, he challenged us and facilitated critical thinking while exposing us to the key concepts of pharmacology. Each student researched a drug and presented on it, then the class discussed the drug. This was a nice format.

Taking this class feels like you're being ragebaited on a daily basis. Exams have nothing to do with lectures and are only based on the homework. He'll make one statement in lecture on the material that actually shows up in the homework. Canvas assignments are posted in the most inconvenient possible way.

TA office hours were very helpful to understand the homework! And tests were entirely based on the homework! The lectures were okay, but definitely got more rushed towards the end of the semester. I had not taken dif eq or bme 2080 as pre reqs and this was not an issue, I just wish I had a better understanding of enthalpy.

He's awful at lecturing and none of the content relates to the homework. I bought the digital textbook and he never linked it in Canvas even after several emails. The TA hardly knew what to do with the HW solutions. The content is so specific that no YouTube videos can help you. I've considered switching to ME because of this prof.

Horrible at lecturing. Hard to know how to apply lecture material to the actual homework. But if you figure out the homework or find the answers somewhere, just use those answers to study for the exams and you'll be good.

Terrible at lecturing. Stopped going to lecture after a week or two bc it had nothing to do with the hw that the exams are based off of. Go to TA office hours to learn how to do the hw. Study just the hw and nothing else for the exams. Hard to contact him via email. Terrible class that I learned nothing in, but at least it's not terribly difficult.

Dr. Sengupta is a really nice guy, he just isn't the best at clearly communicating the course material. He's super smart, he just doesn't have a very concise course plan/layout. The tests are basically straight from the homework and he posts homework keys. Lets you use a cheat sheet on tests. You won't come out of the class having learned much.

I dont understand the other comments. This is literally one of the easiest classes you will have as a BE student. I went to 2 lectures and got like a 99% in the class. Yea he's not the greatest lecturer but he's a REALLY nice guy and he'll help you out. Seriously if this class is too difficult (regardless of the teacher), consider switching majors.

Literally awful teacher. Does not teach jack and expects you to do impossible homework problems when he does nothing related to them in class or even close. I'd say don't take him but, you have to. SUCKS

If you are going to take this professor, take him for his very basic exams. If you take good notes you will be fine. He does not record lectures so you will need to go to every class to keep up.

Before you take this class, know that Professor Wang speaks the most broken english I have seen so far at this school. I took diff eq online and had to keep the lectures muted for the most part because I couldn't understand a single word he was saying. Tests were easy though.

Crazy easy professor yet doesnt speak English very well. Dont be discouraged by lack of English though. I didnt attend a single lecture studied about half as much as calc 1 or 2 and did wayyyy better. All quiz, test and final questions are pulled from practice problems you are given. Learn how to do those and you will do great.

He is by far one of the easiest teachers I have had at Mizzou. Tests are exactly like homework and example problems; only points I missed were because of basic calculation errors. Final exam is a little difficult, which means difficult question out of 10. Get this guy, you will not be disappointed

Awesome teacher. Very organized and does not waste time at all.  Tests are exactly like the notes he gives.  I was a little worried about the accent at first but after the first day, I could understand everything I said.  Don't get into a new section based on his name.

Very straightforward. No homework -- just quizzes (all scheduled) and exams. Quizzes are very easy. Exams are very fair and short. Yes, he has an accent, but his notes are clear. Pretty straightforward about everything, not the most inspiring prof ever, but he does his job, is very fair, and made it all really easy on us.

He has a very strong accent. And I couldn't understand him at all. His notes are straight out of the book. The examples he uses in class normally match test questions. But the whole grade in this class is made up of 4 quizzes (barely worth anything) 2 tests, and a final worth 40% of your grade. Its all about proofs.

Oh Shuguang, you make me smile. He presents the most organized notes I have ever experienced, if you can decipher his thick Chinese accent (I could). For added interest, spell out the words he mispronounces phonetically (cauw-coo-lauhhrs = calculus) in the margins of your notes. Beware of tricky problems, not a lot of chances for points, got an A!

His lectures were really good at thoroughly explaining every topic (even things that for most people did not need to be thoroughly explained). Lectures were all recorded and posted online so if you missed a class/don't feel like going no trouble there. Very accurate practice exams so you always felt prepared for the real ones. Really great teacher!

When it comes to Prof Takeda's teaching, he's kinda all over the place with how he teaches concepts, his accent that sometimes makes it hard to understand what he's saying, and occasional in his lectures. Despite that, he cares about his students and it's shown by his nice way of grading, posting of lectures online, etc.

Honestly, the practice quizzes and exams in this class were so great for preparing for test day! I never got less than an A on an exam, and that was without going to too many lectures (they were optional/posted online). Prof Takeda was also super understanding and promptly replied to all my emails. Best math class I've had so far at Mizzou.

Dr. Takeda is likely the best professor I'll ever have. He managed to explain Calc III in the best possible way. He uploads his lectures to YouTube, making them easy to access and speed up/pause. He's also a very generous grader. There are three midterms and a final exam, along with occasional quizzes and weekly homework. Would highly recommend.

There are 3 midterms and then a final exam. While all the tests are structured similarly, the content increasingly becomes harder as the semester goes on. I second everything the other reviews have said, he's a good reliable professor, but just be prepared for the increase in difficulty.

I can't imagine a better calc 3 professor. Dr. Takeda was amazing, his lectures were great, and the pace of the course was very manageable. His practice exams and quizzes were very helpful. He also recorded his lectures, so it was easy to catch up if you missed a class. Lastly, he is an overall caring person and a very generous grader.

Prof. Takeda has been a fantastic professor and he made calculus 3 perhaps my favorite math class so far. He is clearly an extremely kind man and it's reflected in grading and disposition. He also puts up notes and recordings of his lectures online for if you need to catch up. Before exams, he'll give past exams and solution keys to practice (opt).

Takeda goes at a consistent and manageable pace. He records audio of his lectures and posts in-class notes online, really helpful for review. He frequently gives out practice quizzes and tests along with their keys, which are often structured like the actual exam, so you'll know what to expect. I really lucked out with my math prof this year.
Fun lectures, helpful in and outside of class, enthusiastic about her teaching

This is one of the easiest classes you could possibly take. She is so sweet and gives perfect scores on basically everything. I didn't read a single harry potter book and was fine, you can look up most of the answers!

I absolutely loved Dr. Cohen. She is passionate about the topic and really makes you think beyond the pages. If you haven't read the series yet you definitely need to read the books weekly. Grade based on weekly assignments, discussions & EC, and a final project. The class is really fun and stress free. She cares about her students a lot!

There is up to 225 points of extra credit given in the semester. Each discussion board is worth 50 points and each assignment is worth 100 points. You also get to go back and redo up to two assignments. The easiest class I have ever taken. Loved the professor, she was really nice and very accommodating.

Dr. Cohen is so so nice. She puts effort into every lecture and, while lectures can feel very long, it takes little effort to do well in the class. She wants students to do well and grades papers mostly on effort and thought. Lectures can feel boring though, especially if youve read the books before.

Professor Cohen is amazing. She cares so much about her students and gives so many chances to redo papers that you may have received a bad grade on. She makes class exciting to come to and always has a great attitude. 100% would take a class with her again.

Some people may ask "Why take a Harry Potter class?" I'll tell you why: it's a good GPA booster and there is so much cool behind the scene information you wouldn't otherwise know about. She's super friendly and has a magical way of somehow being in class one second and in her office the next!
This class is absolutely wonderful and Dr. Cohen is very informed and understanding.
Silvia was the goat. All around a great professor and her accent is cool. Use AI to help you learn but don't neglect the discussions.

Silvia is a wonderful professor, given that the class itself is not super easy. The pacing of each chapter is a lot to fit into one semester, yet it's manageable. Very dry sense of humor. Lots of practice in class. Virtually the same as AP Physics I.
A lot of work and test heavy. The lectures were rushed and confusing.

Dr.Bomparde is a great teacher. You can tell she really cares about her students and their learning. Grading is pretty tough; make sure you really understand FBDs and make sure you include units on exams and labs on everything don't forget your calculator
So sweet and understanding even when i struggled in the class

Dr. Bompadre is a pro. Her lectures aren't perfect (feel too fast, not enough "concept" explanation without math), but I always felt ready for tests, labs. PHYSCS 2750 Expert TA homework is tricky, but you get many attempts, hints, feedback. Her tests are reasonable in length and difficulty. Solid resources for test prep. Funny, with a great accent

She is be blunt with all responses in class, but she balances it out with a light humor. I truly loved her as a professor and wish she was teaching more classes that are required for anyone outside of physics majors.

Fun, inspirational professor. Profesora Torres is always engaging with us in class and even talks with us after class to talk about weekend plans. She cares about her students and is the best professor I have had here at mizzou
She is really good at explaining the topic. Finally, someone who knows how to teach finance. Class is definitely not easy but she is a great teacher with great knowledge of the course.

Sima is the first professor in the finance department that taught at a productive level and challenged me to learn skills and tools that were actually applicable to high level finance jobs. Professor Jannati really knows what shes talking about. This has been my favorite class in the business school overall but especially in Finance. She makes you earn your grade, and some students arent used to it, doesnt mean shes a bad prof. 100% recommended taking the class from her
This is not an easy class, but she helps you. She is very knowledgeable and knows the depth of what she teaches. Sima is always available to answer your questions.

Loves the sound of her own voice. Explains concepts that only need a minute worth of talking for like 10 minutes, which makes your lose focus and interest. She's knowledgeable, but cannot explain concepts effectively.

Smita was an incredible teacher of calculus. She explained everything clearly explained all topics in depth. The class is very straightforward. You have homework due every Tuesday morning and four exams. If you go to class and take notes you will do fine.

Hardly responded to emails or allowed the opportunity for an exam to be relooked. The entire 1300 department was difficult to deal with when it came to rounding or showing enough work even while my answers were correct. Difficult to work with, not flexible or helpful whatsoever
Hi, I'm glad to have a professor like her.

She was not very helpful with her lectures, she would just read from the slides and didn't care about students understanding the concepts. She is funny and lecture is very helpful to go to. She makes the slides funny while still being able to teach well. Mandatory icliker attendance but if you get over 60% the final is optional to take. Lots of homework and packback's due every Monday but they aren't worth much. exams are very difficult. Do the homework and study and you'll be okay.

Professor Goyes is not only an amazing professor but person. Halfway through the semester, my mom passed away. As a result my grades during the semester struggled. The class was basically talking about different places around Asia, Europe, Africa and Eurasia and it was not a hard class. Dr. Larsen is an awesome professor. He makes lectures entertaining and does a great job tying the lectures to real life. You can tell that he truly loves what he teaches. Dr. Larsen is the bee's knees. The cat's meow.

Seriously one of the best professors I've ever had. Great guy. Super passionate about what he teaches.

I have seriously considered sitting in on some of his lectures even when I'm not taking one of his courses -they are interesting and passionate and clear. He is always willing to help students and his coursework is engaging and useful.

Dr. Larsen is an amazing professor. His lectures are entertaining, informative, and useful. His grading schema are clear and reasonable, and he makes the class interesting for everybody. I highly recommend any of his classes.

Lots of assignments for this course but they weren't too hard. He's really passionate about teaching this topic and it made his lectures really enjoyable. Overall a pretty easy class, just quite a bit of busy work.
I took him for 4710 there was not an option for that wasn't bad just a really boring class.

His lectures are good and engaging, so its important to go. However, he doesn't really prepare you for the exams. This was just a weird class. everything from the lectures to the structure of grading. The teacher was ok, but theres gotta be a better way to teach statistics.
Make sure to write down any practice problems covered in class, they are very useful when studying. Go to lecture.

Solid professor. Has open book exams that are very straightforward if you pay attention in class. Teaches pretty well but he was largely unavailable outside of class, didn't answer emails in a timely manner and was often not present at his own office hours.
Great instructor. Explains things very well and concise. Hopefully you get this guy.

She is a very kind and compassionate professor. However one of the most unorganized classes I've taken in my life. One of the best professors I've had. Truly cars about her students and is very fair in grading.

Absolutely love her. She really cares and wants to hear everyone's opinions and makes it clear that her class is a safe space for everyone, even if your opinion differs from hers. I actually took WGST 4600 Women & Health with Dr. Prasad, and it was one of my easiest classes of my senior year. I learned so much in this class and really ejoyed the class discussions. She always wants to get everyone involved and hear everyone's opinions--and she also shares her own which is cool. Easy A if you do the readings and just come to class.
Is unorganized most of the time. Very one-sided, opinionated lectures about her liberal/feminist feelings. Has random outbursts of anger for no reason.

Acts like the class will be easy take home midterm and final papers, no exams. Irrational grader. No clear with her expectations at all. She doesn't prepare for lectures. Good person. Great educator.  Fun and thought provoking class as long as you enjoy discussion.  Highly recommended for all considering going into health care.

Dr. Woelfel is incredibly knowledgeable about journalism and filming and drones. However, his lectures and his tone of voice are monotone and dry. I don't know if I ever saw him smile or laugh. Stacey is incredibly knowledgeable. Anybody would be lucky to take one of his classes. This class had lots of small projects, which meant a lot of deadlines but it didn't feel like work. So. She is a good teacher but the ways she grades SUCKS. if u get a bad group for the semester long group assignment ur put of luck. That's what happened to be i got an a on ever exam and did my work but the 30 points i missed because of my teammates are why I couldn't get an A.

Stacie is a great professor who truly cares about her students. She can be a tough grader, but she's supportive and open to concerns. She rocks and has a lot of real world experience
Super easy class would reccomend
Stacie Kane is easily the best professor I've ever had. She really takes the time to get to know her students and cares deeply about their ability to learn. She is seriously so awesome.
Stacie Kane has such an amazing heart. I hope to stay connected to her beyond this class. She always tries to make class fun and interactive. She truly cares for her students.

Stacie is very nice and energetic, the class is "writing intensive" but I wrote 3 papers the whole semester. Very straightforward class, textbook is provided for you but I didn't use it once. There is a group project, but it's fairly easy. We often had guest speakers during lecture which made class interesting.

Very few assignments and tests in this class. Exam questions come straight from the homework and textbook though. Lectures were fast-paced and difficult to follow at times. PAY ATTENTION TO LECTURES!! Dr. Dologou is a difficult professor, but if you lock in to what he is saying and ask questions, you could pass. You gotta be locked in for Dostoglou's class bro but he's a rlly good teacher.

Dr. Dostoglou does a great job at teaching. He talks in a way that is understandable and makes you remember the content. Unorganized lectures and NO TAs make this class unnecessarily difficult to understand the concepts of. Wasn't allowed to see my grade this whole semester so I had 0 indication on my performance. 80% of your grade is Exams. Only posts about 40 questions of homework cumulatively the whole semester. His lectures are unorganized and mainly proofs the whole time rather than actual problems. I loved his lectures for calc 2. I am a visual learner and he helped spell things out in a way I understood. I feel like he was fair on grading exams.

This course is a very easy A. It is a pass/fail course, so you only need to receive a 70%. The course consists of 7 quizzes which are all very easy. The lectures are informative, but you could easily pass this class without watching them. This is a great class to add to your schedule if you are needing more credit hours to stay full time etc.

This class was very boring to me so I was not motivated to put much effort in but I got by just fine. If you do all of the readings and watch all lectures you will be perfectly fine. Dr. Ivey offers extra credit which is an easy grade boost. Most homework is a 5 question Canvas quiz and they are not difficult. There are also 4 exams.

She uses really good analogies and doesn't just drone on. Easily one of the best lecturers of Mizzou, which is saying something because I had her online class and online classes are NOTORIOUSLY boring.

Took it online, would recommend. Easy class and Dr. Ivey cares about what she teaches. I took the online version of this class and would recommend doing so. She's awesome

Wow. She's an amazing teacher. She teaches everything you need to know for the tests in class. She cares about her students, is available outside of class, and has a great sense of style. You'll love this class because it's not only easy, but it's easy to actually use it in real life.

If you are going to miss class, you are supposed to email her or the TA, but neither of them care to answer their emails on what you should do for missing class. All you learn about is music history.

Dr. Shonekan is an amazing professor. She makes lectures bearable and very interesting. She's very involved and loves to hear everyone's opinions on stuff. Extremely easy class! Tests are kind of tough, but you'll pass with an A if you do everything else, i would totally take this class again if i could!

Attendance is mandatory and you HAVE to go to do well in the class but you'll want to bc she is FABULOUS. She also expects you to read! DO IT! The exams aren't hard but they're specific so you actually have to go to class and read to do well on them. I had friends that just spark-noted the books and bombed tests. If you do the work it's an easy A!!

You can't help but to love Dr. S. She is so warm and friendly. She is very passionate about what she does.  If you are going take her course, I have a little adivice. 1) Read. There is a lot of reading, and you will feel foolish if you don't read. 2) Tests are tough! They are over a lot of little specific things, and they are worth a of your grade.

Dr. Shonekan is a hidden gem.  There is a friendliness about her that makes her class comfortable and enjoyable. There is quite a bit of reading expected, but if as you get the main ideas, you should be fine. Despite the class size  being large, she somehow manages to create intimate discussions. In class participation and is essential.
Dr. Shonekan is a very good professor. She has a friendliness about her that made class time comfortable and enjoyable. A easy class if you pay attention, take notes, and come to class.

Incredibly easy class if you show up. Mrs. Shonekan is very easygoing, learns everyone's names, and makes an already easy subject easier. Class participation is required. Only downside is that it's been a month since the semester ended and I still don't have the grade of my final test into blackboard yet. Great teacher and great class though.

Dr. Shonekan is one of Mizzou's hidden gems. She takes time to learn EVERYONE's names, which isn't easy at such a big school. I got to know her personally outside of class, and she's an incredibly intelligent and caring teacher. She's passionate about music and makes the class fun. Extra credit is given frequently, and she takes attendance.
My review doesn't meet the guidelines but I cannot stress this enough: At all costs avoid taking any classes with Klien or his TAs.

Class is a slog to get through, if you aren't a comms major, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. While Klien is a nice guy, you will constantly be berated by redundant video lectures, busy work, and tedious projects all with iClicker and assigned seating. Class is unorganized, prof is months behind on grading constantly, and you'll hear the same lecture twice.

Klien makes an what could be an. easy class ridiculously involved and time consuming. The TAs take months to grade assignments and when they finally do it is all over the place. This class is extremely homework heavy (although it has no real relevance to the class) and attendance and class participation are mandatory.

Worst professor I have had at Miz. I have not yet finished his class, but finals are in less than a month, and grades from January have not been put in. In my opinion, if you are requiring your students to put in as much time as you are asking, the least you could do is grade promptly. He cancels office hours every week and never answers emails.

Klien uses a flipped classroom where you watch a video going through the slides for the week. So essentially, you are sitting through the same lecture two times twice a week. This class is nothing more than a waste of time in my opinion. It's an easy A, but homework is not relevant to the content at all.

Dr. Klien is very passionate about the material he teaches, but the class structure isn't supportive of student learning. Canvas is overloaded with lots of "busy work" type assignments that don't really contribute to learning and just take up time outside of class, group/partner work happens almost every class, and lectures are long-winded.

This class is an easy class generally in content and in the big projects. What bothers me about Klien is his over-bearing and almost ridiculous insistence on using AI. Textbook is unneeded except to do unnecessary and repetitive homework through. He also assigned a 3-4 page essay the week of finals, which I didn't really appreciate.

Klien is a nice guy. He cares about the info he teaches. However, the amount of assignments he gives for a communication class is absurd. The 'career capstone' project is a waste of time. I'm a freshman who's not a communication major yet I have to spend hours researching a random career I don't care about. He's not respectful of students time.

Easily one of my favorite teachers ever. He is so passionate about film and sharing that love with others. Rozier is incredibly respectful about giving honest feedback and is his students' #1 fan. Class time with him is calm, relaxing, fun, and a great learning environment that excites me to continue my education in film. Fantastic teacher!

I would not recommend taking this class. The professor states that he cares about the students, but when there are questions about test grades he will not answer and will not take the time to go over the tests. I find this extremely unfair. Going over the tests should be the bare minimum. He has good lectures, but I wouldn't take the class.

He is an excellent professor in ensuring you are well aware of the course and wants you to learn. Class is very easy with a lot of it being common knowledge. Quizzes are open note, while exams are closed, but handed a detailed review sheet prior. PLA's are very picky on grammar. If you actually study and try you'll be destined for a B+ or higher.

I took NEP_1340 online as a self-paced course. It is an entirely different beast than his in person courses but I enjoyed it nonetheless. It was well organized, his TAs were on point, and his lecture videos were well-done and easy to understand. Tests were the most difficult part of the class. Otherwise, do the work and you'll turn out just fine.

Seriously the best professor I have ever had! A few easy canvas assignments a month, one big project at the end of the class but as long as you complete it and read the instructions you should do well. Four tests and quizzes that he tells you what will be on them. Super interesting class and Dr. Ball is extremely knowledgeable about health.
Phenomenal professor. As long as you go to the class and study your notes, you'll pass.
Dude is a chiller. Very easy class that he tells you some answers on the tests/quizzes in lecture. Lots of points to buffer grade, class was not weighted.
Very good professor and easy to follow along with. Test were never that hard as long as you studied your notes.
He is a great teacher, and like's engaging with the class.
my king. i love him

DONT LISTEN TO EVERY OTHER BAD REVIEW!!!! Attendance is mandatory, but you get two free absences and he is very understanding if you just talk to him. I didn't buy the class textbook and still managed to get A's on every exam and every project. He grades very easily and also will remove questions from your exam score if most people get it wrong.

I barely showed up to class due to personal reasons and still managed to get a B+. This class was very test heavy and had 3 different big projects (so unbelievably easy I got them done in under 1 hour). He is fair w grading. READ THE TEXTBOOK and his slides on canvas and you'll be fine!

Dr. Whitney was amazing. It was discussion based so attending class was important and so was doing the reading before hand. He was a super interesting professor who always had something to add to the conversation while also being very respectful of hearing everyone's views (even if he disagreed). Would take again.
This guy rocks. Most interesting and easiest class I've ever taken

I learned a lot in Prof Whitney's class on truth. He approached the topic from many different angles, which made the in-class discussion really interesting. He's eccentric but approachable and strives to include everyone. The homework is mostly reading the textbook, which isn't too difficult. Grading was based on a midterm paper and a final essay.

Just show up to class and you'll get an A. All of his tests have quizlets for them if you just look up one question from your study guide the whole test will come up for you to study. Also if you just turn something in for your projects you'll get full credit.
I enjoyed this class with Dr. Whitney. He is extremely insightful, and I look forward to having conversations with him each class!

Get ready to not know what your grade is! Weekly discussion posts are required, but criteria is vague and you will not know if you're "participating" correctly, since he posts nothing on Canvas. This (+ many required readings) is most of the work, and it is not worth much grade-wise. Little to no feedback given on papers, which are worth far more.

Karian's General Honors Humanities class at Mizzou was awful. His "old school" approach forces costly physical books weekly, exceeding $200. Feedback on papers is vague, reflecting only his preferences. He doesn't update grades online, putting the burden on students to guess. The class is outdated, expensive, and lacks transparency-not recommended.

The humanities sequence is by no means easy but Dr. Karian is a great discussion leader who made the course a lot more manageable. There are a lot of essays but he gives you fair warning on all of them and discussions are very easy so long as your willing to speak up. He also responds very quickly to emails which is great.

Great professor! Super caring and responsive to questions. The class I took as a part of the Honors Humanities sequence was very interesting, but I definitely struggled getting through the heavy amounts of reading and writing sometimes. He always encourages students to think in his classes while also stimulating discussion topics when needed.

So much reading and writing! Do not take the honors humanities sequence if you don't like reading entire book in short amounts of time and then writing long papers about the books. Class discussions were sometimes forced, and if you don't say something in the discussion you lose participation points.

EnvSci4305- Content is very difficult and Dr. Andersons lectures are a bit boring and unclear. If you ask questions, though, he clarifies well. However, he is the easiest grader I've ever had. You may get every question of the homework wrong and get a 9.5/10 as long as you put in some effort, you will do fine.

Dr. Anderson is such a nice guy! His subjects are generally pretty hard but I think any other professor would be way worse. He can be a little boring sometimes but it is clear how much he cares about students and their success. Just make sure you're ok at math and have an understanding of basic soils and chem before taking his classes.

This course can be confusing since there have been a lot of issues with QGIS working on the computers. the first 6 classes we didn't really do anything. Lots of quizzes in this course, but they have no time limits. This class requires a working understanding of how to use excel, but if you sit next to someone who knows it you can get by.

Dr. Anderson teaches the 2nd half of this class. He is hard to understand/follow during lectures & practice sets, most students don't know what's going on and have to struggle to keep up and understand homeworks. Get a study group for this class ASAP for the transport portion or you will struggle (coming from a 3.95 gpa student).

Dr. Lombardo is a great professor, but thermo is hard. His exams are just like the homework's for the unit. You are able to opt in or out of the homework, but homework was best way to study. During lectures, he reads slides then does example problems that are posted, but he does not post the answers so you must go to lecture to see the answer.
Great guy. Thermo is a hard class and he really tells you how to succeed. Just study and come to class and ask questions if you don't understand.

The material is hard, but he does a good job teaching it. The exams are all very similar to homework problems. He's super funny and makes lectures pretty tolerable. The textbook and homework are 100% the best resources to do well on exams.

Lombardo is a G. However, 4 exams make up your entire grade. Thermo is no easy course. If you do the homework and know how to read the tables, you'll be fine. Don't half-ass this course because you won't pass. Mad respect for Lombardo though; great guy.

The class was pretty simple and exams were pretty much just like the homework. With that said 28 percent had to withdrawal and many more failed. This is due to exams being worth nearly all the points unless you opt in to homework. The exams themselves are very straightforward if you do the homework.

Lombardo tries to make Thermodynamics fun and applicable to the real world. He might not have the best lectures as he just reads off the notes he has posted on canvas, but he tries to crack a joke here and there. 95% of your grade depends on your exam scores and the other 5% is homework. 25% of the class with dropout or fail, you have been warned.

Now this class is not a cake walk but Professor Lombardo definitely makes it a little bit better. He's probably the funniest professor I've had so far. Make sure to nail down the materials from the first two exams, if you do not learn this material, I can almost guarantee you will not pass the class so make sure to study.

Lombardo is a hilarious and very nice dude. The lectures themselves are enjoyable and can give you a base to understand the material, however  you will definitely have to do a lot of learning outside the classroom. He is very strict with grading and wouldn't round me up 0.3% to get a B+ however so get ready for no extra credit or rounding.

Bless his heart, he knows quite a bit, and has done a lot of studying, but he isn't the best professor. It's hard to follow his lectures. If you read the textbook, don't go to class, and if you go to class, don't read the textbook. Could use more clarification on certain theories and it can be more than a little boring, but fine class overall.

Quackenbush is an amazing historian but a horrible teacher. If you want to talk to someone about history he's the one but if you want to save your GPA do NOT take his class. For a 1400 level class it should not have been as difficult to follow along with what he says. I spent more time teaching myself after the classes his slides are HORRIBLE.

Professor was nice but just read off of slides and didn't always know what he was talking about. Final grade is mostly weighted by exams so you have to do good on them, but there are only 3 tests. Attendance was supposed to be taken randomly, but was never actually taken. Class should have been much more engaging and easier than it was.

This was easily my least favorite class this semester. Dr. Quackenbush is a great guy with a lot of knowledge to offer, but the lectures were very hard to follow along with and quite boring. There are not many assignments/help offered in this class, extremely test heavy. Do not recommend/would not take again.

This class was easy in the sense that there were minimal things to submit, however, lectures were not great. He would read off slides and it was hard to follow along with him. He does not give study guides for exams and there is a lot of content to remember for them. Be prepared for exams since there's few other assignments. I would not take again

He knows a lot about the course material, but lectures are very hard to stay engaged with as it just consists of him reading off the slides. Study guides are not provided on exams, so studying for exams can be tough. He's nice enough, this class just wasn't enjoyable.

He is a good guy and very knowledgeable in his field, but the lectures leave much to be desired. The lectures were long and he just read off the slides. If you ask questions he will go more in-depth and that might help more. If you are more of a hands-on learner this class may be difficult for you.
Pretty easy lectures. Tests are all multiple choice and pretty easy. He makes study guides and crosswords for you. Total WW2 nerd

Mr. Smith's class was extremely interesting.  I generally am not a fan of history, but I found myself looking forward to his lectures.  For tests, he gives out an extremely helpful study guide.  If you put in effort, an A is attainable.

A couple of classmates and emailed the whole class to put a study group together. This teacher took time out of his free time and volunteered to come to the study group to help us. He obviously cares about his students and makes his class really interesting. Tests are not easy but I would still recommend this class! Its not a blow off class though.

Mr. Smith was by far the best history teacher I've had in my academic career. He makes class fun and interesting and it's obvious that he is really invested in students' learning. I loved this class and he made me choose to minor in history. If you can, definitely take a class from him!

He keeps lectures very interesting and really tries to appeal to a younger audience.  Unlike history classes I've taken before, there was literally never a boring lecture.  Make sure you go to each lecture though, as he doesn't record lectures.  His class wasn't terribly hard, but requires a little effort.

Project requirements were vague and while Sayers was pleasant and easy to talk to in person he was often short over email. Lectures were dense, but mostly due to material and not his teaching style. This being said, it was the first time that he had taught the course so it is possible that this course will improve.

Dr. Sayers is a great professor, he is truly passionate about the material. He is available for outside of class help. He posts lectures on blackboard, but you should still go to class and pay attention. He gives in class quizzes, but he posts the dates of them on the syllabus. Heavy content in the lectures, but overall interesting information.
Great class!!  Good sense of humor - Jim Morrison lookalike.
one of those professors you can tell is actually a nice person. Actually seems really wholesome.

Professor Christ's aura is unmatched. Favorite professor this semester and probably one of the most interesting people I've had teach me. Funny, smart, and never feels fake. His taste in cologne is impeccable. Easy weekly quizzes + doesn't require attendance.
fav prof i love him

If you want a professor who actually sees you as a human being, take his class. After a bad first semester, he helped me get my confidence back and helped get me on the right path. He's unlike any professor I've had before. He's a fountain of positive kindness and so wholesome. He always has the biggest and cutest smile literally every class.

Take his class. He makes criminology way more fun than you'd expect by having students act out scenarios, and it actually helps you learn. Also volunteer when he asks because he gives out thank you prizes. He's genuinely hilarious, super upbeat, and honestly very charming and good-looking and just has a really likable presence.
He makes the class feel fun and interesting, which is impressive, and the constant smile and whole stud situation definitely don't hurt.

The professor is super smart, honestly kind of a genius, but he has no ego about it. He is really positive and has a lot of charisma, and he seems like he would be a genuinely good friend outside of class too. The class was easy to enjoy and remember.
Dr. Christ is AMAZING! Hands down my favorite professor ever! Charming, friendly, funny, and brilliant.

Dr. Hackley is an incredibly engaging lecturer.  I have never been so inspired to achieve and learn.  I started out not caring, but he talked to me after class to express his concerns, and after that I started attending class and really paying attention.  I learned more than I have from any other psychology class.

He was one of the best prof's I've had at Mizzou.  The lectures are like stories. The tests are sort of hard, but then he grades them so easy. The term papers are only 4 pages long, and you can do them on pretty much any person you are interested in.

It is a tough class because you are learning the history and dates of Psychology, but Dr. Hackley is very interested and enthusiastic about the material he is teaching so it makes the class enjoyable and easier. There is a total of 4 tests in the class and two papers. Other than that there is no homework and no final. I would recommend taking it.
Really unclear in what he expects from you for tests, not my favorite class.

This class  has probably been the worst class I have ever taken at Mizzou. Before reading this do know that I still passed the class. He expects you to study 6 hours a week for his class. He does not have a grading system, your grade is determined by your peers. It its purely a competition. He is sooo boring and does not grade on the + or - scale

He is the nicest professor I have ever had. Genuinely nice and interested in student success. He is also very knowledgeable about the subject matter. Make sure you attend class because he doesn't post notes to Blackboard. You will need to read the textbook for tests as well. Learned a ton from this class!

One of the best professors I've ever had at Mizzou.  He explains things so they are easy to understand and remember for the tests. He is very helpful, nice, and encouraging. Make sure you read the text book as well as attend all lectures.  That will guarantee an A on the tests.  The papers aren't too difficult either.  Great class, Great professor!

Dr. Hackley was the best Psych prof I've ever had. He is extremely nice, a great speaker, and very intelligent. The only drawback of his class was that I paid a decent amount for the textbook but never used it because all of the info you need for tests and labs is discussed in class. He doesn't use blackboard either. Old school, but a great prof.

Professor Berkley was hands down the best professor that I have had at Mizzou so far. His lectures are interactive and fun to go to. The curriculum is interesting and easy to jump into. There are a few group projects but nothing that caused any trouble. He did cancel class last minute here and there, but overall one of my favorite classes so far.

Berkeley was by far one of my favorite professors. He tries hard to relate the topics of his lectures by asking questions to the students. There were no tests, but lots of homework quizzes but they were easy.

Professor Watts' wit and extensive knowledge of history actually makes his lectures enjoyable; Even though attendance was not mandatory, I wanted to go to my 9 am lectures because I enjoyed them so much. You can tell he truly loves what he does, and it shows in class. As long as you show up to lecture/discussion and actively listen you will pass.

I really enjoyed this class but I didnt read any of the books required (if you know u wont read them DONT buy them) and that tanked my grade. What really saved me was my TA Lauren she was amazing and helped my discussion class better understand the lectures. You have to go to class to do well, he doesnt take attendance but its worth it to go!

Professor Watts makes lectures enjoyable and interesting. He doesn't post online so you have to go to class in order to get the notes. The class consists of 7 reading quizzes and 2 essay tests. Essay tests are graded difficult. Andrew Olden was my TA and he was very helpful.

Very interesting class. The lectures were super informative and I sincerely enjoyed listening to them. However, the tests were VERY DIFFICULT. If you think you're going to passively study and take half-hearted notes, you will not get a good grade. Nothing is posted online, so come to class. My T.A. was Andrew Olden and he was extremely helpful.

Loved Professor Watts and even though I got a B in the class, I would take it a thousand times again! Was very knowledgable about the subject he was speaking on, made class interesting, and overall just a great professor! Highly recommend him!

If you take History 1200, please steer clear from Taylor Gruman. He is extremely passive-agressive and he makes me uncomfortable. He is really random with assigning reading questions to his students. I don't know how the other TA's do this, but Taylor only gives us 10 minutes to take the reading quizzes. I recommend Andrew Olden for a history TA :)

Watts is funny and his lectures are straightforward and interesting. He doesn't take attendance, but he doesn't record his lectures so you HAVE to go to class to get the info. Two essay tests and some reading quizzes. Also you read 6 real books but you don't have an actual textbook, which i liked but might not be for everyone. Doesn't use canvas.

Professor Watts is one of the best lecturers I have ever had the pleasure of listening to. I took his Walt Disney and American Culture class. Not only was the content interesting, but Prof Watt delivered clear, concise lectures that kept me consistently engaged. There was quite a bit of reading and note involved, but overall still worth it.

Attend lectures!! Take notes on everything. You will need to review your notes and the book often. The class is graded on a curve. Difficult but very engaging class. I'm glad I had a professor like Dr. Cutkosky or else it would have been terrible. I would take another course by him if I could.

Difficult course, but what can you expect with abstract algebra. I wish Dr. Cutkosky had made the class a little more interactive because I sometimes felt lost in lecture. The homeworks were deceptively long; a four question assignment could really be more like twelve proofs, all of which take quite a while to do. Dr. Cutkosky is a nice guy.

Lecture notes online are ok, but his in class lectures are horrendous due to his atrocious communication skills. Goes over very few examples and expects you to just get everything. When you ask a question he usually says "well I've already went over this multiple times" and doesn't answer your question. You might as well never ask. Worst Miz prof.

Matrix Theory with this guy was a major struggle. He didn't do many examples in class and expected us to learn the material based off of typed up notes we would get online. Wouldn't give all answers to hw problems, even thought it wasn't graded. Hard tests. Got frustrated when you asked questions in class. I had to work really hard to get  a B+.
Does very little examples in class. Never provides the solutions to more than half of the HW problems. Unless your an expert in Matrix Theory stay away from this class!

Professor Gardiner was by far one of the best professors I've had at Mizzou. He is super lenient with homework allowing students to submit after the due date for various assignments. He cares about his class, tells great jokes, and delivers incredible lectures. His feedback on my speeches has helped me grow as a speaker. Literally, the GOAT!
Absolutely does not care about the students. Terrible communication and attitude and offers no help.
Dr. Goldschmidt was super helpful, and I appreciated him !

He teaches math in a way non-math people can understand. The best math teacher by far and the hardest class I have had. He also helps you come to the answer, most professors just give you the answer knowing you dont understand. Not this guy. He has a fun non boring teaching method as well.
awful, mean ,man, don't write on the front of your test or you will get 10% off
Do not get this guy if you can help it. He runs much of the math department and is exceptionally unforgiving.

Goldschmidt's classes were extremely challenging for me- especially the exams. They are structured in a way that may catch you off guard. While, this may seem deceitful, it really helps you learn that in the future, when making real business decisions you need to be careful. Top notch guy- just wants you to work hard, as he should.

Steve is willing to slow down in lectures if people are not understanding the material.  The practice exams are quite similar to the actual exams.  The homework assignments are in Excel and are very practical. He really wants the students to do well.

Goldschmidt was a phenomenal teacher. Once, the highest grade on a quiz was a "C" so he re-taught the lesson and gave another quiz. He said it was his fault we weren't understanding the material. Great professor, great guy. Always willing to help you outside of class too. You can tell he loves not just math but to teach.

He has great lecture content, optional homework that was helpful, and a list of textbook problems he recommends doing. Doing the recommended problems and practice exams was enough to get good grades on the midterms. He is by far the best calc 3 prof you could take if you're trying to actually learn and understand the material.

I took the honours section of Calc 3, and like other ratings, I feel like there is not a better professor for it. Hofmann is extremely knowledgeable and has great, lighthearted lectures, though tests are really demanding (but he does provide good practice exams). Honours section is hardly different than regular. Optional, but helpful, homework.

There was optional homework and difficult exams. Attendance is not taken, but if you miss a class, you miss the notes as there is none posted on Canvas. No note cards for exams, but you get practice exams that are sometimes helpful. The averages on his exames were very low, but ended up getting curved.

Mr. Hofmann was very knowledgeable and would answer all questions that were given to him. However, throughout the course it seemed as if he would speak in higher language than we understood yet. It made it very difficult to follow along in class as well as ask questions since there were times that I didn't even know what question I could ask.

The class is very well laid out and he is incredible at teaching the material. The homework annoying but helpful, and he is very knowledgeable about general math (helped me with some more advanced questions about the concepts). Take this professor for calc 3 at all costs if genuinely learning the material is important to you. Exams are rigorous.

Dr. Hofmann was my professor for the honors 2300 section and I could not be happier with who I was given. Great guy who is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. Lectures are very important and are a must to stay caught up in the class. But lectures were always fun with a lighthearted tone. Practice exams were quite similar to actual exams.

I took the honors section of this course and Hofmann was the best choice I could've made. The course is structured with 3 midterms, a 1-1 exam where he asks you questions and you answer by working it out on a blackboard, and the comprehensive final. He makes everything a lot smoother by giving you practice exams, would recommend for honors students

Hofmann is a great teacher. His lectures were great to listen to and follow. He also had a light and fun attitude during class which made a hard class feel more bearable. His homework extra credit was great practice and a good help to my grade. Would recommend taking his class.

Great example of someone who should not be in education. Boring lectures, bad at teaching, makes an interesting subject terribly boring, and generally unhelpful to students. Get ready to teach yourself, Steve can't teach anything. Wait to take this class from another professor. It's a shame Mizzou only has one professor for this class at a time.
boring lecture
The lecture is torturing boring.

- Lectures are mind-numbingly boring.
- Occasionally does random iClicker checks, and you must be in class to know the answer.
- Exams are very easy and are the exact same as the practice exams.
- The content is interesting, but he makes it uninteresting.
- One homework assignment per week. The homework is very easy.
- That is basically it.
This dude is actually the least enthusiastic person to ever live. Puts me to sleep every class> I would much rather learn the material on my own.

Last week I got home from class and was dumped by my long term girlfriend, so as one does, I went to the bar. I met this chick and spent over $100 on a bar tab just to find out she was a dude. This class has been a worse experience by far. Do not recommend.
Lord Help me
This class is pass/fail and it's a lot of work but it could be worse.
For a pass fail class, there's LOTS of work.

I got 102% in class because of extra credit and being a good test taker, not because of VanDoren's teaching abilities. He cannot work Zoom and often doesn't share slides. He stated the first day that people on Zoom would be able to take quizzes with the in-person students, but then decided on week 2 that this was no longer allowed without warning.

Reads directly off slides in a mind numbingly monotone voice. Easily the most difficult class I've ever taken in my academic career, and unfortunately also the worst professor I've ever had. This combo makes for a GPA-detrimental course that either consumes your entire semester or has you accepting a C.

He just reads off slides, which are just stuff from the textbook. Test averages never went over 65. You CANNOT cram studying in this class. I liked having the physical book, highlighting what is discussed in lecture. My advice: consistently review, TRULY memorize pathways and cycles, draw out concept maps.

Doesnt know what he is talking about, goes on tangents that do not make sense, he mumbles. He's strict and his study materials are 50/50. Lectures/slides are confusing.need a lot of background information to try to understand this course. He is honestly rude. He is not helpful during office hours.PLA's are nice and really do try to help you though.
Doesn't even try to teach. Read off of slides and refused to answer questions in office hours. Degrading
horrible. horrible. horrible. DO NOT TAKE

It seemed like he was learning the material as he was presenting it to us. He also talked painfully slow and stumbled over every word. Lectures were genuinely so painful & I never knew what he was saying. The exams were impossibly long and so hard, averages never got above 62%. He seemed like a nice guy but truly a terrible professor.

Professor Van Doren is currently stumbling over his slides as I'm writing this review. He doesn't want to teach, and you can tell because all of his students have to put in at least 20 hours per week for this class alone in order to get above a C. Every slide is word vomit and impossible to follow and learn from. Mizzou, please fire this man.

Knowledgeable in his field & does care about students doing well, that's about all I can say as a positive. You'll get better grades if you don't disagree with him. Dr. Outlaw provided a lot of resources so that the material could be understood. This class is still hard and very lecture heavy. def one of the best professors. clearly states his topics and makes it easy to connect. the discussion work is a bit tedious but it does pay off when it comes to tests

Very good lecturer, very passionate, clear requirements and generous grading policies. I really liked going to class, would definitely take again.
No comment

A great online class.

Professor McFarland was a great professor. When I first decided to take this class, I was unsure whether or not I would like the subject. He changed my mind completely through his lectures and I truly enjoyed his class! A caring individual who really wants the best out of his students.

She's super nice and super friendly, not to mention she's kind of hot. Regarding math, she's not a tough grader at all. She'll let you take notes and use the notes for your tests and quizzes. It's great if you're mathematically impaired such as myself.
Meh

Class is kind of boring, but Dr. Johnson is one of the few professors I've at had at Mizzou that genuinely cares about the well-being and success of her students. Don't be afraid to approach her for help, because she will go above and beyond for you!
Very willing to help students in understanding assignments. Also, helpful in making sure students felt at ease to participate in class.

This class is boring as her tone is flat. You would want to fall asleep. Her lectures are power-points with tons of words stick together. Dr. Guptas lecture style isnt my favorite, but he does actually give hints as to whats going to be on the test if you are paying attention. His tests are usually long and pretty difficult. The only recommendation I gave was to replace the teacher. Professor Gupta may be smart, but his teaching is pitiful. He should not be teaching students such an important skill as programming in engineering.

Find a different capstone professor if possible. She makes things unnecessarily difficult. You will not learn anything useful and there are weekly group projects and papers. The class is not difficult, but there is tons of busy work. She also can be rude and dismissive

Snarkyts the course by saying "I teach the hardest capstone class" Honestly, the material isn't hard, it's just unnecessary busy work and way too many readings. I immediately switched out of her capstone. She began the class with "This is the hardest capstone, so you might want to transfer out". Enough said.

absolutely loved her! one of my favorite professors thus far. she's very easygoing and patient if you have any late work. as long as you put in some effort, you'll do fine. class discussions were fun and I was rarely bored. 10/10
She is awesome and grades easily as long as you put in effort. Nicest professor I have had in the English department. Take ENG3700 or any of her classes!!
Literally do the work and you will get an A. If it is late, tell her and she will understand. She was super nice and cared about what we had to say. Class was super easy and fun.

best professor I have had in college. She is passionate & is always willing to offer help, it is not hard to succeed in this class at all. She is also the most caring prof.

Virginia was an angel! I loved everything about this class. best professor I have had in college. She is specific in what it is she wants/needs from you in the class for you to get a good grade (& it really is not much.) Impossible to get a grade. ECONOM 8413: Research Workshop I.

Prof. Allbritain is a terrible lecturer. His handwriting is atrocious and mumbles when speaking. When asked questions; he answers with an even more confusing response. She is by the far the best professor I have had in J school. International student here but her English was always very clear to me. She had the classes well designed We did interviews, text-analysis and observations. Not to mention how kind and helpful and efficient she is. I have her on my committee and she has helped me more than my chair.

Very good professor. Professor Shin was super funny, gave really good feedback on every assignment, and overall just made class enjoyable. Grading is mandatory, but he gives you a set amount of absences before it affects your grade. I really liked this class and he's usually a pretty lenient grader. 10/10 would take again. I took English 1000.

He was a nice guy with a clear passion for British Literature, however, he lacked the ability to keep his students engaged. The readings he assigned were multiple and often took me at least 5 hours to complete and analyze, this does not sound like much but it built up over time and I struggled to balance my school work and job.
Very easy English class, you have 5 excused absences.

Just no. He is still a graduate student, and is so unorganized and unprofessional. For a freshman level class, he makes things very overwhelming for new students, and his assignments have very high standards. Each big essay will have you writing ten pages for it. He made me hate my first semester of college.

The lectures are comprised of him reading from slides. He hands back all graded homework and exams, which is a nice feedback. You get an equation sheet for the exam, along with attendance being taken to bump up your grade at the end of the semester. Lectures are not great, but homework will set you up for success.

Won't even write out practice problems herself. She just zooms through them on presentations. Ludicrous amount of homework every week. Labs are complete busy work. You are better off teaching yourself the material over anything she can teach you. All of her lectures are rambling nonsense that waste everyone's time. Dr. Luo is nice, but her canvas page is autorius, she puts everything under files. She grades based on points instead of percentage which is really great, it took me from a B+ to an A- at the end. Professor Luo is a great teacher, and a kind soul. The class is fully online, yet she is always quick to respond to emails. She is a very reasonable lady, and would take our feedback into account and apply it. Her lecture notes were helpful, and she allows a drop exam. I would take this class over again, especially with her!
I liked this class and I liked Yuyan. If you showed up to class and took notes over what she said, you would do well. She does her grading based on addition, not percentage.

She is a nice professor. She's always willing to answer questions and talk with you after class. It's a pretty easy class. All of the tests are open note. There are 12 article summaries that are easy to do and you only need to complete 10. There are 4 random in class assignments so that's why I said attendance is necessary but there's wiggle room.

She is a tough grader. She doesn't explain what she's looking for in short answer questions, only afterwards if you set up an appointment with her after receiving a grade for your test. However, she is very enthusiastic about the topic and going to class is a must so the lecture slides make more sense by taking notes of her verbal explanations.
This is my 4th psychology class and I've never had one this hard. She knows a lot and expects you to know a lot of details, which is very challenging

This class was the worst! Hard to understand her English and she moves too fast in the class. She makes the exams very difficult to pass. If you take it sign up for presentations EARLY in the semester. That will save your grade. I wish I never took her class. Was not a fan. Avoid her if you can!

As a senior, I've have never regretted enrolling in a class more than hers. Her exams are truly impossible, and it's tough to get presentation spots. She is a merciless grader. Do your GPA a favor, and don't click the "enroll" button on this one.

Very nice guy and a very easy grader. Attending class will come with random extra credit days. Nearly impossible to fail his class if you give just 10% effort. Would highly recommend, as he is always willing to give feedback in office hours. Exams were tough, but graded very leniently.

I actually took Dynamics 2600 with him, but that wasn't an option in the settings. This is my first time typing a review, it's that urgent. Listen to me. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS. He is the worst lecturer I've ever had, to the point that most students gave up listening to him at all during class, and the homework is often impossibly hard.

Yuyi does not teach to his exams or homework.Any problems you are given in the class (including exams) are pulled directly from the textbook.The problems from the book require outside information to solve them as there are some sections that don't provide any equations or relevant material properties to the questions you will be asked to solve.
Easy grader and gives lots of feedback, funny guy too.
don't learn anything from Lin. his notes are disorganized on Canvas.
You may get an A and you don't understand anything from the class. I don't know why the department thinks this course is not important !!

Do whatever you can to aviod taking Mech 1 with Lin.  He is very difficult to understand, his teaching is sub-par, and his homeworks are impossible.  The only upside is he passes almost everybody.  You will not learn anything from this class. It is a complete waste of time.  Winholtz teaches this in the spring, take him.

Lin's lectures are very boring, monotone, and not engaging.  This is one of those classes that you finish without feeling like you've really learned anything.  It can be frustrating.  On a plus side, he practically guarantees a B if you finish the homework and tests with at least a little effort.

I had Prof Callahan for a history class about religion in the United States a couple of years ago. It was my favorite class at Mizzou and not like any of my other history classes. I expected a class about the history of religion to be boring because I'm not religious but it wasn't. Lots of cool stuff and different ways of thinking about religion.
I loved this class. Professor Callahan makes you work, but you'll learn a lot.
Easy class that really helps open your eyes to the changing world around you. Callahan shows you how to see religion in so much of our pop culture . Fun class

Good professor, very open minded and accommodating to students. Likes projects, so be prepared for a little group work. He is good to work with, though. I didn't read the book until the final, and that was the only time I actually used it--- we had no tests! Only a final. Attendance is mandatory.
Totally not the class I expected, in a good way. Callahan was great! Enthusiastic, smart, and helpful.
The professor was very informed and could explain the class concepts using examples that everyone could understand. I appreciated the unbiased info we heard in lectures. A very fair professor.

Professor Callahan gives clear lectures and covers as many points of view as possible when talking about class material. He grades fairly, and gives useful feedback during office hours. While taking one of his classes I noticed he was very passionate about his work and excited to see students discuss and learn from each topic.

Religion and popular culture was one of my favorite courses. I learned a whole new vocabulary that isn't just about religion. This isn't a course about world religions. It's really about thinking about where our ideas about religion, society, gender, race, class, and being human come from in popular culture. Easily the best prof I've had at Mizzou.
gives no grace. wouldn't recommend. expects you to be exquisite writer. Not everyone writes so eloquently. has no problem giving out zero's even when you make the effort.
He doesn't work well with students who are dealing with a life crisis. He is not flexible with the rapid courses, and he expects all students to have top-tier writing skills in history.

Dr. Dowdle is a wonderful professor! The class is designed to be led by a different group of students each discussion, so the class only works if you do the assigned readings to you can contribute to the conversation. Readings are due every class period, but they are always really interesting. He lets us really get into good conversations!
Beast, genuinely cared abut his students and his course. Encouraged participation and treated us like friends.

Best teacher I've had in recent memory, leads discussions in a way that inspires conversation and discourse like no teacher I've had. For me, this method of teaching content really helped me retain information compared to other lecture/discussion style classes I've been in. Very funny and easy to get along with. Phenomenal teacher and person.
Really easy going and willing to help. Makes class fun and listens to students.

Zach is a great teacher. He is passionate and knowledgeable about Star Wars, and politics. The classes are always exciting and I never wanted to skip class. Weekly homework reflected what we went over each class that week. Our only other grades were a midterm and final essay. I highly suggest this specific class and any other class taught by Zach.
He did a great job teaching such a unique class. Very knowledgeable and able to explain the concepts in a way the whole class can understand.
Great teacher great class.

Zach is the best. I took his politics of star wars class and I have never been more excited to go to class. Zach makes class a productive conversation and he is genuinely knowledgable on everything he discusses. I'd recommend anyone to take a class with Zach
He has a very good ability to relate star wars to American politics.  The class I took was weekly reflections attendance and midterm and final paper that was short.  Would recommend this class.
Great teacher

Zach is a kind and caring professor who makes lecture material very easy to grasp, and makes the hands on activities feel easy and comfortable. Theatre 1320 was a lot of fun, and I would recommend to anyone looking to gain some stage building or just general architectural experience

Zach is a really cool guy, and this class is pretty easy. In this class you learn about tools and help to build the plays for that semester. The class time is usually spent working, but there are lectures about tools or materials usually something like once a week. the class does have mandatory outside work, but if you show up you should get an A

The few lectures he gives are extraordinarily vague and badly designed. Any instructions given are so unclear that even the TA gets frustrated. He is easily distracted and then angered by this distraction, and he shows frustration towards students. Even experienced students struggle to understand what he asks of us. Out of class hours are required.

I loved her! She was a great professor and you could tell she cared about her students. There was a lot of reading in the class that we would have discussion over so it is important to do the readings. Also there's a lot of group discussion and that's where a lot of participation points come from. Overall easy class, just stay on top your work!

Zahraa is an amazing professor!! She teaches class in a very informal setting that makes it very inviting and more comfortable. She's really big on group conversations and communication as a whole which can be a plus or negative depending on your view on talking in front of a class. Assignments are laid out pretty simple and she doesn't grade harsh

This professor sucksss. He does not care whether you understand the concepts he covers or not. He barely speaks English and refuses to listen to our class concerns. His tests are impossible. He expects us to memorize 300 slides, 200 pages from the book, and 14, 14 page, legal cases for a 10 question test that determines our whole grade. DO NOT TAKE

So this is just a pass fail class. Its super easy and basically just to give you information about nuclear medicine. It gives you an easy way to get shadowing hours because its required to pass. He is super fun super cool and classes dont meet that often. Its very laid back no test but there is a paper and presentation.

Like most Mizzou professors, her English could use improvement. The textbook for class, which she wrote herself, had multiple mathematical  errors and typos. The classes were long,  and notes were taken directly from the book, so attendance isn't required.
Fantastic professor! Really cares that his students actual learn the material instead of being overwhelming

I respect Professor Qin a ton, he is very accessible outside of class. At first when I thought only zoom office hours it wouldn't be productive but it's the complete opposite. He is very good with screen sharing his iPad and computer screens so you can easily follow his steps on problems you don't understand!

Dr. Qin was great. The course itself I regret taking, but the lectures were his personal notes with plenty of definitions, explanations, and examples. He does not post lecture notes regularly, so although attendance is not taken it is important. Assignments are infrequent but long, due at 8 AM. Very professional.

Review for 2320** Professor Qin did an amazing job of explaining the class in a clear and concise way, and managed to keep me understanding everything going on throughout the course. Very easy grader, and the exam questions come from the reviews. Somewhat boring during lecture and can be hard to stay focused, but he does a great job of explaining.

Disclaimer: Had him for 2320, not 2300. It did not give me the option to select 2320. He was lecture-heavy, but if you took good notes and practiced examples from class and homework you will do fine on exams. He was very communicative and always would answer any questions you had outside of class. Overall a great experience with this professor.

Dr. Qin is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is a phenomenal lecturer and very fair grader. He makes it very clear from the start what his expectations are and he never tries to trick you on exams. His exams are a great knowledge check and as long as you do the work and come to class you will do well. I highly recommend Dr. Qin.
He was great! I took him for 4100 and I felt like I learned a lot despite the class being online. Definitely made math fun for me, despite the material being hard.

Best professor I ever had, even with an online format. Was super available to give help outside of class any time you emailed, graded exams and quizzes same-day, and was just a super nice guy. Exams and quizzes were very reasonable.

Dr. Hu is a special professor at Mizzou. Most Civil Engineering profs I've had don't really care about their students, but Dr. Hu is one of the rare ones who does. He's an exceptional teacher, and probably one of the classes where I learned the most
Lots of assigned readings, but Dr. Hu is a very helpful and funny prof to have for your higher level courses

Prof Zhiqiang (Zach) was a great dude to have for CVENG3200. def look over your assigned readings, but he cares about his students a lot and looks out for their success. Bought the whole class pizza when we all got A's on the final which reminded me of high school lol
Lectures are informative. I really liked the layout of the labs. Great professor!
Curved a 80% avrg exam to 92%. Would take any day.

Probably one of the best professors I've ever had, and I'm a second-year graduate student. Quizzes are ridiculously easy, but his lectures are really informative, and he encourages you to learn a lot. I HIGHLY recommend taking a class w/ Zhiqiang, he will really propel your academic career - super nice guy on top of all that too!

Took him for my fundamentals of environmental. He was pretty hard to hear during lectures and had hard to read handwritten notes for some of the material. He would get on tangents or scroll back and forth through the slides so taking notes during the lectures was extremely difficult. The exams were fair with a lot of leeway.
The best

Hard to understand at times and goes through lectures very quickly (my class finished all the material 3 weeks early) so you'll likely have to teach a few topics to yourself. Each class ends with a collaborative quiz which can be helpful when studying for the 2 exams the class has.

Does a fairly decent job of explaining concepts, but goes at a very fast pace. There's only two tests, and no final, so you really have to prepare for those. However, there's collaborative quizzes every class, as well as plenty of extra credit to boost your grade.
Well-structured and comprehensive course content. The material is relevant and up-to-date, reflecting the latest developments in the field. It is a nice course!
This is nice class. Dr. Zhang is exceedingly responsible!

Professor Zhang clearly cares about his students. His class consists of 4 module exams, a case study group project (paper and presentation) and a comprehensive final. He works very hard to have all of the test info on the slides he presents in class. He also goes back and highlights the slides that you need to know for the exams.

Love, love, love! Excellent and efficient lectures. Connects with her students and is easily reachable outside of class. The assignments correlate with exams and she assigns papers that are easy and fun to write.
Freaking awesome and so leinant! Greatly appreciated all the help and flexability!

Jen is one of the best teachers I've had at Mizzou. Her lectures are informative and her tests are really easy if you've paid attention in class. I had a small class and she provided an open environment where we all felt comfortable and had great discussions. She's relatable and kind and understanding. Every student who has her is SOOO lucky!
